title: http: retain anonymous requests under frame ownership through teardown
description:
Retain every managed HTTP request under its issuing frame, independently of the optional public request-id. Ordinary event-originated requests with no request-id currently survive destroy/restore; a late response can mutate a newly created frame with the same id.

Surface: impl_http. Parent: rf2-gwye. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Revalidated against baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261 on 2026-09-13. This is the independent lifecycle finding split from aggregate rf2-fzbj.11, not authorization to implement that aggregate's other findings.

## Evidence and contract

- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:143-209, especially 193-202: record-in-flight! stores a handle only when request-id or actor-id is truthy. Its docstring explicitly says both-nil handles are unindexed.
- registry.cljc:890-921: abort-frame-handles! discovers requests exclusively through in-flight and actor-in-flight. Both abort-in-flight-for-frame! (924-942, epoch restore) and abort-in-flight-on-frame-destroyed! (944 onward) delegate to this incomplete ownership walk.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:257-271 and 433-441: request-id remains optional and is passed unchanged into run-attempt!; plain event-originated calls have no actor owner.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1730-1868 and 2094-2099: the real attempt registers the handle and installs normal completion delivery, but an unindexed handle is never marked aborted by either boundary. Sleeping retry handles use the same incomplete registration at 1111-1138.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc:291-325: reply delivery routes to the carried frame id. It does not distinguish a later frame incarnation when the old request was not suppressed.
- spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:150 makes request-id optional. Its frame-destroy contract at 799-807 explicitly includes plain event-originated managed requests and requires cancellation with no original-target delivery. The actual restore hook likewise promises every request from the restored frame is quiesced.

## Reproducer and fresh result

Use the real managed effect, plain-atom substrate, normal reset-runtime fixture, router, destroy-frame!, and make-frame. Register :review/load to return an :rf.http/managed effect with {:request {:url "http://example.invalid/probe"} :decode :text :reply-to [:review/reply]}, omitting request-id and actor ownership. The reply event handler writes (:value reply) into :late-response in app-db.

1. Make :review/frame. Redefine ONLY transport-jvm/jvm-fetch to return a held java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture and dispatch-sync [:review/load] into that frame.
2. Destroy :review/frame, then recreate it with the same id. Its new app-db is {}.
3. Complete the old future with {:ok? true :status 200 :status-text "OK" :headers {} :body-text "old-incarnation"}.
4. Observe real-router delivery, then await a FIFO interop/next-tick barrier before reading the committed app-db.

Fresh result: indexed-before=0; cancelled-after-real-destroy=false; exactly one :ok reply; successor app-db becomes {:late-response "old-incarnation"}. The identical control adding :request-id :review/request has indexed-before=1; cancelled-after-real-destroy=true; no delivery within the bounded observation; successor app-db remains {}.

A separate fresh hook-level probe directly exercised BOTH abort-in-flight-on-frame-destroyed! and abort-in-flight-for-frame! against actual managed attempts: anonymous futures remain uncancelled and deliver :ok after either hook; the identified controls are cancelled and deliver nothing. This proves the restore HTTP quiesce hook defect; the full Epoch restore transaction/UI was not executed.

Expected: omitting optional correlation must not detach frame ownership. Destroy/restore must cancel owned host work and suppress the old response. Actual: anonymous plain work is invisible to lifecycle teardown, and the real router can commit stale state into a successor frame. The case needs no invalid input or scheduler race. It affects ordinary one-off HTTP in request-scoped, Story, hot-reload and multi-frame usage.

## Suggested repair and acceptance

Use the smallest complete ownership representation that retains all live/backoff handles by issuing frame, independently of public request-id and actor indexes. Make both frame boundaries enumerate it. Remove by handle identity on completion, failure, abort and retry transitions, keeping continuous ownership through handoffs. Preserve nil as the caller's public id and preserve existing frame-scoped request/actor lookup semantics; do not require invented caller ids or introduce new public API.

- The deterministic real-router destroy/same-id-recreate regression above fails on this baseline and passes with the repair: no successor handler commit or app effects. Keep identified and sibling-frame controls.
- Frame destroy and the actual Epoch HTTP quiesce hook cancel anonymous plain requests in both active transport and sleeping backoff, with no late reply or retry.
- Success/failure promptly release ownership; several simultaneous anonymous requests stay distinct; dual-index actor/id handles abort only once by identity.
- Exercise shared behavior on CLJS too, including external abort listener detachment. Existing actor/request publication and supersession controls must remain correct.

## Validation and deduplication

Executed fresh disposable JVM probes using cached dependencies (Clojure 1.12.4, JDK 21.0.10): ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_http/probe-impl_http-1.clj/.log/.exit and probe-impl_http-2.clj/.log/.exit, both exit 0. Probe 1 is hook-level; probe 2 is the real-router committed-state witness above. Both printed resource URLs under the exact SOURCE_ROOT, and both JVMs exited. These are focused witnesses, not a whole-suite green; decisive results and the complete reproduction recipe are recorded here because ignored scratch is not durable evidence storage.

Inspected current retry handoffs, body-preparation cancellation, terminal-once logic, reply/middleware dispatch, machine-wrapper behavior, packaging and relevant tests. Existing http_frame_destroy_abort_test.clj:156 onward uses :request-id :destroy/req, so its successful test cannot distinguish this omission. No source edits, install, shared compile or broad gate was performed; no browser/CLJS execution or exhaustive concurrent lifecycle census is claimed.

Read current aggregate rf2-fzbj.11 and its three newest history records; no newer correction changes F1. Searched current HTTP/anonymous/timeout titles and checkpoint bodies; no identical dedicated open issue was found. Closed rf2-o8ek, rf2-wjfm, rf2-ni74 and rf2-rsv2n were checked with current close reasons and newest history: they repair frame scoping, actor-hook threading, two-index publication and body-preparation issuance respectively, all distinct from a request which enters neither index. Keep those normative closures and the old aggregate unchanged.
notes:
=== VERDICT (worker http-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9745 (commit c0e893b339 on worker/http-a, branched at 031ff49a38). This is finding F1 of rf2-fzbj.11, fixed once for both beads. ===
Re-verified at that base before fixing: it reproduced exactly as described.

The fix: re-frame.http.registry now holds any managed request carrying neither :request-id nor an owning actor in a third index, anonymous-in-flight (frame-id -> handles).
- record-in-flight! writes it.
- The 2-arg clear-in-flight! removes by identity, so completion, retry handoff and every abort release it.
- clear-all-in-flight! walks it.
- abort-frame-handles! reads and clears the frame's slot in one step. That is the single walk behind both :http/on-frame-destroyed! and :http/abort-in-flight-for-frame!.
:request-id stays optional and nil; there is no public API change, and the id-keyed indexes are untouched. Spec 014 §Abort on frame destroy now states the id-less case.

Regression tests: implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_anonymous_frame_ownership_test.clj. Every assertion is behavioural, and the file was run red against the pre-fix source:
- The committed-state witness from this bead. Pre-fix, the successor app-db became {:late-response "old-incarnation"}; post-fix it stays {}, and the old future is cancelled.
- Both hooks cancel two simultaneous anonymous requests while a sibling frame's request still delivers.
- The sleeping-backoff phase issues no attempt 2. Pre-fix: 3 fetches.
- Completed success and failure release their ownership.
CLJS: cljs-destroy-frame-cancels-anonymous-backoff-and-suppresses-reply in http_cljs_test.cljs; red with the pre-fix registry planted (fetch-count 4), green on the fix.

Gates: jvm-http exit 0 (505 tests); CLJS node-test exit 0 (11991 tests).

Skipped suggestions, one sentence each:
- Dual-index handles abort once by identity: that dedupe is unchanged, and existing tests pin it.
- External abort listener detachment on CLJS: it lives in dispatch-aborted!, the single choke every abort reason already routes through.
- The full Epoch restore transaction: the regression drives the actual HTTP quiesce hook, which is all restore calls in this artefact.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9745 (commit c0e893b339), together with its aggregate rf2-fzbj.11. F1, anonymous frame ownership: the registry indexes requests with neither id under their issuing frame (anonymous-in-flight); they are removed by identity and read-and-cleared by the frame-destroy / epoch-restore sweep. F2, the JVM timeout: jvm-fetch arms orTimeout over the whole attempt, cancels the upstream sendAsync on expiry, and TimeoutException classifies as :rf.http/timeout. Both have regression tests shown red on pre-fix code; the jvm-http and CLJS node-test gates exit 0. The skipped suggestions and their one-sentence reasons are in the notes.

title: machines: compatibility reset drops spawned-actor identity and strands the live snapshot
description:
## Finding

The supported handler-entry recovery for an incompatible machine snapshot replaces the entire snapshot with the registered type's fresh initial snapshot. That is correct for authored state/data, but for a spawned actor it also deletes the runtime-owned identity envelope that makes the actor addressable. The event that discovers the incompatibility completes against the fresh definition; the next event to the same still-present actor snapshot resolves no handler and is rejected as `:rf.error/no-such-handler`.

This is a composition bug between snapshot compatibility recovery and runtime-db-derived spawned-actor liveness, not a request for a migration framework.

## Verified current behavior

I exercised the public runtime on the JVM with the machines `:test` classpath:

1. Register child type `:probe/worker` at snapshot version 1 with state `:old` and `{:n 0}`.
2. Register a parent whose transition declaratively `:spawn`s that type; capture actor id `:probe/worker#1`.
3. Re-register `:probe/worker` at snapshot version 2 with initial state `:ready`, `{:n 100}`, and a `:bump` action that increments `:n`.
4. Dispatch `:bump` twice to the actor.

Observed (process exited 0):

```clojure
{:actor :probe/worker#1
 :before-root {:state :old
               :meta #:rf{:snapshot-version 1}
               :rf/machine-type :probe/worker}
 :before-data {:n 0
               :rf/self-id :probe/worker#1
               :rf/parent-id :probe/parent
               :rf/invoke-id [:running]}
 :after-first-root {:state :ready
                    :meta #:rf{:snapshot-version 2}}
 :after-first-data {:n 101}
 :after-second-data {:n 101}
 :version-errors 1
 :no-handler-errors 1}
```

The first dispatch proves version drift is detected and the replacement definition runs. It also drops `:rf/machine-type` plus the actor lineage. The second dispatch cannot lazily resolve a handler, does not increment `:n`, and emits `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, even though the actor snapshot remains physically present in runtime-db.

## Root cause and exact surfaces

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc`, `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` (around lines 334-358), returns only `(assoc @base-initial :rf/bootstrap-pending? true)`. `prepare-machine-ctx` / `reconcile-snapshot` applies this to every existing snapshot, including spawned actors, for both `:version-mismatch` and `:state-not-in-definition`.
- That `base-initial` is derived from the current type definition. It contains authored initial data and fresh transient counters, but it cannot contain per-instance values stamped only by the spawn runtime.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc`, `machine-type-ref` and `stamp-framework-data` (around lines 252-280), establish the missing envelope: root `:rf/machine-type`; data `:rf/self-id`; optional `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc`, `spec-from-snapshot` (around lines 63-82), intentionally resolves an unregistered actor instance only through root `:rf/machine-type`.
- `registration.cljc`, `resolve-actor-handler-meta` (around lines 1347-1389), returns nil when that slot is gone, handing the next dispatch back to the router's genuine no-handler path.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, Snapshot shape invariants and Reserved snapshot-internal keys (around lines 58-87), calls these keys framework-owned and says `:rf/machine-type` persists and makes spawned liveness a function of runtime-db. The reset currently treats the identity envelope like disposable user data.

## Coverage gap

`implementation/machines/test/re_frame/snapshot_compat_test.clj` proves compatibility recovery for singleton/manual snapshots only. Spawned-actor lifecycle tests (including `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/actor_liveness_cljs_test.cljc`) prove spawn/destroy/restore resolution but do not compose it with handler-entry compatibility recovery. Consequently each feature's local tests pass while their combination strands the actor.

## Impact

Hot reload is an explicit pre-alpha productivity path: an author who correctly bumps `:rf/snapshot-version`, or merely removes a live state, can silently turn every affected spawned instance into an inert snapshot after its first post-reload event. The same lost lineage is also used for declarative ownership/finalization, and `:rf/join-child` carries exact-attempt completion correlation for `:spawn-all`; losing it can break parent cleanup or join completion even during the reset event. The directly reproduced impact is the actor becoming unaddressable on the next dispatch.

## Bounded recommendation

Keep the existing fresh-user-snapshot reset, but preserve or reconstruct a deliberately small, canonical spawned-actor identity envelope from the existing snapshot before bootstrap/transition processing. At minimum this includes root `:rf/machine-type` and data `:rf/self-id`; when present, retain the runtime-stamped ownership/correlation values `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`. Implement this through one named helper/catalogue so snapshot recovery and spawn agree on which values are durable actor identity.

Do not merge the old `:data` map wholesale: authored data and transient timer/spawn/history counters should continue to reset exactly as the current compatibility contract intends.

## Non-goals

- No general snapshot migration API or user hook.
- No per-instance handler registry or change to runtime-db-derived liveness.
- No broad merge of old user data, timer epochs, spawn counters, or history into the new definition.
- No redesign of actor ids, spawning, hot reload, or epoch restore.

## Posture rationale

This is a narrow fix with high ergonomic leverage. It makes the documented, simple action (bump the snapshot version during a pre-alpha definition change) safe for the ordinary SPA actor model. Preserving the runtime-owned envelope keeps the API minimal and trusts the programmer; it avoids both a migration subsystem and surprising zombie actors.

## Duplicate and history search

I searched the review-time tracker corpus (923 issues) across titles/descriptions/notes/close reasons and repeated `bd search` queries for `machine-type`, `snapshot-version`, `version mismatch`, `state-not-in-definition`, `compatibility`, `hot reload`, `reset-to-initial`, `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot`, `spawned actor`, `inert snapshot`, and `no-such-handler`. No issue described this reset/liveness composition. Spawn-related matches concerned mixed-prefix teardown, naming, tooling branches, cancellation docs, and websocket correlation; hot-reload matches were unrelated examples/templates/Hicasso work.

Relevant landed history shows why the gap is plausible:

- `6b445ca978` (2026-05-14), snapshot-compatibility checks, introduced `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` with singleton-oriented tests.
- `38b5a25407` (2026-06-03), runtime-db-derived spawned-actor liveness, later made `:rf/machine-type` the dispatch authority.
- `d0ce1cd437` (2026-06-09), spawned-actor version-drift checks on epoch restore, did not exercise a subsequent handler-entry rebuild.

No later commit in the affected files adds a compatibility-reset/spawn composition test or restores the envelope.

## Uncertainty

The live reproduction exercises the version-mismatch branch for a registered `:machine-id` spawn. The state-not-in-definition branch calls the identical replacement helper, so its identity loss is source-proven but was not separately driven. Loss of subsequent handler resolution is directly observed; the additional parent/join lifecycle effects follow from the documented consumers of the erased lineage and should be pinned by focused regression tests rather than assumed beyond those paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a regression test in `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/snapshot_compat_test.clj` (or a narrowly named spawned-compatibility test) that declaratively spawns a registered v1 type, re-registers it with a v2 definition, dispatches at least two events to the same actor, and proves: exactly one mismatch recovery occurs, the first event uses the fresh definition, the second event is processed, no `:rf.error/no-such-handler` occurs, and the snapshot remains handler-resolvable.
- Cover `:state-not-in-definition` as the second entry path into the same recovery behavior, either by parameterizing the regression or with one focused sibling assertion.
- Compatibility recovery still replaces authored state/data and resets transient runtime counters per the existing contract; it does not wholesale merge the old snapshot.
- The recovered spawned snapshot preserves/reconstructs the canonical runtime identity envelope: root `:rf/machine-type`, data `:rf/self-id`, and any present `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`. Registered keyword and inline-definition type references remain valid.
- Add one lifecycle assertion that an affected declarative child can still complete/tear down through its parent after recovery; if the implementation touches `:rf/join-child`, pin exact-attempt `:spawn-all` completion as well.
- Existing singleton compatibility behavior and trace shapes remain unchanged. Update the implementation/spec prose only where needed to state that reset replaces user state while retaining framework-owned actor identity.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor's backlog reread — CHECK 3, a reverted closure. THIRD instance today of the worker-close-mid-tick race, and the discrimination needed a different instrument this time.

WHY THE USUAL TEST WAS NOT AVAILABLE. For rf2-hic-064 and rf2-2hpxo the tell was a notes field unchanged across the newest snapshots. Here NOTES IS EMPTY — 0 characters in every snapshot — so "unchanged" would have been the null-hash trap: an absent field hashes constant and reports a clean walk in exactly the words a genuinely unchanged one does. Believing it would have been believing nothing.

SO I CONTROLLED AGAINST FIELDS THAT DO VARY ON THIS ITEM. The description holds at 7,847 characters and acceptance_criteria at 1,562 across the newest six snapshots, while 23 snapshots in the history DO carry status=closed — so the item was genuinely closed and the only thing that moved back is the status. Control on a bead that is closed and stayed closed (rf2-4thn) returns 19 closed snapshots by the same query, so the query discriminates.

NO AUDIT OBLIGATION. Greps for AUDIT-REOPEN, "REOPENED THIS EXACT", REOPENED, "residual" and "still owed" all return zero, against a control counting rf2- references that returns 1, so the instrument bites. Contrast rf2-c5w1 and rf2-o8ek, which reverted in the same window and DO carry REOPENED markers with residuals — those are audits and stay open. This one wrote nothing, because nothing reopened it.

THE DELIVERABLE IS ON MAIN, verified in the tree: PR #9192 reads state=MERGED, and `carry-actor-identity` resolves at tip in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc. The fix carried a real red witness — 17 assertion failures with the tests in place and the fix absent, 1244 tests / 4528 assertions green after — plus a 210-line snapshot-compat suite and the two-line spec/005 clarification at invariants 3 and 4. Nothing about this bead's output is missing.

MECHANISM, unchanged from the earlier two: the prescribed checkpoint-then-checkout ordering protects the MAYOR's own tracker mutations, because the checkpoint exports them before the checkout restores that same commit. It does not protect a WORKER's close landing between my checkpoint's export and my checkout. All three instances today fit that shape — a worker closed the bead, I verified CLOSED immediately after merging its PR, and a later tick found it open with its text intact.

STILL NOT PROPOSING A PROCESS CHANGE. Three re-closes across a session is cheaper than reordering a sequence that exists to prevent tracker time-travel, and check 3 catches every instance by design. What this one adds is the lesson that the discrimination must use a field that VARIES on the item in front of you — the notes-length test is not universal.

title: hic: workspace.md step 6 says copy the brief FROM brief-<pilot>.md, not the block INSIDE it — a literal copy hands the blinded pilot 4 bead ids and a link to the operator page
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, operator half, re-run after PR #9050 and #9049. Workspace pin cfcc30ae93. This is a BLINDING LEAK on the dispatch path and should be fixed BEFORE the two pilots are dispatched.

THE DEFECT. workspace.md step 6 reads: "Copy the brief and the blank log into <pilot-root>/, from brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md, and from friction-log.md's template section." Note the asymmetry inside that one sentence. For the friction log it names the SUB-PART ("template section"). For the brief it names the WHOLE FILE. But brief-realworld.md's own line 3 says "Copy the block below into <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md. Everything inside it is written to the pilot agent and is the only thing that agent is given" -- the pilot's brief is the content of the fenced markdown block, not the file.

So an operator executing step 6 literally runs "cp brief-realworld.md <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md" and hands a BLINDED pilot all of the following, none of which is inside the fence:

  1. Four tracker ids -- rf2-v04s, rf2-hic-063, rf2-xkhul, rf2-lpfz -- where the read fence's "Not allowed" column explicitly bars "Reading the tracker, git log, or any branch".
  2. A relative link to README.md#what-governs-this-directory -- the governance page, under docs/design/, out of bounds by the fence's own mkdocs rule.
  3. A relative link to workspace.md -- THE OPERATOR PAGE, of which workspace.md line 5 says "A pilot agent is never sent here". The pilot's own brief links it.
  4. The meta-paragraph explaining that the brief "is deliberately free of in-tree references" and that "a brief that leaks in-tree knowledge does not bend a rule, it invalidates the evidence the pilot exists to produce". That tells the pilot it is inside a blinding experiment being measured -- which is itself the leak the paragraph warns about.
  5. The enclosing markdown code fence, left as literal lines 11 and 157 of the delivered file.

MEASURED, BOTH PILOTS, AND THE TWO OPERATORS DIVERGED -- which is the evidence the instruction is ambiguous rather than merely terse:

  source brief-realworld.md ................ 8738 bytes, 4 bead ids
  my LITERAL step-6 copy ................... 8829 bytes, 4 bead ids, starts "# Brief -- Pilot 1: RealWorld/Conduit"
  the PREVIOUS rehearsal operator's copy ... 7066 bytes, 0 bead ids, starts "# Your brief"

The previous operator INTERPRETED step 6 and extracted the fenced block. I executed it literally and did not. Same page, same step, two different artefacts, and only one of them is blind. Both pilots are affected: the linearlite copy carries 2 bead ids by the same route.

WHY IT FAILS OPEN. The copy succeeds, exits 0, and produces a file that reads like a brief -- the pilot-facing content is all present and correct, just preceded by front matter. Nothing errors, nothing is missing, and the operator has no reason to look. The damage is invisible until somebody re-reads the delivered file, and by then the pilot has read it.

MINIMAL FIX, and it is one clause. Make step 6's brief half name the sub-part the way its friction-log half already does: "from the fenced block inside brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md". Optionally add the same "Copy from here into <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md" pointer that friction-log.md's template section carries, so the two halves of step 6 are shaped alike. Do NOT restructure the briefs, move the front matter, or touch the fence -- the briefs are correct as written and say so themselves on line 3; it is workspace.md that under-specifies.

RELATION TO rf2-lpfz. Distinct. rf2-lpfz's reopened residue is pilots/README.md line 30, an operator-facing page a pilot never receives. This bead is about a pilot-facing artefact that step 6 mis-specifies, and it is the one that reaches the agent.

NOT A BLOCKER for the boot check or the baselines, both of which pass; see the rehearsal report on rf2-t4jpz. It IS a blocker for a CORRECT dispatch: per rf2-hic-063's revisit trigger (a), a leaky rehearsal finds no friction and is worthless, so dispatching on the literal artefact would burn both pilots.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058. workspace.md step 6 now names the sub-part for the brief exactly as it already did for the friction log: 'from the fenced block inside brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md, and from the fenced block inside friction-log.md's template section', plus one sentence saying it is the block that is copied and why the front matter above it is a leak. The briefs' front matter, the fence and the briefs themselves are untouched, as the bead directs. PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by reading: I ran the corrected step 6 literally against both briefs and the log template and asserted on the products -- realworld/BRIEF.md 7433 bytes/143 lines, linearlite/BRIEF.md 8967/170, FRICTION-LOG.md 1290/54, and all three carry 0 lines with a bead id, 0 links to workspace.md and 0 stray fence lines. The same three patterns run against the source pages as controls and all bite (brief-realworld.md 2/1/2, brief-linearlite.md 2/1/2, friction-log.md 6/4/6), so the zeroes are checks that passed rather than patterns that missed. Extraction boundaries checked at both ends. For contrast the pre-fix literal copy is 8738 bytes carrying 4 unique bead ids and a workspace.md link.

title: machines/SSR: hydration leaves pre-existing timers absent from the replacement snapshot
description:
## Scope

Repair the SSR-to-client handoff for state-machine `:after` transitions. The scope is active singleton and spawned snapshots under `[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots]`, including flat/compound states, active paths in root-parallel regions, and a root-parallel `:after`. Keep ordinary transition semantics and epoch restore semantics unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The server intentionally suppresses machine wall-clock timers, but the client hydration path only installs the serialized runtime-db snapshot. It does not reconstruct the host-side timer table for active `:after` declarations and does not re-run machine entry. A machine hydrated while sitting in an `:after`-bearing state therefore has the right durable `:state`, `:data`, and `:rf/after-epoch`, but no live timer. It can remain in that state forever unless some unrelated external event moves it.

This contradicts the local contract that timers begin on the client after hydration. It is also the relevant conformity lesson from XState v6 persistence: durable state and host work are distinct, and restoring a snapshot must explicitly reconstruct the timer runtime without replaying historical effects.

## Evidence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (`build-after-fx`, around lines 2059-2144) emits `:rf.machine/after-schedule` only while processing newly-entered nodes. In server mode the effect carries `:server? true` and the timer is skipped.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc` keeps timer handles/watchers in a process-local timer table; they are not part of the hydration payload.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` (`hydrate-event-handler*`) installs the payload's runtime-db and has one late-bound reconciliation hook for Resources. There is no Machines hydration/re-arm hook or machine scheduling effect.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` inventories Machines hooks for SSR projection, timer cleanup on frame destroy/epoch restore, and timer scheduling, but no hydration reconstruction hook.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc` projects durable machine snapshots only; it cannot carry host timer handles.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` lines 1323 and 2444-2448 say server timers no-op and the client schedules them after hydration.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`, section “`:after` is no-op under SSR”, requires `:after` timers to begin running on the client against the preserved snapshot epoch.
- `docs/machines/automatic-transitions.md` states: “The client re-arms timers after hydration.”
- XState v6's official persistence contract includes timers in the durable snapshot shape and restores without replaying historical entry effects: https://stately.ai/docs/xstate/v6/persistence and https://stately.ai/docs/xstate/v6/how-xstate-runs-machines . Exact comparison baseline: `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.50` (`0b52534e`), released 2026-08-27.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Failure scenario/invariant

Given a server-rendered machine whose active state declares `:after {5000 {:target :timeout}}`:

1. Server entry bumps/stores the node's `:rf/after-epoch`, emits the skipped-on-server trace, and schedules no host timer.
2. The hydration payload carries the active snapshot and epoch.
3. `:rf/hydrate` installs that snapshot on the client without entering the state.
4. No client timer exists, so advancing beyond 5000 ms never dispatches the synthetic elapsed event and the machine remains stuck.

Required invariant: after a successful client hydration commit, every live active `:after` declaration represented by the hydrated snapshot has exactly one client timer/watch armed for that snapshot's existing epoch, without replaying unrelated entry behavior.

## Recommended minimal fix

Add one hydration-only Machines reconciliation seam, analogous in ownership to the existing Resources hydration hook:

- Have the Machines artefact publish a late-bound hydration hook/effect that runs only after a valid client `:rf/hydrate` has committed the payload runtime-db.
- Walk the hydrated live snapshots, resolve each actor's registered/inline machine definition using existing resolver paths, enumerate only the currently active nodes (plus the root-parallel node), and schedule their declared `:after` entries through the existing timer scheduler.
- Reuse the persisted `:rf/after-epoch`; do not bump it.
- Resolve literal/function/subscription delays on the client. Because the wire does not carry a schedule timestamp or due-at value, arm the full declared client-relative delay, matching the repository's existing SSR contract.
- Do not re-run `:entry`, actions, raises, spawns, or other effects. Do not reuse the epoch-restore callback: epoch restore deliberately cancels host work and must continue not to revive it.
- Make repeated hydration/scheduling idempotent by the existing timer-table key or an equally small guard, so it never leaves duplicate handles/watchers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused hydration integration test registers an `:after` machine, produces/installs an SSR-shaped runtime-db snapshot, hydrates on a client frame, and proves exactly one timer is armed with the persisted epoch and its callback performs the declared transition.
- The test proves the timer was not armed on the server and that hydration does not re-run an entry action, raise, or spawn.
- Coverage includes a compound active path and root-parallel coverage sufficient to prove active region nodes and root-owned `:after` declarations are enumerated correctly.
- A dynamic subscription/function delay is resolved on the client through the existing scheduling path; watcher teardown/cancellation remains correct.
- Negative controls prove that a snapshot with no active `:after`, a rejected malformed/wrong-frame hydration, and a server-side hydrate arm no timers.
- Existing epoch-restore coverage continues to prove `:machines/on-frame-restored!` cancels timers and does not re-arm them.
- Existing timer traces remain coherent; hydration-created timers emit one normal scheduled trace (with actor, path/state, delay source, epoch, and frame) rather than a misleading state-entry replay.
- Relevant spec/docs wording and late-bind directory inventory match the implemented hydration-only seam.

## Non-goals

- A general durable workflow engine, snapshot migration framework, elapsed-time/due-at persistence, or cross-process clock reconciliation.
- Replaying all machine entry behavior during hydration.
- Reviving timers during epoch/time-travel restore.
- Serializing browser timer handles or subscription objects.
- Matching XState's actor API or persistence wire format.

title: [MERGED #10126] Incomplete unknown-prior handling: nested after-tail containers become false additions
description:
Merged-PR audit #10114, merge b61ad91f75f8c596a69cd241dabf0682492d77e2, source rf2-zk4he. The recovered scalar tail is visible and bounded, but the new ::unrealised before slot is not preserved through container recursion. The claim that an unknown prior no longer becomes a confident addition is incomplete for ordinary nested EDN.

Reproduction with the REAL merged engine and exact merged pure helpers: full = (assoc (vec (range 1050)) 1049 {:keep 1 :other 2 :third 3 :fourth 4}); before = (map identity full); after = full; projection = (engine/project before after). These have identical values: projection :flat-rows is []. sequential-diff-children now correctly emits 1050 rows, with final triple [1049 {:keep 1 :other 2 :third 3 :fourth 4} ::unrealised]. But expanding/recursing into that map calls children-of-pair with the sentinel as before and the real map as after. Its map arm emits ::missing for every prior. leaf-diff-op consequently returns :added for all four children, even though engine/op-at returns :same for each. An unchanged collection gains fabricated additions.

Production chain at this merge: sequential-diff-children:1670-1675 creates the new unknown slot; render-block-child:2735-2738 passes it unchanged into render-node; render-node:3582-3595 forwards it into render-container. classify-container-op:2421-2425 also compares the unknown marker to the map as an actual value and promotes :same to :children, so the unchanged tail is treated as change-bearing. render-container:2895-2900 descends via children-of-pair; its map arm:1433-1436 treats the marker as an absent/non-map before value and invents ::missing slots; render-grid-child-row:2632-2636 passes these to render-node, whose structural addition branch:3557-3577 / leaf-diff-op:3173 overrides the correct projection. The scalar-only sentinel test in this PR does not exercise this path.

Required correction: carry unknown-prior semantics through container classification and recursion, without interpreting unknown as absent or as proof of a change. Preserve the projection classifications when available and represent genuinely unknown prior detail honestly. Keep the before-side realization bound and all accessible after data; do not widen the bound or add a new inspector framework. Add a rendering regression for an unchanged nested container in the recovered tail, checking the descendants as well as the parent and row count, with a real-added control.

This is NOT the exact OPEN rf2-idydb defect. That item covers children-of-pair directly bounding two sequential inputs and filling its truncated sequential before-tail with ::missing; here the projection-aware walker already supplies ::unrealised and the nested MAP recursion converts it back into absence. Fixing only that existing sequential arm leaves this reproduction intact. Hence a separate open finding, not extra corrective work buried on the closed source.

Evidence: source-isolated JVM probe ai/audit-tail-nested-audit-sep20-monitor-3.clj with exact merged helpers and exact merged engine, pinned editscript 0.6.5. ai/gate-tail-nested-audit-sep20-monitor-3.log and .exit: exit 0, correct worktree and merge SHA. It proves four :same -> :added classifications; counted-before control stays four :same; predecessor drops the map tail (1001 rows); repaired scalar-tail control emits 1050 with exactly 1001 before realizations; counted removal alignment still strikes only element 500. This is pure-helper execution plus traced production wiring, not a local mounted-browser claim. Merged CLJS/node, browser, and Xray CI passed but lacks this nested-tail case.
acceptance_criteria: A projection-aware mixed-representation diff with an unchanged nested map beyond index 1000 preserves that map and does not classify its existing descendants as added or force a change solely because the prior is unknown. Add a render-path regression with unchanged nested tail and real-added controls; preserve bounded before realization, scalar-tail visibility, and removal alignment.

All ten P2 assertions passed.

## Mechanism, confirmed at source — TWO sites, as the item's scope says

RECURSION. children-of-pair is reached recursively and the before it is handed can be the
::unrealised sentinel rather than a collection. Every arm asks (when (map? before) before) /
(when (sequential? before) before) and gets nil, because a keyword is neither, so the walk
took its one-sided branch and reported each child's prior ABSENT. ::missing is the STRUCTURAL
sentinel that leaf-diff-op reads AHEAD of the projection, so an unchanged collection gained a
full set of :added rows. An UNKNOWN prior was converted into an ABSENT one at a single when.

CLASSIFICATION. classify-container-op's structural override compares before to value as two
VALUES; differs-within-bound? found a keyword differing from the after map and promoted the
projection's :same to :children, painting the unchanged container change-bearing and
auto-expanding it before its descendants were walked at all.

New private unpaired-prior answers ::unrealised when the before side IS that marker and
::missing otherwise. The four one-sided arms (map, sequential, set, map-entry) route their
before slot through it. Keyed on the marker being PRESENT, never on the before side's kind,
so a genuinely absent prior still says ::missing and still renders :added. It realises
nothing to decide and emits the same row counts, so diff-pair-count still agrees with the
body. classify-container-op now excludes unrealised-sentinel from its override exactly as it
already excluded missing-sentinel.

No new representation and no fourth state: the file already documented the distinction one
arm did not implement, which is what bounded the fix.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, and this is the one place I narrowed the item's wording: the
no-projection differs-within-bound? arm below the override. There an unknown prior really is
undecidable, and :children is the honest answer rather than a claim of change, because it

title: Incomplete reactive keyboard toggle: an open Xray popout keeps consuming disabled shortcuts
description:
Audit of PR #9939 (86cfef4e43844deb36d3222dbfa923191447809d). The new config/keybinding-enabled? watch in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:629-634 only calls attach!/detach!, which manage the opener document's attached-state/attached-fn. The same namespace installs a separate capture listener on the popout document at :565-595, checks the config flag only during installation, and leaves its disposer with mount. The opener detaches, but the existing popout still prevents default / stops propagation / dispatches on Cmd/Ctrl+K and the other shortcuts. The PR's claim that the toggle works at runtime is incomplete across supported surfaces.
Required correction: make the live popout respect both directions of the same switch using the existing per-document listener/disposer lifecycle. A small lifecycle subscription or current-flag guard with an always-installed popout listener is sufficient; no new global listener registry is required. Add a real installed-popout-handler regression covering enabled -> disabled -> enabled and a popout initially opened disabled, plus disposer cleanup. The new tests only redefine opener attach!/detach! and cannot catch this. Preserve the public detach! escape hatch. Source inspection only; no local runtime execution claimed. Existing rf2-y8doi.42 covers stale configuration prose, not this code behavior.

The required `cljs` job compiled `node-test` with a bare `npx shadow-cljs`, so the warnings-fatal gate built for that lane (rf2-4a6ei) NEVER RAN ON THE PR LANE. The local spine has always run `npm run test:cljs`, so the two lanes disagreed about the same tree: the spine refused what this job merged.

THE CONTROL IS THE CLEANEST OF THE WAVE -- one planted fault, one tree, two commands, every number the runner's own CAPTURED exit:
  * BARE form (the old CI step): captured exit 0, WRONGLY GREEN. Four `Use of undeclared Var` warnings, and `Ran 12160 tests containing 60626 assertions. / 0 failures, 0 errors.` -- counts BYTE-IDENTICAL to the clean run. The only number that moved was the warning tally, which nothing read.
  * WRAPPER form (the new CI step): captured exit 1, RED, naming `compiled 2 of 2021 files with 4 WARNING(S)`.
  * Clean runs of the wrapper, before and on the final rebased base: 0 and 0. The second was run DELIBERATELY rather than as a re-confirmation -- arming a warnings-fatal gate on a REQUIRED job is only safe if trunk compiles warning-free, and it does.

THE MECHANISM IS WORTH KEEPING because it explains why identical counts are not evidence of identical behaviour: a bare quote inside a deftest docstring closes the string early, the words after it become bare symbols, and in JavaScript those compile to `undefined` and evaluate harmlessly. description:
# Senior review: routing

Reviewer persona: senior client-side routing engineer (react-router / reitit / Angular-router class) — URL matching, history integration, navigation blocking, scroll restoration, nav-token stale suppression.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc` + every `routing/*.cljc` (29 files, 12,218 lines, all read in full — registry, navigate, url_change, match, url, decisions, resolve, plan, events, scroll, nav_token, nav_counters, history, strategy, link, address, url_bound, prefetch, replan, subs, readiness, reply, tooling, classification, sub_egress, nav_fx, nav_fx_schemas, test_support). Tests skimmed by grep for what is pinned: `routing_navigation_test.clj`, `routing_nav_counters_test.clj`, `routing_history_cljs_test.cljs`, `routing_scroll_test.clj`, `routing_url_strategy_*`.
Owning specs consulted: `spec/012-Routing.md` (all 2084 lines), `spec/011-SSR.md` §Hydration protocol / §The `:rf/hydrate` event / §Client-side hydration boot helper, `spec/Ownership.md` row 59 (by reference). Also `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc` (`registrations`), `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc` where a finding crosses the artefact boundary.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The nav-token allocator is never floored at the token already published in the slice, so a slice installed by any path other than `commit-navigation` can be followed by a commit that re-mints the same token  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/nav_counters.cljc:211-223` (`nav-allocation-cofx` mints from `counter-snapshot` alone), `:153-160` (`release-frame!` drops the high-water mark), `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:225-234, 256` (`commit-navigation` publishes `:token` and reads `prev-nav-token`).
- What: Spec 012 §Navigation tokens says the allocator "MUST NOT wrap or recycle" and a full activation "allocates a FRESH nav-token", but the mint reads only the host counter, never `[:rf.runtime/routing :current :nav-token]`; three doors put a token in the slice the counter has not seen — SSR hydration (`:rf/hydrate` replaces runtime-db wholesale and touches no counter), a `destroy-frame!` + same-id `make-frame` (the counter entry is dissoc'ed, so the new incarnation restarts at `nav-1` while a continuation captured under the old `nav-1` may still be in flight — exactly the "compared across incarnations" bug class), and a hydrate dispatched from `:initial-events` (the owner's initial URL sync then reads identical and skips the counter bump).
- Evidence: traced `nav-allocation-cofx` → `next-nav-token` → `next-id` (no slice read). Grep `nav-token|nav-counter|routing` in `ssr/hydrate.cljc` → one comment hit (:66), nothing executable; control: the same grep in `ssr/ssr.cljc` hits :193. `routing_nav_counters_test.clj:220-233` pins that destroy RELEASES the entry (the leak concern) — which is the recreate door. When `prev-nav-token = token`, `commit-navigation` overwrites `:resource-plan token` in place and a same-route param change (`/articles/5` → `/articles/6`) hands the Resources release the same owner key `[:route :route/article "nav-N"]` it just attached — worth checking on the resources side. Confirm with a JVM test: seed a fresh frame's slice with `:nav-token "nav-7"` (via `:rf/hydrate` or a direct runtime-db write), navigate once, assert the new token is not `"nav-7"` (today it is `"nav-1"`, and a second navigation mints `"nav-2"`… never reaching 7 before colliding).
- Action: in `nav-allocation-cofx`, floor the mint at the live slice token — parse the trailing integer of `(get-in rdb [:rf.runtime/routing :current :nav-token])` and take `(max counter that)` before `inc` (one `let`; the cofx already reads `*current-frame*`). Optionally stop dropping the high-water mark in `release-frame!` (one long per frame id is not a leak worth the recycle). Add the test above; note the floor in Spec 012 §Navigation tokens ¶"Storage".

### 2. `[:rf.route/navigate {:url …}]` on a URL that pattern-matches but fails the route schema is silently rejected, where the identical URL through the URL-driven door lands on the 404 view with `:reason :validation`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:316-327` (takes `(:route-id match)` and `(:params match)` for a validation-failed match), `:458-471` (`route-url` throws on the string params → `::reject`), `:485-486` (returns `{}`); the seam that already computed the not-found target is `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc:213-222`.
- What: Spec 012 §Target form sells `{:url}` as the door "for dynamic or user-supplied URLs the app didn't build itself" and §Param validation rules that "URL-driven navigation is user input — schema failures are 404s, not exceptions"; yet a deep-link handler dispatching `{:url "/articles/zoo"}` against `:params [:map [:id :int]]` gets no slice write, no push, and — per the spec's own ¶"Both rejections survive a release build; neither report does" — nothing on any channel in production. `{:url "/no/such/path"}` (a miss) renders the 404 page; `{:url "/articles/zoo"}` (a match that fails validation) does nothing. The programmatic-door comment (navigate.cljc:286-293) calls this asymmetry "ratified", but the resolve-target table it cites only names the miss case.
- Evidence: end-to-end trace above. No test pins the `{:url}` + validation-fail outcome: grep `:url "/` in `routing_navigation_test.clj` → 25 hits, all misses / malformed / fragment cases; control: the `{:to}` + validation-fail reject IS pinned at `:1183` and the URL-driven `:reason :validation` at `:462`.
- Action: decide — (A) on `validation-fail?` have the `{:url}` branch take `(:route-id target)` / `(:params target)` from `url-resolution` (the not-found fallback the URL door commits), ~3 lines, so a user-supplied URL degrades to the 404 view on every build; or (B) keep the reject and add the sentence to §Target form plus a test. A is what a deep-link handler wants; the `{:to}` reject stays as is either way.

### 3. Nothing sets `history.scrollRestoration = "manual"`, so the browser's own traversal scroll-restore runs after the popstate handler and overrides `:rf.nav/scroll`  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:108-119` (`history-install-listener!`), `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc:457-469` (`scroll-fx-handler`).
- What: with the default `auto`, browsers restore the entry's saved scroll position on Back/Forward asynchronously after `popstate` dispatch; the runtime's `dispatch-sync!` scroll runs first and loses. A route declaring `:scroll :top` or `:preserve` is restored anyway on Back; a fragment `scrollIntoView` on Back is overridden; `:restore` scrolls twice to (usually) the same coordinates, which is visible when the page height changed. Every SPA router that owns scroll (react-router `ScrollRestoration`, TanStack) flips the flag for exactly this reason; Spec 012 §Scroll restoration's first sentence acknowledges the browser default and then specifies runtime-owned behaviour without claiming ownership.
- Evidence: grep `scrollRestoration` under `implementation/` → 0 files; control: `scrollTo` → 42 hits in 13 files including `scroll.cljc`. Confirm in a browser: route with `:scroll :top`, scroll down, push another route, Back, read `window.scrollY` after one frame.
- Action: set `js/history.scrollRestoration = "manual"` in `history-install-listener!` (and `hash-install-listener!`), restore `"auto"` in the teardown thunk; one sentence in Spec 012 §Scroll restoration saying the URL-owning frame takes scroll ownership from the browser.

### 4. `(into (array-map) …)` promotes to a hash-map at the 9th entry, so the "deterministic canonical order" the spec promises for query keys silently stops holding above 8 keys  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1032-1033` (`canonical-query-order`), `:1113-1115` (`query-without-defaults`), `:1847-1852` (`emitted-query` in `route-url`); the raw parse at `:1288` and `coerce-query` at `:1003` promote the same way via `assoc`.
- What: Clojure and CLJS `PersistentArrayMap` hand off to `PersistentHashMap` once a transient/assoc exceeds 8 entries, so each of the three "sorted array-map" sites returns a hash-map whose iteration order is trie order, not `canonical-bytes` order; Spec 012 §Bidirectional URL ↔ params ("query keys are emitted in deterministic canonical order") and the three docstrings claiming an array-map are false for a 9-key filter page. Same key set still iterates the same way on both hosts (same hashes, same trie), so no hydration mismatch in practice — only the stated ordering.
- Evidence: documented core semantics (`PersistentArrayMap/HASHTABLE_THRESHOLD` = 16 slots; `TransientArrayMap.doAssoc` promotes); the CLAUDE.md `source_coords.cljc` note records the same promotion on this tree.
- Action: decide — `(apply array-map (mapcat identity sorted-pairs))` at the three sort sites (an array-map built by `array-map` keeps its order at any size), or drop the ordering sentence from the spec and the docstrings. Don't litigate further.

### 5. A URL-driven rejection restores the address bar with `replaceState`, which overwrites the history entry the user just traversed to  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:280-281, 315, 340`.
- What: Back from `/editor` to `/cart` with `:can-leave` rejecting → `replaceState("/editor")` on the `/cart` entry; `:rf.route/cancel` then leaves the stack `[…, /editor, /editor]` with `/cart` gone (`continue` repairs it via the forced `:replace? true`). An entry denial does the same permanently. Spec 012 §The leave decision locks "a history replace, so no entry is added" and does not name this cost.
- Evidence: `restore-url` is emitted only when `url-driven?` and the rejection path never touches `history.go`; `strategy.cljc` `:push!` stores no index in `history.state`, so a `go(delta)` reversal has nothing to compute the delta from.
- Action: decide — accept and record the cost in the spec sentence (cheap, my recommendation at pre-alpha), or stamp an index into `history.state` on push/replace and reverse a rejected traversal with `history.go(delta)` while ignoring the resulting popstate (the react-router shape; a real change).

### 6. Rebuilding a `:rf.route/not-found` slice's URL yields the not-found route's own pattern (`/404`), not the URL the user is on  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:187-205` (`current-slice->url`), `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc:182-203` (`route-slice-url`, the scroll-cache key).
- What: the slice's `:params {:url "/real/url" …}` carries the URL, but both rebuilds go through `route-url` with the not-found route's pattern, so a URL-driven rejection while on a 404 page restores the address bar to `/404` (and if no not-found route is registered, restores nothing), and every 404 page shares one scroll-cache key.
- Evidence: `route-url` is exempted from the uncaptured-params check for `:rf.route/not-found` (registry.cljc:1638-1648) precisely so this call succeeds — and it succeeds with the wrong answer.
- Action: in both helpers, when `(:route-id slice)` is `:rf.route/not-found` return `(get-in slice [:params :url])`; two lines.

## Considered, left alone
- `match-url` short-circuits on the highest-ranked pattern match even when its schema rejects the URL (a lower-ranked route that would validate is never tried) — Spec 012 §Route ranking pseudocode orders match → rank → validate, and reitit does the same.
- A continued (blocked → `:rf.route/continue`) popstate replays through the programmatic door as cause `:navigate` with a `:top` scroll default (`decisions.cljc:489-491` stores no cause) — one `cond->` line to store `:scroll :restore` if wanted; cosmetic.
- A non-ASCII or space literal in a `:path` (`/café`) is emitted verbatim by `route-url`, stored by `pushState` as `/caf%C3%A9`, and never re-matches on reload — the grammar says literals match as written and only the five reserved chars are validated; trust the programmer (an ASCII check in `validate-literal-segment!` is one line if it ever bites).
- `route-table`'s `identical?` cache key is defeated under an EP-0023 generation resolver (`registrar.cljc:243-255` allocates a fresh map per `registrations` call) — a rank sort per `match-url`, not a hot path.
- `:query-defaults` values are never checked against the `:query` schema at `reg-route` (`{:page "1"}` on an `:int` slot 404s every URL missing `page`) — trust the programmer.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep16 rev-parse --short HEAD` → `d89a41e057`.
- Read (Read tool, full files) every `implementation/routing/src/**/*.cljc`; line total from `wc -l` over `git ls-files implementation/routing` → 12,218 src lines.
- Grep `scrollRestoration` in `implementation/` → 0 files. Control: grep `scrollTo` → 42 hits / 13 files including `routing/scroll.cljc` (2).
- Grep `nav-token|nav-counter|routing` in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` → 1 hit, a comment (:66). Control: same pattern in `ssr.cljc` → hits at :193 and in `payload_policy.cljc` :440-463.
- Grep `:url "/` in `routing_navigation_test.clj` → 25 hits, none a matched-but-invalid URL. Control: grep `:validation|validation-failed` → the URL-driven pin at :462-482 and the `{:to}` reject pin at :1183-1234 (read both).
- Grep `release-frame!|destroy-frame!` in `routing/test` → 30 hits; read `routing_nav_counters_test.clj:220-233` (pins release on destroy; no destroy→recreate→navigate token assertion). Control: the same grep finds `routing_scroll_test.clj:369-376` for the scroll-cache release.
- Read `registrar.cljc:923-959` (`registrations` atom branch returns the stored map by identity — so the route-table cache is sound on the default path) and `:243-255` (resolver branch allocates).
- Read `spec/012-Routing.md` in five chunks (120-2084) and `spec/011-SSR.md` §423-452 (`hydrate!` boot order: the target frame already exists when `:rf/hydrate` runs).

description:
HOLD — AWAITING MIKE. This is a FINDING from rf2-0ae7o.11 (PR #9874), claim (c). The contract gives no verdict, so it needs a ruling before any worker touches it.

THE BEHAVIOUR, reproduced by the rf2-0ae7o.11 worker at base 4c3bfb9242:
- The unfilled real-setup upgrade scaffold (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/view_state.cljc, about :410), pasted unedited, reads {:status :pass :warnings [] :assertions []} on the JVM through story/run.
- In the browser it reads pass on the canvas and in story/run. The Tests pane says "No tests registered", and the sidebar shows no dot.
- So the scaffold an author is told to fill in reads green before anything is filled in.

WHY THE CONTRACT IS SILENT:
- Story spec 017 says a zero-assertion clean run is :pass (vacuously green).
- Its agreement floor counts only a schema failure, a non-:ok epoch outcome and an :error effect row. The placeholder dispatches an event with no handler, which is none of those, so the run does not fail.
- Nothing in spec 017 or docs/story/05 addresses unfilled placeholders.

OPTIONS:
1. Accept it. A vacuous green stays green.
2. Extend the agreement floor so that a :rf.error/no-such-handler raised during setup or script fails the run. That needs one spec 017 sentence plus tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/evidence.cljc.
3. Emit a sentinel placeholder that the variant refuses to run until it is filled.
4. Make every zero-assertion run non-pass.

RECOMMENDATION (the worker’s, and the mayor’s): option 2.
- It removes a false-green class without adding a concept.
- It also catches a misspelt setup event, which is a real authoring error.
- Option 4 would nag every legitimate render-only variant, against trust the programmer.
- Option 3 adds a concept.
- ONE SUB-QUESTION rides with option 2: a recording carrying [:rf/redacted] would also read red. Decide whether redacted events are exempt. The mayor’s lean is to exempt them, since redaction is deliberate.

SCOPE ONCE RULED (not before):
- One spec 017 sentence, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/evidence.cljc, and the tests beside it.
- A JVM regression committed red before the fix, with a control.
- Browser acceptance on the upgrade scaffold: pasted unedited, it must not read pass.
- The acceptance needs the machine-wide browser and shadow-cljs exclusive.

RELATED: rf2-0ae7o.11 fixed claims (a) and (b) in PR #9874, whose close reason routes this claim here.

title: False: canvas data-run-status always identifies the current run
description:
PR #9866 (ff2eee18f39a4cd733746af09995ce258f3117be) fixes the fresh-page visual recipe, but its new data-run-status hook can describe a previous run when the user returns to a variant. The source claim that a previous verdict never stands for a run in flight is false.

Trigger: let variant A settle, select B, then select A again with the same modes/overrides/hot-reload tick. The stable canvas component remains mounted. run-settled retains A's {run-key,status}; run-if-needed! prepares a fresh generation because A's previous generation was already resumed, but never clears that entry. section-props compares only run-key, which is identical on this revisit, so the canvas exposes the old terminal verdict while the new run has not even resumed. A DOM consumer waiting for terminal data-run-status can capture the reset or unfinished world. Clearing only the current variant on canvas unmount does not handle ordinary sidebar selection.

A and B have real setup and script/assertion runs. On A -> B -> A, a delegating resume interceptor observed generation 1 -> 2 with stamp pass BEFORE generation 2 resumed. Changing the run-key instead correctly projected nil (positive control). A temporary one-line invalidation at fresh canvas-run start changed the observed stamp to nil, with all actual runs still PASS. All source bytes restored; tracked diff clean. This is source/lifecycle reproduction, not an independent browser run.

title: Incomplete: promoted regressions lose run inputs in inherited setup
description:

Independent JVM reproduction at the exact merge, using the real runner and default dialog promotion:
- Register :audit/boot to store its event argument as app-db :n.
- Source body: {:args {:n 1}, :setup [[:audit/boot [:arg :n]]], :script [[:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:n] 1]]]}.
- Run source with {:cell-overrides {:n 2}}: FAIL, one assertion.
- Capture with result->artifact(result, variant-play-events(source, opts), opts), then promote with default dialog opts (:extends source, :setup-count 0).

The inherited setup therefore resolves [:arg :n] against the source default (1), not the failing run input (2).

Retain the captured run inputs wherever the promoted program still depends on them, including inherited setup, using the existing args/plan seams. Preserve setup-once behavior and avoid adding another capture path.

title: Streaming SSR example leaks its request frame on outer render failures
description:
Wrap the streaming example's post-allocation request pipeline in try/finally and destroy its request frame in finally. Preserve the existing per-card fallback policy and propagate outer rendering/payload failures normally.

Remediation fence: split from rf2-fzbj.37 F3. Preserve [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. Review/issue creation does not authorize implementation or fixer dispatch.

Ownership and revision
- Slice examples_capabilities; examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:182-273, allocation at 203-205, shell call at 208, final-payload construction at 248-267, lone destruction at 268.
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned paths are unchanged between these revisions and in the working tree.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Trigger and behavior
handle-request allocates a fresh frame, walks the shell, renders continuations, hashes the tree and builds its final payload as successive let bindings. destroy-frame! is the final binding and only runs if every preceding binding succeeds. An outer shell render or payload error bypasses it, retaining the per-request frame in a long-lived host.

Fresh process-local JVM witness on 2026-09-13:
1. Initialize rf.ssr/adapter, require unchanged ssr-streaming.core and capture the frame registry baseline.
2. The ordinary handle-request returns four chunks, reports failed-boundaries #{:card.flaky}, and leaves no frame. The intentional failing card is correctly isolated.

This concerns failures outside the deferred-card recovery boundary; the deliberate throwing-card itself is not a defect.

After successful frame allocation, run shell rendering, continuation collection, hashing and final payload construction within try/finally; move destroy-frame! into finally. title: HTTP RealWorld: correlate home-feed replies with selected feed
description:
Correlate HTTP home-feed replies with the selected feed before they signal the shared home machine. A departed feed's empty response can permanently hide the current feed's nonempty result.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. Independently actionable split of confirmed finding 2 in rf2-fzbj.21, revalidated under rf2-gwye. Review/issue creation only; no implementation authorization.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs:250-276; articles.cljs:115-160,245-300,345-361,544-549; favorites.cljs:80-105. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: sign in, select Your Feed and hold its request; select Global Feed before it settles; release the old empty Your Feed response, then the active nonempty Global Feed response. The shipped demo starts with no follows, so this empty/nonempty contrast is ordinary application data. Reverse the feed selections with appropriate data for the symmetric case.

Expected: the active Global Feed settles from its own response and shows its articles. Actual: :feed/loaded and :articles/loaded both emit the same uncorrelated [:realworld/articles-home [:fetch-succeeded ...]]. Their transport IDs differ (:feed/load vs :articles/load), so neither supersedes the other. The old empty reply moves the shared :data region to :empty; that state has no :fetch-succeeded transition. The current global result writes nonempty articles into app-db, but the machine ignores its success and the home view remains empty. A departed failure can strand it similarly in :error.

Suggested repair: capture the active home selection/request identity in the success and failure targets and reject departed selections before writing active lifecycle state or emitting machine signals. The framework's current routing nav-token is available if useful. A shared request identity/cancel may supplement ownership, but queued callbacks still need the ownership gate. Preserve same-feed supersession, filters, pagination and refresh behavior; do not add a generic request manager.

Acceptance: use held production HTTP requests in the existing external RealWorld harness for Your Feed -> Global Feed and the reverse. Deliver old success/failure before and after the active reply, with empty/nonempty contrasts. Only the current selection controls busy/error/empty/render state. Retain a positive current-response case and same-feed/page supersession. No tests under examples/.

Validation performed: source-probe.clj evaluates the actual home-machine definition and both loaded reducers from current source; routes the reducers' actual machine events through re-frame.machines.parallel/machine-transition; then evaluates the actual :articles.home/render selector. probe-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0, SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. Old empty feed plus new global returns machine {:data :empty :feed :global :filter :none}, render :empty, while global app-db contains hello-conduit. Removing the departed reply from the identical sequence yields :some. The reverse feed case also produces :empty over populated feed data. Request IDs, routing on-match, failures and view dispatch were separately inspected. No browser/held live transport/CLJS compile was run.

Deduplication/references: rf2-fzbj.21 is the only current open aggregate matching these paths; no dedicated open issue was found by current realworld/real-apps/feed searches and the active index. Closed rf2-8icg and rf2-iy3d6 fix profile/article correlations, not this shared home lifecycle; their current guards were inspected. Closed rf2-2xzc fixes boot validation, not this after-navigation race. Preserve those statuses and decisions.

title: ssr-node: settle startup when a worker exits before readiness
description:
Reject startup when a worker exits before readiness; currently that exit clears the boot deadline but leaves the startup promise permanently unsettled. Ownership: impl_ssr_node; implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs:132-144 (boot deadline), :202-227 (exit handler), src/pool.cjs:94-120 (startup/allSettled), :144-161 and :267-281 (replacement/close). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce674e5107b34834ebbfd81d1af7e2cd with no source difference for this slice. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Trigger: createService({modulePath: absolutePath, isolates: 1, bootTimeoutMs: 500}) against this valid module shape: module.exports = {protocol: 1, buildId: 'review-boot-exit', entries: {'app/root': {stateAllowlist: [], runtimeAllowlist: []}}, boot() {process.exit(0);}, render(_request, emit) {emit('

unreachable

');}}; Nonzero process.exit has the same outcome. This is a failed module startup that the bounded service must report, not a request to make exiting during boot a successful initialization. Expected: an early exit rejects startup promptly as CODE.MALFORMED_MODULE so pool startup can close healthy siblings and replacement startup can report its failure. Actual: the exit event clears bootTimer, marks the isolate dead through _failPendingRender, and never rejects start(). No render is pending during boot, so _failPendingRender has no promise to settle. No timer or future worker event remains to recover it. Impact: public createService/readiness remains pending indefinitely despite bootTimeoutMs. Source composition shows Pool.start's Promise.allSettled cannot reach sibling cleanup while a start never settles; an early-exiting replacement leaves startingReplacements pending, which Pool.close awaits. The precise witnessed claim is an unresolved promise, not that every empty single-isolate process must remain alive: a promise alone does not keep Node running. Suggested repair: give startup a clearly owned settlement path and reject it from worker exit whenever readiness has not completed, with a boot refusal and service-owned context (exit code if useful). Preserve render-phase ISOLATE_LOST and detail.afterChunks. Let the existing pool cleanup and replacement reporting observe that rejection; another timeout would mask the missing lifecycle transition. Acceptance criteria: - Exit 0 and nonzero exit during module evaluation or boot reject createService inside its boot bound; healthy startup still succeeds. - Multi-isolate startup with an early exit closes successfully booted siblings and rejects without leaving workers alive. - A replacement exiting before ready settles its tracked start, reaches the existing operator/caller failure handling, and permits service.close to complete. - Render-time exits, hard timeouts, replacement and afterChunks keep their current behavior. Fresh validation: Node v24.13.0; actual Isolate.start with a scratch-only fixture exiting 0 and 7. At 1000 ms with bootTimeoutMs=500, both promises remained pending, dead=true and worker.threadId=-1. Explicit close still did not settle them. The public createService call with exit 0 remained pending at 1000 ms. Existing bad-protocol fixture rejected with malformed-render-module; the existing chunked fixture booted/rendered/closed successfully. Reproduction script and receipts are ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_ssr_node/probe-impl_ssr_node-1.cjs, .log and .exit (exit 0 for assertions of the current defects). All worker threads were exited/closed. Multi-isolate partial-start and replacement consequences are source-inspected, not separately executed; no shared build/full suite/JVM/browser run. Deduplication: split/revalidated Finding 2 of rf2-fzbj.22. Read current bounded histories and closure records for rf2-rhyi (render-phase exit identity), rf2-kirm (render failure afterChunks), rf2-2hmg/rf2-c38b (error egress), and relevant boot notes. Their landed fixes are present; none owns settling BOOT exit. Current ssr-node/bootTimeoutMs tracker searches found no dedicated open match. Preserve the exact rf2-fzbj remediation fence: creation is a review deliverable, not authorization to implement. Parent rf2-gwye; do not change prior statuses/notes.
notes:
VERDICT (worker ssrnode-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9744 (one commit on implementation/ssr-node/**).

Re-verified at the branch base before fixing. implementation/ssr-node was byte-unchanged since the reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce, and the rf2-gwye review probe, copied to scratch and re-rooted at the worktree, reproduced all four defects with exit 0:
- // and http://[::1 each killed the child process with ERR_INVALID_URL at http.cjs:236;
- boot-exit start() stayed pending at 1000 ms against bootTimeoutMs 500;
- the split surrogate streamed as hex 3c703eefbfbdefbfbd3c2f703e;

What landed, finding by finding:
- rf2-gwye.22 (fzbj.22 finding 1, malformed request target). src/http.cjs guards new URL() inside the request listener and answers with the existing MALFORMED_REQUEST refusal (400, x-rf-ssr-refusal). handleRender now receives the already-parsed URL, so the second, unguarded parse is gone.
- rf2-gwye.23 (fzbj.22 finding 2, worker exit before readiness). The worker exit handler in src/isolate.cjs rejects start() as MALFORMED_MODULE, with detail {modulePath, exitCode}. Once ready has resolved this is a no-op, as the error arm's reject already is. It adds no new state and no second timer. Pool.start's allSettled sibling cleanup and release()'s replacement-failure arm observe the rejection unchanged.
- rf2-gwye.24 (fzbj.22 finding 3, surrogate pair split across streamed chunks). The streaming writer holds back at most one trailing high surrogate (holdTrailingHighSurrogate) and writes it with the next chunk, or alone before res.end(). That matches the buffered join's encoding of an unmatched surrogate.
- rf2-gwye.25 (requestId that no header can carry). http.validateHeaderValue('x-rf-ssr-request', requestId) now runs before service.renderFrames. Failure is refused BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 with detail.field "requestId", and the JSON refusal body still echoes the token. The in-process string contract is unchanged, and the README documents the HTTP constraint.

- test/timeout.test.cjs: eval exit 7 and boot exit 0 each reject createService promptly with bootTimeoutMs at its 30 s default. A 2-isolate start where one sibling exits rejects, the healthy sibling is terminated, and both threadIds read -1. A replacement that exits before ready refuses its queued waiter with REPLACEMENT_FAILED_REFUSAL, writes the operator stderr line, and close() completes.

close_reason: Fixed in PR #9744. In src/isolate.cjs, the worker exit handler now rejects start() as MALFORMED_MODULE, carrying the exit code, whenever readiness has not completed. No new state and no extra timeout. Render-phase ISOLATE_LOST and afterChunks are unchanged. Three regression rows in test/timeout.test.cjs cover it. First, an exit during module evaluation (code 7) and an exit from the boot hook (code 0) each reject createService promptly with bootTimeoutMs at its default. title: surface-review(examples-patterns): preserve correlated outcomes and correct repeated-submit feedback
description:
Recommendation: keep the existing pattern architecture and fix two local outcome-display defects: make the WebSocket callback the sole writer of the correlated result, and let Nine States leave its success state when the next submission is invalid. Confirmed findings: one P2 and one P3. Boot and long-running-work have no actionable finding from this bounded review. Leave this bead OPEN until both repairs and their focused regression witnesses land.

## Scope and revision
