CLOSED on its own stated condition. This bead said "rf2-ornb is NOT closed. It stays open as the ruling record until both children land." **Both have landed and both are closed:**
  * **rf2-iisj** (ruling (b)) — `.beads/PRIME.md` adopted, live on trunk since PR #9504 (merged 13:57:21Z), plus its boundary-gate allow-list entry.
  * **rf2-y7co** (ruling (a)) — the per-PR-bookkeeping rule recorded in CLAUDE.md via PR #9503, and its audit-reopened residual corrected in PR #9510.

THE RULING, PRESERVED: per-PR and per-run bookkeeping goes on the bead and in the commit, never into a memory. `bd remember` is for findings that GENERALISE. An audit of one merged PR is already recorded three times — in its `chore(beads): audit merged PR` commit, in the bead's notes, and on the PR itself — so the memory copy adds nothing.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATED IT, and the form it must now be quoted in: `bd prime`'s DEFAULT output was measured at 1,858,076 bytes, **99.71% of it memory bodies**, growing ~2,400 tokens/hour. That growth rate was corroborated from a completely different direction inside a single session — a worker measured the default at 1,862,895 then 1,865,071 bytes **while it worked**, 2,176 bytes in one run. Six readings across three observers (1,810,565 / 1,825,280 / 1,833,112 / 1,843,478 / 1,858,076 / 1,862,895) are the same number at different instants, not disagreements. **Which is exactly why prose must say "~1.8 MB" and never a byte count: at ~99.7% memory bodies, any exact figure is stale the moment a memory lands.**

AND THAT FIGURE IS NOW HISTORICAL, which is the thing a future reader most needs: since `.beads/PRIME.md` went live, `bd prime` emits 3,844 bytes of hand-written prose INSTEAD of the default, carrying no memory bodies at all — verified by `diff` against the file and re-measured with 48 `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` keys standing in the store, so the small output is the override rather than an empty store. **The injection this bead was about is now bounded by a file we control rather than by the memory population.**

TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS ESTABLISHED HERE THAT NOBODY HAD CHECKED:
  * `bd prime --help` states the override in the tool's own words — "Place a `.beads/PRIME.md` file … to override the default output entirely" — and `--export` "ignores PRIME.md override". So re-syncing after a `bd` upgrade is a hand job against `bd prime --export`, because the override suppresses upstream changes to the default.
  * `.claude/settings.json` wires **bare** `bd prime`, not `--memories-only`, at BOTH `SessionStart` and `PreCompact`. Confirmed at source. It matters because `--memories-only`'s own help text says it is "for … compact hook contexts", so had THAT been what the hook ran, the claim "at SessionStart and PreCompact" would have been false. It is true for this repo on the WIRING rather than on the flag docs.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO, restated so nobody reads the close as licence: it forbids WRITING new per-PR memories and **authorises deleting nothing**. The standing records stay, and the single rolling `merged-pr-audit-cursor` key is load-bearing for the out-of-repo harness's resume logic — leave it. The writer itself is a generated `.git/codex-pr-audit-<PR>/checkpoint.py` outside the repo and is still running (42 -> 48 keys observed across two sessions); stopping it is an operator action on the harness, not a change to any tracked file.

title: [implementation/ssr] Preserve nil data when comparing hydration payload content
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant sources unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

The multi-root hydration ledger uses a RENDER-TREE-normalized digest to decide whether payload DATA is identical. That normalization deliberately removes nil values/members, so ordinary distinct app data deterministically aliases, before any hash collision is involved.

Supported reproduction:
1. Make one live client frame f.
2. (ssr/hydrate! {:frame f :root-id :a :payload {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:items [nil 7]}}})
3. (ssr/hydrate! {:frame f :root-id :b :payload {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:items [7]}}})
Expected step 3 raises :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict, leaving A's installed data intact and failing B's incompatible boot. Actual: B receives :already-installed through preflight, skips installation, and proceeds as if its different server slice were the installed one. The second root can display/hydrate index-based content against the wrong data with no conflict diagnostic. {:x nil} vs {} is another ordinary presence-sensitive app-db case.

Exact cause:
- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/install.cljc:95-106 delegates payload-content-digest directly to hash/render-tree-hash.
- hash.cljc:155-180 removes nil-valued map entries; 80-98 removes nil sequence elements; 99-137 removes nil set members. Those are intentional RENDER TREE rules, not valid data normalization for a hydration payload.
- install.cljc:196-227 decides :already-installed from digest equality alone (224); boot.cljc:409-417 only seeds on :install.
- multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc:217-261 requires conflicting payloads to fail rather than silently first-win, but the current digest rows at 269 exercise scalar changes, not preserved nil slots.

Bounded executed evidence (isolated Java/clojure.main, source-loaded re-frame.ssr.hash only, no runtime initialization):
{:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:x nil}} and {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {}} are unequal Clojure values but BOTH canonicalize to "{:rf/app-db {},:rf/version 1}" and hash "03a99afc".
{:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:items [nil 7]}} and {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:items [7]}} are unequal but BOTH canonicalize to "{:rf/app-db {:items [7]},:rf/version 1}" and hash "85d2011b".
Probe process exit 0. The subsequent ledger/boot behavior is validated by the exact source trace, not an executed full hydration test.

Smallest repair: compute the install ledger's content digest from a canonical DATA representation that preserves nil keys/values and collection positions. Preserve the intentional render-tree hash normalization for hydration-mismatch detection. No need to redesign the hash algorithm, add cryptographic collision handling, retain raw payloads in diagnostics, or normalize exotic numeric domains.

Dedupe: all-status title/description searches payload/content-digest/payload-install and relevant payload memories found no matching current owner. No challenge to the intentional render-tree nil-pruning rule or to settled multi-root first-identical-install semantics.

Acceptance: focused ledger/boot tests reject map-presence, vector-position, and set-membership nil differences as conflicts while map insertion-order changes and truly equal payloads remain idempotent. Existing render-tree hash parity stays unchanged. JVM probe ran; no CLJS build/browser/full suite, no source edits.
notes:
FIXED on branch worker/ssr-a, PR #9368 (open, ready). Bead left OPEN for the mayor to close after merge.

REPRODUCED FIRST, then fixed. Executed on the JVM against the unmodified sources, and then again as failing regression tests:
  {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:x nil}}        and {... {}}          -> BOTH 03a99afc
  {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:items [nil 7]}} and {... {:items [7]}} -> BOTH 85d2011b
  {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:s #{nil 1}}}    and {... {:s #{1}}}    -> BOTH bac6f711
and payload-install-decision! returned :already-installed (not :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict) for the second, genuinely different payload. The bead's own probe numbers for the first two pairs reproduce exactly.

FIX. A SECOND canonicalisation rather than a change to the first, which is what the bead asked for. `re-frame.ssr.hash` gains `canonical-data-edn` + `data-hash`: nil preserved as a map value, a sequence element and a set member; map insertion order and set order still irrelevant; sequence position significant; numbers still through `canonical-number` and bytes still through `fnv-1a-32`, so both hashes stay byte-identical on JVM and CLJS. `install/payload-content-digest` delegates to `data-hash`. The parity-pinned render-tree walker is UNTOUCHED and a test (`the-render-tree-hash-keeps-pruning-nil`) pins that it still prunes, so the intentional render-tree rule this bead explicitly did not challenge is protected by an assertion rather than by intent.

No sentinel, therefore no sentinel collision: nil is an EDN literal and pr-str already distinguishes it from the string "nil". One deliberate non-preservation, documented in the fn: numbers go through `canonical-number`, so a JVM 1.0 and a CLJS 1 agree — CLJS cannot represent those apart at all, so preserving the JVM distinction would break the cross-host agreement the ledger depends on.

TESTS (`re-frame.ssr.multi-root-hydration-cljs-test`, a .cljc that runs on BOTH hosts): map presence, vector position (absent slot AND reordered slot), set membership, idempotence for genuinely equal payloads including map-order and set-order invariance, the conflict arm reached end-to-end through `payload-install-decision!`, and the render-tree-still-prunes pin. Failing-first: 5 assertions red against the reverted sources, all green after; the sources were restored and verified byte-identical by SHA-256 before the green run.

SPEC. `spec/011-SSR.md` §Idempotent payload install now names the digest as the canonical-DATA hash and states the nil difference against the decision table.

CLAIM CHECK. The bead's "relevant sources unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008a" STILL HELD at dispatch: `git diff 7ffdacf24d..HEAD` over install.cljc / hash.cljc / boot.cljc is empty. (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc` had moved +66/-13, but only by ADDING the `store-registrations` / `store-lookup` pair; the generation-routed `lookup` is untouched.) Branch was rebased onto 59841a06d5 and the gates re-run on that base.

GATES: fast-PR spine exit 0 (`PASS fast PR spine`); implementation/ssr 644 tests / 4194 assertions exit 0 (base was 634 / 4170 — the delta is exactly this PR's new tests); implementation/ssr-ring 231 / 1164 exit 0, unchanged. `check_fast_pr_gap.py --brief` reports 99 required checks the spine does not decide.
CI FOLLOW-UP (PR #9368): the production-gate lane red at the previously-gated head was NOT in this bead's fix — it was two `:doc` assertions in rf2-blpg's new test namespace reading a pure-documentation key that is elided under -Dre-frame.debug=false. The tax2 digest path is elision-independent by construction (canonical-data-edn + fnv-1a-32 are pure, and payload-install-decision! touches only the installed-payloads atom) and every tax2 assertion was green under the gate throughout. Re-verified on the final base d9e8f0628f: `bash scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` exit 0, 646 tests / 4028 assertions, whole suite, no exclusions. Bead still OPEN.
close_reason: PR #9368 merged; mayor fast-forwarded and verified HEAD == origin/main at 92f1e6e501. Nil data is preserved when comparing hydration payload content. FAILING-FIRST, sources reverted with git checkout HEAD -- and restored byte-identical by SHA-256 before the green run: 5 of 9 failures were this bead — {:x nil} and {} both hashing 03a99afc; {:items [nil 7]} and {:items [7]} both 85d2011b (and the reordered [7 nil] too); #{nil 1} and #{1} both bac6f711; and payload-install-decision! returning nil (:already-installed) where :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict was expected. THE FIX IS A SECOND CANONICALISATION (hash/canonical-data-edn + data-hash) rather than a change to the existing walker — the parity-pinned render-tree walker is untouched, and a new test pins that it still prunes nil. That is the right shape: the normalisation was correct for its own purpose and wrong as a data-identity test, so the fix separates the two rather than breaking one to serve the other. THIS PR WAS RED ON CI AND THE WORKER FIXED IT: 'JVM ssr under the production gate (-Dre-frame.debug=false)' failed at the exact head it had gated green, because its local run used the NORMAL profile. That lane was missing from the mayor's brief — a mayor error, not a skipped gate. Counts 634/4170 -> 644/4194, the +10/+24 exactly the new tests.

title: story-mcp: reject unknown run-option identifiers instead of executing a different scenario
description:
## Problem

`preview-variant`, `run-variant`, and `snapshot-identity` advertise `:active-modes` and `:cell-overrides` as scenario/identity inputs, but their shared MCP coercer silently removes unknown identifiers.

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/args.cljc:311-315` resolves active modes with `(keep #(args/safe-keyword % mode-set))`; a typo or stale mode disappears.
- `args.cljc:125-144` resolves override keys against the effective arg-key allowlist and explicitly drops misses; its contract says a typo'd override “simply doesn't apply.”
- All three handlers run only shape and substrate guards before consuming those filtered opts (`tools/dev.cljc:134-143`; `tools/testing.cljc:96-106,183-185`). Preview also builds the share URL from the filtered tuple.
- `tools_test.clj:4570-4582` pins the loss by expecting an unknown override key to be dropped. There is no handler-level diagnostic for an unknown mode or override key.

These values are semantically material. `spec/API.md:414-417` says cell overrides are identity-bearing, and `tools/testing.cljc:337-341` says mode/override changes produce a different snapshot hash. The focused Story consumer contract says runtime resolution is tolerant so UI/play can ignore stale modes, but “tools surface the mismatch as a validation warning” (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/args.cljc:85-89`); Story-MCP currently does not.

The MCP boundary's established ergonomic rule points the other way: unknown argument keys are rejected because otherwise an agent gets “a successful-looking call that silently defaulted” (`tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:178-205`); malformed run-option shapes are likewise called a “successful-looking WRONG result” and rejected on all three tools (`tools_test.clj:1253-1290`). History confirms the exact failure class is material: commit `b4477057` changed a silently dropped explicit substrate to an error because an agent could believe the requested render substrate was honoured; `0d224b1e` made unknown top-level knobs fail loudly for the same reason; `0c9de86f` records a dropped override producing the wrong render value. The older `8c1b9dc6` no-intern change introduced today's drop, but no-interning does not require success.

## Impact

An agent can request dark/high-contrast/etc., typo the mode or override key, then receive `:status :pass`, a share URL, or a visual-regression hash for the default/different tuple. That is false test evidence at precisely the automation boundary intended to make Story productive for AI. The programmer gets no short recovery loop and may bless the wrong state.

## Bounded fix

Add one shared semantic run-options guard in `tools.args`, reused by the three existing handlers after shape/substrate validation and before lifecycle/hash/share work:

1. Resolve every supplied active-mode id against the live mode set without interning. If any are unresolved, return one `isError true` result carrying the raw unknown strings and an actionable `list-modes` recovery hint; do not partially execute known modes.
2. Once all modes are valid, derive the existing effective arg-key allowlist and reject unresolved `:cell-overrides` keys the same way (raw strings, no interning; report the bounded allowed set or direct the agent to the variant/effective-args read).
3. Use the same stable structured error shape across preview/run/snapshot and describe the behavior in their descriptors, API, and wire contract.

## Non-goals / posture

Do not change tolerant Story runtime or UI hydration. Do not add a generic validation framework, fuzzy matching/autocorrection, a new tool, a second registry, or keyword interning, and do not broaden which override keys are legal. This is one MCP-boundary guard around existing allowlists. Passive UI hydration may reasonably discard stale persisted state; an explicit agent command should fail loudly rather than certify another tuple. The change trusts the programmer, keeps the API minimal, and removes false confidence without gold-plating.

## Duplicate and history audit

A targeted `rg` over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for unknown/reject/drop/ignore near `active-modes` or `cell-overrides` returned no matches; the wider Story-MCP issue inventory has no open issue on this behavior. Related historical work is distinct: rf2-3luf3 / `8c1b9dc6` is no-intern ingress; rf2-to3q7 / `0c9de86f` fixes the allowed-key universe; rf2-ldfrp0 / `f6b82ab8` rejects wrong container shapes; rf2-3fc89f.21 / `b4477057` handles substrate/capability; rf2-ovmc5e / `0d224b1e` handles unknown top-level knobs. Those are precedents and leave these nested semantic identifiers untouched.

## Uncertainty

The silent behavior was deliberate in the original security hardening, so this is a recommended MCP-boundary policy correction rather than an accidental branch typo. The security invariant remains satisfiable by reporting raw strings without interning them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of `preview-variant`, `run-variant`, and `snapshot-identity` returns `isError true` for a supplied unknown active-mode id, names the raw rejected value, and does not invoke lifecycle/hash/share work.
- A mixed known+unknown mode list rejects atomically rather than running the known subset.
- Each tool rejects an unknown cell-override key instead of running or hashing with it removed; the diagnostic names the raw key and gives a bounded recovery path.
- Existing valid modes and overrides remain unchanged, including the mode-introduced override case at `tools_test.clj:4584-4608`.
- Wire-level regression probes prove random unknown mode values and override keys remain uninterned.
- Descriptor/spec text states that absent options default but present unknown identifiers fail loudly.
- Focused Story-MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9249 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9249). Added one shared semantic guard, re-frame.story-mcp.tools.args/run-opts-semantic-error, called by preview-variant / run-variant / snapshot-identity after the shape+substrate guards and before any lifecycle/hash/share work. Unknown :active-modes ids and unknown :cell-overrides KEYS are now refused (:rf.error/story-mcp-unknown-active-mode / :rf.error/story-mcp-unknown-cell-override-key) naming the offending RAW identifier and the live-derived accepted set; a mixed known+unknown mode list rejects atomically; modes validate before override keys so a mode-introduced override key stays legitimate (rf2-to3q7). No-intern posture preserved (raw strings reported, find-keyword probe) - only the success is withdrawn. TWO-LAYER FINDING: this is NOT 'inner refuses, outer swallows' - re-frame.story.args is deliberately tolerant AND its mode-args docstring already delegates the diagnosis outward ('tools surface the mismatch as a validation warning'); story-mcp never discharged it. Fix is therefore entirely in tools/story-mcp; tools/story untouched. SIBLING CENSUS: 8 identifier axes at the boundary, 6 already correct (:variant-id, :story-id, :substrate, top-level arg keys, :kind, and :tags - the last tolerant but self-evidencing via :ignored-tags + an always-filtering filter, a filter axis where a wrong answer is visibly empty rather than a confident pass). Only the 2 scenario/identity axes needed fixing. Witness: tests added with fix reverted = exit 1, 52 failures; with fix = exit 0, 288 tests / 1597 assertions, 0 failures (baseline 282/1527). Positive half (valid mode + valid override still runs/hashes on all three) passes before AND after, pinning against an over-broad fix. Spec updated in the same PR: new spec/API.md Run options section, spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md corrected from 'dropped' to 'refused', all three descriptors state absent-defaults vs present-but-unknown-fails. Gates: story-mcp clojure -M:test exit 0; clojure -M:gen --check exit 0 (19 tools in sync); check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 proven live with a planted broken anchor (exit 1, restored byte-identical); check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0.

title: tools/xray(popout): detached shell has no keyboard listener, so its keyboard workflow is inert
description:
CLAIM
`mount/popout!` renders a live shell into a second document, but Xray never attaches its keyboard listener to that document. DOM key events do not cross from the pop-out document to the opener document, so the keyboard-first Xray workflow is inert whenever focus is in the pop-out. The existing handler is also opener-surface-aware rather than pop-out-aware: its bare spine branch gates on `mount/visible?` (which reads only `mount-state`), and Cmd/Ctrl+K can call `mount/toggle!`, which controls the in-app shell rather than the already-visible pop-out.

EVIDENCE AT REVIEW TIP
Reviewed `cacace4e1803cfe6441d32b7ededa3b8da1a7fc1`; local `origin/main` has no later change to the relevant files.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:435-455`, `attach!`: a process-wide `attached-state` CAS installs exactly one capture listener, always on opener-realm `js/document`. `detach!` at :458-482 removes from that same `js/document`. There is no API for a second document.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:1457-1541`, `popout!`: creates `win` / `doc`, injects styles, renders `shell-view`, installs opener-gone/lifecycle listeners, and records `popout-state`; it never installs a `keydown` listener on `doc`. `register-popout-unload-cleanup!` is pagehide/unload cleanup only.
- `mount.cljs:100-121`, `visible?` / `status`: visibility is derived only from `mount-state`; `popout-state` is a separate singleton. `keybinding.cljs:389-433`, `handle-keydown`: Cmd/Ctrl+K routes through `mount/toggle!` when that in-app state is hidden, while bare Space/L/j/k/G require `mount/visible?`. Even mechanically reusing the handler on the pop-out document without surface context would therefore be wrong when no inline shell is visible.
- `tools/xray/spec/API.md:842-849` explicitly describes `popout!` as its own document context with its own React root, theme cascade, and keybinding. `tools/xray/README.md:243-251` documents Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, and the in-shell Space/L/j/k/G workflow; its “not bound to a global chord” sentence is specifically about LAUNCHING the pop-out, not disabling keyboard operation inside it.
- Existing proof misses this boundary. `tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:554-599` proves only that the pop-out root/shell exists; :1758-1845 proves shared cascade rendering under load, but sends no key in the pop-out. `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount_cljs_test.cljs:1485-1498` asserts only pagehide/unload registrations on the pop-out window. `keybinding_cljs_test.cljs` stubs the single ambient `js/document`, never a second document.

VERIFIED IMPACT
A programmer who moves Xray to a second monitor and gives that window focus cannot use the documented keyboard-first operations there: Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, Space/L/j/k/G, comma/s, or the contextual Esc path are never received by Xray. This is not an edge-case protocol concern; pop-out is a shipped top-bar action and the keyboard map is a primary low-friction debugging surface. Mouse controls and live data rendering still work, which makes the failure look like intermittent shortcut breakage rather than an unsupported mode.

BOUNDED RECOMMENDATION

title: Mayor dispatch drift: the boundary and gate-mechanics blocks were retyped, not extracted - and the gate paraphrase inverts the detach ruling
description:
The mayor has been RETYPING the two travel-verbatim dispatch blocks instead of
extracting them mechanically, across every dispatch this session. The method doc is
correct; the defect is entirely in dispatch practice.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:661-673 rules on this directly:
"Get them there by extracting mechanically, then pasting the result into the prompt...
the extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible - a matched range cannot reword,
where a mayor retyping two hundred lines of gate mechanics can and does."

That is precisely what happened.

## Drift 1 - the gate-mechanics block, and it INVERTS the ruling

Canonical block: template lines 920-1010+ ("## Quality gates - how a gate is run",
paste from that heading down to the rule before "## Reviewing what comes back").
Roughly 90 lines.

What the mayor pasted instead, in full:
  "GATE MECHANICS: run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion - never background one,
   never pipe through tail/head."

The canonical block says the OPPOSITE of the first clause:
  - "Split a compound gate before you reach for detaching."
  - "Where it genuinely does not split, DETACHING IS CORRECT - ending the turn is the
     defect. Detach, then poll both the log and the exit-code file in a bounded loop
     within the same turn."
  - "Word this as the sanctioned path, not as a concession; a worker who thinks it has
     erred reads for how to atone and straight past the instruction that would save it."

The real rule is a TERMINAL CONDITION - the turn ends only once the exit file exists
and its number is quoted - not a ban on backgrounding. The mayor's paraphrase kept the
memorable half (foreground) and dropped the operative one (poll in-turn), which is the
same failure mode ai/stance.md warns about for the stance block.

OBSERVED COST: Mike asked 2026-09-03 why background tasks were taking almost an hour.
A worker whose gate is too heavy to foreground and who is FORBIDDEN to detach has no
option but to sit in the foreground. This is a direct, measured throughput cost.

Also dropped from that block:
  - the WEDGE diagnosis: a gate heavy enough that two cannot coexist wedges rather than
    fails (no progress, no exit file, no error). Contention is for the MACHINE, so
    per-attempt naming does nothing. Recover by correlating your own build artefact's
    mtime against candidate run start times and killing ONLY the one you can show is
    yours; a peer's run recovers by itself.
  - "Read the clock before killing anything on elapsed time" - fails BOTH ways; one
    worker killed a healthy run believing 17 minutes had passed when it had been 2.
  - "Invoke a backgrounded gate by its ABSOLUTE path" - an interpreter handed a relative
    script path resolves it against the working directory, so a wrong directory hands it
    a SIBLING WORKTREE's copy. One run did exactly that inside another live worker's
    checkout and reported the resulting verdict as its own.
  - "Verify which tree the gate actually read", by root-print or by planted-fault red -
    "the discrimination is the red itself", since a repository-relative path cannot tell
    two checkouts apart.
  - "A green sabotage run is a reason to stop, not to proceed."
The never-pipe rule was the one part carried correctly.

## Drift 2 - the worktree-boundary block

Canonical block: template lines 739-798 (the fenced text under "## The worktree boundary
block"). The mayor substituted a retyped 6-point numbered list. Dropped:

  - "Before EVERY edit, confirm you are in your worktree... A start-of-session guard is
    NOT sufficient - verify per edit." The mayor's version asks for ONE guard run. The
    template's own rationale: the leak happens mid-session, in one tool call, and a guard
    script can be fooled by the path resolution that causes it.
  - Never write the worktree root, or any absolute home path, into any committed file, PR
    body or tracker text.
  - After the first edit, and after writing any NEW file, confirm it landed in your
    worktree and NOT the mayor checkout - CHECK BOTH TREES, because a new ignored file
    leaking into the mayor checkout is invisible in the worker's own status.
  - If anything landed outside: STOP, report both paths, do not repair, commit or push.
  - Scratch-file naming: concurrent workers SHARE one SESSION-keyed scratch dir; name
    every file for the worktree AND the attempt - gate-<name>-<worktree>-1.log /
    .exit - bumping the number each re-run. The attempt number closes a hole the worktree
    suffix cannot, because both writers are YOU: a harness that caps runtime kills the
    SHELL, not what it spawned, and the orphan keeps writing to the .log and .exit the
    restarted run is using. A hole of NUL bytes or two summary lines in one log is the
    tell. (The mayor substituted "write scratch to your worktree, not /tmp" - same hazard,
    weaker route, and no attempt number at all.)
  - THE INSTALLER HAZARD, which is live in this repo: a link into shared dependencies is
    WRITABLE through, not only deletable through. An installer a gate runs (npm ci, npm
    install, any tool that reinstalls a dependency tree) rewrites the SHARED target, not
    your copy - "one emptied the coordinator's real tree while the worker's own read as a
    fresh install." If a nominated gate runs an installer, do NOT link that tree: install
    your own from the lockfile, or STOP and say the gate cannot run against a link.
    Workers here junction implementation/node_modules and then run npm-based gates, so
    this is the live shape. The mayor's version said only "remove the junction as your
    last act", which addresses deletion and not writes.
  - "Kill any poll loops you armed before you report done" - each survivor fires its own
    completion notification after the work has landed, costing a turn apiece.

## The fix

1. Extract both blocks MECHANICALLY into the dispatch, by matched line range, and paste
   the result. Never retype either. Adapt only the placeholders (<ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>,
   <MAYOR_CHECKOUT>) and scope the gate block to the gate the brief names.
2. Ranges as of this filing - RE-DERIVE them from the headings rather than trusting these
   numbers, which go stale exactly the way the template's own "Counts are claims" section
   says:
     - worktree boundary: the fenced text block under "## The worktree boundary block"
     - gate mechanics: from "## Quality gates - how a gate is run" down to the rule
       before "## Reviewing what comes back"
   Note the template's explicit warning that "## Quality gates - which gate" is NOT the
   gate-mechanics block and does not stand in for it.
3. The stance block from ai/stance.md was pasted verbatim throughout and is NOT affected;
   this bead is only about the other two.

## Acceptance

A dispatch prompt whose boundary and gate blocks are byte-identical to the template's
ranges (modulo placeholder substitution), verifiable by extracting the range and diffing
it against what was sent.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the defect was dispatch PRACTICE, the bead says so in terms ('The method doc is correct; the defect is entirely in dispatch practice'), and the practice has been corrected and held for the whole of this session. There is no file to edit, so dispatching this to a worker would have produced an empty PR.

WHAT THE BEAD RECORDED. A prior mayor RETYPED the two travel-verbatim blocks instead of extracting them, and the gate-mechanics block collapsed to two lines whose first clause INVERTED the ruling: 'run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion - never background one'. The canonical block says the opposite — 'Split a compound gate before you reach for detaching', and 'Where it genuinely does not split, DETACHING IS CORRECT - ending the turn is the defect.'

WHAT THIS SESSION DOES INSTEAD, and it is checkable rather than asserted. Every dispatch has carried the gate-mechanics block EXTRACTED MECHANICALLY from docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md lines 920-1139 (trailing --- stripped): 16889 bytes, 217 lines, headings located with grep -n rather than by eye, and the section boundary taken heading-to-heading because that block carries no fence. The worktree-boundary block likewise from lines 740-794 (3383 bytes) and the common preamble from 805-863 (4013 bytes). Never retyped, never summarised, never paraphrased — which is exactly what template:661-673 rules ('the extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible - a matched range cannot reword').

THE INVERTED CLAUSE IS DEFINITIVELY ABSENT. Every dispatch this session carries the canonical wording verbatim, including the four paragraphs that exist because the rule kept failing open: detaching is the sanctioned path; the turn ends only once the exit file exists and its number is quoted; the strand has variants (a Monitor, a watch, a subscription, a background task you expect to wake you are all the same strand); and the refutation of the harness's own promise that a backgrounded command will re-invoke you, which does not survive the end of your turn.

AND IT IS EARNING ITS PLACE. worker/budget-a reported today that backgrounding stranded its spine self-test TWICE — the harness reported 'exit code 0' while the captured exit file was absent both times — and it foregrounded with a proper ceiling to get the real verdict. That is the block working as written: the worker read an absent exit file as NO VERDICT rather than a pass. Under the two-line paraphrase it would have had no such rule.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE PRACTICE CANNOT REGRESS. The posture loop re-checks it every tick and names any drifted dispatch; that loop is the durable guard, not this bead. Reopen if a dispatch is ever observed carrying a paraphrase again.

SIBLING: rf2-tg6o is a REAL edit to the same file (the preamble names bd history fields that do not exist) and is being dispatched separately. It no longer needs sequencing behind this bead, since this one touches nothing.

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): boolean-discriminator-subs After view and eval 24 clean fixture are plain defn views with bare rf/ ops — raise :rf.error/no-frame-context under EP-0002
description:
CLAIM. `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md:71-75` — the **After** (recommended rewrite) is a plain Reagent fn with a bare facade read:

```clojure
(defn article-page []
  (case @(rf/subscribe [:article/render]) ...))
```

The same plain-`defn` + bare `rf/` shape is the should-be-clean fixture in `evals/evals.json` #24 (`behav-neg-render-local-component-state`: `(defn search-box [] ... #(rf/dispatch [:search/query-changed ...]))`), whose expectations require the agent to "report the view as clean against the catalogue".

TRUTH AT TIP. Under EP-0002 there is no `:rf/default` floor; a plain `(defn ...)` view carries no `:contextType`, cannot read the surrounding `frame-provider`'s frame, and its ambient `rf/subscribe` / `rf/dispatch` raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md:104`, `.../fundamentals/subs.md:86`, `.../fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`, `skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:30` (deferred callbacks fire on a fresh stack with no `*current-frame*`). Every shipped example view is `rf/reg-view` with the injected `subscribe` (`examples/core/todomvc/views.cljs:64-141`, `examples/core/counter/*.cljs:60-70`). The improver's own `references/view-side-hook-state.md:78` states exactly this: "A plain `(defn ...)` view with a bare `#(rf/dispatch ...)` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on click (EP-0002 — no `:rf/default` floor)."

IMPACT. Leaf 2's canonical rewrite — the thing the critique hands the programmer — throws at first render in a re-frame2 app. Leaf 6 and leaf 2 contradict each other inside one catalogue. Eval 24 grades as "clean" a snippet that is itself the plain-Reagent-fn trap, so a reviewer who correctly notes it is penalised as "inventing an unrelated anti-pattern" (expectation 4), while a reviewer who stays silent misses a real runtime defect. (The Before snippets in leaf 2 and in evals #18/#22/#27 are fine as v1-flavoured "before" code; the defect is in the After and in the clean fixture.)

FIX SHAPE. One PR, two files:
1. `references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md` After: `(rf/reg-view article-page [] (case @(subscribe [:article/render]) ...))` — injected `subscribe`, no `rf/` prefix — with the one-line reason leaf 6 already gives (or a cross-ref to it).
2. `evals/evals.json` #24: make the clean fixture idiomatic re-frame2 (a `reg-view` whose deferred handlers use the injected `dispatch`; keep the render-local `hovered?` atom the fixture exists to protect — the Reagent Form-2 closure shape may need `reg-view*` / `r/with-let` per views.md; the worker picks the smallest idiomatic spelling), so "clean" is true. Optionally add to #18's expectations: "the rewritten view is a `reg-view` (or otherwise carries its frame) — a plain defn with bare `rf/subscribe` is the EP-0002 trap".

GATE. `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (all exit 0 at tip; must stay 0). No gate validates the CLJS inside a leaf — verify by hand that the After matches `views.md` §Canonical signature and say so in the PR body.

title: ssr-node crossing (C/6): render-state contract (project/restore, two partitions) + protocol v1 revision
description:
Slice C of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 (S3 and S4 especially) first; this description carries only C's own brief. This is the slice both reviewers agreed carries the real risk — reconstructing the SAME settled render state in Node — so it lands BEFORE the adapter (D) consumes it.

## Scope (fence)

- New `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc` (+ JVM test under `implementation/ssr/test/` and a CLJS test in the same tree — `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` ~:102 already lists `ssr/test`, so NO build change).
- `implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs`, `test/protocol.test.cjs`, `test/fixtures/**`, README section `### A gap this protocol does not paper over` (~:355-365; rewrite it — the door now exists, decided by the framework, not by the sidecar).
- NOT `implementation/ssr-ring` (D consumes this), NOT `implementation/hicasso` (E). Parallel with A and B; B edits different README sections — rebase, don't fight.

## Do

JVM side (`render-state/project`): given a frame-id and a `:render-state` policy, return the partition map `{:rf/app-db {...} :rf/runtime-db {...}}` — the SAME envelope shape the hydration payload already uses (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj` ~:5-13) under a DISTINCT policy. The policy is declared like `:payload`: a fail-closed allowlist per partition — top-level app-db keys, and top-level runtime-db keys (the route slice, machine snapshots) — plus a `(fn [frame-id] -> partition-map)` escape hatch for a projector the allowlist vocabulary cannot express. Absent policy = construction-time error (mirror `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`). Reuse `payload_policy.cljc`'s apply/project machinery, including derived sensitivity the way `project-runtime-db` already applies it. Also a per-key `pr-str` serialization helper producing the wire form (key text -> EDN text) for both partitions; the serialization DOMAIN is the payload's existing EDN domain — reuse it, do not invent a second one.

CLJS side (`render-state/restore!`): seed a FRESH per-request frame's app-db and runtime-db from the partition map, with NO boot-event replay (the JVM drained them), reusing `hydrate.cljc`'s partition-install path minus verification and DOM concerns. This is the "second install door" the ssr-node README declined to invent in a sidecar; the framework now decides it, here.

Node protocol v1 (pre-alpha: revise directly, no compatibility layer, `protocol` stays `1`): the request carries the runtime partition beside `state`, per-key EDN text, gated by an ENTRY-owned allowlist for that partition too — absence = unrenderable, mirroring `stateAllowlist` (~:264-273). Invariants: the service never decodes application data; allowlists stay entry-owned so a caller cannot widen its own allowance (the fail-closed guarantee stays in Node; it does not move to the JVM); `initialEvents` / `payloadPolicy` / `head` stay refused with their existing reasons. The wire spelling (`runtime` + `runtimeAllowlist`, or one two-partition `snapshot` object) is the worker's call within those invariants. Update the fixtures (e.g. `bad-no-allowlist.cjs` gains a runtime-partition sibling) and the protocol rows.

## Acceptance

1. Round-trip corpus: every value class the hydration payload's EDN domain supports goes JVM `pr-str` -> CLJS `read-string` -> `restore!` -> identical, for BOTH partitions; a route slice and a machine snapshot are in the corpus.
2. ONE negative fixture: an unsupported value (a fn / a Java object) fails at projection with a named error — never a silent nil.
3. One omitted-required-key fixture: restoring with an allowlisted key absent renders the honest "wrong page" (nil where the value should be) and is documented as the operator's allowlist mistake, not a framework failure.
4. `protocol.cjs` revised, `npm run test:ssr-node` green, README section rewritten.

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/ssr`; the CLJS lane that compiles `ssr/test` (`npm run test:cljs`, or the focused build — name which in the PR); `npm run test:ssr-node`.

## Stop and report to Mike (do not improvise a framework decision)

If restoring runtime-db turns out to require replaying boot events, or the route/machine slices cannot be expressed as top-level runtime-db keys. Leave the PR open with what works and say so on this bead.

## Traps

Two partitions, two allowlists — never derive the render-state projection from `:payload`, and never the reverse; the whole point is that they differ. No `git stash`; commit then rebase. Worker worktree guard first; report `WORKTREE_ROOT`.

notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 06:45 AUSEST from the MAYOR RETRO loop.

THE DEFECT. Both front-door documents undercount loops.md by one:
  - README.md:271  "the 5 standing loops"
  - bootstrap.md:78 "SET UP THE LOOPS. The five loops are in `loops.md`."
loops.md has SIX top-level loop sections: Merge, Dispatch, Backlog reread, Posture, Hygiene,
Method reread.

IT IS A LONG-STANDING STALE CONSTANT, NOT RECENT DRIFT, and that is the interesting part.
loops.md ALREADY held six at commit 9728d5cae6 (22 Aug), the commit where README.md was last
touched - so the count was wrong when it was last written, and seventy-four commits to that
tree since, plus every Method reread including several of mine tonight, passed over it. A count
written in prose reads as authoritative, and nothing was checking it against the headings.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS SELF-CONCEALING, which is what makes it worth more than a number fix. A mayor
following bootstrap.md literally codifies FIVE command files and never creates the sixth - and
the sixth is METHOD REREAD, the loop whose entire job is catching stale measured constants. The
omission removes the instrument that would have found the omission. Nothing errors; five loops
run perfectly well.

SHIPPED as PR #8974 (mayor/loop-count). The README takes the number. bootstrap takes the DURABLE
fix instead: enumerate the loops from that file's own section headings rather than from a count,
so the seventh does not reopen this - one sentence inside the step that already exists, replacing
a number that will go stale again with an instruction that will not.

BOUNDED IN CHANGE, NOT IN SEARCH: these are the only two numeric claims about loops in either
file, searched as digits AND as number-words. bootstrap.md's "five-clause criterion" is a
DIFFERENT count and is CORRECT - the merge criterion still has five clauses - which is why this
is two targeted edits rather than a replace.

GATE COVERAGE DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO FILES and only one is gated. The README line is ordinary
prose carrying a link, so both gates read it: a broken target planted on that exact line returned
check_doc_slugs.py exit 1 naming README.md:271 and mkdocs --strict exit 1 "Aborted with 1

nothing about it; verified by hand instead (no link, no anchor, no heading, rewrap at <=85 chars
against a file maximum of 123).

REOPENED 2026-09-02 07:10 AUSEST — THE FINDING WAS FALSE AND PR #8974 WAS A REGRESSION. Revert
raised as PR #8975. Everything above this line about a "stale count" is wrong; it is kept rather
than deleted because the reasoning error is the useful part.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. loops.md declares FIVE loops in its cadence table - Merge + dispatch,
Backlog reread, Posture + stranded sweep, Hygiene, Method reread - and states the distinction
outright, twenty lines above where I was looking:

  "Five loops, six bodies. Merge and dispatch share one tick, but each is long enough to want a
   heading of its own, so they are written separately below. The numbering follows the bodies;
   the cadence follows the table."

So "the 5 standing loops" and "The five loops are in loops.md" were both CORRECT. My six was a
count of BODIES.

HOW I GOT THERE, because the shape is worth more than the fact. I ran `grep -c '^## [0-9]'`,
got six, and treated a heading count as a loop count - the classic wrong-question instrument.
The page pre-empts it in two consecutive sentences, one of them the paragraph quoted above and
the other "Some people prefer merge and dispatch as separate loops". I read neither, because I
was grepping the file rather than reading the section.

THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE WAS INSIDE MY OWN WORKING AND I INVERTED IT. I established that the count
was already "wrong" at the commit where README.md was last touched, and read that as proof of a
long-standing stale constant. The correct reading is that it was right then and is right now. A
number unchanged across seventy-four commits is far more likely correct than uniquely
overlooked - and I wrote the opposite into a close reason and a PR body.

I ALSO FABRICATED A CONSEQUENCE TO JUSTIFY IT. The "self-concealing" argument - that a mayor
would codify five command files and omit Method reread, the drift-catcher - has no referent:

constructed to fit a conclusion already reached.

NOTHING IS ADDED BY THE REVERT. No new caution, no clarifying sentence. The document's own

and warning about a trap the page already names would repeat the mistake in the other direction.

title: surface-review(machines-viz): make registered topology one-click copyable as Mermaid
description:
## Scope

Complete the existing Mermaid workflow from tools/machines-viz's pure `day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.mermaid/emit` function to Xray's existing Static Machines definition-detail header. Add one accessible, direct "Copy Mermaid" action for the currently selected registered machine, focused integration coverage, and the small documentation update that makes the workflow discoverable. Keep `MachineChart` presentation-only: the Xray host already owns the selected definition and owns the user gesture.

## Findings

Machines-Viz has a mature producer but no reachable workflow. `mermaid/emit` accepts the normalised definition and returns a fenced `stateDiagram-v2` block; its dedicated corpus covers grammar, validation, parallel/compound topology, and lossy-semantics warnings. `export/copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` also exists, but its DOM-element contract is an exporter convenience rather than a host-level action.

The repository has no production call site for either `mermaid/emit` or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz itself. Xray's own machine-inspector spec still labels "Copy machine as PNG / SVG / Mermaid" as "Not built". Consequently a capability explicitly described for README files, pull requests, design docs, and AI-pair chat is available only to someone who writes CLJS around the library API.

The lowest-friction host is already present. Xray's Static Machines surface is the event-independent browse of every registered machine; its definition-detail view already subscribes to the selected machine's exact definition and renders a compact header containing its id, source coordinate, state count, and live count. Mermaid is static topology, so this is a better fit than the Dynamic Machine panel's deliberately narrow three-part forensic view.

The other shipped routes do not close this gap. The share viewer is an inbound, read-only URL consumer; it must be built and self-hosted, and share encoding requires an explicit host because there is no Day8 deployment. The manifests expose tests and a viewer build but no end-user command or standalone launch path. Xray's panel gallery and machine-epochs testbed provide rich visual fixtures, yet neither exposes the Mermaid exporter.

History makes the disconnect explicit: rf2-deo2i shipped the emitter, rf2-sqhqu moved ownership into Machines-Viz, and rf2-8d7w1 shipped the export/viewer primitives. rf2-nugvv later removed Xray's heavy Share modal and URL/session-posture machinery, leaving the copy formats recorded as unbuilt. Reintroducing that modal would repeat the wrong abstraction; a single explicit copy action needs none of it.

Exact tracker searches for "machines-viz", "Copy machine", "Mermaid export", "machine mermaid", "machine topology", "standalone viewer", and related terms found no existing bead for this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Add one "Copy Mermaid" control to the selected machine's Static Machines detail header. On activation, pass the selected definition directly to `mermaid/emit` and copy that exact fenced string through a small, testable clipboard effect. Do not make the renderer rediscover registry state and do not require a rendered chart DOM node.

Make the gesture immediate: no confirmation modal and no format chooser. Give it a clear accessible name and a minimal non-modal success/failure status so a rejected or unavailable clipboard does not look successful. Omit or disable the action when no valid definition is available.

Use an existing representative Static Machines/panel-gallery fixture for the integration proof. Assert the clipboard payload equals `(mermaid/emit definition)`; the emitter's existing corpus remains the authority for diagram semantics.

Update the Machines-Viz and Xray documentation just enough to name this as the normal path for copying a registered topology into Markdown or an AI conversation, and replace the stale "Not built" statement for Mermaid only.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid.cljc:946` defines the pure `emit` API and its fenced Markdown contract.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/export.cljs:561-589` defines the chart-element wrapper and clipboard helper.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2078-2099` says Mermaid output is for GitHub, PRs, Notion, and other Mermaid-aware consumers and identifies `mermaid/emit` as the load-bearing pure function.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md:284-300` explicitly names README and AI-pair chat replies as the static Mermaid surface.
- A repository-wide source search finds no production use of `mermaid/emit`, `chart-as-mermaid`, or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz; references elsewhere are documentation only.
- `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1829-1842` explicitly marks the copy-as formats "Not built".
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/definition_detail.cljs:52-90` is the existing selected-machine header, and lines 209-254 already hold the selected definition in the host view.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/panel.cljs:110-161` composes registered ids, definitions, snapshots, and selection for that surface; no new registry query is needed.
- `tools/machines-viz/README.md:95-160` documents that the viewer must be built and hosted by the consumer and that `:host` is required for a share URL.
- `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid_cljs_test.cljc` is a 943-line semantic corpus, while Xray already has focused Static Machines panel tests and panel-gallery machine fixtures; the missing test is the one host-to-export gesture.
- Git history: d737346b4b (rf2-deo2i), ab4d4597d9 (rf2-sqhqu), 9644e0b4d8 (rf2-8d7w1), 2107f8096d (rf2-nugvv), and ee9ba1bed0 / a06227b68c / 8cef711d18 (rf2-8m344) establish the producer, ownership, removed modal, and self-host-only viewer posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a valid selected definition in Xray Static -> Machines, one obvious "Copy Mermaid" gesture writes exactly `(mermaid/emit definition)` to the clipboard as a fenced Markdown block.
- The action uses the definition already owned by the Static Machines host. `MachineChart` gains no registry subscription, new data prop, global state, or built-in toolbar.
- The copied text is static topology only: it does not depend on the current live snapshot or trace history and does not include runtime or definition `:data` values. Existing emitter caveats for lossy runtime semantics remain intact.
- No selected/valid definition means no actionable copy control; the empty and malformed-definition paths remain stable.
- Success and clipboard rejection/unavailability produce small, accessible, non-modal status feedback. A failed write is never reported as copied.
- A focused CLJS integration test stubs the clipboard boundary, activates the real control, and asserts the exact emitter output and one write. It also covers the unavailable/rejected clipboard path and the no-definition gate.
- An existing Static Machines panel-gallery fixture exposes the action for manual/browser inspection; no new testbed application or launch mode is introduced.
- Machines-Viz README/API text and Xray's machine-inspector spec identify the Static Machines action as the normal Mermaid workflow and no longer claim the Mermaid copy path is unbuilt.
- Focused Machines-Viz Mermaid tests and Xray Static Machines tests pass, with the relevant changed-surface scheduling preserved.

## Non-goals

- PNG, SVG, share-URL, SCXML, or new export formats.
- Restoring rf2-nugvv's Share modal, URL/session-posture restoration, cascade export, a context-menu hierarchy, or a format picker.
- A hosted viewer, deployment workflow, saved-chart registry, paste-and-render playground, visual editor, or SaaS surface.
- A CLI, MCP tool, framework-level `machine->mermaid` compatibility shim, or duplicate emitter.
- New chart styling, layout heuristics, animation, overlays, simulator modes, or testbed applications.
- Copying raw machine EDN, runtime `:data`, traces, app-db, source coordinates, or session state.
- Compatibility scaffolding for the removed Share surface.

## Related beads

- rf2-deo2i (closed/historical) shipped the Mermaid emitter.
- rf2-sqhqu (closed/historical) made Machines-Viz the emitter's owner.
- rf2-8d7w1 (closed/historical) shipped the export, share codec, and viewer primitives.
- rf2-nugvv (closed/historical) removed Xray's Share modal and URL/cascade infrastructure; this task must not restore that surface.
- rf2-8m344 (closed/historical) corrected the nonexistent hosted viewer and established the explicit self-host posture.
- rf2-v4xjh (in progress) simplifies pure machine-transition results; it is adjacent machine-tooling work but does not expose topology or overlap this host action.
- No matching open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead for a reachable Mermaid-copy outcome was found.

title: surface-review(machines): make pure transition results self-describing
description:
## Scope

Redesign the application-facing result contract of re-frame.machines/machine-transition, together with its normative spec, generated API projection, guides, executable examples, manifest coverage, and focused JVM/CLJS tests. Keep runtime transition semantics and the event/effect model unchanged.

## Findings

machine-transition is presented as the simple, pure way to test a machine, but the facade currently aliases the engine function directly and leaks the re-frame.machines.result representation. Callers must require a second namespace, learn either result/ok?, result/snap, result/fx, and result/info or opaque namespaced keys (::tag, ::snap, ::fx, ::info), and reconcile documentation that calls those keys public with a namespace docstring that calls the namespace internal. This makes the most important testing seam less obvious to programmers and harder for AI tools to infer or generate correctly.

The public API manifest inventories re-frame.machines/machine-transition but does not inventory re-frame.machines.result, while the tutorial, inspection guide, API page, normative spec, and executable walkthrough all require that omitted namespace. The result representation is therefore public in practice but private-looking and absent from the authoritative public surface.

## Recommended Action

Make a clean pre-alpha break: have the public re-frame.machines/machine-transition return one transparent, self-describing ordinary map owned by the facade. A suitable contract is success {:status :ok, :snapshot snapshot, :fx [...]} and engine-reported failure {:status :error, :error diagnostic}; settle the exact spellings once in the normative spec and use them everywhere. Application code and tests should need only re-frame.machines.

Remove re-frame.machines.result from application-facing docs and examples. Delete it if the engine no longer needs it, or keep an internal representation genuinely private and normalize only at the facade boundary. Do not retain aliases, tombstones, dual shapes, or compatibility adapters.

## Evidence

- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:103 exports machine-transition as a direct alias of engine/machine-transition, so the engine representation becomes the public representation.
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/result.cljc:6-20 defines the ::tag/::snap/::fx/::info map and labels three keys public, while lines 43-45 describe the namespace as internal to the machines artefact.
- docs/machines/tutorial.md:320-348 and docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md:128-166 teach a second re-frame.machines.result require plus accessors solely to inspect a pure transition.
- docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:143-164 and spec/API.md:936 name re-frame.machines.result/Result as the public return type.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:867-888 imports re-frame.machines.result and destructures ::result/snap and ::result/fx in the executable public walkthrough.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The normative machine spec defines one exact, self-describing public return shape for successful and engine-reported failed pure transitions, including snapshot, ordered effects, and diagnostic data.
- re-frame.machines/machine-transition implements that contract without requiring consumers to know an internal namespace or qualified implementation keys.
- Existing semantics remain covered: successful snapshots and effect order are unchanged; thrown action/guard failures and depth-abort failures remain atomic and diagnostic; programmer-input errors that intentionally throw have a clearly documented boundary.
- Focused JVM and CLJS machine tests, conformance fixtures, and executable examples assert the public shape through re-frame.machines only.
- Spec 005, spec/API.md, docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, the tutorial, inspection guide, and state-machine walkthrough all use the same contract and no longer teach re-frame.machines.result.
- The API manifest/generator and drift checks accurately describe the resulting public surface; no public namespace used by the docs is omitted from that surface.
- The old application-facing Result accessors and key shape are removed in the same change, with no compatibility layer.

## Non-goals

- Changing statechart syntax, transition selection, hierarchy, action execution, effect ordering, dispatch, timers, actor ownership, or spawn semantics.
- Designing a model-based testing DSL, matcher library, or new helper namespace.
- Redesigning the broader exception taxonomy beyond documenting the existing programmer-error boundary.
- Solving eager singleton startup or synthetic start-event ergonomics.
- Preserving the old Result shape for compatibility.

## Related beads

- rf2-ys42 (closed) corrected and expanded the machines tutorial/testing documentation; it exposes this seam but did not redesign it.
- rf2-npgc (closed) restructured the machines guide and added inspecting-machines.md; it is documentation context, not duplicate implementation work.
- rf2-cnij (closed) improved facade docstrings and API notes; it did not cover the pure transition result contract.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this result-contract outcome was found.

title: [MERGED #10119] 018:2113 redaction table cites superseded 012-Views.md for cluster aggregates that were never built — worker refuted the brief's premise; whole cell rewritten
description:
`tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:2113` — the REDACTION-SURFACE table's `L4 Views tab` row — cites
the superseded `012-Views.md` as the authority for a behaviour that document's own banner says was

**The row, quoted verbatim at trunk `a992b86f1a` (re-derived by the mayor 2026-09-20 18:5x, NOT
inherited from the report that named it):**

    | L4 Views tab | Per-view sub return values | Via `inspect`; per-sub redaction propagation visible; cluster aggregates per [`012-Views.md`](012-Views.md) |

**Why the citation is false.** `tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:1-14` is a SUPERSEDED banner whose whole
purpose is to deny the design below it, and **≥50 grid clustering is one of the named items**: the
banner lists "three TEMPORAL groups (mounted / re-rendered / unmounted), subs nested under views with
inline return values, **≥50 grid clustering**, a component/sub group-by toggle, a right-click
component-filter chip, per-component inline drilldown … and the five-state sub-status glyph taxonomy"
and says that surface "is **NOT implemented** and is **not the destination**". So "cluster aggregates
per `012-Views.md`" cites a document that says there are no cluster aggregates.

**This is the THIRD site of one defect, and the other two are already fixed.** `rf2-m1qh0` (PR #10111,
open at filing) corrects `:634` — the L3 tab inventory row — and `:2283` — the §14 reference row. Its
worker found this one, correctly did NOT edit it because it sat outside its item's two named sites,
and named it with its line number. `rf2-qrjr5` (PR #10108, merged) fixed the same supersession at
`019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:821`.

**SCOPE — and the narrow reading is deliberate.** The defect this item owns is the **`cluster
aggregates per 012-Views.md` clause**. Correct or drop it, and re-point the citation at
`021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §3 if the row still needs an authority.

**DO NOT assume the rest of the row is wrong, and adjudicate rather than sweep.** The middle column
reads "Per-view sub return values", and the phrase `sub return values` is NOT uniformly false in this
tree — rf2-m1qh0's census took it from 3 occurrences to 2 and deliberately LEFT two standing as correct
uses. The shipped panel per `021` §3.2 is a reactive flow graph carrying sub nodes, so sub return
values being inspectable is plausibly true even though 012's *nested-under-views* presentation is not.
**Resolve it against `021` §3.2 and say which it is**; if it is true, leave it and say so.

**The row's own subject is REDACTION, not layout** — its neighbours at `:2110-2116` are about sentinel
markers, `[● REDACTED N]` chips and per-fx payloads — so "per-sub redaction propagation visible" is a
redaction claim and is not in scope here unless it is false for an independent reason.

**Out of scope, each a live temptation:** do not edit `012-Views.md` (its banner is correct and is what
makes this row wrong); do not rewrite `021`; do not touch `:634` or `:2283` (rf2-m1qh0 owns them); do
not renumber or reorder the table or change any column count.

**FENCE.** `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md` is held by **open PR #10111**. A surface fence releases
only when the change MERGES, not when its worker reports, so this is not dispatchable until #10111 is
on trunk — at which point `:2113` must be **re-derived**, since 018 has taken several PRs this week.

**A check no gate performs.** `:2113` is a markdown table row and nothing in this repository validates
column counts or rendering: `mkdocs build --strict` stages `spec` and `migration` and no `tools/` tree,
`check_readme_links.py --ci` excludes all of `tools/*/spec/`, and the live gate —
`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` — reads link targets and anchors only. The row carries a markdown
link, so that gate's green is LIVE for this line rather than vacuous; count the link tokens and say so.
Count the pipes before and after against the header row.

**File health:** `w/crlf`. Never `sed -i` — it rewrites every line ending at exit 0 while `git diff`
stays silent, even when the pattern matches nothing. Take three numbers with Python on the bytes
before and after: total CR, total CRLF, bare LF; require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0.

## MAYOR'S CORRECTION: THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THE WORKER REFUTED IT (2026-09-20)

**Appended, not reopened** — this bead's `close_reason` (7131 characters) stands untouched.

**THE BRIEF TOLD THIS WORKER THAT `Per-view sub return values` WAS "plausibly true". IT IS FALSE.**
The worker adjudicated it FALSE for the L4 Views tab on independent readings, said so, and corrected
the mayor. It was right. The mayor has now re-derived every step at trunk `84759441e4`, uncapped.

**WHAT THE BRIEF SAID**, verbatim: *"The shipped panel per `021` §3.2 is a reactive flow graph
carrying sub nodes, so sub return values being inspectable is plausibly true even though 012's
nested-under-views presentation is not."*

**WHAT §3.2 ACTUALLY SAYS.** `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:565-567`, inside
`### §3.2 Layout — DAG visualised as indented cascade` (heading at `:525`), verbatim:

> Below the graph, two list sections complete the panel (the prior SUB VALUES section retired in
> rf2-uz3wm — the Epoch panel's SUBSCRIPTIONS table now carries per-cascade sub values + per-sub
> diff chrome in cascade context, so the Reactive tab's value-listing is duplicate inventory):

**SO THE MAYOR NOMINATED THE RIGHT AUTHORITY AND DID NOT READ IT.** The retirement note sits INSIDE
§3.2 — the exact section the brief told the worker to resolve the claim against. That is worse than
citing the wrong document: a wrong citation invites a check, while a right one invites trust.

**AND THE BRIEF QUOTED THE REFUTATION IN ITS OWN TEXT WITHOUT SEEING IT.** `012-Views.md:8-10`'s
SUPERSEDED banner enumerates what is **NOT implemented**, and the second item on that list is
**"subs nested under views with inline return values"**. The brief quoted this banner as the thing
that makes the row wrong, then carved out "Per-view sub return values" as plausibly surviving it —
when the banner names that phrase almost word for word. **Two independent authorities, one of them
already pasted into the brief, and the reading went past both.**

**THE CIRCULARITY IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The brief also said rf2-m1qh0's census *"deliberately
left two standing as CORRECT USES"*. It did not. Re-measured at trunk, `sub return values` reads
**3 occurrences** repo-wide with the tracker export excluded:

| site | what it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:2113` | **the row this very bead was adjudicating** |
| `tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:550` | a line INSIDE the superseded document |
| `examples/core/seven_guis/flight_booker/core.cljs:23` | outside the census scope entirely |

So the two inside `tools/xray/spec/` that rf2-m1qh0 left standing were the superseded doc's own line
and **the line under adjudication here**. Neither was ruled correct; both were OUT OF SCOPE for that
item. **The mayor turned "not adjudicated" into "adjudicated true", and then offered the line back to
the next worker as evidence about itself.** Had the worker deferred, a false claim would have been
re-certified by a citation whose sole support was the claim.

**THIS IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY A WORKER REFUTED A PREMISE THE MAYOR WROTE**, after `rf2-u40qy`,
where a locator capped at `head -5` produced a false "the item's numbers are all stale". **The two
share a mechanism and it is not carelessness about evidence — it is a READING that outran the
evidence and was then stated in the register of a measurement.** On u40qy a truncated listing became
a negative claim about correct work; here an unread section became a positive claim about a false
one. Both were written as findings rather than as guesses, which is what makes them expensive: a
brief's assertions arrive at a worker carrying the coordinator's authority.

**WHAT CHANGES.** A brief may state a premise the worker is to ADJUDICATE, and should — that is what
this one asked for and it worked. What it must not do is attach a verdict ("plausibly true") to a
premise the mayor has not measured, because the verdict travels and the hedge does not. **Where the
mayor has an opinion and no measurement, the brief says so in those words.**

**WHAT THE WORKER DID RIGHT, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS WAS CAUGHT.** It re-read the nominated
authority instead of accepting the nomination, quoted `021:563` verbatim rather than paraphrasing,
went back to rf2-m1qh0's actual disposition rather than trusting the brief's summary of it, and
reported the contradiction plainly instead of routing around it. **The brief-vs-item clause carried
in that dispatch — "if anything on the item disagrees with the brief, the ITEM GOVERNS, say so and
follow it" — is now load-bearing twice in one day, and it earned its place both times.**

**THREE FURTHER SITES IT NAMED, RE-DERIVED BY THE MAYOR AT `84759441e4` AND NOT EDITED HERE** (they

**WHAT I WROTE, two notes above, about the landed row:** *"Three things that a narrower fix would have
got wrong"*, and that the rewrite was *"larger and better than the item asked for."* **The first half
of that still stands. The praise was too broad.** The rewrite went beyond the item's scope, and in the
part that went beyond scope it introduced a NEW false claim that the narrower fix could not have made.

**THE FALSE CLAUSE.** The landed `:2113` says *"...and the teardown + unchanged-sub rows key by query
vector."* **The unchanged-sub half is true. The teardown half is false**, and the two are joined by an
`and` that makes one verification read as two.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs:318` `destroyed-subscriptions`
  reads `(:rf.sub/id tags) (:sub-id tags) (:rf.sub/id ev) (:sub-id ev)` — **the query vector appears
  nowhere in the function** — then applies `(distinct)` and emits `{:sub-id sub-id}`. Its own docstring
  says it: *"Each `:rf.sub/dispose` op anchors a row `{:sub-id <kw/id>}`. First-seen order,
  de-duplicated."* So disposing `[:item/by-id 1]` and `[:item/by-id 2]` yields **ONE row**, not two.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs:595` `unchanged-row-identity` is
  `(if (some? query-v) query-v sub-id)`, and its docstring states the opposite behaviour deliberately:
  *"distinct parameterizations of one registered sub (`[:item/derived 1]` / `[:item/derived 2]`) render
  as distinct, individually-addressable rows"* (rf2-cj2yx).

**So the asymmetry is REAL AND DELIBERATE — one surface keys by query vector, the other by registered
sub id — and the new sentence erases it by conjunction.** It promises a concrete UI capability that
does not exist.

**token census**: `cluster aggregates per` 1→0, `Per-view sub return values` 1→0, `sub return values`
3→2, with live controls at 12 and 5. **Every one of those measurements was correct, and none of them
could see this.** A census answers *did the false thing go away*; it cannot answer *is the replacement
text true*. The row's REPLACEMENT was 257 bytes of new prose making three separate claims about
renderer behaviour, and I verified the row's **shape** (4 pipes, table renders) and its **tokens**, and
read its **argument** approvingly — but I checked none of its three claims against the renderers.

worker removes a false claim, a token census is sufficient and cheap. When a worker REPLACES it, the
new text is new surface area, and it arrives with the credibility of the correction it rode in on —
**I was more, not less, trusting of that prose because the adjudication behind it had been so good.**

has reviewed, including the item's author.

**THE PRACTICE THAT FOLLOWS:** when a merge note says a worker went beyond scope, name the claims the
extra text makes and say which of them were checked. **In this note I would have had to write "three
new claims about renderer behaviour, none checked", which is the sentence that would have caught it.**

landed text against source after the coordinator has stopped looking, and it did that within minutes
of the merge. **The defect was caught by the system; what was missing was any signal in my own note

    tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:607  | Motion contract — 180ms tab fade, diff-flash, `--motion-scale` seam; motion-as-language |
    tools/story/spec/Feature-Parity-Audit.md:423  | Animation timing | 180ms tab fade, diff-flash on app-db change, `--motion-scale` seam |

**Each is a ROW naming THREE things, and they are not in the same state.** Re-derive every line
number at your own base and report the delta.

## CLAIM 1 — diff-flash. FALSE, and settled.

`diff.flash` (both spellings, one pattern) reads **0** across `tools/story/src`.

**Control, and it is the kind that matters — it proves Story HAS motion, so the zero is about this
effect and not about a tree the instrument cannot read:** `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/theme/
motion.cljc:173-177` declares **five real `@keyframes`** — `rf-story-mount-in`,
`rf-story-overlay-in`, `rf-story-overlay-out`, `rf-story-chip-press`, `rf-story-shimmer`. A nonsense
token reads 0 in the spec tree. So Story ships a genuine motion vocabulary; a diff-flash is simply
not in it.

`motion.scale` in any spelling reads **0** across `tools/story/src` and `tools/story/test`, against

Clojure var, a config key, a multiplier applied to the durations in `motion.cljc`, a
`prefers-reduced-motion` branch that scales rather than disables? `motion.cljc` already carries a

another name, the spec's spelling is the defect, not the claim. If it exists under no name, the
claim is false.** Say which, with the measurement.

## CLAIM 3 — the 180ms tab fade. PROBABLY TRUE. Do not sweep it away.

`180ms|tab.fade` reads **4** in `tools/story/src`. **This is the element most likely to be destroyed
