title: dispatch pipeline never names scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh - the mandatory guard reaches a brief only if the mayor retypes it, and the OS-neutral form that IS emitted reports rather than refuses
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the mayor while verifying an assembled dispatch brief, and caught only by a
probe that read 0 where 1 was expected. **This is the STANCE's homelessness, reached through a
different door** — a MANDATORY project instruction that the standing dispatch procedure does not
carry, so it survives only by being retyped into each per-dispatch task file.

## THE OBSERVABLE

CLAUDE.md § Workflow is unambiguous: *"Worker worktree guard is mandatory before edits. Background
workers must run the guard from their intended checkout before editing, and report the printed
`WORKTREE_ROOT`. Use `sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` (POSIX primary) or
`powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1`."*

**Neither file the brief assembler draws from names that script.** Measured at trunk `03b51187e4`:

    docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md   assert-worker-worktree  0   (control: worktree 38)
    ai/dispatch-blocks.md                               assert-worker-worktree  0   (control: worktree 32)

What the assembled boundary block prescribes instead is the OS-neutral form: *"ask version control
for the top level of <worktree> and check it prints <worktree>."*

## WHY THE OS-NEUTRAL FORM IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE — IT REPORTS, IT CANNOT REFUSE

`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers where you are. **The script REFUSES where you should not
be**: it derives the mayor checkout as the repository's primary worktree and the worktree parent as
its `re-frame2-worktrees` sibling — no hardcoded paths, both overridable — and rejects the mayor
checkout and any root outside that parent. CLAUDE.md records that this exists to mitigate observed
harness path-resolution leaks.

So a worker following the brief exactly gets a reading, compares it by eye, and proceeds. A worker
running the script gets a refusal. The difference is the entire value of the guard, and it is the
same shape CLAUDE.md's own shadow-cljs bullet states as a general principle: **"a rule phrased as
'announce X' tells you what to SAY and not what to CHECK... absent an arbiter, the exclusive is not
exclusive."** A guard that cannot refuse is not a guard.

## THE MISS RATE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — 1 IN 4 THIS SESSION

Every brief assembled in this session's scratchpad, probed for the script name against the
OS-neutral form:

    brief-journey3.txt      script-named 1   os-neutral 1
    brief-subequals.txt     script-named 1   os-neutral 1
    brief-xraynightly.txt   script-named 1   os-neutral 1
    brief-trigkeys.txt      script-named 0   os-neutral 1   <- the miss, caught before dispatch

The three that carry it carry it **because the mayor typed it into that dispatch's task file by
hand**, since the assembler emits it from nowhere. The fourth dropped it. The OS-neutral form is
present in all four, which is exactly what makes the miss hard to see: the brief still contains a
worktree check, reads careful, and satisfies a casual probe for "does this brief guard the
worktree?"

**It fails in the REASSURING direction**, which is why it is worth an item rather than a shrug.

## THE FIX SHAPE IS ALREADY SETTLED BY PRECEDENT — DO NOT PUT IT IN THE TEMPLATE

`dispatch-prompt-template.md` is the reusable, OS-neutral method and must stay that way. CLAUDE.md
already rules on exactly this division for the stance: that page *"does NOT carry it and must not"*,
the stance is *"PASTED rather than pulled"*, and it *"lives in its own file"*. A POSIX-versus-
PowerShell script path is project- and OS-specific in precisely the same way.

So the candidate homes are the project side:

  * **`ai/assemble-brief.sh` emits it** alongside the stance it already pastes — mechanical, and the
    assembler already reports `stance 5/5 verbatim`, so it could report the guard line the same way;
  * **`ai/dispatch-blocks.md` carries it** — but note that file is GITIGNORED, which is the exact
    fragility CLAUDE.md records for the stance (*"its one working copy was `ai/dispatch-blocks.md`,
    which is gitignored"*), so this is the weaker option and repeats a known failure;
  * **leave it to the task file and accept the retyping**, which is the status quo and is what
    measured 1 miss in 4.

**Prefer the first.** The assembler is the only mechanical point in this chain, and a check it
performs cannot be forgotten by a tired coordinator.

## WHAT IS NOT WRONG — DO NOT OVERSHOOT

  * **The OS-neutral boundary block is correct and stays.** It is not to be replaced; the script
    nomination sits BESIDE it. Per-edit verification is still wanted.
  * **`dispatch-prompt-template.md` needs no edit**, per the precedent above. Do not add an
    OS-specific path to an OS-neutral page.
  * **CLAUDE.md is already correct** — it names the script, both spellings, and calls it mandatory.
    The gap is that the dispatch pipeline does not read it.
  * **Do NOT add a CI gate.** Nothing in a PR can observe whether a dispatch brief named a script;
    briefs are untracked local artefacts by design.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * **Whether any worker has ever actually edited the wrong tree because of this.** Not searched. The
    guard exists because path-resolution leaks were OBSERVED, but no instance is known to trace to a
    brief that omitted the script, and this session's one miss was caught before dispatch.
  * **How far back the omission goes.** Only this session's four briefs were probed; earlier briefs
    are not retained, so the base rate over the project's history is unmeasured and 1-in-4 should not
    be quoted as one.
  * Whether `assemble-brief.sh` has a natural insertion point that keeps its "0 placeholders left"
    self-check meaningful. Not inspected.

CLOSED 2026-09-17 by the mayor, same tick it was filed. **No PR and no branch — the fix lands entirely
in the gitignored `ai/` tree**, which is why this was never a worker dispatch: all three candidate homes
the description weighed sit under `/ai/`, so there is nothing for CI to grade and nothing to merge.

## WHAT WAS DONE — OPTION ONE, THE ASSEMBLER EMITS IT

`ai/assemble-brief.sh` now emits a PROJECT GUARD block in worktree mode, immediately after the
OS-neutral boundary block, naming both spellings (`sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` and the
PowerShell sibling), stating that the boundary block only REPORTS a root while the script REFUSES one,
and telling the worker to run it IN ADDITION to the per-edit check rather than instead of it.

Chosen over the other two for the reason the description gave: the assembler is the only MECHANICAL
point in the chain, and a check it performs cannot be forgotten by a tired coordinator. `ai/dispatch-
blocks.md` was refused explicitly — it is gitignored, which is the exact fragility CLAUDE.md already
records for the stance, so putting the guard there would repeat a known failure rather than fix one.
`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` was NOT touched, per the precedent CLAUDE.md sets
for the stance: that page is the reusable OS-neutral method and a POSIX-vs-PowerShell path does not
belong in it.

## PINNED BY CONTENT, NOT BY A RETYPED LINE

Two refusals guard the emission, modelled on the stance's non-circular clause pins:

  * the script must EXIST at `scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh`;
  * `CLAUDE.md` must still NAME it.

So a rename that updates only one of the two refuses at assembly rather than emitting a path no worker
can run. Both pins measured live: CLAUDE.md names it (1) against a nonsense variant (0), and the file
is present.

A third check runs at the end beside the stance's 5/5: the guard must SURVIVE into the assembled brief.
That is a separate fact from emitting it, because the brief is built inside a redirected group — a
future edit to that group could drop it while every step still exits 0, which is precisely how the
script went missing in the first place. No-worktree dispatches edit nothing and are exempt by
construction, reported as `guard n/a (no-worktree)`.

## MEASURED BOTH WAYS, WITH THE CONTROL TAKEN FROM A TASK FILE THAT NEVER MENTIONS IT

The decisive test: assemble with a task file carrying ZERO occurrences of the script name, so the brief
can only get it from the assembler.

    A  worktree mode      exit 0   guard in brief 2   WORKTREE_ROOT 1   "guard named"
    B  --no-worktree      exit 0   guard in brief 0                     "guard n/a (no-worktree)"

Gate block unchanged at 14037 chars and stance 5/5 verbatim in both, so nothing else moved.

**And the survival check was shown RED rather than asserted.** The emission was removed from a COPY of
the script (797 characters, 0 occurrences of the heredoc terminator left) and that copy run: exit **3**,
`REFUSED: the mandatory worktree guard did not survive into the assembled brief`, guard absent from the
output — while the real script exits 0 and reports `guard named` on the same inputs.

## THE FIRST SABOTAGE ATTEMPT WAS ITSELF DEFECTIVE, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT FAILED RED

The first plant sliced from `cat <<GUARDEOF` to the next `GUARDEOF\n`, which matched the END OF THE
OPENING LINE rather than the terminator — so it deleted one line and left the heredoc body standing as
raw shell. The run exited **2** with no `REFUSED:` line at all, and the character count read **-22**,
i.e. the "removal" made the file LONGER.

This is the sabotage-control hazard the dispatch template names, met from the reverse side: the template
warns that a plant which silently NO-OPS makes the run come back green, so the worker reports a guard
that fired when nothing was broken. Here the plant did not no-op — it broke something ELSE — and the
run came back red for the wrong reason, which is the reading that would have passed as success. **The
two tells were both present and both numeric**: a wrong exit code (2, the usage arm, not 3), and a
negative removal count. Re-planted against `\nGUARDEOF\n` at column 0, the control behaves as above.

## WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED

  * **No instance of a worker actually editing the wrong tree because of this is known** — not searched
    then, not searched now. The guard exists because path-resolution leaks were OBSERVED, but the one
    miss measured this session was caught before dispatch.
  * **The 1-in-4 miss rate is this session's four briefs only** and must not be quoted as a base rate;
    earlier briefs are not retained.
  * `scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1` is emitted as the Windows spelling on CLAUDE.md's authority and
    was NOT independently exercised here.
  * CLAUDE.md was not edited: it already names the script, both spellings, and calls the guard
    mandatory. The gap was that the dispatch pipeline did not read it, and that is what moved.

title: CLAUDE.md: a late-bind hook change is grade-able only in the node lane — a green browser lane plus green JVM artefacts is not evidence about it
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-ty246 WORKER (PR #9904, shortlist item 8) 2026-09-16, and worth a tracked home because it is a COVERAGE-TOPOLOGY fact about this project's test lanes, not a defect in any change.

THE FACT. A change that adds a LATE-BIND HOOK is grade-able ONLY in the node lane. Neither of the other two lanes can see it:
  * The BROWSER lane cannot. The publication cross-check lives in a namespace ending `-cljs-test`, not `-dom-cljs-test`, so `test.yml`'s `:browser-test` ns-regexp never loads it.
  * The JVM lane cannot. It is a `.cljs` test, so the JVM artefacts never compile it.

HOW IT PRESENTED, which is the part that earns the entry. The worker held a GREEN browser lane at 1111 tests / 6083 assertions / 0 failures AND 21 of 21 JVM artefacts green, WITH A REAL FAILURE SITTING BETWEEN THEM: `reagent_slim_late_bind_publication_cljs_test.cljs`'s `reagent-slim-adapter-hooks-cross-checked-against-directory` asserts `(= expected-hook-keys (directory-hook-keys-for 're-frame.adapter.reagent-slim))`, and adding a key to the directory made the two sides unequal. TWO CLEAN COLUMNS AND A LIVE RED IN THE GAP.

THIS IS THE "TWO ZEROS SHARING ONE BLIND SPOT" SHAPE CLAUDE.md ALREADY CATALOGUES, REACHED THROUGH A NEW DOOR. The existing instance (rf2-p0b0) is two SEARCHES corroborating each other -- a name-grep zero and a `spec.cjs` count -- until `check-examples-compile.cjs --list` refuted both. Here the corroborating instruments are TWO GREEN GATE LANES, and the routing is by NAMESPACE SUFFIX rather than by search pattern. Same failure shape, different mechanism, and the existing entry does not cover it.

AND THE SAME REGEXP FACT CUTS BOTH WAYS, which is why it is worth stating rather than just warning about. The worker used it CORRECTLY minutes earlier to predict that two assertions it had added would appear in the node column and NOT the browser one -- a prediction that made its green run falsifiable and which the measurement confirmed (+6, not +8). The suffix rule is a sound instrument; what bit was not knowing that ONE CLASS OF CHANGE is graded by exactly one lane.

PROPOSED HOME: CLAUDE.md, the paragraph in "## Build & Test" that already explains lane routing and the `--list` enumeration lesson. One or two sentences: name the late-bind publication cross-check, say which lane grades it and why the other two cannot, and say that a green browser lane plus green JVM artefacts is NOT evidence about a late-bind hook change.

The dispatch method tells workers to run the NARROWEST gate covering their diff, and for tools/story CLJS that is exactly a --test= selection. A worker following that instruction gets a node crash instead of a verdict, and either burns a cycle diagnosing an unrelated Xray timer or falls back to the full 12k-test run. Several workers in one wave on 2026-09-14 ran tools/story CLJS lanes locally.

title: O-18 observability sweep calls the internal re-frame.elision walker directly; route its two samples through rf/project-egress
description:
Found during rf2-z9xl's census of the namespaces the migration corpus tells migrators to require. It was not fixed there, for two reasons: it sits outside that worker's file fence, and it is not an M-1 allowlist omission.

DEFECT. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md` (O-18) calls the elision walker directly in app-authored forwarder code, at two sites: `(re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value v opts)` in §3 "The cap pattern" (about line 152) and `(re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value floor-redacted opts)` in §4 Shape A (about line 294). Re-derive both line numbers at tip.

`spec/API.md` §Size-elision wire-boundary walker rules otherwise: "Internal mechanism, not a façade door (rf2-kuky.9 ruling A, executed by rf2-kuky.90)". The walker carries no `re-frame.core` re-export and no manifest row, and `rf/project-egress` is the single projection door. So the O-18 sample teaches a require of an internal namespace. The migration skill's M-1 sweep correctly flags `re-frame.elision`, which means the sample and the sweep disagree: a migrator who follows O-18 ends up with an M-1 site.

FIX. Rewrite both samples to go through `(rf/project-egress v opts)`. The opts the samples pass (`:rf.egress/threshold-bytes`, `:rf.egress/include-sensitive?`, `:rf.egress/include-large?`, `:frame`) all sit inside project-egress's closed opts set, so the swap looks direct. The dropped-count logic that follows stays as it is. Confirm the returned value shape at the rewrite.

Do NOT add `re-frame.elision` to the M-1 allowlist in `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md`. That would contradict the ruling above.

Gates: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (path: migration/). The code samples sit inside fenced blocks, which no gate reads, so check the fence by hand.
notes:
REMEDIATED in PR #9771 (draft opened, branch worker/skillsb-a, based on origin/main c09c413ad6). Premise re-verified at tip before the fix.

PREMISE CONFIRMED. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc records that the path-walker facade export is RETIRED (rf2-kuky.9 ruling A, executed by rf2-kuky.90) and that rf/project-egress "is now the ONLY projection door on the façade", delegating the per-slot walk to re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value, which "stays public at its home namespace for the framework's own emit-time chokepoints". So an app-authored forwarder calling the walker directly is exactly the M-1 site the migration skill's sweep flags.

FIXED, both sites, line numbers re-derived at tip. migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md:152 (§3 "The cap pattern", inside cap-or-elide) and :294 (§4 Shape A's cap-or-elide) now call (rf/project-egress v opts) and (rf/project-egress floor-redacted opts).

RETURNED VALUE SHAPE CONFIRMED AT THE REWRITE, as the bead asks, by reading implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc. Three things make the swap direct rather than merely plausible. (1) OPTS: project-egress-opt-keys is DERIVED from re-frame.elision/walker-opt-keys ("so the two doors cannot drift into disagreeing about the vocabulary") plus :rf.egress/profile plus the three epoch-only keys — and all four opts the samples pass (:rf.egress/threshold-bytes, :rf.egress/include-sensitive?, :rf.egress/include-large?, :frame) are members of walker-opt-keys, so the closed-opts guard cannot fire. (2) PROFILE: resolve-elision-opts' first cond arm is `(nil? profile)`, which passes the opts through verbatim minus the absent key — the samples name no :rf.egress/profile, so the resolved walker opts are exactly what the old call passed. (3) SHAPE: a kindless value is not a recognised record (recognised-record? tests :kind against record-kinds), so project-record-by-kind takes its default arm, `(walk-slot record elision-opts)`, which is a direct delegation to elide-wire-value. The return is therefore the same walked value the old call produced, and the dropped-count tree-seq and the pr-str byte-budget backstop that follow are untouched, exactly as the bead requires.

NO ALLOWLIST CHANGE. re-frame.elision stays an M-1 site in skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, per the ruling the bead cites; the prose now says so explicitly at both the §3 bullet and inside the cap-or-elide docstring, so the sample and the sweep agree instead of contradicting each other.

ONE ADJACENT REPAIR IN THE SAME TWO SAMPLES, recorded rather than smuggled. Both `(rf/register-listener! :my-app/audit-forwarder f)` calls were TWO-argument against register-listener!'s single fixed [stream id f] arity (core.cljc), so the recipe this rule tells a migrator to write could not run at all. Both now pass :trace explicitly. Taken because it is broken sample code inside the fenced blocks this bead sends a worker into, and two tokens; not taken as licence to widen scope further — see below.

GATES. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, nominated by PATH (migration/ is one of its roots): captured exit 0. Also `python -m mkdocs build --strict` exit 0 — mkdocs_hooks.py's on_pre_build stages migration/ into docs_dir, so the strict build DOES cover this file. check_readme_links.py --ci 0, and the verify-skill-mcp-drift repo invariants 0 (check_egress_walker_residue.py among them, which is the gate most directly adjacent to this change). The changed-surface classifier arms skills_structural only; nothing else is scheduled by this path.

GATE DISCRIMINATION PROVED, not assumed. Neither gate prints a worktree root, so a broken relative link was planted in this very file and BOTH went red naming it — check_doc_slugs.py exit 1 ("BROKEN TARGET: ... observability-logging-sweep.md:123") and mkdocs --strict exit 1 with the same target. The plant was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and verified by blob hash: `git hash-object` in its default form matched `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (a622945e34370a07d0a7c7d03d21baaae8d79a34) and `git diff --quiet HEAD` exited 0.

FENCE CHECKED BY HAND, as the bead requires, because no gate reads inside a fenced block: the two rewritten call forms were read against project-egress's actual signature and opt vocabulary in projection.cljc and elision.cljc rather than against prose, and the surrounding dropped-count / byte-budget forms were left byte-identical.

NO REGRESSION TEST ADDED, and the reason is recorded rather than omitted: this leaf has no executable assertion surface, the change is two call forms inside fenced samples that no gate reads by design, and the two plant-and-restore runs above are the discriminating evidence available here. Wiring a new prose-presence gate for it would be the kind of one-off ratchet the project's stance declines.

STOPPED ON — a WIDER retired-listener cluster in this same file, deliberately NOT taken, and it wants its own bead. Beyond this bead's two sites, the leaf teaches `register-event-listener!` / `register-error-listener!` as the corpus-wide production door at lines 3, 5, 220 and 255 — verbs the corpus's own M-69 row states do not exist ("There are no register-event-listener! / register-error-listener! facade aliases") — and names Shape B after the retired `register-epoch-listener!` facade at lines 217, 351 and through the §Shape B body, although its sample already uses the correct `(rf/register-listener! :epoch ...)`. That is a coherent repair of its own, it moves a section-heading anchor, and it is the corpus-side twin of rf2-fzbj.39's F1 rather than anything this P3 asks for. Named in PR #9771's body under "Stopped on".

New rf2-vin7n owns O-18 stale trace record operations/fields; new rf2-2cgzg owns its removed dropped-counter registrar. title: Nine States keeps success selected after the next invalid submit
description:
Handle `:submit-invalid` while the Nine States form is in `:correct`, transitioning to `:incorrect`. A valid submit clears the draft, but pressing Add again leaves the success state selected even though the new submission correctly fails validation.

Ownership: examples_patterns, `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:458-464` (success-state transitions), `:603-629` (submit handler), `:681-707` (render priority), and `:799-814` (enabled form submit). Baseline: `9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261`. Revalidated at `9291090725fa3ebcad67ea81a74946fc3aac96a4`; all 25 assigned paths remain identical to baseline.

SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)

Remediation fence: split from finding 2 of `rf2-fzbj.34`, which remains open and unchanged. Preserve `[FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]`; this fresh review authorizes issue creation, not fixer dispatch or source remediation.

Reproducer: initialise the example, edit the title to "Buy milk", and submit successfully. The handler adds one todo, resets the title to an empty string, and selects `:form/:correct`. Without typing anything else, press Add again. The input/button remain enabled in active mode, so this is an ordinary supported UI sequence.

Expected: second submit keeps exactly one todo, records the required title error, transitions the form to `:incorrect`, removes `:form/success`, and makes `:ui/render` select `:incorrect`.

Actual: the submit handler records `{:title ["Title must be at least 3 characters."]}` and dispatches `:submit-invalid`, but `:correct` only handles `:edit` and `:reset`. The form remains `:correct` with `:form/success`, which wins render priority. The main panel continues saying "Todo added" alongside the new field error. No duplicate todo is added; the defect is incorrect state and feedback in the example teaching those states.

Suggested repair: add `:submit-invalid :incorrect` to the `:on` map of `[:regions :form :states :correct]`. Preserve the existing edit/reset and valid-submit behavior. Keep validation in the existing pure validator; no disabled-button policy, extra state field, or state-machine restructuring is necessary.

Acceptance:

- Drive initialise -> valid edit -> successful submit -> submit again with cleared draft through the actual handlers. Assert one item, title error present, `:form/invalid` present, `:form/success` absent, and `:ui/render=:incorrect`.
- Edit a subsequent valid title and submit; return to `:correct` and add exactly one further item.
- Add the sequence to the framework-owned Nine States CLJS tests (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/nine_states_cljs_test.cljs`), not under examples/. The old transition table must fail the witness.

The existing Nine States state-7/state-8 fixtures each start from a fresh frame and do not cover success followed by invalid submit. Prior report `rf2-fzbj.34` was read with newest-first history (limit 3), and its status/fence/notes were preserved.

After second submit it observed state `{:data :one :form :correct :mode :active}`, the title error above, one item, and render `:correct`. An in-memory-only control adding the proposed transition changed the same event to render `:incorrect`. title: filters/Modal kept as a reg-view on a refuted premise — the docstring now states something false
description:
`filters/Modal` was left an `rf/reg-view` during the chrome-satellite migration, with a docstring
recording the reason. TWO SIBLING WORKERS HAVE SINCE REFUTED THAT REASON WITH SHIPPED EVIDENCE, so
the docstring now states something false in the tree.

## THE CLAIM THAT IS WRONG

The recorded reason was, in substance: a `defview` mints a React component rather than a legal
Reagent head, so migrating a shell-root modal needs an edit to `shell.cljs` that all five satellites
would each also need — i.e. the conflict the parallel split exists to avoid.

THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE. The bridge solves exactly this and it is SHIPPED AT TIP:

    cancellation_cascade.cljs   Popover-component = (rf.fresco/as-component PopoverView), top level
    cancellation_cascade.cljs   (defn Popover [] [:> Popover-component {}])
    its docstring               "what `shell.cljs` mounts as a hiccup head", and
                                "Since rf2-k97c.3 it is the migration bridge rather than the view"
    shell.cljs:3167             [cancellation-cascade/Popover]     <- a Reagent hiccup head

Keeping the PUBLIC NAME a callable bridge and making the boundary private behind it needs NO
`shell.cljs` edit at all. The constraint is real only if you make `Modal` ITSELF the `defview`.

## HOW IT WAS ESTABLISHED — TWO INDEPENDENT WORKERS, NEITHER PROMPTED

`spinefilt-a` migrated `spine-filters/Modal` and `RowContextMenu` this way and refused a mayor
instruction to revert them, citing `shell.cljs:3177`/`:3183` sitting in the SAME mount block, ten
lines from the cancellation-cascade head. Its branch touched three files and `shell.cljs` was not
one of them. Node lane green; sabotage bit.

`palmig-a` migrated `palette/Modal` the same way, independently, and said the same thing: "the
sibling's constraint was real only for making `Modal` itself the `defview`." Browser sabotage proved
it mounts and paints.

Both are merged (PR #9668) or green and ready (PR #9665). So the pattern is demonstrated twice more
on top of the shipped precedent.

## THE MAYOR'S PART IN THIS, RECORDED SO THE PATTERN IS NOT REPEATED

The mayor took the filters worker's conclusion and passed it to two other satellites as a general
constraint WITHOUT CHECKING WHETHER THE PREMISE HELD ON THEIR SURFACES. Both refused it, correctly,
with evidence. That is the same error the dispatch briefs warn workers about — carrying a conclusion
from one file to another without measuring — committed by the coordinator.

## THE WORK

1. Decide whether `filters/Modal` should now be migrated on the same bridge pattern. It probably
   should, and it is a small change: the public `Modal` becomes `(defn Modal [] [:> Modal-component {}])`
   over `as-component` of a private `ModalView`, no `shell.cljs` edit.
2. EITHER WAY, CORRECT THE DOCSTRING. If the migration happens the claim goes with it. If a reason to
   keep `filters/Modal` as a `reg-view` survives scrutiny, the docstring must state THAT reason and
   not the refuted one. A docstring giving a false technical reason is worse than none — it will stop
   the next reader from doing something that works.

## SCOPE

`filters.cljs` only. Do not widen to other modals; the other four satellites' surfaces are settled.
Check `filters.cljs` is not held by a live worker before starting.

## GATE

Whatever lane covers the filters surface. Note: the node lane CANNOT grade head legality — its
`expand-tree` invokes a fn head, so `[Modal]` and `(Modal)` expand identically. If this migration
lands, the proof that the boundary actually mounts and paints is the browser lane's, and the modal
renders only when OPEN, so the state must be seeded.
close_reason:
Done. PR #9683 merged e07e702ae7a10a024dc3d9a60669520e622496d1, at band 87 with nothing
non-terminal and a clean merge-tree against trunk. +520/-81.

Both halves landed: filters/Modal is now a Fresco boundary behind an as-component bridge, and the
refuted docstring is gone. The premise held -- shell.cljs needed NO edit, which is the claim two
siblings had already refuted the old docstring with.

THE MIGRATION WAS NOT THE SMALL CHANGE THIS BEAD AND MY BRIEF BOTH DESCRIBED, and the reason is
worth carrying. The prescribed shape -- public Modal becomes [:> Modal-component {}] over a private
ModalView -- WOULD HAVE RAISED on the popup's first open. popup-view performed three ambient
@(rf/subscribe ...) reads of its own, and an ambient subscribe is REFUSED inside a boundary render
(:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused), with the refusing extent reaching a parens-called helper too.
They could not simply become rf.fresco/sub in place either, because that refuses OUTSIDE a render
and popup-view has direct callers in two node-lane suites. One read cannot serve both lanes, so the
reads were hoisted and popup-view made pure -- the same hoist, for the same recorded reason, as
settings/view/popup-tree.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT. There was a FIFTH dependent sentence, not four: a comment
at edit_popup.cljs:288-289 claimed a plain-fn head "is legal" there -- true of a Reagent tree, an
ERROR in a Fresco one, and the migration inverts it. And filters.cljs:60 was the ONLY remaining
shell-root modal reg-view at tip (census: 43 defviews against 8 reg-views, none of the eight a
modal), so this closes that class rather than one instance of it.

Proven by sabotage: 7 failures, every one in the two new rows, restored and verified against the
committed blob object with git diff --quiet as a second instrument.

title: self-noise/xray-internal-event? carries the same hardcoded (= :rf/xray) literal rf2-bgol fixed — the trace surface has the same custom-frame blind spot
description:
FOUND BY `frescoframe-a` WHILE FIXING rf2-bgol, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED THERE — different
surface, and widening a bounded repair is how a bounded repair stops being one.

## THE DEFECT

`self-noise/xray-internal-event?` carries the IDENTICAL `(= :rf/xray …)` literal that rf2-bgol was
filed against. So the TRACE surface has the same blind spot: an Xray shell seated at a CUSTOM frame
id is not recognised as the tool, and its own internal events can present as application evidence.

rf2-bgol established the underlying fact and it is not re-argued here: `spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md`
explicitly permits N shells with distinct `:frame-id` values and `ensure-xray-frame!` accepts them,
so a hardcoded `:rf/xray` comparison is wrong wherever it decides own-ness.

## WHY IT IS LESS URGENT THAN rf2-bgol WAS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ITEM

The finder was explicit: this is the BELT-AND-BRACES arm. The emit-site frame gate DOES cover a
seated custom shell, so this literal is a second line of defence rather than the only one. rf2-bgol's
case was different — there the filter was the only thing standing between the tool and the
application's evidence roster.

So: real, same root cause, lower consequence. Do not treat it as urgent, and do not let it be
forgotten either.

## THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS ALREADY LANDED — REUSE IT

PR #9658 solved exactly this for the presentation filter. `fresco-helpers/own-frames` is a SET:
`:rf/xray` unconditionally (it is reserved, and the L1 picker already refuses it as inspectable) PLUS
the shell the panel is inside, taken from `rf/current-frame-id` in the boundary's render and passed
as the query's argument. The pure `.cljc` helper takes the set as DATA — the same shape
`palette/sources` uses for `frame-switcher/internal-frames`.

Read that landing before designing anything. The constraints it honoured apply here too: do not
infer ownership from `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` (a row pins that), keep unknown frames, keep mixed
intents, and add no new configuration surface.

ONE THING THAT MAY NOT TRANSFER: #9658 could not read the frame inside the sub and had to pass it as
a query argument. Measured there — `subs/memo` invokes the body inside `rf.trace/with-handler-scope`
only, `call-with-frame-resolution` binds `*generation*` rather than `*current-frame*`, and no binder
exists in `subs.cljc`, `subs/memo.cljc` or `derivation/**`. Whether the trace path has a frame in
scope is a different question with a different answer; check rather than assuming either way.

## GATE

Whatever lane covers the trace surface. Note what #9658 measured about the node lane, because it
corrects a claim that has been circulating: a `*_dom_cljs_test` namespace is not always merely
LOADED-and-skipped under `npm run test:cljs` — `fresco_live_panel_dom_cljs_test` proved to be ABSENT
FROM `out/node-test.js` ENTIRELY, contrary to that file's own ns docstring. The conclusion is
unchanged (the browser lane is the only lane for a DOM witness) but do not repeat the mechanism
without measuring it on the file in front of you.

If you add a DOM witness, prove it can fail. And heed the green-sabotage lesson from #9658: the
panel's boundary reaches the collector's entry table ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so ticking in the same turn as
the mount recomputes the sub before the census carries it — a witness written that way comes back
green having observed nothing. Poll the census for your own boundary first.

## SEQUENCING

Nobody holds the trace self-noise surface as of filing, but `panels/trace.cljs` is in a live
worker's tree — check for a holder at dispatch time.
close_reason:
CLOSED WITHOUT CODE CHANGE, 2026-09-11. RULED: fold into rf2-bgol's existing revisit trigger.
The defect is REAL and is not disputed; the fix is not worth its cost at this item's size, and the
item as filed is roughly half its true size. Dispatched to `selfnoise-a`, which investigated and
correctly declined to build. No commits, no PR, tracker untouched by the worker.

THE PREMISE HOLDS. `self_noise.cljc:80` still carries `(= :rf/xray (rf.trace/trace-event-frame
event))`. One executable call site, `trace_collector.cljs:307`.

=== WHY NOT FIXED — FOUR MEASURED REASONS, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT

(1) THE EXPOSURE IS NARROWER THAN THE ITEM ASSUMES, AND THIS WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INFERRED.
    `seat-xray-frame!` sets `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` on EVERY seat, custom frame ids included.
    So the emit-site frame gate already covers a shell seated at a custom id, and this literal is
    genuinely the second line of defence the filing said it was — not the only one.

(2) THE ONLY AVAILABLE SOURCE IS A DERIVED PROXY WITH A REAL HOLE. Frames seated by Xray carry
    Xray's IMAGE: `seat-xray-frame!` calls `make-frame {:id … :images [(xray-image)]}` with
    `xray-image-id` = `:rf.xray/image`, readable through the public, tool-sanctioned
    `rf/frame-generation` -> `:rf.gen/images` -> `:rf.image/id` and enumerable via
    `live-frame-ids`. But `seat-xray-frame!` SKIPS `make-frame` when `xray-frame-seated?` is
    true, and that probe is `(some? (live-frame frame-id))` — true for ANY image-loaded frame. A
    shell seated onto a pre-existing frame is therefore never stamped, and the proxy misses it.
    (That same probe was already flagged in the dispatch brief as unsafe for own-ness; the worker
    reached the same conclusion independently, from the other direction.)

(3) IT CANNOT LIVE IN `self_noise.cljc`, SO IT LANDS ON THE HOT PATH. Reading the stamp is a LIVE
    REGISTRY QUERY. `self_noise.cljc` is pure-data and JVM-runnable — a property its docstring
    states three times and on which the whole JVM test corpus for this predicate rests. So the
    set would have to be computed in the collector and passed in as data (the #9658 shape), on

    presentation-filter fix this item was modelled on.

    and is named by neither the bead nor my brief:

read `rf/current-frame-id` in a BOUNDARY's render, and `collect-trace` is a global listener with
no boundary, no render and no component. So the precedent's mechanism is not merely unavailable

title: hygiene: three UNREGISTERED directories in the worktree parent are invisible to every git-worktree-keyed sweep (hicasso-b holds 19 entries)
description:
Found 2026-09-09 during a routine §4 worktree sweep, which enumerates the worktree PARENT directory
rather than `git worktree list` — and that is the only reason these were seen at all.

THREE DIRECTORIES SIT IN `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/` AND ARE NOT REGISTERED
WORKTREES. `git worktree list` does not name any of them, so every instrument keyed on it — the
hygiene loop, the stranded-worker sweep, the reap test — is blind to them by construction:

  _preserved-provenance    4 immediate entries
  hicasso-b               19 immediate entries
  pairing-2026-07-17       1 immediate entry

Counted with `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1`, never bare `ls`, which omits dotfiles (CLAUDE.md
instrument item (i)).

WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT A CLEANUP. `hicasso-b` at 19 entries is the size of a real checkout, and
its name follows the live worker-worktree convention (`<topic>-<letter>`), so it is plausibly an
abandoned worker tree rather than scratch. **Nothing has been deleted and nothing should be until
somebody establishes what each holds.** A worktree that `git worktree list` disowns has no branch
association to read a `git cherry` verdict from, so the standing delete-only-on-`-` rule cannot
even be evaluated — that rule presumes a registered worktree with a branch.

THE SPECIFIC HAZARD IF SOMEBODY REACHES FOR THE OBVIOUS CLEANUP: a worker worktree junctions
`implementation/node_modules` at the mayor checkout's real one, and a recursive delete follows that
junction and empties the mayor's real tree — silently, exit 0, breaking every local build. That is
why `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` exists and unlinks first. **But that script takes a
REGISTERED worktree**, and these are not, so it is not obviously the right instrument either. Check
for a junction with `[ -L ]` before anything recursive touches these paths.

THE WORK: for each of the three, establish (a) whether it contains a git checkout at all, (b) whether
it holds any commit not reachable from `origin/main`, (c) whether it holds uncommitted work, and
(d) whether it carries a junction into shared dependencies. Then propose a disposition per directory
— salvage to a bead, or release. Report; do not delete under this bead's authority.

RELATED, DO NOT DUPLICATE: [[rf2-9gyp]] covers the three FOREIGN-harness worktrees under `~/.grok/`,
which ARE registered and are a different population. [[rf2-bipw]] covers six orphan local BRANCHES,
which have no worktree at all. This bead is the third case: a directory with neither registration
nor a branch pointing at it.
notes:
## INVESTIGATION 2026-09-09 (gitspace) — all four questions answered, READ-ONLY, nothing deleted

Measured 2026-09-09 ~15:00-16:10 AUSEST from a worker worktree; the mayor checkout was read but never
written. **The headline is that (a) collapses the other three: NONE of the three directories is a git
checkout at all.** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fatals in each with `not a git repository (or any of
the parent directories)` — and it does not climb into the mayor repo, because the worktree parent is a
SIBLING of the mayor checkout, not a child. So there is no HEAD, no branch, no index and no reflog in
any of them, which is why `git worktree list` disowns them: they were never registered because they are
not worktrees. The bead's framing — "a directory with neither registration nor a branch pointing at it"
— is exactly right, and the reason is that they are plain directories.

That makes (b) "does it hold any commit not reachable from origin/main" VACUOUS for all three: no
repository, no commits. It also makes (c) "uncommitted work" the wrong question as posed — everything in
all three is uncommitted in the trivial sense that nothing is under version control — so I replaced it
with the question that actually decides disposition: **is the CONTENT reachable from git anyway?**

**(d) THE JUNCTION HAZARD IS ABSENT, and I checked it first, before anything recursive.**
`find <dir> -type l` reads **0** across all three, and `implementation/node_modules` does not exist in
any of them (`[ -L ]` false, `[ -e ]` false). So the recursive-delete-follows-junction hazard the bead
raises does not apply to this population. Counted with `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1`, never bare `ls`.

### The three, measured

| Directory | What it is | Size | Age | Unique content? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_preserved-provenance` | 82 files (42 `.json` + 40 `.log`) in 4 subdirs: `ladder-ymi6j`, `-A`, `-confirm`, `-refused`. Raw per-run benchmark output from the hicasso candidate-clock band ladder | 11.1 MB | all mtimes within a 2-second burst on 2026-08-02 09:39:3x | **YES — and it is the only copy. See below.** |
| `hicasso-b` | A .git-less scratch COPY of the repo used to run a build: 45,757 of its 49,833 files are `implementation/out/` shadow-cljs output, plus `site/` (mkdocs output) and `__pycache__`. No `docs/`, no `examples/`, no `bench/`, no `adapters/`, no `.github/`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no `.beads/` | 3,438 non-build files | **2026-09-07 19:49-22:03, i.e. TWO DAYS OLD, not abandoned-in-July** | **Effectively no — 3,433 of 3,438 are byte-identical to committed blobs; of the 5 that are not, 4 are build caches and 1 is STALE. See below.** |
| `pairing-2026-07-17` | 3 markdown files, `docs/core/{events,hiccup,introduction}.md`, nothing else | 15.4 KB | mtimes 2026-08-07 16:46 — these do NOT match the 2026-07-17 in the directory name | **YES — all three blobs are ABSENT from the object store** |

### `_preserved-provenance` — DO NOT RELEASE. It is the physical referent of a claim in a committed doc.

This is the one finding I did not expect and it inverts the obvious disposition.

  was removed in the freehand retirement — verified by reading it back (needs `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, since
  ref and path both carry slashes; instrument item (d)).
* The **raw per-run files were never committed and never could be**: `bench/hicasso/.gitignore` line 2 is
  `out/`, and `git check-ignore -v` confirms it matches `bench/hicasso/out/ladder-ymi6j/L0-r1.json`. So

title: [template] two test lookups derive a framework root as implementation/adapters/<substrate> — both break on Hicasso (implementation/hicasso); repair before the rf2-8urba variant cell
description:
LATENT TRAP. Two independent test lookups in `tools/template/test/` derive a
framework source root from the substrate NAME by string convention. Both are
correct for `:reagent` and `:uix` and both BREAK on `:hicasso`, which lives at
`implementation/hicasso`, not `implementation/adapters/hicasso`. They fire the
moment the rf2-8urba variant cell is added — before any of its API usage is
evaluated — so a worker briefed only on "add a registry entry, a case arm and
three resource files" will hit them cold.

MEASURED 2026-09-09 at HEAD, in this checkout:

  1. `emitted_test_run_test.clj` (the behavioural runner's local-root rewrite,
     ~:130-131):
         adapter-coord (symbol "day8" (str "re-frame2-" (name substrate)))
         adapter-path  (str "implementation/adapters/" (name substrate))
     For `:hicasso` the COORDINATE it builds is right and the PATH is wrong.
     Confirmed: `implementation/adapters/hicasso` does not exist;
     `implementation/hicasso` does; `implementation/adapters/{uix,reagent}` do.
     The failure mode is the dangerous one — a `:local/root` pointing at a
     directory that is absent, or worse a smoke that silently exercises the
     wrong package.

  2. `template_emission_test.clj`'s `framework-ns-file` (~:108-130) — the
     static framework-surface drift audit, a SEPARATE lookup the dossier
     missed and the Codex review caught. It resolves a `re-frame.*` namespace
     to a file under `implementation/core/src/re_frame/**`, plus, only for a
     name starting `re-frame.adapter.`, a leaf whitelisted as
     `#{"uix" "reagent" "reagent-slim"}` under `implementation/adapters/`.
     `re-frame.hicasso` and `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` match NEITHER arm, so
     the lookup answers nil and `audit-framework-symbol!` (~:220-229) takes its
     `(is false ...)` arm: "... but no source file was found under
     implementation/". A hard fail, not a skip.

WHAT TO DO
  Replace the string convention in BOTH places with an explicit
  substrate -> local-root (and namespace-family -> source-root) map, so a
  substrate whose package does not sit under `implementation/adapters/` is
  expressible. Land this BEFORE the `:hicasso` cell, not with it: the repair is
  independently correct and testable against the two substrates that exist
  today, and doing it first keeps the variant PR to the variant.

FENCE: `tools/template/test/**`. Nothing outside it.

PROVENANCE: surfaced by the rf2-8urba decision review (2026-09-09). Lookup 1 was
already recorded inside rf2-8urba's 2026-09-02 ruling notes as a hard
requirement, but was never given a bead of its own; lookup 2 was not recorded
anywhere. Both verified at source this session. This is a prerequisite for
rf2-8urba, which is itself held behind the publication chain (rf2-kmqx3) — but
this repair is NOT gated on publication and can land at any time.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #9543 alongside [[rf2-j908]], merged at band 87 on all five clauses (the full grading is on rf2-j908's close reason; head oid `2caf3863ef`, 0 failure-or-cancelled, 0 non-terminal, merge-tree rc=0).

Both test lookups derived a framework root as `implementation/adapters/<substrate>`, which breaks on Hicasso (`implementation/hicasso`). Both line references held on verification. Each string convention is now an explicit map, so the Hicasso case is expressed rather than computed.

## A SECOND DEFECT SURFACED THAT NOBODY BRIEFED — AND IT IS THE MORE INTERESTING ONE

The whitelist's `reagent-slim` arm **could only ever have answered nil**: it spelled the file with the NAMESPACE's dash where disk carries the ClojureScript UNDERSCORE. It had never fired, and nothing noticed, only because no emission requires that namespace — so the arm sat there looking like coverage while matching nothing.

That is this project's standing reassuring-zero class reached through a new door: not a search returning zero, but a LOOKUP ARM returning nil, which the caller's else-branch absorbs silently. Deriving the path once from the namespace fixes it, and a new test pins it so the two spellings cannot drift apart again.

## SCOPE HELD

No `:hicasso` variant cell, no registry entry, no resource file — that is [[rf2-8urba]], for which this bead was the stated prerequisite. It is now unblocked on this axis.

title: docs(claude): catalogue the silent 'bd list --status' last-flag-wins truncation (read 3 where the truth was 24)
description:
`CLAUDE.md`'s instrument catalogue (§ Workflow, the lettered list of "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport
on this machine") is missing a hazard that was hit for real on 2026-09-09 and that fits its stated
subject exactly. Add one lettered item.

## THE DEFECT

**A repeated `--status` flag on `bd list` does NOT union the statuses — the LAST occurrence silently
wins, and every earlier one is discarded with no error, no warning and exit 0.**

Measured on this tree 2026-09-09, both directions, with the union as control:

    bd list --status open --limit 0 --json | jq length                    ->  23
    bd list --status deferred --limit 0 --json | jq length                ->   3
    bd list --status open --status deferred --limit 0 --json | jq length  ->   3   (== deferred alone)
    bd list --status deferred --status open --limit 0 --json | jq length  ->  23   (== open alone)
    bd list --status open,deferred --limit 0 --json | jq length           ->  26   (the true union, 23+3)

**The comma-separated form is the one that unions.** Reversing the flag order flips the answer to the
other single status, which is what makes "last wins" the diagnosis rather than "one of them is
ignored".

## WHY IT BELONGS IN THAT LIST SPECIFICALLY

The list's own opening says each entry "hands back a clean-looking answer, so nothing on screen
betrays it, and every one of them was reached by a worker taking the obvious route". This qualifies on
every clause:

  * **Silent.** Exit code **0**, **0 bytes** on stderr. Nothing to read.
  * **Plausible.** It returns a well-formed JSON array of real beads. Nothing about the output says it
    is a fraction of the answer.
  * **Obvious route.** Repeating a flag to widen a filter is the natural spelling, and it is how the
    four non-terminal statuses were first asked for.
  * **FAILS IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION**, which is the property that makes it dangerous rather than
    merely wrong: a SHORTER backlog reads as less work. It returned **3** where the truth was **24** —
    a mayor who trusted it would have reported a near-empty backlog and re-read 3 of 24 beads while
    believing the reread complete.

**It was caught only by a control**, not by the output: the same tick's status tally read
`deferred=3 open=21`, and 3 != 24 is the only thing on screen that disagreed.

**And note the list's own preamble licenses this addition** — "THE LETTERS BELOW ARE LABELS, NOT A
CENSUS — this list grows", with a standing warning that a count in its opening sentence goes stale
first. So add a letter; do not renumber, and do not write a total anywhere.

## SCOPE — ONE ITEM, AND THE GUARD IS ONE LINE

The guard: **use the comma form (`--status a,b,c`), or filter with `jq` over an unfiltered
`bd list --limit 0 --json`, and control any status census against a second spelling before believing
it.** Worth noting inside the item that `bd list` ALREADY excludes closed beads by default, so
`bd list --limit 0 --json | jq '[.[]|select(.status!="closed")]|length'` is an independent instrument
that agreed at 24.

Do NOT expand this into a survey of every bd flag. One item, its measurement, its guard.

## THE TRAP IN EDITING THIS PARTICULAR FILE — READ IT BEFORE YOU START

`CLAUDE.md` instrument item (e) records, about editing `CLAUDE.md` itself: writing an entry once
"inserted four REAL carriage returns where the escape was meant literally, git reclassified
`CLAUDE.md` from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, stopped normalising it, and staged **156 changed lines** for a
one-clause edit." **After editing, confirm the file's total CR count equals its CRLF count**, and
confirm `git diff --stat` shows a change proportional to what you wrote rather than the whole file.

title: spec: two sites describe the hand-emitted spawn counter as keyed by <machine-id>; the code and spec/005 both say <id-prefix>
description:
Two normative sites describe the HAND-EMITTED `:rf.machine/spawn` counter as keyed by `<machine-id>`. The implementation has always keyed it by `(or (:id-prefix args) (:machine-id args))`, and `spec/005` already says so — so the spec contradicts itself and the code is right.

* `spec/Conventions.md:616` — the app-db/runtime-db key table row for `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-counter]` calls it a "Per-frame **hand-emitted-spawn fallback counter** — `{<machine-id> <int>}`".
* `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2934` — the schema's trailing comment on `[:spawn-counter {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword :int]]` reads "per-machine-id integer counter for hand-emitted `:rf.machine/spawn` fxs".

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:1082` binds `machine-id-for-alloc (or (:id-prefix args) (:machine-id args))` — an `:id-prefix` supplied to a hand-emitted spawn selects the counter bucket, and `:machine-id` is only the FALLBACK. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2826` already states the counter lives at `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-counter <id-prefix>]`. So this is a two-line correction to bring two stale descriptions in line with the spec's own primary statement and with the code.

Surfaced by the rf2-r9ey worker (PR #9535) as a side-finding it correctly declined to sweep, since both files are hot-zone one-touchers it did not hold. **That report named FOUR sites; only these TWO are wrong.** I checked each before filing: `spec/Conventions.md:641` and `:1048` describe `:rf/spawn-counter`, the DECLARATIVE snapshot counter — a different counter — and both correctly say `{<id-prefix> <int>}`. ## SCOPE

Prose only, two lines, no code and no schema shape change (`[:map-of :keyword :int]` is already correct — only its comment is wrong). Both files are HOT-ZONE one-touchers and must be sequenced against anything else holding them. Unrelated to rf2-1sip's option (e), which remains unruled.

title: Adopt a 2-4KB .beads/PRIME.md, plus the boundary-gate allow-list entry that lets it exist (rf2-ornb ruling (b))
description:
RULED by rf2-ornb 2026-09-08. Adopt a short `.beads/PRIME.md` overriding `bd prime`'s output. EDITORIAL TARGET 2-4 KB — not a ceiling to build up to.

WHY. `bd prime` emits 1,858,076 bytes, 99.71% of it ~950 memory bodies, on every SessionStart and PreCompact from tracked `.claude/settings.json`. The host's preview keeps HEAD AND TAIL — verified live, the workflow header (byte 189) and SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL (~byte 1,830,274) both arrive — so the memory bodies in the middle are serialised and discarded. 459 recorded hook runs: p50 765 ms, p90 8.2 s, p99 20.1 s, max 26.6 s, 17.7 min of blocking wall-clock, plus 857 MB of persisted hook-output files. THE OVERRIDE IS ABOUT ELIMINATING THAT WASTED WORK AND CHOOSING DELIBERATELY WHAT RIDES IN THE WINDOW. DO NOT SELL IT ON LATENCY: the severe stalls correlate with MISSING memory output (all 40 intact memory-free runs took >10 s; only 4 of 421 large-output runs did), so reduced work is a reasonable expectation, not a promise.

CONTENTS, workflow-context-FIRST (the ordering `bd prime` gets backwards):
  1. A PROVENANCE LINE, non-negotiable: this file is advice from a tool; CLAUDE.md is the repo's committed instruction and wins where they differ; do not cite this file as "CLAUDE.md says". (`provenance-trap-at-session-start-the-bd-prime` records that confusion happening once already, and a short confident file is MORE mistakable for CLAUDE.md than 1.8MB of noise ever was.)
  2. Session-close protocol and the core `bd` rules (bd for all tracking, no TodoWrite/markdown TODOs, bead before code, `--append-notes` never `--notes`).
  3. Finding-work commands, with `bd memories <topic>` and `bd recall <key>` PROMINENT.
  4. One paragraph: ~950 memories exist, are deliberately NOT injected, and are expected to be searched before any non-trivial census, sweep or worktree operation.
  5. Pointers only — one line of substance plus a `bd recall <key>` — for the few silent-failure hazards CLAUDE.md does NOT already carry.

SELECTION RULE: a memory earns an always-on line ONLY IF not knowing it produces a confident wrong answer or destroys state, AND the failure is silent, AND CLAUDE.md does not already say it. The third clause is what keeps the file at 2-4 KB.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED: the expanding shell-trap catalogue, the "search before every non-trivial operation" mandate, and the universal positive-control obligation. Already in CLAUDE.md; duplicating them makes a third competing source of truth. Do not copy the command reference wholesale. Do not build to a 28 KB budget — that figure was derived from the minimum of observed OVERSIZED results, which bounds the wrong end; the documented cap is 10,000 chars for hook JSON output strings, and Codex hosts preview ~2,500 tokens head-and-tail.

FOUR FILES, ONE PR. A tree carrying the file without the allow-list entry reds the boundary gate on every subsequent PR that touches it.
  1. `.beads/PRIME.md`
  2. `scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh` — add `.beads/PRIME.md) return 0 ;;` to `rf2_beads_is_permitted_path` and update its permission diagnostic. VERIFIED 2026-09-08: the classifier is an ENUMERATED allow-list (README.md, config.yaml, .gitignore, hooks/*) and `.beads/PRIME.md` falls to the `.beads/*) return 1` arm, so it is refused today. The CI arm runs on every PR at `.github/workflows/test.yml:1314` and `:1325`.
  3. CLAUDE.md — the Beads-durability enumeration of human-authored config.
  4. `scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh` — a case pinning the new permission. The file contains ZERO occurrences of `PRIME` today.

DECIDED: add the allow-list entry and let the file go through normal PR review. The alternative reading — leave the gate alone so `PRIME.md` is structurally mayor-only — is REJECTED: a gate exception is an implementation detail to correct, not a permission model to invent.

VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON IT. `bd prime --help` documents the override ("Place a .beads/PRIME.md file in the local clone or resolved workspace to override the default output entirely"), but IT HAS NOT BEEN OBSERVED FIRING. Verify override selection in an ISOLATED FIXTURE first, then inspect real delivery on each intended host at both SessionStart and SessionStart:compact: complete text present, no spill into a persisted-output preview, `bd memories`/`bd recall` usable, latency OBSERVED AND REPORTED rather than promised. Run the boundary tests with absolute paths and negative controls. `bd prime --export` dumps the current default and is the re-sync source when `bd` is upgraded.

HONEST COST, to be accepted knowingly: curation becomes a standing obligation (a memory written next week is invisible unless promoted); the override replaces `bd`'s default output ENTIRELY, so future upstream improvements must be re-synced by hand; and a third instruction source joins CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.

OUT OF SCOPE: no memory deletion or pruning; the hook command in `.claude/settings.json` is unchanged and the redundant PreCompact invocation is not removed until delivery is verified; `bd prime --mcp` is rejected as an alternative (~193 KB, still oversized, and non-deterministic here — 191,440 bytes on 8 of 10 runs, 1,240 on 2); no upstream `bd` issue is filed by this bead.
acceptance_criteria: One PR carrying four files: .beads/PRIME.md (2-4KB, workflow context first, provenance line, memories-are-searchable paragraph, pointers only); the .beads/PRIME.md arm in rf2_beads_is_permitted_path plus its diagnostic; the CLAUDE.md Beads-durability enumeration; a pin in scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh. Override verified to actually fire in an isolated fixture BEFORE merge, then real SessionStart and SessionStart:compact delivery inspected on each intended host — complete text, no preview spill, bd memories/bd recall usable, latency reported not promised. Boundary tests run with absolute paths and negative controls.

title: Remove the derivable :var-count from the generated spec/api-manifest.edn (RULED: no merge-policy change, no new gate)
description:
RULED 2026-09-08. The menu of options is closed; this is now one small code-only PR.

DO: remove the `:var-count` field from `spec/api-manifest.edn`. It restates the file's own
row count, so a generated file states the same fact twice — and two independent PRs each
deleting a different public var compute the SAME new value, producing a textually identical
edit that git merges without conflict while both row deletions survive. Delete the field and
that particular silent merge cannot happen.

DO NOT: change any merge policy under this bead — no `strict_required_status_checks_policy`,
no merge queue, no branch-protection edit. No new CI job, no red-trunk alerting. And do NOT
re-dispatch the lint.yml concurrency fix: it already shipped as PR #9494 / `cb703356f1`
(rf2-vktd, closed).

WHY THIS IS SMALL. Measured at HEAD `432a93da15`: `spec/API.md` carries no var count of any
kind, so this drift never reached the surface an app author reads. Its whole cost is
operational. Detection is already owned by the existing `api-manifest` lint job, whose
`check!` compares the COMPLETE rendered file — so it catches a wrong `:var-count` even when
every row is right — and PR #9494 restored that job's trunk reliability hours before this
ruling. Nothing new is needed.

GENERATED vs CURATED — this bounds the diff. `spec/api-manifest.edn` is GENERATED OUTPUT
ONLY and is the only file carrying the field; regenerate it, never hand-edit it.
`spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` is CURATED INPUT (hand-edited by design) and carries no
derived count. `spec/API.md` is curated prose and carries no count. NEITHER CURATED FILE IS
TOUCHED. All three still ride one lint surface, so the PR is HOT-ZONE — sequence it against
any other manifest work in flight.

THE DIFF (details, measurements and acceptance in the RULING note below):
  1. `gen.clj:1132` — delete `:var-count    (count rows)` from `build-manifest`'s `:meta`.
  2. `gen.clj:1210` and `:1231` — the two console messages take `(count (:vars ...))`
     instead. The human-facing count stays on screen; it just stops being persisted.
  3. Stale comments at `gen.clj:264`, `:945`, `:1058`; docstring at `gen_test.clj:14`.
  4. Regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn`.

RETAINED DELIBERATELY: `check!`'s whole-file comparison (equal counts cannot establish
correct var identities, kinds or classifications), and `tags-column-paired-floor` in
error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj — same defect class, but it records an
independently reviewed expectation and deriving it from the corpus under test would erase
its regression signal.

title: [tools/story] Report text clipboard completion only after a successful write
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:521-526 calls review-dialog/copy-to-clipboard! then immediately mark-copied! for Copy URL, Copy EDN and Copy static-build command (:737/:748/:776). review_dialog.cljc:279-288 no-ops without navigator.clipboard, returns nil unconditionally, and does not observe a rejected writeText Promise. Thus a normal permission denial, missing clipboard API (for example an insecure served dev host), or delayed write displays copied success without a completed clipboard update; asynchronous rejection is also unhandled. The dialog's screenshot path :589-634 already demonstrates truthful async completion and a visible unavailable/error state.

Expected: success only after fulfillment; unavailable/rejected writes leave no false success and give usable feedback/manual-copy affordance. Smallest repair: expose/await a completion result from the existing shared copy shim and use the existing mark-error! path for text commands. Preserve the manual snippet fallback and trusted-local unredacted sharing policy; do not add privacy gating. Historical screenshot rf2-ehc5bq is referenced by source but is absent from current tracker; this is the independent text-copy path, not its repaired image path. Inspected snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; latest mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant source drift. Active+closed title/description and relevant Story memory searches found no matching owner. Source-only causal evidence; no browser/CLJS build or shared suite executed.
acceptance_criteria: With absent clipboard API or rejected writeText, Copy URL/EDN/command do not show copied and present failure/manual-copy feedback. With a pending Promise, no success yet; on fulfillment, success appears. Rejections are handled and screenshot behavior remains unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9378. share.cljs copy-text! called review-dialog/copy-to-clipboard! then mark-copied! on the next line for all three text commands; the shim no-opped without navigator.clipboard, returned nil unconditionally and never observed a rejected writeText. The shared shim now resolves a boolean OUTCOME (true only on fulfilment; false on absent API, throw, or rejection) and never rejects, so the eight other fire-and-forget :on-copy callers stay safe from unhandled rejections; copy-text! awaits it and routes failure through the existing mark-error! path. Manual-copy affordance and the trusted-local unredacted sharing policy untouched, no privacy gating, screenshot path unchanged. CAVEAT: the four failing-first tests are CLJS (share.cljs is Reagent/DOM-only; the shim body is a :cljs reader branch) and the only runner is the consolidated npm run test:cljs node-test build, which the dispatch excluded on cost — so they were NOT run locally, red or green. CI's cljs job is the first check to read. tools/story JVM suite exit 0, 1903 tests / 7010 assertions, covering that review_dialog.cljc still reads/compiles on the JVM arm.

title: loops.md clause 5 states outright that a job-name addition IS a new required check — false for a workflow no PR runs
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the claudemd-a worker while landing rf2-e3ak (PR #9283), which added the same qualification to CLAUDE.md's trap (a). The worker was fenced out of loops.md and reported this rather than editing it.

THE DEFECT. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:231-232, inside clause 5, states outright:

  "four changed lines that add a job name with its own condition ARE a new required check."

That is FALSE for a job added to a workflow that no pull request runs. Clause 5's general instruction gestures at the right idea, but the ENUMERATED BULLET A READER LANDS ON gives the wrong verdict, and an enumerated example beats a general instruction every time — which is exactly why this needs fixing rather than leaving to the general text.

Clause 5 currently enumerates THREE cases (cache steps / job-name addition / display-name rename). This is a FOURTH it does not carry: a job key added to a workflow whose `on:` block has no `pull_request` trigger contributes NO check to any PR rollup, so the check set is unchanged and the merge should proceed.

MEASURED, 2026-09-05, on PR #9277: merge-base b86310b3c1 to origin/main gave jobkeys=1; the key was `mcp-live-windows`, added to .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml, whose `on:` is `schedule: cron "17 15 * * *"` plus `workflow_dispatch` and nothing else. Corroborated empirically: the band was 87 on the four PRs merged after that job landed, and #9277's own rollup was 87. The claudemd-a worker added a further measurement worth carrying over: SEVEN OF THE ELEVEN workflow files in this repo carry no `pull_request` trigger at all, so this is the common case rather than an exotic one.

DIRECTION MATTERS AND MUST BE STATED. This case fails CLOSED — it flags a merge that should proceed — whereas the traps CLAUDE.md enumerates all fail OPEN. That asymmetry is why the CLAUDE.md fix was written as a QUALIFICATION to trap (a) rather than a fourth trap: adding it as a peer would have falsified that bullet's framing sentence ("each fails OPEN"). Check whether loops.md clause 5 has the same framing constraint before choosing where to put it.

THE FOLLOW-UP COMMAND THAT DISCHARGES IT, already landed in CLAUDE.md and worth mirroring: the `+++ b/<path>` lines are in the same diff, so
  git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -E '^(\+\+\+|\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$)'
names both the count and the file, after which you read that file's `on:` block.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE TWO-SPACE RULE while editing. The job-key discriminator needs TWO LEADING SPACES because job keys nest under `jobs:`; the unindented form matches nothing and reads a reassuring zero. That is a separate, fail-open hazard and it stays exactly as written.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: re-read loops.md clause 5 at tip and confirm the quoted sentence is still there and still at :231-232 — CLAUDE.md and the method docs both moved several times on 2026-09-05. Also read CLAUDE.md's trap (a) as landed by PR #9283 and make the two agree without restating one in the other; CLAUDE.md's own text says it is the CLI concretion and does not restate loops.md clause 5.

FENCE. IN: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md ONLY. OUT: CLAUDE.md (already fixed by #9283), docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, .github/workflows/** (a peer holds it).
notes:
2026-09-05 — PR #9299 opened (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9299), ready for review, not draft. Bead left in_progress; not closed.

VERIFIED AT TIP BEFORE EDITING. The quoted sentence was still present and still at loops.md:231-232, unchanged by the 2026-09-05 method-doc churn. Clause 5's list still held exactly two bullets (cache steps / job-name addition), with the display-name rename carried as prose below it.

FRAMING-CONSTRAINT FINDING — the question the item asked. Clause 5 has NO analogue of CLAUDE.md trap (a)'s "each fails OPEN" framing. Its framing sentence is "The count alone gives opposite verdicts for the same number", and its two bullets already point in OPPOSITE directions (bullet 1 merges, bullet 2 blocks), so a fail-closed case falsifies nothing. Clause 4 immediately above even bolds one of its own two traps as failing "closed", so the document already has a house spelling for direction. The constraint that DID bind is a different one and is a count word, not a direction: the paragraph under the list reads "A display-name rename is a third case and reads like the second" — two ordinal references bound to the two bullets, BOTH of which a third bullet inserted into the list would have silently falsified. Combined with the item's own thesis (the enumerated bullet is what a skimming reader acts on, so a separate case leaves the wrong verdict where it is read), the correction went ON bullet 2 as a qualification. Same placement as the CLAUDE.md fix, reached by a different route.

BOUNDARY BETWEEN THE TWO DOCUMENTS. loops.md declares the division itself at its head (:10-16): "This page is the generic body; your copy pins the concrete values ... your gate command, your tracker CLI, your hot-zone file list ... belong in that repository's agent-instructions file." CLAUDE.md's trap (a) mirrors it from the other side, calling itself the CLI concretion. So loops.md got the discharge at ITS altitude — "the diff that gave you the count also names the files it came from, so read which events run each" — and the grep command, the paths, the PR numbers, the 7-of-11 count and the test.yml carve-out all stayed in CLAUDE.md. Measured before writing: loops.md carries ZERO fenced code blocks over 1703 lines, and its 50 inline code spans are file names and generic literals, never a recipe; "pull request", "pull_request" and "GitHub" each appear zero times (the page says "change"). The edit therefore adds no backtick, no fence, no command and no repo-specific path. The TWO-SPACE job-key discriminator was not touched or narrowed.

INSTRUMENT CORRECTION worth recording. A first pass measured "0 backticks in loops.md" using Bash grep with an escaped backtick; the escape was eaten and the count came back as the LINE COUNT on one form and 0 on another. Both were false. Re-measured with a controlled Python character count: 50 backticks, 0 fence lines, control on CLAUDE.md read 1036. This is the CLAUDE.md "false zero / read stderr, prefer the ripgrep-backed tool" hazard reached through a shell escape rather than a flag pair.

title: reagent-slim: parity_cljs_test carries its own 22-name canonicalisation set, now six short
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 from two findings the rf2-4hjw worker recorded in its close reason and deliberately did NOT file, leaving the call to the mayor. Both are real; both are small; neither blocks anything.

FINDING (b), THE DRIFT SURFACE — the reason this bead exists. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/.../parity_cljs_test.cljs` maintains its OWN 22-name canonicalisation set, independent of the production roster PR #9224 just widened. It is now six names short. The worker left it alone rather than silently widening it, which was right — but it is a second copy of a list that has already drifted once, and the drift is invisible because the test's corpus does not exercise the missing six. That is the same shape as the defect this campaign keeps finding: a check that reads as present and inspects nothing.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE, and it is a design call not a mechanical one: should that set exist at all? PR #9224's new `boolean_attr_react_parity_cljs_test.cljs` derives its candidate names from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` at RUN TIME under `:node-test`, so a react-dom bump reds with nothing to regenerate. If the older test can read from the same source, the hand-maintained set disappears rather than being corrected — which is the better outcome and the one to try first. If it genuinely needs a fixed corpus for a different reason, say why and leave a note beside the set so the next reader knows it is deliberate.

FINDING (a), SEPARATE AND SMALLER, worth doing in the same PR since it is the same file family: `{:disabled ""}` and `{:disabled 0}` emit the bare attribute name where react-dom omits it. This is a CLJS/JS truthiness gap — `""` and `0` are falsey in JS and truthy in Clojure — is PRE-EXISTING rather than introduced by #9224, and is invisible to a boolean-only probe because neither value is a boolean. Confirm it still reproduces before fixing; the emitter changed in #9224.

WHY P3 AND NOT HIGHER: the production path is now correct for booleans after #9224, so this is about a test's maintainability and one edge case with non-boolean falsey values. Real, not urgent.

CONTEXT WORTH INHERITING. `reagent2.dom.server` is a pure-CLJS serializer that exists specifically to avoid pulling in `react-dom/server` (~22-27 KB gzip), so its roster IS the entire boolean implementation on that path — nothing upstream classifies. And `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` hydrates exactly this markup, so a divergence here is the attribute-only hydration mismatch that spec/011 records React as NOT guaranteeing to patch. That is why these rosters matter more than they look.

ONE TRAP THE #9224 WORKER HIT AND DOCUMENTED, which will bite anyone re-deriving names from react-dom: react-dom LOWERCASES `autoFocus`, so a case-sensitive read of React's own bytes reports it absent. Its probe reddened on itself before it reddened on the code. The `react-class` docstring in the new test records this.
notes:
Post-merge audit — PR #9224 confirmation on merged commit `cb02d7476dcfd68cac91a8d7bd7e1b2d006d0c39`: follow-up (a) still reproduces exactly, so this open bead remains the owner and no duplicate was filed. In `reagent2/dom/server.cljs:741-789`, only nil and boolean false take omission paths; the non-boolean arm classifies a presence name and emits it unconditionally. Because `""` and `0` are truthy in ClojureScript, `{:disabled ""}` and `{:disabled 0}` therefore emit bare `disabled`. The installed react-dom 19.2.0 independently renders both as `<button>x</button>` (no attribute), while `true` and `"yes"` render `disabled=""`. The main PR fix for actual boolean values and its React-derived roster probe are otherwise sound. This is the bounded truthiness/parity residue already described here; retain the same owner alongside the stale parity canonicalisation set.
PR #9244 audit residual (2026-09-05): presence-value-truthy? claims strings and numbers are the only JS-falsey cases after nil/false/undefined, then returns true for every non-string/non-number. That omits the standard primitive BigInt zero. The installed react-dom/server 19.2.0 renders disabled=0n as <button>x</button> and disabled=1n as <button disabled="">x</button>. Compiled cljs.core/number? expands to typeof x === "number", so (js/BigInt 0) reaches the helper's :else true and reagent-slim emits a spurious bare disabled. The new parity matrix covers ""/0 and "0"/1 but not 0n/1n.

Bounded fix: implement actual JavaScript Boolean coercion (for example the Closure-safe js/Boolean call) instead of maintaining a partial falsey roster, and add 0n/1n to the live React parity and raw-byte assertions. Preserve the sound name-roster removal and all other attribute classes. If BigInt is deliberately unsupported as an attribute value, reject it consistently and narrow the documented “JavaScript truthiness” contract rather than silently diverging.
PR #9268 (2026-09-05). CENSUS DELTA — the headline count is stale: parity_cljs_test.cljs carries NO canonicalisation roster at tip (7eb631e30e). 22 -> 0, not "six short". Commit e21b733d53 removed it and replaced it with a class rule (an empty attribute value collapses to the bare name, whatever the name), which is the outcome this bead asked for first. Production rosters at tip: presence-attributes 28, stringifying-attributes 8, overloaded-boolean-attributes 2. A set-literal search under reagent-slim/test/ returns zero and the same pattern returns six hits under reagent-slim/src/, so the zero is real. Finding (a) ("" and 0) was fixed by the same commit. What this PR answers is the newest note, the PR #9244 audit residual: presence-value-truthy? enumerated the JS-falsey values and returned true for the rest, and cljs.core/number? compiles to typeof x === "number", so a bigint zero fell through and emitted a bare disabled. Replaced the roster with js/Boolean — the coercion react-dom itself performs — and turned the parity corpus into a labelled table spanning the falsey-capable primitive TYPES (string, number, bigint), each with a falsey member and a truthy neighbour, checked against live react-dom and pinned again on raw bytes; NaN on the bytes alone, since React logs a warning for it. RED/GREEN measured against the installed react-dom 19.2.0 as oracle with both predicates transcribed to JS: old RED on the bigint-zero row and green on the other six, new GREEN on all seven, and only that row moves. Left alone: overloaded/ordinary attribute paths already agree with react-dom for a bigint (attribute-value-string str-ifies, react-dom stringifies). GATES: reagent-slim clojure -M:test exit 0 (10/10); clj-kondo --fail-level error exit 0. The CLJS parity suite runs in CI (the shadow-cljs gates were fenced off by the dispatch).
close_reason: presence-value-truthy? now calls js/Boolean (the coercion react-dom performs) and the parity corpus spans the falsey-capable primitive types incl. 0n/1n — PR #9268. The 22-name roster the title names was already gone at tip (22 -> 0, e21b733d53).
