Read the ruling on rf2-7ngc for the reasoning; everything needed to act safely is repeated here.

WHY THE STANDING DELETE TEST REFUSES THESE AND WHY THE RULING OVERRIDES IT. loops.md section Branches deletes only on git cherry reading "-" for every commit (proof of containment); "+" is only the absence of proof. Both branches read "+" and neither has a MERGED PR, so no hygiene tick will ever delete them on its own. The ruling authorises deletion on containment proofs stronger than cherry:

worker/liveframe-ma8r (remote only; no local ref). Tip c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58 = scratch probe d923a84356 + its exact revert. The branch tip's TREE OBJECT equals its merge-base's tree object (58818f8fd2923731cc7e5df87911b06e00041225 on both sides at merge-base bb07ef531d): the complete snapshots are identical, so there is no change that could be unmerged. PR #9000 CLOSED not merged, its closing comment holds the no-code diagnosis; rf2-ma8r is closed. GitHub still retains refs/pull/9000/head = c3924bece3 (verified 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST), so even the probe text stays reachable, though the ruling does not depend on that.

worker/retire-delete (remote + local ref). Tip 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, one PARTIAL commit from parent 2ab9a42843 changing 273 paths (256 D + 17 M). Its content landed via the ATOMIC commit ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 (PR #8322, merged 2026-08-16), which is an ancestor of origin/main. Measured 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST at origin/main df66b1679496: all 17 modified paths have blob oid at 87571272d8 EQUAL to blob oid at ef3131f4a2 (17/17), and all 256 deleted paths are absent from origin/main (0 present). Main once held the branch's exact postimage for every modified path and holds none of the deleted ones: complete containment. This comparison is against a FIXED commit, so it does not go stale as main moves (rf2-lafmr's 2026-09-03 note recorded the tip-relative form going stale; this form ends that cycle).

worker/receipts-hic081 is NOT in scope: KEEP under rf2-lafmr (release condition: counts-only capability receipts implemented on main with both owed witnesses discharged, or the design explicitly abandoned). Its tip must still read ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c after you are done.

THE DRILL (mayor checkout; read-only until the push). Any deviation from an expected value means STOP and re-read the ruling; do not delete.

1. date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"
2. git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete worker/receipts-hic081
   expect exactly: c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58, 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c. A moved tip means new commits the ruling never saw: review them independently, do not delete.

   mb=$(git merge-base origin/main c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58); git rev-parse "$mb^{tree}" "c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58^{tree}"
   expect two identical lines.
5. retire-delete containment against the fixed atomic commit:
   git merge-base --is-ancestor ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 origin/main && echo ancestor-ok
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="M"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do [ "$(git rev-parse "87571272d8:$p")" = "$(git rev-parse "ef3131f4a2:$p")" ] || echo "DIFFERS $p"; done
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="D"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do git cat-file -e "origin/main:$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "PRESENT $p"; done
   expect ancestor-ok and no DIFFERS/PRESENT lines.
6. Delete, lease-protected so a concurrently moved tip turns the push into a refusal rather than deleting new work:

   (Equivalent without the lease, only after step 2 read clean seconds earlier: git push origin --delete worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete)

   [ "$(git rev-parse refs/heads/worker/retire-delete)" = "87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4" ] && git branch -D worker/retire-delete
   (git branch -d would refuse: the branch is not an ancestor of main; the containment proof is step 5.)

title: routing: the bench route-link comment still names the retired :routing/prefetch-on-intent! seam — and the fn itself now has no caller
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the mayor from worker/routedoc-a's out-of-fence report on rf2-fhwd (PR #9167). Two related things on one symbol; the first is verified by that worker, the second by me.

PART 1 — THE STALE MENTION, verified by routedoc-a and OUT of its fence.
bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 names :routing/prefetch-on-intent! as what would replace a declined passthrough. That seam was RETIRED by PR #9165 (the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio: three set-fn! publications and three late_bind/directory.cljc rows removed together). The comment is not describing its own direct call, so it is genuinely stale rather than retirement bookkeeping — routedoc-a judged it against the code and left it only because bench/ was outside its fence.

PART 2 — THE SYMBOL MAY NOW BE A VESTIGE, and this is the part that needs a judgement rather than a fix.
routedoc-a established that rf/route-link does NOT call prefetch-on-intent! — prefetch-intent-attrs composes the same behaviour itself from compose-intent-handler. With the seam retired, the function has NO IN-REPO CALLER AT ALL. Its control for that zero: activate-link!, its click sibling, reads 46 references across 14 files under the same search, so the instrument bites.

MY OWN CENSUS, taken untruncated and with the count read separately from the listing:
  6 occurrences total, across 3 real files (plus the .beads export, which is not a source):
    bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs   (the stale comment above)
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc
  NOT in spec/api-manifest.edn (0 hits), against a control on route-link returning 3 — so that zero is a check that passed rather than a broken instrument.
  NOT in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (0 hits).

SO THE QUESTION IS: is prefetch-on-intent! a public affordance a consumer is expected to call, or a vestige of the retired seam? Absence from the api-manifest is EVIDENCE, not proof — do not treat it as decisive on its own. Read what the function does and whether any documented consumer path reaches it before recommending anything.

THREE HONEST OUTCOMES, and the worker should pick with reasons rather than defaulting:
(a) It is a live public affordance -> fix the bench comment only, and say what consumer path justifies keeping an uncalled public fn.
(b) It is a vestige -> retire it with its docstring and the bench comment, in one PR.
(c) It is ambiguous -> fix the bench comment, report the ambiguity, and leave the symbol for a ruling. That is a complete deliverable.

FENCE WHEN DISPATCHED:
  bench/hicasso/**  and  implementation/routing/**  are the surfaces.
  WATCH THE ALIAS RATCHET: bench is a BASELINE SURFACE reading 701, and implementation/routing reads 0 found / 0 floor — so routing has NO HEADROOM IN EITHER DIRECTION. The gate is TWO-SIDED: it fails when a surface rises above its floor AND when it falls below. Removing a require can red it from below. If a count moves, STOP and report — scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn belongs to whichever alias-campaign slice holds it, and rf2-7sx1 is live.
  Do not touch spec/009-Instrumentation.md: its :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch row names prefetch-payload as a validation site and is STILL ACCURATE. That row separately names ui/route-link, a retired artefact — pre-existing, unrelated, hot-zone, and reported by routedoc-a rather than touched.

GATE: from implementation/routing/, clojure -M:test reads 553 tests / 3451 assertions. NOTHING VALIDATES A DOCSTRING'S OR COMMENT'S TRUTH — the check is reading the code each sentence sits on, and the PR body should name what was read for each.
notes:
SEQUENCED 2026-09-04 by the mayor — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9167 MERGES. This is a file-collision hold, not a ruling; no operator decision is needed.

WHY. This bead's Part 2 asks whether prefetch-on-intent! is a vestige, and that symbol's docstring lives in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc. PR #9167 (worker/routedoc-a) is OPEN and rewrites four docstrings in that exact file, including prefetch-on-intent!'s. Two workers editing one file is a merge conflict, and worse, the stale-copy hazard: a branch that started before #9167 landed would silently revert the four corrected docstrings while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and compiles.

RELEASE CONDITION: PR #9167 merged. Then re-read link.cljc at tip BEFORE briefing — #9167 rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring to record the no-caller state, so this bead's Part 2 starts from that text rather than from the text it was filed against.

AND NOTE bd ready CANNOT SHOW THIS. It filters dependency blockers only; a hold written in prose is invisible to the scheduler. I dispatched a fenced bead off that list earlier today for exactly this reason. Read this bead's notes before briefing it.

PART 1 IS NOT BLOCKED BY #9167 — the bench comment at bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 is in a different tree entirely. If a future tick wants to move sooner, Part 1 alone is dispatchable the moment nothing else holds bench/. But splitting buys little: both halves are small, they concern one symbol, and the Part 2 judgement is what makes the Part 1 fix say the right thing.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-04 by the mayor — PR #9167 MERGED, so the file-collision hold is released. AND RE-READING AT TIP CHANGED THIS BEAD, exactly as the fence note said it might; do not brief from the description alone.

WHAT #9167 ALREADY DID TO PART 2. It rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:519 to record the no-caller state honestly. At tip it now reads, after describing the behaviour: "NO in-repo caller at present. This was published as the :routing/prefetch-on-intent! late-bind seam for a view artefact's own..." So the docstring no longer makes a false claim, and the URGENT half of Part 2 is discharged. What remains is the JUDGEMENT — is an uncalled, unmanifested public fn a vestige or a live affordance — and that is now a considered question rather than a defect on the tree.

WHAT PART 1 ACTUALLY IS, read in context rather than from the filing. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs, in the docstring of the prefetch-decline path, says:

  "If HD-027 is deliberately reopened to admit prefetch, what replaces this is
   routing's full three-handler behaviour (`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` at
   `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` / `:on-touch-start`). A passthrough is not
   the middle ground between the two."

THAT IS A CONDITIONAL FUTURE STATEMENT, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT TODAY, which makes it narrower than "a stale mention". The BEHAVIOUR it describes — routing's three-handler prefetch — still exists and is still what would replace the decline; it is reached through prefetch-intent-attrs and compose-intent-handler. What is stale is only that it names the mechanism by its RETIRED SEAM KEYWORD, :routing/prefetch-on-intent!, which no longer resolves to anything. So the fix is to name the live mechanism instead of the dead seam, keeping the sentence's meaning intact.

MY OWN CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing and excluding the .beads export: 4 occurrences across 3 files — the bench comment above, implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc, and link.cljc. Down from 6 before #9167.

SO THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN FILED: one comment in bench/, plus a judgement recorded on this bead. Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — #9167 handled it.
AUDIT PR #9167 (2026-09-04) — scope correction after independent call-graph read. The newer note says “Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing”, but origin/main implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 still states that rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call. That is false: link.cljc:203-220 builds the live handlers through prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while link.cljc:530-535 correctly says rf/route-link does NOT route through prefetch-on-intent!. A non-ledger fixed-string census finds the symbol only in this false retirement note, its own zero-caller definition/docstring, and the already-owned bench comment. Add routing.cljc:574 to this bead's repair surface; the existing keep/delete judgement and bench wording remain the exact owner. No separate bead filed for this symbol.

WORKED 2026-09-04 by worker/benchdoc-a — PR #9169. Both parts discharged.

PART 1 DONE. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs,
prefetch-declined!'s docstring. The retired seam keyword
`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` is replaced by the live mechanism:
"(`rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent!`, called directly at each
`prefetch-intent-keys` position — `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` /
`:on-touch-start`)". Conditional framing and meaning unchanged; the surrounding
fail-open argument untouched. One hunk, one file, comment-only.

WHY THAT NAME AND NOT prefetch-intent-attrs. The dispatching brief steered toward
naming `prefetch-intent-attrs` / `compose-intent-handler`. THAT PREMISE DOES NOT
HOLD FOR THIS FILE, and the item's own framing is what settles it. Those two are
`defn-` PRIVATE and CLJS-only (link.cljc:191, :203), and they are `rf/route-link`'s
internal path. This bench front is NOT rf/route-link — it is a VIEW ARTEFACT'S OWN
route-link, consuming routing through `:routing/link-model` and
`:routing/activate-link!` (its ns docstring says so in terms). It cannot reach a
private var. The symbol routing publishes for exactly that consumer class is the
public `prefetch-on-intent!`, whose own docstring at link.cljc:519 names it: "Kept
as routing's one statement of the intent-dispatch law, for a view artefact that
needs it to call directly." "called directly" is load-bearing because routing.cljc:572
records that there is deliberately no late-bind seam for the trio.

PART 2 VERDICT: KEEP. prefetch-on-intent! is a live public affordance, not a vestige.
Three reasons, all re-checkable:
(1) THE CONSUMER PATH IS NAMED AND CONCRETE, not speculative — it is the one the
    Part 1 comment documents: a view artefact's own route-link that reopens HD-027.
(2) THE ALTERNATIVE IS CLOSED TO THAT CONSUMER. Retiring it leaves a link-model seam
    consumer able to VALIDATE AND ACCEPT `:prefetch :intent` (link-model calls
    validate-prefetch!) with no published way to HONOUR it — exactly the fail-open
    shape both link.cljc and the bench front exist to refuse. Retirement would
    manufacture the defect the bench comment is about.
(3) THE API-MANIFEST EVIDENCE DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — this REFINES the description's
    premise rather than contradicting it. The description reads the 0 hits against a
    route-link control of 3 and concludes the instrument bites. It does. But the
    broader control settles the inference: the string `prefetch` appears 0 times in
    spec/api-manifest.edn ENTIRELY. prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys are
    equally absent and are indisputably live (both called directly by rf/route-link).
    So manifest-absence is SILENT on this question, not evidence of vestige. The
    description was right to say "evidence, not proof"; measured, it is not even
    evidence here.
Under the stance — pre-alpha, no back-compat obligation, trust the programmer — an
uncalled public helper with an honest docstring is not a defect, and #9167 already
made that docstring honest. Nothing manufactured to close a bead.

CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing: 4 occurrences across 3
source files (7 across 4 including the .beads export, not a source) — matching the
mayor's count. bench front_route_link.cljs:127, routing.cljc:574, link.cljc:519 and
:531. Control: activate-link! reads 72 occurrences across 27 files under the
identical search.

ONE RESIDUAL INACCURACY REPORTED, NOT TOUCHED — needs a ruling or a follow-up bead.
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:574 states that `rf/route-link`
"reaches rf.routing.link/prefetch-payload, prefetch-on-intent! and
prefetch-intent-keys BY DIRECT CALL". True of prefetch-payload and
prefetch-intent-keys; FALSE of prefetch-on-intent!, which rf/route-link does not
call at all — link.cljc:531 says so explicitly ("rf/route-link does NOT route
through here"). Two files 45 lines apart contradict each other at tip. #9167 fixed
link.cljc and did not reach this clause. It is inside the item's declared surface
(implementation/routing/**) but outside the dispatching brief's MAY-EDIT fence, and
this item's newest note says nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — so
it was left alone deliberately rather than silently.

GATE: python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose — exit 0, 2773 files /
10773 edges / 5586 non-canonical, identical to trunk. RATCHET DID NOT MOVE in either
direction. Routing suite not run: the verdict is KEEP, so no code changed.
Provenance proven by planted fault (gate red exit 1, "bench: 702 violation(s), floor
701", naming route_link.cljs:77), restored and verified by git blob hash
15bd145e51de3e13afdb5e748ae46cca8ed23c02. That proves the gate reads this worktree;
it proves nothing about whether the prose is true — that rests on the reading above.
AUDIT PR #9169 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The PR fixed the bench comment and made a defensible KEEP ruling, but it closed this exact owner while explicitly leaving implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 false. That comment says rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call; link.cljc:203-220 and :385 show the live path is prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while the public helper at :519 has no caller and its own docstring says rf/route-link does not route through it. Correct that one retirement note; do not duplicate the bead or revisit the KEEP ruling.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, seventeenth instance today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main with a control that fired (29 'prefetch' hits in the file, so the instrument read it): the retired seam name :routing/prefetch-on-intent! reads ZERO, and the live name rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent! reads ONE.

Delivered by worker/benchdoc-a in PR #9169, MERGED.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE REPLACEMENT NAME AND THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. I steered it to name prefetch-intent-attrs / compose-intent-handler. Both are defn- PRIVATE and CLJS-only (link.cljc:191, :203), and they are rf/route-link's INTERNAL path — the bench file is a view artefact's own route-link consuming routing through late-bound seams, so it cannot reach them. Naming them would have produced a fresh false statement in place of a stale one. It read the bench file's own ns docstring to establish which consumer class it belongs to, then named rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent! called directly at each prefetch-intent-keys position.

Retiring prefetch-on-intent! would leave a link-model seam consumer able to validate and ACCEPT :prefetch :intent — link-model calls validate-prefetch! — with no published way to honour it. That is the exact fail-open shape both files exist to refuse.

IT ALSO CORRECTED MY REASONING ON MANIFEST EVIDENCE. I had said absence from spec/api-manifest.edn was 'evidence, not proof' of privateness. Measured: 'prefetch' appears ZERO times in that manifest at all, against a control where route-link returns a row — so prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys, indisputably live and directly called, are equally absent. For this family manifest-absence is not even evidence.

AND IT FOUND A CONTRADICTION #9167 CREATED, reported rather than edited out of fence: routing.cljc claimed rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call while link.cljc 45 lines away denied it. Filed as rf2-w0s6 and fixed in PR #9170.

title: spec-resource: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn still describes the non-ClojureScript walk-up fallback that PR #9106 removed
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the mayor, from worker/cifreehand-a's out-of-fence report on rf2-6r9j.80 (PR #9159). The shadow-cljs.edn site I VERIFIED MYSELF; the second site is that worker's claim and is marked as such below.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main (ref-addressed git reads are unreliable here — see memory ref-addressed-git-search-false-empty). implementation/shadow-cljs.edn around line 168 reads:

    ;; the `../spec` root below go through it, and it is on
    ;; this classpath so they can: it owns the shadow-cljs
    ;; recording read, the non-ClojureScript walk-up fallback,
    ;; and — the reason it is ONE namespace rather than a
    ;; helper copied into each consumer — the cold-load

The middle clause is the defect: PR #9106 REMOVED the non-ClojureScript walk-up fallback, so this comment justifies a namespace's single-owner design partly on a responsibility it no longer has. The rest of the sentence is still true, which is what makes it worth a careful edit rather than a deletion — the cold-load clause and the shadow-cljs recording read are both live.

THE SECOND SITE IS A RELAYED CLAIM, NOT A FINDING. cifreehand-a reported the same staleness at 'cljs_publics.clj:101-102'. I could not confirm it: the file is at implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj (NOT the spec-resource tree), and a search of it for 'walk-up' returned zero against a working control. Either the wording differs from the phrase I searched, or the line numbers moved. CHECK IT AT SOURCE; do not take my zero as proof of absence, because I got a false zero elsewhere in the same investigation (below).

MY OWN CENSUS IS UNRELIABLE AND HERE IS WHY, so the worker does not inherit it. A repo-wide recursive grep for 'walk-up fallback' returned BLANK, which I nearly recorded as 'no other file names it'. The same string in shadow-cljs.edn alone returns 1. The blank was the scan being KILLED at the command timeout — partial output, status swallowed by a pipe, nothing on screen to say so. So THE CENSUS FOR THIS BEAD HAS NOT BEEN DONE. Do it scoped (per-directory, no multi-pattern --include list, never piped) and control every zero. Recorded as memory timed-out-search-reads-as-no-matches.

WHAT #9106 ACTUALLY DID, per cifreehand-a and to be re-verified: it landed the api-manifest sidecar, and the reader's docstring now reads 'today the api-manifest sidecar'. That landing is what makes this a correction rather than a premature one.

FENCE AND SEQUENCING. implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is HOT-ZONE — sequential, never parallel, comment only, and nothing that changes a build id, a :dev-http port or any build config. Testbed build-ids live in this file too (see memory reference_testbed_buildids_in_hotzone_shadow), so a careless diff here collides with any live testbed dispatch. Check for a live holder before dispatching.

title: hic docs: chapter 07 never says a route deeper than one segment changes what relative asset paths resolve against - the page silently loses its stylesheet
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F13 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to** Deep-link straight to the new card-detail URL, `/issues/srv-1`,
and have the page look right.

**Expected** It to work, since the routing chapter treats `"/articles/:id"` as
the ordinary case.

**Instead** The application booted and rendered correctly, and the page was
**unstyled**. The host page `index.html` carries `href="_shared/css/style.css"`
— a *relative* URL, which was fine while every route was `/`. On `/issues/srv-1`
it resolves to `/issues/_shared/css/style.css`, 404. Same for the favicon.
Only `<script src="/js/main.js">` survived, because it happens to be absolute —
which is exactly why the failure is quiet: the app boots and behaves, and only
the styling is gone.

**Looked at** The browser console (one bare `Failed to load resource: 404`, with
no URL in the message); then `[...document.querySelectorAll('link')].map(e=>e.href)`
in the page, which named it. `07-routing-and-navigation.md` in full — nothing on
host-page assets.

**Resolved by** Making the three asset paths absolute in
`app/public/index.html`. Verified: `document.styleSheets` now reports the sheet
with 52 rules, and the console is clean.

Logged because it is a self-inflicted bug that **arrived with the first nested
route** — every application adding its first `/:id` page hits it — and neither
chapter 07 nor chapter 00 mentions it. Chapter 00 prints an `index.html` with
`<script src="/js/main.js">` absolute, so the guide's own example is safe by
accident while saying nothing about why.

**Bead** One line in chapter 07, near "Deep links, Back, and Forward": a route
deeper than one segment changes what relative URLs in the host page resolve
against; use absolute asset paths, or a `<base>`. Cheap to say, and the failure
it prevents is silent.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137. Premise HOLDS. Mechanism confirmed rather than assumed: it is browser URL resolution, not Hicasso - a relative URL resolves against the DOCUMENT url, and under the default history strategy the document url IS the route. Measured with new URL() over four cases: '_shared/css/style.css' on '/' gives /_shared/css/style.css, on '/issues/srv-1' gives /issues/_shared/css/style.css; a leading-slash path is unaffected; a '<base href="/">' restores the root resolution. The silence is because the script tag is usually absolute already, so the app boots and routes with no stylesheet. Fix: an admonition in ch07 'Deep links, Back, and Forward' naming the mechanism and both remedies - absolute asset paths (as ch00's own index.html already uses for /js/main.js) or one <base href="/">, with rf.routing/with-base-path on the frame's :url-strategy for a sub-path deployment (verified to exist at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc) - plus a troubleshooting row for the symptom. NOT FIXED, for the mayor: examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html carries href="_shared/css/style.css" beside an /articles/:id route, so the repo's own routing example is latently this bug; examples were outside the dispatch fence.

title: schemas storage.cljc: the schema-validator-unavailable diagnostic may advise a require the facade already does
description:
`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`'s `:rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable` diagnostic still advises the developer to "Require `re-frame.schemas.malli` at app boot".

That instruction is now stale in the same way the twelve test-level requires retired by rf2-6r9j.51 (PR #9121) were: the facade loads the malli adapter automatically. Verified there by the strong route - deleting the FACADE's own require turns the JVM schemas suite to 494 failures / 1 error, which is what proves the facade is the loader.

The distinction from rf2-6r9j.51, and the reason this is its own bead rather than part of it: .51 was about TEST POSTURE - requires in test namespaces. This is a RUNTIME DIAGNOSTIC shown to a consuming developer, so getting it wrong sends a real user to add a require they do not need, and it is read at exactly the moment they are already confused about validation not working.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE EDITING. The advice may still be correct for a consumer who has NOT required the facade - that is plausibly the whole population who can see this warning, since the warning fires when the validator is unavailable. So establish what actually reaches this diagnostic: if the facade is required, is the adapter always wired, making the warning unreachable? If the warning is reachable WITH the facade loaded, the advice may be right and the bead's premise fails. If it is reachable only WITHOUT the facade, the advice should name the facade, not the adapter.

A verified "the advice is correct as written" is a complete deliverable. Do not reword a diagnostic without establishing which population reads it.

Surface: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`. Discovered on PR #9121 (rf2-6r9j.51).
notes:
--- INVESTIGATION 2026-09-03 (worker gatetruth-a) — PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD; NO CHANGE MADE ---

VERDICT: the advice is CORRECT AS WRITTEN for every population that can
actually reach the diagnostic, and both the bead's premise AND the bead's own
named refutation are refuted. Left open for a mayor/Mike disposition only
because the one improvement worth considering needs a HOT-ZONE spec touch
(see LAST SECTION); the investigation itself is complete.

HOW ESTABLISHED — three JVM probes run from implementation/schemas, each
captured to an exit-code FILE (all three exit 0; probes print their own result):

  A2  public route, facade LOADED
      require re-frame.core + re-frame.schemas; explicit {:frame ...} so the
      registration COMPLETES rather than tripping :rf.error/no-frame-context
        -> :schemas/malli-validate bound = TRUE
        -> reg-app-schema COMPLETED
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 0        (SUPPRESSED)

  B   public route, facade NOT loaded
      require re-frame.core ONLY, then call rf/reg-app-schema
        -> :schemas/malli-validate bound = FALSE
        -> :schemas/reg-app-schema  bound = FALSE
        -> reg-app-schema THREW :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 0        (NEVER REACHED)

  C   facade BYPASSED into the internal ns
      require re-frame.schemas.storage directly, call storage/reg-app-schema
        -> facade ns loaded = FALSE, malli adapter ns loaded = FALSE
        -> storage/reg-app-schema COMPLETED
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 1        (THE DIAGNOSTIC FIRES)

SO THE DIAGNOSTIC IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE SUPPORTED PUBLIC API IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS. With the facade, re-frame.schemas.cljc:21 requires
re-frame.schemas.malli, whose body publishes :schemas/malli-validate in EVERY
build (malli.cljc ns docstring), so the gate
`(nil? (late-bind/get-fn :schemas/malli-validate))` is false and the warning
is suppressed. Without the facade, core_schemas.cljc:148 declares the
:schemas/reg-app-schema hook `:on-absent :throw` and re-frame.schemas.cljc:128
is its ONLY publisher, so rf/reg-app-schema throws
:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing and storage.cljc's warn site is never
reached. Namespace loading is depth-first, so there is no load-order window
either: .malli's body runs before re-frame.schemas' own set-fn! forms.

WHY THE BEAD'S NAMED REFUTATION ALSO FAILS. The bead expected the readers to
be "people who have NOT required the facade, for whom the advice is correct".
That population does not exist on the supported route — probe B shows they get
a throw, not a warning. The actual reachable populations are narrower:

  (1) a caller that reaches PAST the facade into the internal
      re-frame.schemas.storage ns (probe C). The advice WORKS for them:
      requiring re-frame.schemas.malli does bind the hook and does activate
      Malli validation.
  (2) a substitute-validator port or fixture that leaves :schemas/malli-validate
      unbound while the framework-default validator is still installed. For
      them the FIRST clause is the wrong steer, but the SECOND clause
      (`set-schema-validator!`) is the right one and is ALREADY in the string.
  (3) anything that mutates the late-bind hook table at runtime.

This is not a new finding in the tree — the JVM suite's own ns docstring
(schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj) already records it:
"Post-rf2-v96fh the re-frame.schemas facade auto-requires the Malli adapter,
so the common path keeps the hook bound and the warning is effectively
reserved for a substitute-validator port or this test's deliberate unbind."

TWO REASONS NOT TO REWORD, beyond the verdict itself:
  * spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2118 PINS the reason's content ("names the two
    fixes — require re-frame.schemas.malli at app boot, or call
    set-schema-validator! with a non-default fn"). That file is hot-zone /
    one-toucher and was not this worker's to touch.
  * schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj:110 asserts
    (re-find #"re-frame\.schemas\.malli" (:reason tags)), so dropping the ns
    name reds the JVM schemas suite.

THE ONE THING A FUTURE TICK MIGHT STILL WANT (a Mike call, not a defect).
malli.cljc's own ns docstring says "Applications do not require this namespace
explicitly: the re-frame.schemas facade requires it for its ns-load side
effect." The diagnostic therefore steers its one real-world reader (population
1) at an ns the adapter tells applications not to require, when the idiomatic
repair for them is `(:require [re-frame.schemas])`. ADDING a facade mention
alongside the existing one would keep the test green; it would still touch
spec/009-Instrumentation.md. Given the diagnostic is unreachable on the
supported path, the pre-alpha posture ("not litigating every last fine
detail") says leave it. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it.
close_reason: Investigation completed with no defect to fix. Three controlled JVM probes established that the warning is unreachable through the supported public API: loading the facade binds Malli and suppresses it; omitting the facade throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing before the warning site. The only reachable internal/substitute-validator populations already receive correct advice, including set-schema-validator!. Per this bead's own criterion, that verified verdict is a complete deliverable; the optional hot-zone wording refinement would be unnecessary detail under the pre-alpha posture.

title: Clarify Hicasso reverse-edge MCP tool name
description:
Scope: public Hicasso reverse-edge operation naming across tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Exact evidence: src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs defines read-read-attribution with wire name read-read-attribution; tools/hicasso_tool.cljs exports read-read-attribution-tool and registry.cljs binds the handler; tool-descriptors.edn, README.md, spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, test/fixtures/tool-names.json, live-hicasso-wire.cjs, and conformance_test.cljs repeat the operation name. The doubled read verb obscures that this operation is the reverse edge from subscription to reading boundaries, while the payload already calls the concept read-attribution. Ambiguity cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, plus inconsistent source symbol versus payload vocabulary. Compatibility constraint: this is a public MCP tools/call name embedded in generated descriptor artifacts, closed-world allowlists, live fixtures, and wire conformance; do not silently rename or change payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, or fixtures. Phase-1 fences: do not touch unrelated vestigial or generated-manifest cleanup targets, and do not alter MCP conformance wire-vocabulary scanner beads rf2-6r9j.239, .240, or .241. Recommendation: choose a migration-compatible canonical name such as read-attribution, retain the old name as an explicitly deprecated alias for a compatibility window, update descriptors and generated manifest together, then update docs, allowlists, tests, and live fixtures. Acceptance: canonical and deprecated alias behavior is specified; tools/list advertises the policy without duplicate ambiguous entries; both names produce identical reverse-edge envelopes during migration; old callers remain functional until the documented removal gate; tool-descriptors.edn is regenerated and drift-check passes; focused CLJS conformance and live-wire tests pass; no public JSON or EDN schema keys change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical reverse-edge wire name and a time-bounded deprecation policy for `read-read-attribution` are documented before the public rename lands.
2. During the compatibility window, canonical and deprecated names invoke the same handler and return identical envelopes; tools/list presents an unambiguous discovery policy.
3. Descriptor source, registry binding, generated `tool-descriptors.edn`, docs, fixture allowlists, conformance tests, and live-wire tests move together.
4. Descriptor drift, focused CLJS conformance, and live Hicasso wire checks pass for the migration.
5. Payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, and unrelated MCP vocabulary remain unchanged.

notes:
2026-09-03 — PREMISE REFUTED for the RENAME half; the CLARIFY half landed in PR #9121 (head e78349f355e683ea5a7acbdd08228c8b201f4d34). LEFT OPEN for a ruling, because meeting acceptance criteria 1-3 as written would override an existing naming ruling, which is not a worker's call.

Three grounds, each checked at source.

(1) IT IS ALREADY RULED. docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md row 51 (rf2-hic-065) reads the re-frame.hicasso.tool reader door name by name — read-mounted-boundaries, read-read-attribution, read-intents, explain-render — and rules 'keep all four as shipped', with a stated reason rather than a default: the read- prefix is 'load-bearing rather than decorative', marking the reads as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob. explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. The same row is restated in naming-packet.md row 249. This bead's evidence section does not cite that ruling.

(2) THE WIRE NAME IS THE PROVIDER FN NAME — one string, not two. hicasso_tool.cljs's projection-form interpolates (pr-str read-fn) into (cljs.core/unchecked-get d (cljs.core/munge ...)), so the literal 'read-read-attribution' passed to door-read-tool is munged and looked up on the door's namespace object at RUNTIME. The ns docstring states the invariant outright ('The wire names and the framework fn names AGREE, exactly') and hicasso_wire_test.cljs is the both-sides witness: it parses the ACTUAL EMITTED FORM and asserts every reader fn named there is defined publicly in the provider's own source.

MEASURED, not argued. Renaming the wire string to 'read-attribution' while the provider keeps read-read-attribution reds four suites: hicasso-wire-test/every-emitted-read-is-defined-by-the-provider, hicasso-wire-test/the-emitter-names-nothing-the-provider-does-not-publish, hicasso-tool-test/each-tool-emits-a-runtime-resolved-door-call, and the pair-mcp conformance corpus (4 failures, 0 errors). Control applied and restored; the restored suite is green at 1120 tests / 4070 assertions, exit 0. So a wire-only rename is not available: it would require decoupling wire name from emitted fn name — a structural change contradicting the invariant the witness exists to keep — or renaming the provider fn, which is in implementation/hicasso/ and consumed by tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_reads.cljs, skills/re-frame2-pair/, spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn.

(3) THE STATED AMBIGUITY COST IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's harm is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, and the descriptor's FIRST CLAUSE already reads 'Which boundaries read each subscription — the reverse edge, exactly.' A model reading tools/list is not left guessing what the operation does; the descriptor also names the provider fn and gives three worked examples. Nothing about tool selection is improved by the rename, and lengthening the description would add tokens to every tools/list for a naming footnote.

Also worth stating: acceptance criteria 1 and 2 require a deprecated alias and a compatibility window. That is a back-compat shim, and the standing posture is pre-alpha with no back-compat shims. If Mike ever does rule the rename in, the right shape here is a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in one PR, not an alias.

WHAT DID LAND (PR #9121, docstring only): hicasso_tool.cljs now explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table — the outer read- is the door's own prefix marking a pure projection, read-attribution is the payload's noun and the literal the envelope's :read slot carries — cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. No wire name, payload key, schema, id, path, handler or fixture changed. tool-descriptors.edn untouched; its drift check is in sync (30 tools, exit 0). descriptors_data.cljs was deliberately NOT edited: its description already leads with the reverse edge.

TO WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the question for Mike is narrow — override naming-ledger row 51 for this one name, or close this bead as ruled-against. The mechanics are settled and recorded above; do not re-litigate them, and do not attempt a wire-only rename, which is measured red.

The reason is stated rather than defaulted: the read- prefix is LOAD-BEARING, marking these as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob — and explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. (2) THE STATED HARM IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction. (3) THE CHEAP REMEDY IS MEASURED RED. ON THE STANCE, THEREFORE: 'we are not over-engineering or gold plating... we do not need to litigate every last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.' IF MIKE WANTS IT ANYWAY, the shape is recorded and does not need rediscovering: a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in ONE PR, no alias. Reopen with that instruction and it is a straightforward dispatch. What I will not do is keep it open as a question when the project's own stated position answers it.

NOT CLOSING THE UNDERLYING WORK: PR #9121's docstring already explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table, cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. A future reader meets the explanation where the confusion arises.

title: spec-resource race control: name cold-load actors and phases
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/spec-resource/test/re_frame/build/spec_resource_test.clj` is the deterministic control for the cold-load race closed by `resolve-after-require`. Its concurrency harness uses generic names that obscure which actor and phase each value belongs to: `counter` generates unique namespace and gate names, `fixture-root` is specifically a temporary classpath root, `generate-fixture!` writes a namespace whose initializer is deliberately blocked, and `run-probe` observes a resolver while that load is held open. Inside the probe, `answer`, `loaded`, `armed`, `observed`, `loader`, `observer`, `sym`, and `in-window` require repeated backtracking to distinguish loader-thread results, observer-thread results before/after release, the probe Var, and the held-open phase. The returned keys repeat that ambiguity (`:sym`, `:in-window`, `:observed`, `:loaded`).

This matters because the test's proof depends on actor and phase identity: the known-broken resolver must return an unbound Var during the held-open load, while the shipped resolver must block and both actors must see a bound Var after release. Misreading `loaded` as a load-status flag or `observed` as the during-window observation weakens review of the one deterministic witness for the defect.

History confirms these are original names from `5311835961`, when the whole control was introduced. Searches across all-status beads for `spec-resource`, `run-probe`, `recording-slurp`, and `resolve-after-require` found only Phase-1 removal beads `rf2-6r9j.80` and `.82`; neither owns this retained race control.

## Recommendation

Rename private test helpers, locals, and result keys by role and phase: for example `cold-load-iterations`, `unique-name-sequence`, `fixture-classpath-root`, `write-blocked-fixture-namespace!`, `observe-resolver-during-load`, `probe-var-symbol`, `observe-var-state`, `loader-result`, `observer-entered-resolver`, `observer-result`, `loader-thread`, `observer-thread`, and `:during-load` / `:observer-result` / `:loader-result`. Update docstrings and every test consumer together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is test-private vocabulary only. Preserve the public namespace/file names, `resolve-after-require`, `slurp-resource`, the known-broken `requiring-resolve` control, thread/gate timing, assertion semantics, and production serialized data. Do not rename or edit `classpath-root`, `spec-file`, the non-CLJS branch, the root dependency, or bench classpath entries: those are Phase-1 deletion targets owned by `rf2-6r9j.80` and `.82`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The cold-load harness names every generated identity, actor, synchronization point, and result by its role and phase; generic `counter`, `run-probe`, `answer`, `loaded`, `armed`, `observed`, `loader`, `observer`, and old result-key roles are absent.
2. The known-broken control still deterministically observes an unbound Var during load, while `resolve-after-require` still blocks during load and both actors observe bound Vars after release.
3. Public source APIs, namespace/file names, production data, Phase-1 deletion targets, iteration count, synchronization, and assertion behavior are unchanged.
4. Exact old/new searches, the artifact JVM suite with a planted negative control, and diff validation pass.
close_reason: Implemented in 1145dcda8e: private cold-load control names now distinguish generated identities, loader/observer actors, synchronization facts, and during/post-release results. Public APIs and Phase-1 targets are unchanged; artifact tests, pinned clj-kondo, exact searches, and diff checks pass.

title: ssr-node isolate pool: name lifecycle state by ownership and phase
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/isolate.cjs` and `src/pool.cjs` implement the worker lifecycle. The isolate's private state machine uses `_nextRequestSeq` for an internal render-dispatch ID distinct from public `requestId`, `_settle(id, act)`, `_fail`, `_die`, and repeated `p`/`w`/`msg` locals. The pool calls its boot-and-register operation `_spawn`, its replacement-only race-safe wrapper `_spawnTracked`, stores only replacement boots in a generic `spawning` set, and stores the full membership in `all`; teardown and replacement paths use `fresh`, `w`, `i`, and another `all`. `_spawnTracked`/`spawning` were added by 8ab673ea78 specifically to close the replacement-vs-close race, so their lifecycle purpose is stable and more precise than the mechanism name.

These names blur ownership and phase in code whose correctness depends on exactly those distinctions: public versus isolate-local IDs, initial boots versus replacement boots, pending render settlement versus worker termination, and all isolates versus idle isolates.

## Recommendation

Use private role names such as `_nextRenderId`, `_settlePendingRender`, `_failPendingRender`, `_terminateWorker`, `pendingRender`, `worker`, `_startIsolate`, `_startReplacement`, `startingReplacements`, `isolates`, `startedIsolates`, `failedStart`, and `replacement`. Keep public stats and refusal payload keys unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

The affected methods/fields are package-private and have no repository consumer outside these two files. Preserve public `Isolate.render/start/close`, `Pool.acquire/release/stats/close`, `busy`, worker message keys, refusal detail keys, and health JSON. Do not remove `renders` or the `WORKER_PATH` export; rf2-6r9j.84 owns those vestiges.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Private isolate names distinguish render settlement/failure from worker termination and internal render IDs from public request IDs.
2. Private pool names distinguish starting any isolate from starting/tracking a replacement and identify full membership explicitly.
3. Public class methods/properties used by tests, stats/health keys, message keys, and refusal detail fields are unchanged.
4. rf2-6r9j.84 deletion targets remain untouched.
5. Exact searches, concurrency/isolation/timeout tests, lint, and the full ssr-node gate pass.

title: Routing namespaces: finish the canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Partition: implementation/routing namespace and require-alias vocabulary across production source, tests, recipes, and helpers.

Evidence:
- `spec/Conventions.md` §Require-alias dialect requires `re-frame.core` to use `rf` and every framework subsystem `re-frame.<tail>` to use the dotted `rf.<tail>` alias; it explicitly reserves bare leaf aliases such as `routing` for application namespaces.
- A clj-kondo namespace-usage census over all 88 routing code files, deduplicated by `[file target alias]` so CLJC host analysis does not double-count, found 438 noncanonical aliased framework edges in 83 files: 145 in 26 production files and 293 in 57 test/recipe files. Common examples are `re-frame.routing :as routing` (40), `re-frame.frame :as frame` (27), `re-frame.interop :as interop` (25), `re-frame.fx :as fx` (23), and `re-frame.late-bind :as late-bind` (21).
- The facade and internal routing namespaces also alias routing siblings inconsistently (`registry`, `routing-events`, `routing-subs`, `route-reply`) instead of deriving the canonical aliases from their namespace tails (`rf.routing.registry`, `rf.routing.events`, `rf.routing.subs`, `rf.routing.reply`).
- Commit `d848371f60` made the alias rule normative while explicitly deferring SCOPE 2, the repo-wide implementation sweep. Two later routing naming passes (`2df2d88a37`, `eed266f99a`) deliberately limited themselves to local/private names. All-status searches for bare framework aliases and routing namespace aliases found only the new core-specific sibling `rf2-6r9j.161` plus closed docs/machines rulings, not a routing implementation owner.

Ambiguity cost:
Routing source currently contradicts the normative and published dialect, and bare framework aliases consume names the convention reserves for application namespaces. At call sites, a reader cannot tell whether `routing/...`, `frame/...`, or `events/...` denotes framework code or an application's same-named feature without consulting the ns form. Inconsistent aliases for routing siblings add a second local dialect.

Recommendation:
Migrate routing in reviewable namespace families to exact dotted aliases (`re-frame.routing` -> `rf.routing`, `re-frame.routing.registry` -> `rf.routing.registry`, `re-frame.frame` -> `rf.frame`, etc.), keeping `re-frame.core` -> `rf` as the sole root exemption and leaving side-effect-only unaliased requires alone. Update every qualified use with syntax-aware tooling. Add or extend a parsed CI ratchet so new noncanonical framework aliases cannot enter while the broader migration proceeds.

Risks/contracts:
Aliases are compile-time source vocabulary, not runtime API, but this is a high-churn 83-file CLJ/CLJS/CLJC change with reader conditionals, macros, test fixtures, and app-like recipe namespaces. Mechanical replacement must not touch keyword/event/fx/late-bind IDs, namespace symbols, quoted data, public vars, external library aliases, or genuine application aliases. Stage separately from semantic routing changes and coordinate the ratchet with sibling surface bead `rf2-6r9j.161` rather than building duplicate enforcement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every tracked implementation/routing source/test namespace aliases `re-frame.core` as `rf` and other framework subsystem namespaces with the canonical `rf.<namespace-tail>` spelling, except documented convention exemptions and unaliased side-effect requires.
- Every qualified use is updated; a parsed, CLJC-deduplicated census reports zero non-exempt routing-surface violations.
- A shared syntax-aware CI ratchet prevents regressions without duplicating the enforcement planned by `rf2-6r9j.161`.
- Routing JVM tests, all routing CLJS builds/tests, lint, production-gate/bundle-isolation gates where applicable, and git diff --check pass.
- No public var, namespace declaration, keyword/event/fx/late-bind ID, serialized value, quoted symbol/data, external dependency alias, or application namespace alias changes.
close_reason:
PR #9103. All 438 noncanonical framework require edges in implementation/routing (83 files) migrated to the spec/Conventions.md dialect: re-frame.core keeps rf, every other re-frame.<tail> takes the dotted rf.<tail>, every qualified use moved with it.

The bead's premise 'finish the migration' did NOT hold — a census over routing found ZERO canonical aliases, so nothing had been started. Repo-wide the only namespace already speaking the dialect was implementation/http (rf.http), which is what this matched rather than inventing a variant. The 438 figure reproduced the bead's own clj-kondo census exactly, which is the cross-check that both scans measured the same thing.

Documented exemptions, both stated in the PR: (1) eight *_cljs_test.cljc suites bind ONE alias to two namespaces across reader arms (#?(:clj [re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as substrate] :cljs [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as substrate])) — the shared name is the point of that form and per-arm tails would give the single use site two names; (2) routing_path_census_test.clj's fixture STRINGS are sample application source the census parses, not requires.

Also corrected the two :url-strategy doc snippets in routing.cljc and routing/strategy.cljc that were teaching users the retired spelling.

Gates: routing JVM 554 tests / 3454 assertions exit 0; node bundle 11170 tests / 55749 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo 0 errors and the SAME 831 warnings origin/main produces, diffed line by line against a pristine archive of main. CI on the merge head: 86 checks, 73 success / 13 skipped, 0 failures.

NOT done here: the syntax-aware CI ratchet in the acceptance criteria. It belongs in scripts/ + .github/workflows/ (held / hot-zone this tick) and should be ONE ratchet for the repo rather than one per artefact — carried on rf2-j5or.

title: Make schemas walker structure and alignment names self-describing
description:
Partition: implementation/schemas schema reflection and privacy walker.

Locations and evidence:
- implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:72-102 names private schema projections `props-of`, `children-of`, and `decl-from-props`, leaving both their subject and returned domain implicit.
- walker.cljc:167-259 repeatedly uses `maybe-prop`, `has-prop?`, `tail`, `d`, `elem-schema`, and `entry-decl` while decoding several different Malli child-entry grammars.
- walker.cljc:603-724 and 805-938 use `in`, `out`, `aligned`, `seg`, `val-schema`, and `seg-out` in two lockstep privacy-path walkers.

Ambiguity cost:
The walker distinguishes Malli properties, child schemas, declaration maps, raw paths, aligned paths, sanitized trace paths, leftover subschemas, and leaf schemas. Generic/positional names make it difficult to verify that a value-bearing segment is scrubbed, that an opaque subtree fails closed, and that a declaration is associated with the right coordinate system.

Compatibility and migration risk:
All function renames are private and all other changes are lexical or comments. Preserve public walker entry points, namespace/file, operator sets and semantics, return tuples, extracted declaration maps, sentinels, schema IDs, and privacy behavior. Update every test/doc reference to old private names and rely on the existing exhaustive security corpus for behavioral proof.

title: Make UIx registered-view diagnostic facts self-describing
description:
## Scope

The UIx registered-view diagnostic test family:
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs

This partition covers private helpers, locals, and private result-map keys only.

## Naming finding

Two capture helpers misstate their channels: with-captured-errors also records console.warn and window error events, while capture-warnings also records console.error. Their internal calls/orig-* names and returned :msgs facts conceal that the values are diagnostic messages. The direct-mount result uses context-free :initial, :after, :child, :children, and :ops keys; the source-coordinate result similarly uses :node?, :coord, and :view. Production-elision rows use user-fn/render/out for the registered view function, component head, and rendered React element.

## Ambiguity cost

These tests distinguish several subtle failure channels and multiple phases of one mount. Generic or channel-inaccurate names make an assertion's provenance unclear and encourage future coverage to inspect the wrong channel or confuse a view head with its rendered element.

## Proposed names

- with-captured-errors -> capture-render-diagnostics; capture-warnings -> capture-console-diagnostics.
- calls -> messages; orig-warn/orig-error -> original-warn/original-error; matching -> matching-messages; re/msg(s) -> pattern/message(s).
- Direct-mount facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :initial -> :initial-text, :after -> :updated-text, :child -> :child-text, :payload -> :observed-payload, :children -> :children-present?, :ops -> :frame-ops; give corresponding locals full names.
- Source-coordinate facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :node? -> :view-root-present?, :coord -> :source-coordinate, :view -> :view-id-attribute; expand output locals.
- Production-elision locals: user-fn -> view-fn, render/wrapped -> view-head, out -> rendered-element, props -> element-props where applicable.

## Compatibility and risks

All names are private to tests. Preserve public rf/reg-view*, rf/view, adapter functions, UIx/React interop properties, data-rf2-source-coord/data-rf-view attributes, regex contents, event ids, and classifier filenames. Result-map key changes must update every producer/destructure/assertion atomically.

## Acceptance criteria

- Helper names accurately describe every channel they capture.
- Result facts distinguish mount phase, DOM text, observed CLJS values, hook operations, and annotation attributes without reading producer code.
- Repository searches find no stale old private helper names or old result-key destructures in these files.
- Focused registered-view browser and production-elision tests pass.
- git diff --check and focused lint pass with no new warnings.

title: Remove retired UI dependency helpers from the shared EDN reader
description:
