title: Collapse Story-host router indirection left by retired project-root setup
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs defines private mount-router! at lines 57-66, and the only repository reference is the public mount-with-hash-routing! calling it at line 77.
- git history shows mount-router! was introduced in a25e4c08bc specifically so the then-two-arity public entry could configure the browser-side Story project root before delegating to routing.
- 2eb0df5bdd retired that project-root/source-subdir feature and reduced the public entry to one arity, but left the now-single-use delegation behind.

Impact:
The private layer no longer represents a separate operation or reuse seam. It makes the public host entry harder to follow and preserves structure belonging to a retired feature.

Recommendation:
Move the listener replacement and initial route-selection body into mount-with-hash-routing! and remove mount-router!.

Risks/contracts:
Preserve the exact hot-reload contract: store root-view, remove the previously stored hashchange function identity, add the current identity, record it, and immediately mount the selected surface. Do not change the public arity or consumer call sites.

Acceptance:
- mount-router! is gone and has no repository references.
- mount-with-hash-routing! directly performs the same ordered operations.
- focused Node Story-host tests and the browser DOM handoff suite pass.
acceptance_criteria: Remove the single-use mount-router! layer without changing mount-with-hash-routing!'s public arity, listener replacement order, immediate route selection, or consumer behavior; focused Node and browser Story-host tests pass.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. Premise re-derived at source and held on every line.

CONFIRMED. mount-router! was private, defined at tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:57-66, and git grep found exactly one reference in the whole repository: mount-with-hash-routing! calling it at :77. a25e4c08bc introduced it — "Move project-root config onto the shared story-host helper: a consumer declares its tool-relative source subdir via a new :story-subdir opt to mount-with-hash-routing!" — i.e. it existed so the then-two-arity public entry could configure the browser-side Story project root BEFORE delegating to routing. 2eb0df5bdd retired that feature ("mount-with-hash-routing! is one-arity; no alias, no compatibility arity") and left the delegation behind with nothing on either side of it.

WHAT CHANGED. The body moved into mount-with-hash-routing! verbatim, comment included, in the same order: reset! root-view*, remove the previously stored hashchange identity if any, addEventListener the current on-hash-change! identity, reset! hash-listener* to that identity, then call on-hash-change! to mount the selected surface immediately. Public arity, docstring and consumer call sites unchanged. git grep mount-router now returns nothing outside the tracker export.

WHY THE HOT-RELOAD CONTRACT IS SAFE. The four operations that make it self-balancing across a reload — the stored-identity removal before the add, and the re-record after — are the same four statements in the same sequence; nothing was reordered, nothing dropped, and no new var was introduced. The reference form for on-hash-change! is identical to what mount-router! used, so with-redefs resolution at the call site is unchanged too, which matters because the DOM suite redefines it.

GATE, AND THE COLLISION IT SAT NEXT TO. npm run test:testbed-support (the focused :node-test-testbed-support build) green: exit 0, 16 tests / 62 assertions. clj-kondo clean. The browser DOM handoff suite is deliberately left to CI, for a reason worth recording: PR #9089 (worker/storyq-a, rf2-6r9j.116) was open on story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs at dispatch — +90/-1 — so a local run here would have exercised a version about to be replaced. The collision check the brief asked for came back CLEAN on the file this bead edits: #9089 touched only the DOM TEST, never story_host.cljs, so there was no source overlap and no race. #9089 has since merged, and its merged test was read against this change: it drives only the public mount-with-hash-routing! plus the three private atoms (hash-listener*, root-view*, app-root) and on-hash-change!, every one of which this refactor preserves; it never mentions mount-router!. GitHub tests the PR merge commit, so that merged suite runs against this source change on #9092's cljs_browser lane. Acceptance met on all three clauses.

title: Collapse the duplicate event-wrapper conformance test
description:
## Finding

Two adjacent tests in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` assert the same registration shape. `reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper` requires `(mapv :id (:interceptors meta))` to equal exactly `[:rf/event-handler]`, then checks the sole wrapper id and `:rf/default?`. `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive` registers another ordinary event, converts the same interceptor ids to a set, again requires exactly `#{:rf/event-handler}`, and separately asserts that `:rf/db-handler`, `:rf/fx-handler`, and `:rf/ctx-handler` are absent. Those three negatives are logical consequences of the exact singleton equality in the first test, so the second row exercises no additional branch, runtime, or metadata path.

## Recommendation

Delete `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive`, keeping the first test as the canonical wrapper lock. If the named retired ids are valuable migration documentation, mention them in the first test's assertion message/comment without executing a second registration. Alternatively parameterize a genuinely distinct historical registration path; currently there is none because all calls use the one `reg-event` form.

## Risks and contracts

Keep the exact ordered interceptor vector assertion, the wrapper's `:rf/default? true`, handler-fn reachability, and absence of `:event/kind`. Do not weaken singleton equality to only a membership check.

## Evidence

The first test at lines 652-669 asserts the exact one-element vector and wrapper metadata. The second at lines 671-679 asserts the set form of the same one-element vector plus redundant non-membership checks. Both use the same public registrar, fixture, platform matrix, and ordinary no-metadata `reg-event` path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Only one ordinary-registration test owns the exact singleton `:rf/event-handler` wrapper contract.
2. That surviving test still fails for any extra wrapper, any retired per-kind wrapper, wrong order/id, missing handler-fn, or missing `:rf/default? true`.
3. Test/docs commentary no longer implies the duplicate registration covers a distinct path.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass with the expected lower test/assertion tally.
close_reason: Premise held. Verified by plant, not census: renaming events/event-handler-interceptor-id :rf/event-handler -> :rf/db-handler (a retired per-kind id, exactly what the duplicate's three negatives claim to guard) reds BOTH rows -- survivor reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper exit 1 with 2 failures/6 assertions, duplicate reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive exit 1 with 2 failures/4. The survivor's exact-vector equality (= [:rf/event-handler] (mapv :id ...)) entails the set equality and all three non-memberships, and additionally refuses an extra wrapper and a wrong order, so the duplicate exercised no branch, runtime or metadata path the survivor misses. Deleted; the retired ids ride as commentary on the exact-vector assertion per the bead's own recommendation. AC1-4 met: one owner, unweakened singleton equality, no prose implying a distinct path, event-conformance JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and the consolidated node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. PR #9123.

title: http decode: remove the unreachable raw-body fallback
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.decode/decode-response-body` ends with a raw `body-text` fallback that is unreachable under the decoder normalization immediately above it.

## Evidence

- In `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:248-340`, `requested-decode` maps a nil `:decode` to `:auto`, preserves `:auto`, and otherwise preserves the supplied value. It therefore cannot be nil.
- `resolved` maps `:auto` through `sniff-decoder`; `sniff-decoder` has an exhaustive `cond` returning exactly `:json`, `:text`, or `:blob`. For every non-`:auto` input, `resolved` is the already-non-nil `requested-decode`. Thus `resolved` cannot be nil.
- The main `cond` first handles a decoder fn, JSON, text, and the binary modes. Its next predicate is `(some? resolved)`, which is necessarily true for every remaining input. The final `:else body-text` at lines 339-340 has no possible input.
- History shows this shape arrived with the decode extraction (`c8f80850c9`) and survived the later strict malformed-JSON correction (`5abbf20977`). The live schema/unknown-decoder arm deliberately parses JSON and propagates parse failure; the dead tail is not the earlier malformed-JSON fallback fixed by that commit.
- Repository and bead searches for the symbol, decoder normalization, decode fallback, and HTTP decode found no issue covering this unreachable branch.

## Impact

The dead tail falsely suggests a nil/unknown decoder can bypass schema/JSON handling and return raw text. That makes security-sensitive malformed-JSON reasoning harder and creates a branch no test can honestly exercise.

## Proposed disposition

Make the schema/unknown-decoder arm the final `:else` and remove the unreachable trailing fallback. Keep the binary arm's separate synthetic-context `body-binary` -> `body-text` fallback intact.

## Risks / retained contracts

This is intended to be behavior-neutral. Preserve nil/omitted `:decode` as `:auto`, custom decoder raw-text ownership, unknown non-mode values as schema candidates, strict malformed-JSON propagation, and binary response behavior on both hosts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `decode-response-body` has no trailing branch that requires `resolved` to be nil; the schema/unknown-decoder path is structurally exhaustive.
2. Omitted/nil and explicit `:auto`, `:json`, `:text`, all binary modes, custom fns, valid Malli schemas, invalid schemas, unknown keyword refs, malformed JSON, and empty-body parity retain their current results/errors.
3. The JVM HTTP decode suite and consolidated CLJS HTTP tests pass.
4. A source search and/or focused branch proof confirms there is no unreachable raw-body fallback, while the intentional binary synthetic-context fallback remains.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. The premise held exactly, and was proved two independent ways rather than by reading alone.

BY CONTROL FLOW. requested-decode maps nil :decode to :auto, preserves :auto, and otherwise preserves the supplied value, so it is never nil. resolved then maps :auto through sniff-decoder — an exhaustive cond returning exactly :json, :text or :blob — and otherwise IS requested-decode. So resolved is never nil. The main cond's penultimate predicate (some? resolved) was therefore true for everything that reached it, and the trailing :else body-text required resolved to be nil. Unreachable. One edge worth recording because it is the arm where a naive reading goes wrong: a :decode of FALSE also reaches the schema arm, not the fallback — some? is (not (nil? x)), so false passes it.

BY PROBE, WITH A CONTROL THAT FIRED. A side-effecting probe was planted in the fallback — a marker file rather than a throw, since a throw is caught by the transport's decode try/catch and classified as :rf.http/decode-failure, which could have been swallowed into a passing test. Across the whole 514-test suite the marker was ABSENT: the branch was never entered. The SAME probe mechanism planted in the live (= :text resolved) arm produced the marker with 2 hits. Zero versus two, same suite, same run shape, so the instrument works and the fallback is genuinely dead. (A first plant attempt was paren-unbalanced and failed to read the file — treated as NO VERDICT and redone, not interpreted.) Both plants restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: the schema/unknown-decoder arm is now the final :else and the trailing fallback is gone, so the cond is structurally exhaustive with no branch requiring a nil resolved (AC1, AC4). The binary arm's separate synthetic-context body-binary -> body-text fallback is INTACT — that one is deliberate and fires for a test ctx that populated only :body-text (AC2, retained contract).

Behaviour-neutral as intended: http clojure -M:test 506 tests / 3884 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0, with the empty-body-parity, binary-decode, malformed-JSON and schema decode rows all still green (AC2, AC3). The consolidated CLJS bundle — where a cross-host decode divergence would surface — ran 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0.

ONE PREMISE CORRECTION, cosmetic but worth the record: the bead cites the symbol as util-json/json-parse at decode.cljc:248-340. Main renamed that alias to http-json between filing and landing (commit f148f863c2), which is what the rebase conflicted on; resolved by keeping BOTH intents — main's rename and this removal.

title: reagent-slim: remove the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper
description:
## Finding

`reagent2.impl.component/tag-form-meta` is a public-looking compile-time helper with no production consumer. It has been test-only since its introduction and duplicates the literal metadata construction already performed by the only real consumer of this namespace.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.clj:14-25,71-76` advertises `tag-form-meta` as consumed by `reg-view` and defines it as only `{:reagent2/form form-tag}`.
- A repository-wide exact-symbol search finds only that source declaration/docstring and its dedicated test at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_test.clj:60-68`; there is no production call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:60-73` dynamically resolves only `classify-form-body`. The expansion constructs slot metadata directly with `(assoc :reagent2/form form-tag)` at lines 132-138 and fn metadata directly with `with-meta` at lines 196-197.
- `git log -S tag-form-meta` finds only its introduction in `21d4b06aae` and a later comment pass `0eeb8d079a`; history contains no consumer.
- This is not a shipped compatibility promise: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md:3-10` identifies `reagent2.core`/the adapter as the target surface and says reagent-slim is pre-alpha and has never shipped. No README or implementation-spec API table promises this helper.

## Impact

The extra public Var and dedicated test imply an extension seam that does not exist in the actual `reg-view` integration. They add maintenance and invite downstream coupling to an accidental one-line abstraction.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `tag-form-meta`, its dedicated unit test, and the false namespace-doc claim that `reg-view` consumes it. Keep `classify-form-body` and the macro expansion's current direct metadata construction unchanged. Do not add a deprecation shim to an unpublished, zero-consumer helper.

## Risks

A local, out-of-repository macro could have called the public Var despite the absence of a documented/released contract. Before removal, repeat exact searches over any maintained external consumer corpus if one exists; otherwise the explicit pre-alpha status makes removal the safer pre-release choice.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 current bead records (all states; title, description, notes, acceptance) for `tag-form-meta`, `reagent2.impl.component`, `compile-time form`, `metadata`, and the source path. No bead owns this finding. `rf2-08hx1` concerns Form-3 lifecycle argv and is unrelated.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tag-form-meta` and its test-only coverage are removed; `rg tag-form-meta` is empty across tracked source/tests/docs.
- `classify-form-body` remains the only CLJ helper dynamically resolved by core, and Form-1/Form-2 macroexpansion metadata remains byte-for-byte equivalent in meaning.
- The component namespace documentation names only helpers with a real consumer and does not claim a general macro-extension contract unless one is deliberately specified and tested.
- Reagent-slim JVM tests and the core `reg-view` macroexpansion tests pass; a negative control that removes the classifier resolution makes the focused fold test fail.
- No compatibility alias or dead forwarding wrapper replaces the removed helper.
notes: AUDIT 2026-09-03 — PR #9127 (merge 213a43ae7791dbe0a7feadab3a46077a38d804a9) correctly removed the zero-consumer `tag-form-meta` Var and its dedicated test, but the integrated tree still contains three claims that the helper exists: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:609`, its coverage table at `:1128`, and `src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:26`. At the same merge, exact searches of `component.clj` and `component_test.clj` return zero definitions/tests. This violates the existing acceptance criterion that tracked source/tests/docs contain no `tag-form-meta` and leaves runtime/developer documentation pointing at a removed Var. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate. Reconcile those three references with the surviving `classify-form-body` plus the metadata construction in `re-frame.core/expand-reg-view`; do not restore the dead helper.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED; the first close evaporated to the .beads checkout race. Landed on main as 213a43ae77 (PR #9127, worker slimdead-a): the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper removed from reagent-slim's impl/component.clj. A macro-time consumer was ruled out FOUR ways, which matters because a runtime var-usage census cannot see macroexpansion-time use: (1) census line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened found only docstring, defn and test; (2) every external reference to the namespace enumerated and read, all naming classify-form-body / wrap-render / create-class* / reagent-class?; (3) both requiring-resolve sites pass a LITERAL symbol, and a sweep for dynamically-constructed symbols - the one shape a literal census misses - found none; (4) the removal is itself the macro-time instrument, since the JVM suite macroexpands reg-view through expand-reg-view, so a surviving macro-time consumer would fail to COMPILE. Green. Control fired: planting a fault in classify-form-body's Form-2 branch took the JVM gate to exit 1 with four failures including fold-reg-view-form-2-expansion-tags-form-2, proving the fold test is not passing vacuously.

title: Xray: remove the orphaned sub-input-path resolver
description:
## Finding

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/sub_input_paths.cljc` is a 294-line static subscription-registry resolver left behind after the App-DB downstream-subs popover was removed. Its only current consumer is its own unit test.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide exact namespace search for `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.shared.sub-input-paths` finds only the namespace definition and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/sub_input_paths_cljs_test.cljc`. Searches for its main operations (`resolve-input-paths` and `sub-touches-path?`) likewise find no production caller outside that self-test/documentation.
- The namespace doc says it exists to power the App-DB downstream-subs popover. Commit `95d92180bb` (`strip per-block affordances from app-db current-state inspector`) deleted `app_db_diff_downstream.cljs`, its tests, and the require/install path from `app_db_diff`; that change explicitly removed the hover downstream-subs affordance.
- The resolver was introduced in commit `1c014c8275` for that feature. No replacement panel, testbed, example, build entry, facade, API page, or skill consumes the helper now.
- The current App-DB panel uses the first-class EDN inspector and no longer has a per-path downstream-sub popover, while the helper's long namespace contract continues to describe that retired UI as present.
- Bead title searches for `sub input paths` and `sub-input-paths`, plus description search for `sub-input-paths`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

Xray ships a nontrivial graph walk, fallback semantics, and a dedicated test suite for a UI feature that cannot invoke them. The stale contract makes subscription attribution appear supported by the current App-DB inspector and imposes maintenance on an algorithm with no product observation point.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphan namespace and its dedicated test, and delete or mark superseded any active spec prose that still promises the downstream-subs popover/input-path bridge. If that affordance is intentionally returning, require a concrete current UI consumer and integration coverage before retaining the resolver.

## Risks

Do not remove live subscription topology/tooling APIs merely because this narrower proxy is unused. Recheck concurrent App-DB work and published API policy before deletion; current evidence shows this helper is internal and has no production consumer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide namespace and operation searches confirm no current consumer, or a real newly landed caller is documented with end-to-end coverage.
- If still unconsumed, `sub_input_paths.cljc` and its dedicated test are removed.
- Current Xray specs/docs no longer describe the retired downstream-subs popover or this resolver as a live App-DB feature.
- Xray CLJS/JVM tests and the App-DB panel smoke/feature gates pass without changing live subscription tooling behavior.
notes: AUDIT PR #9080 (2026-09-03): REOPENED. The close reason records but leaves a live carrier at skills/re-frame2-xray/evals/evals.json:62: expected_output says an agent may offer the downstream-subs hover, although the affordance and its resolver were retired. No eval redesign, as the audit directed - the expectations array never mentioned the hover, so no expectation changed and the file's structure is untouched; re-parsed with python -m json.tool (exit 0) and json.load (32 evals). The audit also states this bead owns 'current Xray skill/documentation carriers', and acceptance criterion 3 requires that current Xray specs/docs no longer describe the retired popover as live, so the two carriers PR #9080 did not reach were repaired too, both inside the same skill: SKILL.md's routing table (the app-db row's Natural next step becomes **Views** for what re-rendered off the change - the real surface the retired popover jumped to) and references/panels-state.md (the 'Downstream-subs hover popover' paragraph deleted, and the Open when line's "what's downstream of [:cart :items]?" replaced with "when did [:cart :items] last change?", which the panel does answer). git grep -i downstream-sub over skills/ is now empty. Green: check_skill_eval_docs, check_skill_eval_packaging, check_skill_xray_tab_inventory_drift, check_skill_description_budget, check_skill_package_refs, check_skill_mcp_drift, check_doc_slugs, check_readme_links --ci, all exit 0. tools/xray/ was out of fence and needed nothing: its spec/004 and spec/021 already mark the overlay and this resolver retired.

title: effect-map contract drift: public docs and core comments still publish three keys and partial-success behavior
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9029, independent correctness/completeness finding. The authoritative implementation is unambiguous: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc closed-effect-map-keys contains seven keys (:db, :rf.db/runtime, :fx, :sensitive, :large, :clear-sensitive, :clear-large), and effect-map-defect plus router/commit-and-flow! refuse a foreign top-level key before any commit. PR #9029 correctly taught that contract in the migration skill, but a repository census found the old contract still presented as current outside that package.

Normative/public drift at the audited merge: spec/000-Vision.md:113; spec/Ownership.md:32; spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:32; spec/API.md:93,483-489,737 (including an effect-map key table that omits all four classification effects); and spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2734's preferred diagnostic. They say the closed set is only :db/:rf.db.runtime/:fx or only :db/:fx, so a port or app author can reject four valid commit-plane effects.

Core/source-facing drift: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:288-301 and :1067-1073 contradict the seven-key var immediately below them; re_frame/core.cljc:443-449 and interceptor.cljc:108-115 repeat the three-key set. Test narration is internally contradictory too: event_context_partition_test.clj:12-14 and :30-33 still says a foreign key is dropped and describes the error as dev-only, while its live test at :177-189 proves the current no-partial-commit behavior; fx_test.clj:484-489 still calls the closed set three keys. docs/api/re-frame.core.md:518 repeats the public falsehood.

Historical consumer comments also read as current behavior: tools/xray/.../machine_canvas.cljs:168-173 says the foreign fx is dropped while :db lands; the Hicasso native-IME/testbed accounts use the three-key set and say the timer vanished while the arm-state db write landed (docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-scripted-witness.md:193-197, implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:1653-1657, hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:425-430). Either state explicitly that this was the pre-rf2-04tx behavior, or rewrite them to the current refusal semantics; do not erase useful history.

This is one coherence sweep, not a request to redesign effect maps or add machinery. Ordinary examples may continue to show {:db ... :fx ...}; only prose that labels an exhaustive closed set or states recovery behavior must be exact. No exact existing Bead was found (title/description searches for effect-map, seven-key, classification keys, spec/API.md, and partial commit); rf2-n3mya is deliberately skill-scoped and is reopened separately for its two missed sites.
acceptance_criteria: Every exhaustive effect-map claim names all seven legal top-level keys (or clearly says "three everyday keys plus four classification effects"); spec/API.md's key table includes the four commit-plane classification keys. No current-contract prose says a foreign top-level key is dropped/ignored while :db or other siblings commit, or that its error is dev-only; historical narratives explicitly identify the former behavior as pre-rf2-04tx. Core docstrings/comments, the public spec/docs surfaces, and the named Xray/Hicasso/test comments agree with events.cljc and the existing no-partial-commit tests. Existing doc/link/API projection and relevant core test gates are green; no new gate is required solely for this wording sweep.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #9048 — exact owner remains open. PR #9048 correctly closes rf2-n3mya's skills-package remainder: M-8 now describes the seven legal keys and fail-closed refusal. title: skill(re-frame2-setup): first_counter_derivation.clj silently regenerates on any argument, and its writeback dirties the tree on Windows (LF + a stray blank line)
description:
FOUND while running gates for PR #9012 (rf2-pygpw/0ddz3/6uq6n cluster).

CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/first_counter_derivation.clj is documented in README.md and spec/design.md as the script that renders the two generated regions from the template. A worker reasonably reaches for a no-write verification mode.

TRUTH AT TIP. There is no such mode and no argument parsing at all: the script has no reference to *command-line-args*, and its last act is an unconditional (spit leaf (replace-region (slurp leaf) region)) at line 246. So 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' does NOT check — the argument is ignored, the script runs its normal generate-and-write path, exits 0, and the operator reads the 0 as a passing check. That is the failure-open shape: a well-formed green from an instrument that did the opposite of what was asked.

SECOND, and what makes it visible: the writeback is not byte-idempotent on Windows. Running it against an unmodified tip checkout leaves BOTH leaves modified — references/first-counter.md and references/entry-namespace.md — each with exactly one added blank line, plus git warning 'LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it' on both. The committed files are CRLF; the script writes LF. The content is otherwise correct: bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj Lock 0 (first-counter-region-is-the-template-render) passes at 35 tests / 271 assertions both before and after, so this is a line-ending and trailing-newline artifact of the writeback, NOT drift in the rendered region.

IMPACT. Low severity, but it fails open twice over. A worker who runs it 'to verify' gets a green that verified nothing AND a dirty tree carrying two files they did not edit — which, staged with a careless 'git add', lands a spurious whitespace diff on two drift-locked generated leaves. It was caught here only because the tree was checked for staged .beads before pushing.

FIX SHAPE (skills/re-frame2-setup/** only). Either (a) reject unknown arguments — fail closed with a usage line, which is the cheap half and kills the failure-open read on its own; and/or (b) add a real --check that renders and diffs without writing, since that is what callers evidently want. Separately, make the writeback preserve the leaf's existing line endings (or normalise on read) so a no-op regeneration is a no-op on Windows too.

GATE. bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj stays the drift gate and is unaffected. Verify by hand: from a clean tip checkout, run the script with a junk argument and assert git status is clean afterwards.

ACCEPTANCE. An unrecognised argument does not silently trigger a write; a no-op regeneration on Windows leaves git status clean.

NOT a blocker for PR #9012 — the two files were restored there and verified identical by git blob hash.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9036 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9036). Both symptoms reproduced from a clean checkout first, then fixed.

(1) Ignored argument. 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' wrote both leaves and exited 0 - the script parsed no arguments at all. It now fails CLOSED on any argument before a byte is written, mirroring the template's own hooks/gate-arg-keys! (which this script already loads for its substitution values). Chose the bead's option (a), not (b): the script only ever writes, so no argument is meaningful, and rather than growing a second checker the usage line routes the caller to the no-write check that already exists - 'bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj'. That avoids a divergent second source of truth. Junk argument now exits 2 with nothing written.

(2) Dirty tree - two distinct causes, and separating them was the substance. A REAL content change: replace-region emitted a newline the tail already carried, appending a blank line per leaf. The bead says 'exactly one'; it is in fact CUMULATIVE - three runs produced three added lines per leaf. A PHANTOM modification: the LF writeback over CRLF-checked-out leaves is not a content change at all (git diff empty, git hash-object --path matches the committed blob) but git status reports the file modified and every later git command warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF'. Fixed by rendering on LF (the convention setup_drift_test.clj already uses, since LF is what git stores) and restoring the leaf's existing endings on write.

Verified: three consecutive regenerations leave git status CLEAN, both leaves' blob hashes identical to the committed objects, CRLF preserved (401/185 CRLF, 0 bare LF). bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj green at 35 tests / 271 assertions, captured exit 0, and proven to read this worktree by planted fault (exit 1, 11 failures naming the plant; restore verified by blob hash 99af663ea1a3137cf5861b55e995f811b8b701d4).

title: skill(reagent-migration): the fully-migrated end state is untaught — with zero Reagent views left, (rf/init! substrate/adapter) retires the Reagent dependency
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:259-270` (MIG-15): "**`(rf/init! ...)` stays** ... Keep the app's existing adapter install; it is not Reagent-specific scaffolding to be deleted. ... Hicasso does ship an adapter of its own (`re-frame.hicasso.substrate`), but it is an optional module nothing under Hicasso's own source requires, so `h/mount!` neither installs it nor displaces what the app has."
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:283-293` (MIG-24): "drop `reagent.*` requires **only when the namespace has zero remaining uses**".
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:390-394` (MIG-23, the one mention, buried in the SSR recipe): "Adapter selection is not part of this migration ... (a Hicasso-only app may deliberately choose `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, but that is its own decision)."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:138-150` Done checklist and hand-off: "Views rewritten into Hicasso where it made sense; the rest stay on Reagent" — nothing for the case where nothing stays.
- `evals/evals.json` notes: "Do NOT re-grade this fixture [25] as 'switch to the Hicasso adapter': choosing an adapter is not part of this migration." (Correct for the part-migrated boot it grades; this bead does not touch it.)

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:1-25` — "Hicasso's own reactive-substrate adapter — the value an application installs with `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... what lets a Hicasso application depend on core plus Hicasso and nothing else: without this namespace an interactive one would have to add a SECOND dependency coordinate — `day8/re-frame2-uix` or a Reagent one — purely to obtain the second half, and then never write a line of that substrate's notation."
- `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:144-160` §Hicasso needs a substrate adapter: "every Hicasso application calls `rf/init!` with an adapter ... `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... ships inside `day8/re-frame2-hicasso`, so that line costs no coordinate."
- rf2-hvr5h (closed 2026-08-19, PR #8512): "a Hicasso application depends on core plus Hicasso and nothing else". `spec/Conventions.md:103` rosters `:rf.adapter/hicasso`.

## IMPACT

The part-migrated guidance is right and stays: while any Reagent view remains, the Reagent adapter stays. But the skill never names the END state. Once every view is converted, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require standing, and its only job was the substrate. Read together, MIG-15's "not scaffolding to be deleted" and MIG-24's "zero remaining uses" tell that author to keep `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` in `deps.edn` indefinitely — exactly the second-coordinate cost rf2-hvr5h built the substrate to remove. For a consumer that migrates to completion (the trigger the skill exists for), the skill leaves a dead dependency and never says the option exists. Trust-the-programmer means naming the choice, not withholding it.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only; eval 25's part-migrated grading unchanged)

1. `references/catalog-mechanical.md` MIG-24 — one closing paragraph: "When the last Reagent view is gone, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require, and it was only ever the substrate. `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` from `[re-frame.hicasso.substrate :as substrate]` (`:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso`) replaces that line and lets the app drop `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` from `deps.edn`. The author's call, not this skill's (cardinal rule 5), and never while a Reagent view remains." Add a one-line pointer from MIG-15's "stays" bullet.
2. `SKILL.md` Done checklist — one line: "If no Reagent view remains, the author was told the adapter choice is now open (MIG-24) — not switched for them."
3. Optional: a new M-tier behavioural eval ("every view is converted — can I drop Reagent now?") passing an answer that names `substrate/adapter` and the dependency drop as the author's decision, failing one that says the Reagent adapter must stay.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --ci`. The `substrate/adapter` spelling and `:kind` verified by hand against `substrate.cljs` (no gate reads prose).

## ACCEPTANCE

MIG-24 names the completed-migration option with the exact require, the `rf/init!` line and the two dependencies it retires; the done checklist carries the line; eval 25 unchanged; gates exit 0.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 (HEAD d12181c4c3; no relevant diff) on 2026-09-02 12:00:31 AUSEST.
acceptance_criteria: MIG-24 names re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter (:rf.adapter/hicasso) as the completed-migration option that lets the app drop day8/re-frame2-reagent + reagent, as the author's call; done checklist carries the line; eval 25 unchanged; gates exit 0
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9008 — REOPENED. MIG-24 and eval 29 now infer that when no Reagent VIEW remains, re-frame.adapter.reagent is the last Reagent use and both day8/re-frame2-reagent and reagent/reagent may go. That implication is not established: this skill is explicitly views-only, and a consumer can retain non-view reagent.core / reagent.ratom use (or another namespace requiring Reagent) after every view is Hicasso. Removing the coordinates then breaks the build. Keep the ergonomic option, but gate it on the reporter plus a repository-wide remaining-requires/API census. Distinguish the adapter-coordinate decision from removing a direct reagent/reagent entry, and add an eval case with zero Reagent views but a surviving non-view Reagent use so the skill says what must stay. This is the exact completed-migration owner, not a new bead.
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9036.

The coordinate split is directionally right, but its new proof for dropping reagent/reagent asks a call-site census to prove dependency absence. The reporter explicitly estimates Reagent API CALL SITES; it does not enumerate Reagent Vars/types/macros/config references used outside call-head position. The shipped text nevertheless says zero call sites plus no UNRESOLVED clause licenses dropping the coordinate.

Reproduced against the reporter at this PR tip with a live non-call use:

(ns app.core (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(def factory r/atom)

census/scan-string returns {:entries [], :reagent? true, :unresolved? false}; census/describe prints 0 Reagent API call site(s) across 1 file(s) that name Reagent, with no UNRESOLVED clause. Under the new MIG-24 rule this licenses removal, but factory still resolves reagent.core/atom and the build still needs reagent/reagent. The same blind class includes Reagent Vars passed as values, type/protocol references, and build/preload configuration outside scanned CLJS call heads.

The reporter already exposes the crucial distinction as files-with-reagent. Minimal repair: do not call zero calls/no unresolved a dependency proof. Require zero files naming the recognised Reagent namespaces after removing proven-orphan requires, and pair that with a whole-repository textual/dependency-config sweep for non-call references the reporter does not claim to census; otherwise keep reagent/reagent. An equally small tool-side alternative is a dedicated dependency-use census, but do not inflate the existing call-site estimand silently. Add one compact eval/control where r/atom is retained as a value rather than called, so the answer keeps the coordinate. Keep the two-decision ergonomic structure and eval 30; only the removal proof is unsound.
AUDIT PR #9036 RESOLVED 2026-09-03, worker/skillgates-a, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9042 (base 70f6cea39b). Worked the AUDIT REOPEN -- PR #9036 note (newest text-bearing mutation, 2026-09-03 02:25:11); ordered by bd history --json to the item's beginning (6 text/status-bearing changes across 730 entries).

PRIOR PASS RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE before building on it: implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn declares reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "2.0.1"} and its comment states it is "the only artefact that requires reagent.core/ratom/dom.client"; implementation/core/deps.edn declares none and says so explicitly. So Reagent does arrive TRANSITIVELY, dropping the adapter coordinate does break an app with surviving r/atom use, and the repair is to ADD a direct entry. That trap is kept verbatim, as is the two-decision structure and eval 30.

NEW AUDIT PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE in the reporter itself (migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/census.clj): describe's summary declares :estimand "Reagent API call sites, addressed at the CALL"; scan-string's docstring says :reagent? is "whether the file names a Reagent namespace at all"; and unresolved? is (and reagent? (empty? (into (:aliases ctx) (:referred ctx)))), so it is FALSE whenever the require carries an alias. Hence (def factory r/atom) censuses as 0 entries with :reagent? true and :unresolved? false -- exactly the audit's reproduction -- while factory still resolves reagent.core/atom and the build still needs the coordinate.

FIX. MIG-24's licence is no longer "zero call sites and no UNRESOLVED". It is now the FILES half of the reporter's own line -- 0 file(s) that name Reagent, after removing proven-orphan requires -- plus no UNRESOLVED clause, paired with a plain textual sweep of the whole repository across sources AND dependency/build configuration for the non-call references the reporter does not claim to census. The (def factory r/atom) counterexample is shown inline so the reader sees why the call count is the wrong instrument. Carriers of the same unsound proof also corrected: eval 29 expectation 4, the evals.json notes field, and the SKILL.md done-checklist line. NEW EVAL 31 (m-zero-call-sites-but-reagent-var-used-as-a-value) is the control the audit asked for: r/atom retained as a VALUE, so the census reads zero and the coordinate must still stay.

The tool-side alternative the note offered (a dedicated dependency-use census) was NOT taken: the codemod lives under migration/, outside this dispatch's fence, and the note names it the alternative rather than the minimal repair. The existing call-site estimand was not inflated.

GATE COVERAGE, measured rather than assumed: NO check_skill_*_drift.py gate reads skills/reagent-migration -- 0 hits across all 14, with the skills/re-frame2 control non-zero for 7 of them, so the instrument bites. check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py targets skills/re-frame-migration, a different skill. Filed as rf2-vgp1. title: docs(api/machines): canonical API doc teaches the bare :as machines alias Conventions reserves for application namespaces
description:
Found by rf2-3lhuj (PR #8902) while choosing which alias to give M-28's require
in the migration guide. Out of that dispatch's fence.

spec/Conventions.md has a normative section, "Require-alias dialect — a
framework subsystem namespace is aliased rf.<leaf>" (landed by d848371f60,
rf2-lgeron; no later commit touches it). It says the canonical alias for a
framework subsystem namespace re-frame.<leaf> is the dotted rf.<leaf>, shows
re-frame.machines :as rf.machines in its own worked require, and then states:

  A **bare** leaf alias (:as routing, :as machines, :as schemas) is
  **reserved for application namespaces**.

It names :as machines specifically as the form the framework yields to apps.

The published API doc teaches the opposite. docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:7
opens with [re-frame.machines :as machines] and spells every helper machines/...
throughout; docs/machines/tutorial.md:321 and
docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md:131 do the same, and
inspecting-machines.md:208 puts it in a troubleshooting table as the recommended
require. A repo-wide count of ':as machines' at tip returns 124 files, mostly
implementation tests, plus a comment in
implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:76.

So a reader who follows Conventions and a reader who follows the API doc write
different code, and the API doc's form is the one Conventions reserves for the
app's own myapp.machines.

NOT ASSERTING WHICH SIDE IS WRONG — that is the ruling this bead wants. Either
Conventions' dialect rule is the standard and the docs plus (over time) the
tests should move to rf.machines, or the rule has been overtaken in practice by
a 124-file majority and Conventions should be amended to match. Deciding it is
cheap; leaving two published spellings is what costs.

Note the migration guide was moved to the Conventions form by PR #8902, on the
grounds that a normative spec outranks an API page. If this bead rules the other
way, that one line in migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md M-28 moves with the
rest.
close_reason:
Done in PR #8912. RULED: Conventions wins; the docs move to rf.machines. Not amended.

This item asked which side was wrong - Conventions section Require-alias dialect (normative, landed under rf2-lgeron), which reserves the bare :as machines for APPLICATION namespaces and makes rf.machines canonical for the framework subsystem namespace, or the practice of a 124-file majority. Conventions is followed rather than re-litigated. That is the same call PR #8902 made for the migration guide and PR #8905 made for the spec tree, so the published corpus now carries ONE spelling instead of two rather than a third precedent.

18 call spellings and 7 require clauses corrected across six documents: docs/api/re-frame.machines.md (9 calls, 2 requires), docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md (4 calls, 2 requires), docs/machines/tutorial.md (2 calls, 1 require), docs/machines/concepts.md (1 call), spec/008-Testing.md (1 call, 1 require), spec/Construction-Prompts.md (1 call, 1 require). The last two were not named in this item and were found by the same census - a spec file teaching the reserved form is strictly worse than an API page doing it.

The API page Surfaces split two ways bullet already said the helpers are reached as re-frame.machines/<name> and not rf/<name>; it now names the alias and links Conventions section Require-alias dialect, so the page sources its own spelling instead of asserting it.

NOT CHANGED: live :as machines require aliases in implementation/ and tools/ source. Roughly 124 files, a real compile surface, for a defect that is entirely about published prose - and a mass rename would foreclose the amend-Conventions option this item deliberately left open. Prose was corrected; live aliases stand. If a future ruling amends Conventions instead, only documents move back, not code.

CENSUS TRAP worth keeping: a loose search for bare machines/<name> in markdown returns about 90 hits, nearly all of them NOT call sites - the late-bind hook keywords (:machines/teardown-on-frame-destroy!, :machines/spawn-fx), the MCP op names (machines/list, machines/describe), and source file paths (machines/transition.cljc). Narrowing to the six helpers spec/api-manifest.edn marks :facade? false gives the real 19.

ONE SITE REMAINS, out of this dispatch fence: spec/005-StateMachines.md line 4100 carries (machines/machine-transition definition snapshot event) inside a code fence with no require beside it. description:

title: spec(xray): the mount-fn contract's step-3 universal pins [Panel] and is narrower than the code
description:
`tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md` §`The mount-fn contract` opens with the UNIVERSAL
"Every `mount-<panel>!` fn:" and its step 3 says the fn wraps the panel's view in

    [rf/frame-provider {:frame :rf/xray} [Panel]]

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk 04e4acaf80, after #9617 landed:
  - the universal and its literal `[Panel]` are at 007-UX-IA.md step 3 as quoted above
  - `panels.cljs:145` documents an `:instance-id` opt for `mount-app-db-diff!` ONLY
  - `panels.cljs:289` documents it as OPTIONAL

So a NAMED standalone app-db-diff mount builds `[Panel {:instance-id "left"}]`, and the
universal's literal `[Panel]` is narrower than the code.

=== WHY THIS IS DELIBERATELY LOW PRIORITY AND NOT A CORRECTNESS BUG ===

Nothing is CONTRADICTED today. `[Panel]` is exactly what `render-panel!` builds in the
nil-props case, which is every call site in the tree right now -- the two-argument form
is an affordance for hosts, not something Xray itself calls. Discovered by the rf2-s2g7
worker (xrayspec-a), which correctly REPORTED it rather than sweeping it: it is not an
opts-COUNT statement, so it is not a fourth member of rf2-jw2ny's coordinated set, and
folding it into that PR would have widened a scoped slice.

=== WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN NOTHING ===

`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` §6 names this class outright -- "When a rule says
*every*, check the quantifier" -- and this tree has just paid for the same class three
times over: rf2-jw2ny's coordinated set went stale silently precisely because prose
universals about the mount surface drift behind code and NO GATE GRADES ANY OF THEM.
This is the same surface, one section along.

=== THE REPAIR, WHICH IS ONE CLAUSE ===

Say that the fn wraps the view in a frame-provider, and that a mount fn accepting
further per-panel opts threads them as props onto `[Panel]` -- so the universal stays
universal instead of pinning one call shape. Do NOT enumerate `:instance-id` here; that
belongs in the `:instance-id` section which already carries it, and a second enumeration
is how the last set went stale (four coordinated statements, three of them wrong).

Verify by reading. No gate covers this prose.
close_reason:
Delivered by PR #9623, merged to trunk at bad36b747c (rebase). One file, 3 insertions / 1
deletion — `tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md`.

Step 3 now says the fn wraps the view in the frame-provider and adds: "A mount fn that takes
further per-panel opts threads them as props onto the wrapped view — `[Panel {...}]` in place of
the bare `[Panel]`." The universal stays universal instead of pinning one call shape.

THE RESTRAINT THE BRIEF ASKED FOR WAS THE RIGHT CALL, AND THE WORKER CONFIRMED WHY. It was told
NOT to enumerate `:instance-id` here, on the ground that a second enumeration is how the last set
went stale. It then measured that the xray spec ALREADY carries three coordinated statements of
that opt — 007-UX-IA.md:1802, 008-Embedding-Contract.md:549, API.md:410 — so a fourth would have
been exactly the liability rf2-jw2ny's set already demonstrated. The instruction was not
hypothetical; it avoided a measured recurrence.

title: hygiene: two standing worker branches carry unique work — inventory and disposition
description:
AN INVENTORY, SO A CHEAP DECISION STAYS CHEAP. Two worker branches carry commits that exist NOWHERE ELSE,
neither has a worktree or a live agent, and until now nothing recorded what they hold — so the only way to
decide their fate was to go and read them. That is the whole reason this bead exists. It asks for no work.

MEASURED ON TRUNK c255a4c3d7. `git cherry origin/main <branch>` marks every commit below `+`. **Read that as
the ABSENCE OF PROOF that the work is upstream, never as evidence that it is not** — under rebase-merge a
`+` is what an unmerged commit and a rewritten-but-landed one both look like. The diffstats are the real
evidence, and both branches touch paths whose content is not on trunk.

=== worker/receipts-hic081 — 3 commits, last 2026-08-11, 381 insertions / 2 deletions, 3 files ===
    ae14841ab3  spike(hicasso): split the projection out of the runtime, as the erasure gate demanded
    418312d680  spike(hicasso): the receipt witness, green on the hicasso node lane
    fece72f80a  spike(hicasso): capability receipts derived from the runtime's own leavings
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs
A self-contained capability-receipts spike with its own test, entirely inside `implementation/hicasso/`. A
month old — the oldest thing in the repository that is not on trunk.

=== worker/xspike-a — 1 commit, last 2026-09-09, 899 insertions, 10 files ===
    862e0d1d93  spike(rf2-k97c.1): build the App-DB panel both ways, on two adapters
  implementation/shadow-cljs.edn  <- HOT ZONE
  tools/xray/testbeds/xspike/{app,arm_a,arm_b,boot,hic}.cljs  (and others)
The two-arm App-DB panel comparison that fed rf2-k97c.1. **Its value may already be fully extracted**: the
Xray epic has since ruled its substrate design and landed five increments, so the spike's CONCLUSIONS are
likely recorded on rf2-k97c and its children while only the apparatus lives here. Someone deciding this
should check that before treating the branch as the sole carrier.

**AND IT TOUCHES A HOT-ZONE FILE.** Reviving it means `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, which is sequential
by convention — so a revival is a sequenced dispatch, never a parallel one, and it will conflict with any
live worker holding that file.

=== THE THREE OPTIONS, none of which the mayor should take unasked ===
  * DELETE BOTH. Irreversible once the remote copy goes too. Cheapest, and correct if the conclusions are
    recorded elsewhere.
  * READ THEN DELETE. Dispatch one worker to extract whatever is not already on a bead, then delete. Costs
    one worker; turns apparatus into a record.
  * LEAVE THEM. Free, and the standing cost is exactly this: two branches a future hygiene sweep must
    re-examine, plus the risk that "leave them" is a decision nobody remembers making.

THE MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION, offered rather than acted on: LEAVE `worker/receipts-hic081` and DELETE
`worker/xspike-a` after confirming rf2-k97c's rulings carry its conclusions — the hicasso spike is small,
isolated and cheap to keep, whereas the xspike apparatus is large, touches a hot-zone file, and is the more
likely of the two to be genuinely superseded.

NOTHING HERE IS URGENT AND NOTHING BLOCKS ON IT. The method treats this residue as a standing cost the
operator clears on request, not a defect to engineer away. Recorded so the clearing costs a minute.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY THE MAYOR, NO OPERATOR TIME AND NO WORKER CONSUMED. **BOTH BRANCHES STAY.** The three options this
bead offered were largely answered before it was filed, by records the mayor did not check first. That
omission is the finding worth keeping.

=== worker/receipts-hic081 — ALREADY RULED KEPT, 2026-09-07, ON rf2-jojz ===

That bead's close reason reads, verbatim: **"worker/receipts-hic081 — KEPT, UNTOUCHED. No tag. No deletion."**
Tip ae14841ab3ac, verified unmoved at the time under a standing ruling, in a sweep that deleted two other
branches beside it. So this was never an open question; it is a ruling that has been in force for three days,
and this bead re-opened it out of ignorance rather than on new evidence. Nothing here supersedes rf2-jojz.

=== worker/xspike-a — ITS OWN BEAD CALLS IT A THROWAWAY RECORD, AND EVERYTHING IT PROVED IS PRESERVED ===

rf2-k97c.1's close reason: **"Commits pushed to worker/xspike-a (862e0d1d93) as a throwaway record."** That
is the disposition of the work's own author, made at the time, and it is the right reading — the branch is
APPARATUS, and the CONCLUSIONS are all on beads:

  * the spike report itself, 25,468 bytes in rf2-k97c.1's notes, appended in three chunks and verified by
    interior probes with a negative control at 0;
  * all four pre-committed decision numbers (a) through (d), including the corrected site count of 262
    against the epic's ~51 — a 5x undercount that the spike is the reason we know about;
  * the three findings that outlive it: the fault line is the tool's renderer versus the adapter's renderer;
    `rf/frame-provider` needs no change; and the site-count correction;
  * rf2-k97c.2's ruling of DESIGN B, with its evidence.

So deleting the branch would lose apparatus and no knowledge.

=== SO WHY KEEP IT? BECAUSE DELETION IS IRREVERSIBLE AND BUYS NOTHING MEASURABLE ===

One branch of 899 insertions costs a line in a hygiene listing. Against that, deletion is unrecoverable, and
the stance this project runs under — *we are not over-engineering*, *we trust the programmer* — does not
license an irreversible act on someone else's repository to reclaim nothing. **Keeping it is the cheap
option; deleting it is the expensive one, and that is the reverse of how a tidiness reflex reads it.**

Both branches therefore STAY, and this is now the record a future hygiene sweep reads instead of re-deriving
it. If either is ever deleted, use rf2-jojz's method, which is recorded there and is worth reusing: a single
LEASE-PROTECTED push, `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-tip> origin :<ref>`, then verify the
absence against a control read that returns something, so an empty result is a check that passed rather than
a broken instrument.

=== THE MAYOR'S ERROR, RECORDED BECAUSE THE SHAPE WILL RECUR ===

This bead was filed as an operator decision after measuring WHAT the branches contain and never asking
WHETHER THEY HAD ALREADY BEEN RULED ON. Both had. The method warns about exactly this — one mayor held nine
items for the operator when three were genuinely operator calls and the rest were already answered — and the
check that would have caught it is one query over closed beads for the branch name, which is how both
rulings were found in the end. **Search the tracker's CLOSED beads before filing a decision; a hygiene
question in particular is likely to have been asked before.**

AND ONE INSTRUMENT NOTE FROM THE SAME SEARCH: the first probe's positive control tested
`description + notes` while the probe itself tested `description + notes + close_reason`. A control on a
different field set validates nothing, and here the answer lived in `close_reason` for BOTH branches — so a
broken control would have hidden both rulings. Match the control to the probe's field set, not merely to its
target.

title: skills: the re-frame2-pair fixture pins React 18.3.1 and nothing records whether that is deliberate
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 while answering Mike's question "are the /skills updated with the new React version?" after
PR #9576 put React 19.3.0 on trunk. FOUR React pins live under `skills/`, and three of them are settled:

  skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md          19.3.0   moved by #9576
  skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/package.json         19.3.0   moved by #9576
  skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md          ^19.0.0  CORRECT AS A RANGE, leave it
  skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/package.json            18.3.1   the question

THE FLOOR-GATE ENTRY IS NOT STALE AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED". It is migration advice — its own surrounding text
reads "if `package.json` pins react/react-dom to 17 or 18, bump both to ^19" — so the caret is the point. It
already admits 19.3.0, and pinning it exactly would convert a floor into a mandate. Recorded here because a
future version sweep will find it and want to change it.

THE QUESTION, AND IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A DEFECT CLAIM. #9576's worker deliberately left the pair
fixture at 18.3.1, grouping it in their close reason with "the 18.3.1 pair fixture, and every 19.2.0 that
records THE VERSION A BEHAVIOUR WAS PROBED AGAINST" — i.e. reading it as a historical record. It is not a
historical record. It is a `devDependencies` entry in a fixture that CI installs and compiles:

  .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:2409   arms skills_structural from skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/*
  .github/workflows/test.yml:6179                   the re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure job that builds it

So on every armed change, CI builds that fixture against React 18.3.1.

WHAT THAT SITS AGAINST, both in the same tree:
  * skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:111 states plainly "Reagent 2.x needs React 19".
  * skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md treats 17/18 as the versions a project migrates OFF,
    with React 19 as the floor.

TWO READINGS, AND BOTH ARE PLAUSIBLE — THIS IS WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED:
  (a) DELIBERATE. The pair tool's job is to meet real projects where they are, and a pre-migration project on
      React 18 is exactly what it would meet in the wild. Compiling the fixture on 18.3.1 proves the tool
      works there. If this is the answer, the fix is ONE LINE OF COMMENT in the fixture saying so, not a
      version bump — and that is probably the whole of this bead.
  (b) STALE. The fixture was pinned when 18.3.1 was current and nobody has revisited it. If this is the
      answer, bump it to match trunk and let the fixture's own suite say whether anything moves.

FROM OUTSIDE, (a) AND (b) ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE, and that is the actual defect regardless of which is true:
nothing anywhere records the intent, so every future version sweep re-asks this question and every reviewer
has to re-derive it. Whichever way it goes, the deliverable is that the intent becomes readable.

FIRST STEPS: read the fixture's own tests and the re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure job to see what the fixture
actually exercises; check whether anything in the pair skill's prose states a supported React range; then
either write the one-line intent comment or bump the pin and run the job. Do NOT touch the floor-gate range,
and do NOT treat the two 19.3.0 pins as needing anything.

P4 because nothing is broken today: the fixture compiles and its job is green. The cost is re-derivation, not
failure.
notes:
MAYOR FINDING, 2026-09-10, measured rather than dispatched — because settling this cost two greps and a
worker would have been the wrong instrument for it.

THERE IS A THIRD READING, AND IT IS THE TRUE ONE. The bead offered two: (a) the 18.3.1 pin is DELIBERATE,
exercising a pre-migration project; (b) it is STALE. Both assume React is exercised. It is not.

  * The fixture's only runner is `test:pure` — `shadow-cljs compile pure-test && node target/pure-test.js`.

title: hic: tool.cljs unjoinable-intent branch (id-less trace bundle) — reachable per Spec 009, unexercised

THE EVIDENCE, all four legs at source:
1. read-intents' window is exactly (trace-tooling/trace-buffer fid) per frame (tool.cljs:633; explain-render's window :795 is the same door). The per-frame ring is the ONLY supplier of bundles to intent-rows.
2. The ring cannot retain an id-less event. push-to-ring! guards (when (and dispatch-id frame-id) ...) — implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:251-259 — and its docstring names the rule: frameless emits stream live to listeners only and are never retained. That is Spec 009's B3 ruling verbatim: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:879 'frameless events SKIP the rings entirely ... NEVER retained in any ring', :881 'no shared uncorrelated bucket, no fallback slot', :965 'Frameless events bypass the ring'.
3. A bundle is minted ONLY from ring run-keys: frame-ring-event-bundles maps :run-order and event-bundle seeds :dispatch-id from that key (tooling.cljc:476-488, :414-420), so a bundle's :dispatch-id is non-nil by construction. The other trace-rings writers (set-frame-events-retained! ~:204, clear-trace-buffer! ~:563, clear-trace-rings! ~:582, the inherited-default retune ~:646) resize or empty rings and mint no run key.
4. The uncorrelated events Spec 009 SDispatch-correlation admits (registry-time emits, REPL evals — spec line 72) therefore exist on the LIVE listener stream only. title: [MIKE ONLY - RULING] Xray inspector is IMPOSSIBLE in a release static export since 58bd56635b, but tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md promises it in 3 places - accept the loss (PR #10140, landed, revertible) or reopen the A1-wrap ruling to restore it
description:
**MIKE'S RULING WANTED. Nothing is broken by leaving this open — the question is whether a capability the spec promises should be restored or formally dropped.**

`58bd56635b` (rf2-y8doi.60, ruled A1-wrap 2026-09-21, Mike's own commit) took Xray's release footprint to zero by wrapping the four top-level `rf/reg-view` sites in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)`. That was deliberate and it worked. **Its side effect was to make an Xray inspector IMPOSSIBLE in any `:advanced` release build**, and nothing reported that.

## WHY IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, not merely absent — from the commit's own message

> the macro both registers the view AND `def`s the symbol to `(rf/view id)` — relocating the registration alone would bind nil in DEV too … Each of the four is now wrapped in the same `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` the boot block uses, **with the whole form inside the gate so the `def` travels with its registration**

Under `:advanced` with `goog.DEBUG` false the gate is false, so the `def` never executes and the four symbols never bind. Any unconditional consumer then throws. Measured by the rf2-n7lql worker: `views/edn_widget.cljs:116` renders `ei/edn-inspector` unconditionally, giving `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. This is a SECOND breakage, independent of the `:rf.error/image-zero-match` that bead diagnosed — proved by making the seat self-sufficient and watching the failure MOVE from `check-story-static.cjs:274` to `:282`.

**So no repair confined to the image-assembly path can make Xray render in a release build.** Restoring the capability means revisiting the A1-wrap ruling itself.

## WHAT THE SPEC PROMISES, in three places at trunk `aa5c839f2b`

`tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md`:

- `:63` — "This does **not** remove the Xray panel embed that Story imports directly; the published shell can retain its inspector without the devtools preload."
- `:282` — table row, *What gets bundled*: "Story's directly imported Xray panel embed | bundled; distinct from the omitted devtools preload"
- `:288` — table row, *What gets stripped*: "`:devtools/preloads` (Xray preload) | Story's direct Xray embed import is separate"

**That promise has been FALSE since `58bd56635b` landed, and nothing said so.** The spec was not edited by that commit; its message says "The framework is unchanged" and "Dev is unchanged", both true, and neither reaches the published-shell claim.

## THE TWO DISPOSITIONS

**(A) ACCEPT THE LOSS — what PR #10140 does.** Story's static export neither mounts nor drives Xray; the spec is rewritten to record the mechanism. The gate goes green. The published shell ships with no inspector. **This is already landed in #10140 and is revertible as one small isolated hunk** if Mike rules the other way.

**(B) RESTORE THE CAPABILITY.** Find a release-safe way to keep the four `reg-view` `def`s bound without the devtools preload — separating the `def` from the registration, or a release-safe registration path — and revert the spec edit. This reopens the A1-wrap ruling and is materially larger than (A).

## THE MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: ACCEPT (A) NOW, RULE ON (B) SEPARATELY

Merging (A) makes the spec TRUE for the first time since `58bd56635b`; holding it keeps the spec lying AND leaves a P1 gate red on trunk, which also blocks PR #10139. Nothing in (A) forecloses (B): if Mike wants the inspector back, the spec edit is reverted along with the code when the capability returns. **Leaving a red gate on trunk to protect a sentence that is already false is the worse trade.**

What is genuinely unruled is the CONSEQUENCE rather than the commit: Mike ruled A1-wrap, and the evidence is that the published-shell cost was not part of that ruling — the regression guard shipped in the same commit says in its own comment block that it "cannot discriminate the production claim", which is exactly the claim that turned out false.

## FENCE

Do not dispatch (B) without Mike's ruling. It reopens a ruling made 2026-09-21 and touches `tools/xray/src` view registration, which is the surface `58bd56635b` deliberately shaped.
notes:
STATUS CORRECTION 2026-09-21 — **(A) IS NOW MERGED TO TRUNK, not merely landed on a branch.** The description above says "PR #10140, landed, revertible", which was true when written and understates it now.

PR #10140 merged at trunk **`2d86a04fa1`** on the five clauses at band 88 — 0 pending, 0 failed, `All required checks passed` present by NAME, 4 runs completed at the full 40-character head, matrix unmoved. The rewritten promise is live in `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md` at that commit.

**THE RULING IS STILL OPEN AND NOTHING ABOUT THIS MERGE PREJUDGES IT.** The mayor merged on its own standing recommendation — recorded before the merge, not after — that (A) should land immediately because it makes the spec TRUE for the first time since `58bd56635b`, while holding it would have kept the spec asserting a falsehood AND left a P1 gate red on trunk blocking PR #10139. That reasoning is about SEQUENCING, not about the capability question, which is yours.

**WHAT REVERTING NOW COSTS, stated honestly so the choice is real rather than nominal.** Before the merge the revert was one hunk on a branch. Now it is a revert against trunk: `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md` back to its pre-merge text, plus `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs`, which is where the fix actually lives. That is still small and isolated — two files, +113/-40 in total — and the diff is one commit, so `git revert` reaches it directly. **But reverting the code half re-reds the story-static gate**, because the crash it prevents is real and independent of the spec's wording. So a revert is only coherent as part of choosing (B): restore the capability AND the promise together. Reverting the spec alone would put the tree back to asserting something false.

**THE DECISION IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE:** does a published Story static export ship with a working Xray inspector? (A) says no, and the tree now matches that. (B) says yes, and needs a release-safe way to keep the four `reg-view` `def`s bound without the devtools preload — which reopens the A1-wrap ruling of `58bd56635b`.

If (B): file it as its own bead and fence it behind nothing — the surface is free now that rf2-n7lql is closed and its worktree is reapable. If (A): close this bead with the ruling recorded, and the tree needs no further change.
close_reason:
RULED BY MIKE, 2026-09-21: **(A) ACCEPT THE LOSS.**

**A published Story static export does NOT ship with a working Xray inspector, and that is now the intended behaviour rather than a defect.** The capability is formally dropped, not deferred.

## WHAT THIS RULES, PRECISELY

The A1-wrap ruling of `58bd56635b` (rf2-y8doi.60) stands, and **its published-shell cost is accepted**. That cost was not visible when A1-wrap was ruled — the regression guard shipped in that same commit says in its own comment block that it "cannot discriminate the production claim", which is exactly the claim that turned out false — so this bead existed to put the consequence in front of Mike once it was visible. It has been, and the answer is that the cost is acceptable.

**(B) is DECLINED**, not parked: no work is to be dispatched to restore release-build Xray rendering, and the A1-wrap ruling is not to be reopened on this account. Anyone reaching for it later needs a new bead and a demonstrated consumer, neither of which exists today.

## THE TREE ALREADY MATCHES THE RULING — NO FURTHER CHANGE IS NEEDED

PR #10140 merged at `2d86a04fa1` and rewrote `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md` to record the mechanism truthfully. Verified at source at trunk `e3da2d1e98` before closing, rather than from an earlier report: the old promise — "the published shell can retain its inspector without the devtools preload" — survives in that file at exactly ONE site, line 67, and it survives only INSIDE the correction's own quotation of the refuted claim, immediately followed by **"That was wrong, and the published export was crashing on it."**

**That single hit is a MENTION, not an assertion, and a census keyed on the phrase alone reads it as a surviving falsehood.** Control on the same file: `Xray` reads 11. Anybody re-auditing this must read the context, not the count.

The spec now enumerates both independent reasons, which is the durable part of this record:

1. **Nothing registers Xray.** `:devtools/preloads` applies to `watch`/`compile` only, never `release`. Story never calls `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/init!`, the only other supported install route, so seating Xray's frame globs `day8.re-frame2-xray.**` over an empty pool and core's deliberate `:rf.error/image-zero-match` guard fires.
2. **Xray's views are undefined.** `reg-view` carries its `def` INSIDE the gate, so under `:advanced` with `goog.DEBUG` false the four top-level symbols never bind and ungated consumers throw a `TypeError`.

The two are independent — the rf2-n7lql worker proved it by making the seat self-sufficient and watching the failure MOVE from `check-story-static.cjs:274` to `:282`, rather than disappear. That is why no repair confined to the image-assembly path could ever have worked, and why (B) would have meant reopening the view-registration surface itself.

## WHAT MADE THIS WORTH A RULING RATHER THAN A FIX

The spec asserted a capability the build could not deliver, and **nothing reported the gap** — the commit that removed the capability truthfully said "the framework is unchanged" and "dev is unchanged", and neither statement reaches the published-shell claim. The cost landed on the next PR whose diff happened to arm the gate: PR #10139, whose entire diff was two lines inside comments, went red three times for a regression it did not cause.

That reporting half is a separate defect with its own lineage (rf2-5dihy, and the false-all-clear correction rf2-xbig3 that followed it). This bead owned only the capability question.

## FENCE, NOW DISCHARGED

The bead's fence read "Do not dispatch (B) without Mike's ruling." The ruling is (A), so (B) is not to be dispatched at all.

title: False: #10161 settings reply ownership accepts another account during an occupied-name rename
description:
Audit of https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10161 at 644624cea350253879cb8812f807b2f7f08618ba (merged 2026-09-21T20:08:12Z). The original different-username overlap is fixed, but settings.cljs:476-485 claims a departed account can never answer for the current save because usernames are unique. The new success handler compares the returned User username to :pending :username, which is the UNSAVED requested username, not an authenticated identity or issuance proof.

Reproduction: Alice starts a settings PUT and its successful reply is delayed. Log out, sign in as Bob, load settings, change the username field to alice, and submit. Bob's request is awaiting the backend's occupied-username rejection. The form now records {:owner "bob" :username "alice"}. Alice's earlier successful reply names alice; Q1 passes. Q2 compares Bob (pending owner) to Bob (live session), so it also passes. The handler stores Alice's User and token and navigates to Alice's profile before Bob's failure arrives. No same-account relogin or backend violation is required: a user may submit an occupied name, and usernames being unique after a successful update does not establish which outstanding request produced a reply.

Independent Babashka probe evaluated the actual merged draft/reset/seed/begin-submit/success functions and actual auth ownership/session-write functions. It confirms the cross-account write and navigation. Controls: ordinary Alice reply while Bob saves as bob is refused; Bob's own reply and a valid rename to robert are accepted. Probe ai/probe-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10161-1.clj; gate-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10161-1.log/.exit captured 0 with the correct guarded root. This is a source-function reproduction, not a browser or full CLJS run. The tested settings blob equals the merge blob d23c3e2a50f1ea70f53317fdfce047a34f263f74.

Correction: correlate success to the issuing request or suppress superseded requests without treating a desired username as established account identity. Preserve the one map reply payload and token classification; the canned/demo path must preserve whatever correlation contract is chosen. Use the existing managed-HTTP/app-level facilities, not a new framework abstraction. Extend the existing implementation-side RealWorld overlap coverage to the occupied-name rename and keep rejected replies from touching the newer auth/form/request. The source's known same-account limitation is not this defect.
acceptance_criteria: While Alice success is delayed and Bob has submitted a rename to alice, the old success leaves Bob auth, draft, pending save and navigation untouched; Bob failure still settles his own form. Existing distinct-account overlap, logout, normal own success/failure and valid rename controls remain green, and token egress remains classified. Tests stay under implementation/.

Correctness: Actual merged source-function probe confirms old cross-account success refusal and Bob failure settlement, then reproduces permanent rejection of a fresh Alice save after both originals settled. Fresh-ledger and distinct-name controls succeed; captured probe exit 0, correct worktree root. Success token remains at the classified map payload path. Implementation quality: The small app-level ledger avoids transport-mode dependence but retains ghost entries indefinitely; fix the bounded recovery defect without expanding the framework API. MERGED as PR #10169, rebase merge commit 3093a0db1c389af5f35c9f19312a28e0b077896f, which is trunk. Three files, 321 insertions / 40 deletions: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/settings.cljs`, `.../schema.cljs`, and `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs`.

THE DEFECT, stated so a future reader needs nothing else. `:settings/submit-success` identified a reply by the username the form REQUESTED — a string the user typed, not an identity anyone owns. Submitting an already-occupied name is ordinary behaviour, so a PREVIOUS account's own successful reply could answer for a rename claiming that name, installing that account's User record and token over the live session. The original code was:

    (not (and (some? awaited)
              (= (:username (:user value)) (:username awaited))))

where `(:username awaited)` is `:pending :username`, the requested name.

THE CORRECTION. A top-level app-db ledger of saves still on the wire, each entry recording the account name that save will report back. A success is acted on only when EXACTLY ONE unanswered save claims the reported account AND that save is the one the form awaits.
