title: xray: snap-to-LIVE spelled L at eight further sites against keybinding.cljs's unshifted l, and spec/018-Event-Spine.md contradicts itself (l at 175/2055, L at 307/1385)
description:
The snap-to-LIVE keybinding is spelled `L` at EIGHT further sites, against `keybinding.cljs`'s unshifted `l`. PR #10170 (rf2-bc17l finding 1) corrected two of ten; these are the remaining eight, and leaving the tree at two-of-ten is worse than either end state.

## The authority

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:298-299`:

    ;; L (lowercase, unshifted) — snap to LIVE
    (and (not shift?) (or (= "l" k) (= "KeyL" code)))

**Unshifted `l`.** The binding immediately below it requires `shift?` for `G`, so these spine listings encode shift state IN THE CASE OF THE LETTER — which is why `L` is not a cosmetic inconsistency: inside its own local convention it positively asserts a modifier that does not exist. `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:474` and `docs/.../launch-lifecycle.md:79` corroborate, the latter saying in terms that "Shift+L does nothing".

## The eight sites

Found by a three-pass census (line-oriented / flattened / comment-stripped-then-flattened) over all 5571 tracked files:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:36` — **visible ONLY to the flattened pass**; the phrase spans lines 35-36.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:312`
- `tools/xray/test/.../edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs:5381` and `:5494`
- `spec/API.md:46`
- `spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:397`
- `spec/018-Event-Spine.md:307` and `:1385`

**`spec/018-Event-Spine.md` CONTRADICTS ITSELF**: it reads `l` at lines 175 and 2055 and `L` at 307 and 1385. So this is not merely staleness — one file currently teaches both spellings.

**One site was excluded after being read, and do not re-flag it**: `tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:350`, where `M`/`L`/`T`/`P` are route badges rather than keybindings.

## Sequencing

`spec/API.md` is a HOT-ZONE file (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) and is one holding with `spec/api-manifest.edn` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`. This change is a keybinding LETTER IN PROSE, not a public name, so it should not move the manifest — **verify that rather than assuming it**, and if the manifest gate disagrees, stop and report rather than regenerating.

No other item is in `spec/API.md` at the time of filing, but re-check before editing.

## Verification

**No gate reads a keybinding letter out of prose.** That is the point of this item: the deliverable is verified by hand against `keybinding.cljs` and by nothing else. Expect a plant to come back green and treat that as a result rather than a failure — it is how you establish that hand-verification is the whole of the evidence.

`tools/xray/README.md` and `docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md` are already correct — do not touch them.

## WHAT IS MEASURED AND CERTAIN

    examples/core/login/index.html          data-rf-xray-host  ->  0
    examples/core/login/stories.index.html  data-rf-xray-host  ->  2

PR #10174 added the layout-host shell to **`stories.index.html` only**. `index.html` was not touched and carries none.

## WHAT THE README PROMISES

`examples/core/login/README.md:94`, inside the **How to run** section and attached to the `examples/login-with-stories` command:

> Open the printed URL for the live login app, or append `#/stories` to it for the Story shell with every reachable state as a variant. Press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd> on **either surface** to open Xray over the auth-submit cascade.

"Either surface" is the live app AND the Story shell. `#/stories` is a HASH route, so both surfaces are the same served page — whichever page that is.

## WHY THE FIXED PAGE IS PROBABLY NOT THE SERVED ONE

  * `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:637` gives dev-http port 8041 the roots
    `["../examples/core/login" "out/examples/login-with-stories"]`. A request for `/` resolves against
    the FIRST root that has an `index.html` — `examples/core/login/index.html`, the page with 0 hosts.
  * `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:216` stages with
    `fs.copyFileSync(entry.htmlSrc, path.join(entry.outDir, 'index.html'))` — it RENAMES the source page
    to `index.html` in the output dir. Its header (line 20) says it derives the source folder and
    `index.html` from `shadow-cljs.edn`, and the `:examples/login-with-stories` build block
    (`:2010-2018`) names no html file of its own.
  * So on both readings the served page is an `index.html` derived from the example folder, and
    `stories.index.html` is reachable only by asking for that filename explicitly — which the README
    never tells a reader to do.

**If that holds, the chord still reaches `layout-host()`, finds no `[data-rf-xray-host]`, reports `:missing-layout-host` and mounts nothing — on BOTH surfaces — which is exactly the defect finding 2 was filed against.**

## WHAT IS *NOT* ESTABLISHED, AND MUST BE BEFORE ANYONE EDITS

**I did not run it, and I did not read `examples-staging.cjs` end to end.** Two things could still falsify the above and each is cheap to settle:

  1. What `entry.htmlSrc` actually resolves to for `:examples/login-with-stories` — if the resolver
     prefers a `stories.index.html` when the build's `:init-fn` names a stories host, the staged page is
     the FIXED one and only root ORDER decides.
  2. Whether the dev-http server prefers the first root or the last. If it prefers
     `out/examples/login-with-stories`, the staged page wins over the source folder's.

**Settle it by RUNNING the documented command and reading what is served**, not by further static reasoning — `npm run dev:example -- examples/login-with-stories`, open the printed URL, and check the served HTML for `data-rf-xray-host`. That is one command and it is decisive where this note is not.

## SCOPE OF THE FIX, ONCE SETTLED

Almost certainly one line: give `examples/core/login/index.html` the same shell `stories.index.html` now carries (itself copied from `examples/core/counter/index.html`, the proven one). Do **not** remove the shell from `stories.index.html` — the `rf2-fn0kx.5` worker deliberately gave both login pages identical bodies because an open A/B question about that file rests on their being byte-identical apart from `<title>`/meta, and diverging them would destroy that evidence.

`rf2-fn0kx.2`'s close reason states that finding 2 was fixed by adding the shell, and quotes the README's "either surface" promise as the thing repaired. **What landed is narrower than that sentence implies.** The close reason is accurate about WHAT changed (`stories.index.html`) and wrong in its implication that the promise is now satisfied. ## The decision in one sentence

The flagship registers two abort events that nothing in the app ever dispatches, and its README and docstrings present them as the example's cancellation story — either give them a real caller (A: a route-leave, for which the framework deliberately has no hook) or delete them and rewrite three sentences so the example teaches the two mechanisms it actually uses (B).

## The problem, carefully

**What is registered.** Two events, one per home-page load, each a one-line `:rf.http/managed-abort` by `:request-id`:

```clojure
;; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:339-345
(rf/reg-event :articles/cancel
  {:doc "Abort an in-flight :articles/load — say the user wanders off the home
         page before it lands. No sense letting a reply arrive for a screen
         nobody's looking at. See the HTTP guide on aborts:
         ../../../docs/async/http.md#the-search-box-race-cured"}
  (fn [_ _]
    {:fx [[:rf.http/managed-abort :articles/load]]}))

;; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/favorites.cljs:87-93
(rf/reg-event :feed/cancel
  {:doc "Abort an in-flight :feed/load — say the user leaves before it lands.
         No point delivering a reply to a screen that's gone. ..."}
  (fn [_ _]
    {:fx [[:rf.http/managed-abort :feed/load]]}))
```

**Nothing dispatches them.** Grep (ripgrep) for `articles/cancel|feed/cancel` over the whole tree at trunk `155ff6871c` returns, under `examples/`, exactly the two registrations, their two docstrings, the two loaders' docstrings that advertise them (`articles.cljs:233`, `favorites.cljs:60`) and `README.md:21` — no `[:articles/cancel]` or `[:feed/cancel]` vector anywhere. Control from the same files: `[:articles/load]` is dispatched at `tags.cljs:276` and `[:feed/load]` at `tags.cljs:275`, inside `:home/load`, the `:on-match` of both home routes (`routing.cljs:59`, `:71`). The only other hits repo-wide are `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_frame_scoped_cancellation_test.clj:111` (a test that registers its OWN `:articles/cancel` and dispatches it at `:236`/`:268` — same keyword, unrelated frame) and two `spec/findings/` prose inventories. History agrees: `git log -S':articles/cancel' -- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs` names one commit, `210f812fe2` (the examples reorganisation), and `git log -S'[:articles/cancel]' -- examples/` and `-S'[:feed/cancel]'` return nothing at all — no commit ever dispatched them (control: `-S'[:articles/load]'` returns 4 commits).

**What the prose claims.** `README.md:21` (the "Abort by `:request-id`" bullet under *What this example demonstrates about managed HTTP*) says `:articles/cancel` / `:feed/cancel` "issue `:rf.http/managed-abort` to cancel an in-flight load outright"; the Files row at `README.md:59` sells `articles.cljs` as "managed-HTTP with retry + abort"; `articles.cljs:233-234` says "and `:articles/cancel` can abort it outright"; `favorites.cljs:59-60` says the id is carried "so :feed/cancel can pull the plug if the user wanders off mid-load". The worker on PR #10149 left all four alone on purpose so the choice was not made by prose (bead description; PR body §Held for Mike).

**The job the docstrings describe is already done by something else.** Both loaders capture the committed navigation's token and put it on BOTH reply targets (`articles.cljs:272`, `:286-287`; `favorites.cljs:71`, `:84-85`), and all four settle handlers refuse a reply whose navigation the reader has left (`(when (rh/same-navigation? rt nav-token) …)` at `articles.cljs:307`, `:331`; `favorites.cljs:105`, `:121`; the helper and its REPLY OWNERSHIP rationale at `http.cljs:166-193`). So "a reply arriving for a screen nobody's looking at" writes nothing today — which is exactly what the spec says the correctness story for a plain request is: Spec 014 §Stale-suppression lists four registry triggers and states "Route / navigation staleness for a **plain** request is not one of these — it is owned by resources / nav-tokens" (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1494-1501`), and Pattern-RemoteData §Cancellation says a host cancellation primitive "MAY [be layered] on top … as a bandwidth/CPU optimisation, but correctness lives in stale-detection" (`spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md:224-228`). This behaviour is pinned by five `testing` blocks in `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:4018-4068` (departed feed reply refused, departed failure does not strand the machine, late reply after the current one changes nothing, same-feed page-change control).

**The framework has no route-leave hook, so A is not the "cheap" wiring the PR body assumed.** PR #10149's body says "`:can-leave` machinery already exists in this app (`routing.cljs:92`), so (A) is cheap." That conflates two things. `:can-leave` is a boolean guard SUB — `routing.cljs:92`/`:99` name `[:editor/can-leave?]`, which is `(not dirty?)` at `article_editor.cljs:580-583`; Spec 012 fixes its contract as `true` allows / `false` blocks / anything else blocks (`spec/012-Routing.md:291`). A sub cannot issue an effect. The declarative leave-side companion of `:on-match` — an `:on-leave` slot — was considered and **deliberately deferred, not shipped** (`spec/012-Routing.md:1993-2000`, §Open questions): the spec says leave-side teardown is already covered by machine `:exit` and by route-owned resource release, and "adding a third leave-side mechanism before the gap is demonstrated would be redundant surface". The implementation's closed route-metadata key set is `:tags :parent :on-match :scroll :can-leave :can-enter` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:168`) — no `:on-leave`. The `:rf.route/deactivated` lifecycle is a TRACE event (`spec/012-Routing.md:98`), not something an app handler can act on. What remains for A is the cross-cutting form the spec reserves for policies "spanning many routes uniformly": a `reg-interceptor` attached to the frame's `:interceptors`, which "**must cover all three entry doors**, or it fails open" (`spec/012-Routing.md:1767-1769`).

**A neighbour in the same shape.** `:articles/reset` (`articles.cljs:347-350`) is likewise registered and never dispatched (grep `articles/reset` under `examples/`: the registration only; the other hits are `pattern_smoke_test.clj:190` and `skills/re-frame2/patterns/remote-data.md:99`, each registering its own). Its body is byte-for-byte the body of `:articles/initialise` (`articles.cljs:215-220`), which IS dispatched (`core.cljs:87`). Pattern-RemoteData makes the fourth `reset` event optional — "register it where the feature needs to clear the slice" (`spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md:128`, `:277`) — and this feature clears through `:articles/initialise`. The skill that lifts its slice-form sample from this file (`remote-data.md:28`, `:188`) already differs from the source (its `:articles/reset` has no machine reset), and no `scripts/` gate ties the two (grep `remote-data.md` under `scripts/`: 0), so deleting it moves no gate.

**Who it affects.** A programmer reading the flagship as the "canonical demonstration of the effect" (`README.md:9`) is told the example cancels loads on leave, looks for the caller, and finds none. An AI writing against the API copies the shape — a per-request-id cancel event — with no lesson about WHEN to fire it, which is the only hard part. Production is untouched either way: the events are inert.

**Measured versus asserted.** The grep census, its controls, the git history, and every `path:line` above are mine at `155ff6871c`. The PR-time census (definitions only; control `tags.cljs:276`) is the worker's and agrees. An independent Babashka probe recorded in the appendix (another agent, same day) evaluated the real settle handlers and found a departed cancellation reply returns nil and a cancellation whose navigation is still current lands as `:status :error` / "Request cancelled." — I did not run it, but the second half follows from source and is walked through below.

## Make it tangible

**What a reader sees today.** README:21 promises abort; `articles.cljs:339` delivers a handler; Xray shows what actually happens when the reader leaves `/` mid-load for `/article/hello-conduit`: no abort row, the `GET /articles?limit=10&offset=0` completes, `[:articles/loaded <token> {…}]` is dispatched, and the handler returns nil because the token is stale (`articles.cljs:307`). Correct, silent, and the two events never appear.

**Under A — the honest minimum.** Since no leave hook exists, the wiring is a registered interceptor on the frame that resolves the target from whichever of the three navigation events fired and, when the current route is a home route and the target is not, appends the two aborts (sketch, untested; the shape follows `spec/012-Routing.md:1767-1769`):

```clojure
;; routing.cljs — sketch. Must see :rf.route/navigate, :rf.route/url-requested
;; AND :rf.route/handle-url-change, or a link click / Back leaves without aborting.
(rf/reg-interceptor :realworld/abort-home-loads-on-leave
  {:after (fn [ctx]
            (let [leaving-home? (#{:realworld/home :realworld/home-tag} (current-route-id ctx))
                  entering-home? (#{:realworld/home :realworld/home-tag} (target-route-id ctx))]
              (cond-> ctx
                (and leaving-home? (not entering-home?))
                (update-in [:effects :fx] (fnil into [])
                           [[:dispatch [:articles/cancel]] [:dispatch [:feed/cancel]]]))))})
;; core.cljs — attach by reference on the URL-owning frame's :interceptors.
```

Roughly 30-40 lines with its comment block, plus the frame wiring, plus the door-resolution helper — and it must NOT fire on the home-to-home transitions (page flip, tag change, feed toggle), which supersession and the nav-token gate already handle. It also has an ordering subtlety worth seeing once, because it is the kind of thing a copier would not: a manual abort is not a supersession — it DELIVERS a reply to the failure target, `:status :cancelled` with `{:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :user}` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:659-663`; `docs/async/http.md:315`). That reply reaches `:articles/load-failed`, which projects it through `failure->message` to the string `"Request cancelled."` (`realworld_shared/http.cljs:144`), writes `[:articles :error]`, and broadcasts `:fetch-failed` into the home machine (`articles.cljs:330-337`), whose `:data` region goes to `:error` (`articles.cljs:157-160`); render-priority then picks `:error` (`articles.cljs:382-387`) and the page shows `"Couldn't load articles: Request cancelled."` (`articles.cljs:510-515`). The nav-token gate discards all of that IF the navigation has committed by the time the reply runs — and the guards run at stages 4-5 BEFORE commit (`decisions.cljc:225-226`), and a deferred entry denial commits nothing and navigates nowhere (`routing.cljs:218-222`). So the interceptor has to add its aborts on the commit branch only, or a logged-out reader whose deep link into `/settings` is parked during session restore watches the home page they are still on flip to an error banner. Tractable, but it is a second contract to teach in an example that already carries the first.

What A teaches: "when you leave a route, abort its loads" — expressed through the one mechanism the spec did not want to bless declaratively, in the example whose README (`README.md:5`) exists to show the pieces fitting together.

**Under B — the three sentences after.** `README.md:21` becomes, in substance: *`:articles/load` and `:feed/load` carry stable `:request-id`s; a load re-issued mid-fetch under the SAME id (a page flip, a tag change) supersedes the in-flight request, so a slow first reply can never land after a fast second one. Supersession only fires within one id: Your Feed and the Global Feed are different ids settling one machine, so both reply targets carry the navigation token they were issued under and refuse a reply for a navigation the reader has left (REPLY OWNERSHIP, `http.cljs`). Explicit abort by id is `:rf.http/managed-abort`, shown in `examples/core/managed_http_counter/` and the HTTP guide.* (Note the existing sentence's "the user flips feed or page" is half wrong — a feed flip changes the id, so it is the nav-token, not supersession, that protects it; `articles.cljs:240-244` already says so and the README should agree.) `README.md:59` reads "retry + supersession"; `articles.cljs:233-234` and `favorites.cljs:59-60` lose their cancel clauses; `articles.cljs:339-350` and `favorites.cljs:87-93` go. Net: about -22 lines of code, ~6 lines of prose.

What B teaches: the two mechanisms the app really runs — same-id supersession and nav-token reply ownership — with nothing advertised that the reader cannot find running. Manual abort keeps its three homes: `docs/async/http.md:307-327` (§Cancellation: supersession, manual abort, `:abort-signal`; `:327` names the counter as the end-to-end demo), `docs/async/tutorial.md:167-182`, and Spec 014's own example E (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1005-1020`, a search-box abort-then-reissue). The resources twin already demonstrates leave-driven release through route-owned resources (`realworld_resources/routing.cljs:170`; `article_editor.cljs:296-340` on why that cancellation is best-effort and the slug still has to be checked) — which is the contrast the two twins exist to draw (`http.cljs:240-243`).

## Options

### A. Wire the two events to a route-leave

- What changes: a registered navigation interceptor in `routing.cljs` covering all three doors and firing only on a committing home-to-elsewhere transition; attach it on the frame in `core.cljs`; README:21 and :59 rewritten to say leave aborts; the two docstrings become true as written. `:articles/reset` untouched (unrelated) or deleted in passing.
- Consequences: programmer — sees a working abort, learns the interceptor door-coverage rule and the abort-delivers-a-reply rule on top of the nav-token rule; AI — copies a leave-abort interceptor into apps whose correctness never needed it; tools — Xray gains `:rf.http/aborted` rows on leave; production — bytes saved on an abandoned list fetch; spec — none, but the example demonstrates the very leave hook Spec 012 §Open questions declined to add, through the mechanism the spec reserves for cross-cutting policy.
- Cost: one worker-morning. Files: `routing.cljs`, `core.cljs`, `README.md`, possibly `articles.cljs`/`favorites.cljs` docstrings. No hot-zone file. Gates: compile sweep, `npm run test:cljs` (the realworld suites drive `:rf.route/handle-url-change` directly, `realworld_cljs_test.cljs:4014-4016`, so the interceptor runs under `with-held-comment-fx`, and a held lowered request now meeting an abort is a plausible test-harness breakage in `implementation/`, outside the examples fence). Sequencing: touches `routing.cljs`, which rf2-67vjf (base path, `routing.cljs:253-254`) also touches — sequence behind or ahead of it.
- Risk: medium-low in code, higher in what it teaches. The commit-branch-only condition is easy to get wrong in the direction the reader never notices until the deferred-entry case; and an example that models a deferred spec surface invites "why isn't this declarative?" — the question rf2-uu19xv's deferral answered by saying wait for a real gap.

### B. Delete the two events (and `:articles/reset`) and rewrite the prose

- What changes: remove `articles.cljs:339-350` and `favorites.cljs:87-93`; drop the cancel clauses at `articles.cljs:233-234` and `favorites.cljs:59-60`; rewrite `README.md:21` as above (fixing the "flips feed" half-truth in the same sentence) and `README.md:59`'s "retry + abort". Nothing else. The shared `:rf.http/aborted` arm at `realworld_shared/http.cljs:144` STAYS — README:23 sells the projection as an exhaustive `case` over the closed set, and that is a property of the projection, not of who reaches each arm.
- Consequences: programmer — the README's cancellation bullet now describes exactly what runs; AI — nothing dead to copy, and the per-id supersession + nav-token pairing is the pattern it inherits; tools — no change; production — an abandoned list fetch still completes and is refused at settle (the "bandwidth/CPU optimisation" Pattern-RemoteData says a host MAY add, deliberately not added); spec — none.
- Cost: an hour. Files: `articles.cljs`, `favorites.cljs`, `README.md` — three, none hot-zone. Gates: compile sweep (`:examples/realworld`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1787`), `npm run test:cljs` (control that nothing in `implementation/` dispatches the deleted events: the only same-named registrations are the http test's own, `:111`, and `pattern_smoke_test.clj:190`), `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` for the README (link targets unchanged, so it is honest but narrow — say so), README Files-table column count by hand. Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Sequencing: shares `favorites.cljs` with rf2-zfr7w (latch at `:157-203`; this deletion is `:87-93`), different hunks — parallel is fine, or let the latch land first.

## Recommendation

**B.** Argued from the stance's second half. "Trust the programmer" cuts against A: the framework already refuses the departed reply, the spec already calls a host abort an optimisation rather than a correctness tool, and the example already pins the correctness half in five tests — wiring an abort on top is the belt-and-braces the stance names as gold plating, in the example whose job is to show the pieces "fit together" rather than to demonstrate every effect the artefact exports. "Don't litigate the minutiae" cuts against A twice more: its cheapest honest form needs the three-door interceptor rule and the commit-branch-only condition, which are exactly the fine details this dossier had to spend a paragraph on, and it would have the flagship model a leave hook that Spec 012 §Open questions deferred on purpose. B costs an hour, deletes dead code, corrects a half-true README sentence, and leaves the example teaching precisely the two mechanisms it runs. The earlier 18-line draft of this file reached the same letter; so does the appendix.

What would change my mind: a ruling of B on rf2-8slzk as well. Grep `managed-abort` under `examples/` at trunk returns only `realworld_http` (these two events) and `managed_http_counter` (`core.cljs:324-333`, the live fx on a seeded handle) — so B here plus B there leaves no example under `examples/` firing `:rf.http/managed-abort` at all, and `examples/README.md:88` sells the counter on "abort". The guide, the tutorial and Spec 014's example E still carry it, and the framework tests pin it (rf2-8slzk's own description), so I would still rule B here; but if Mike wants one clickable abort somewhere in `examples/`, the counter is the right home for it (its subject is the effect; the flagship's is the app), which argues for A on rf2-8slzk rather than A here.

**What the tool does today.** `eval-cljs` evaluates the form text verbatim in shadow-cljs's default REPL namespace, with no alias of any kind:

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:758-764` — `cljs-eval` builds `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval <build> "<form>" {})`. The opts map is the literal `{}`: no `:ns`, no alias rewrite.

## Recommendation

**A.** Argued from the stance: the point of the skill is that the AI can be productive against a live app with low friction, and an instruction that cannot be typed as written is friction of exactly the kind "excellent tools" rules out — five times over, once in the always-loaded router. A is also the *smallest* option that actually removes the failure: five lines, no hot-zone file, no shadow lane, no gate, no parser, and it leaves 80 `rf/` citations exactly where they are, because the rule it applies is a reading test (*would the agent paste this into `eval-cljs`?*) rather than a spelling sweep. B adds a rule where a fix is cheaper than the rule — "trust the programmer" cuts against a nagging translation step the agent must apply to lines where it is meaningless. C is defensible under "don't drown in the minutiae", but the minutiae here is the *sweep* the bead already forbids, not the five lines; and C leaves the router contradicting its own recipe.

What would change my mind: if Mike wants the skill to teach a single citation style on principle (every prose form is `rf/`, always) — then B, with the rule at `SKILL.md:80` widened, and the five sites left; or if he reads the five sites as too small to spend a dispatch on — then C, closed with the rule recorded so the next review does not re-raise it.

This is a recommendation for Mike, not a ruling or authorization to implement it.

title: core-reactive: dev annotation walk treats :r>/:f> interop roots as DOM tags and displaces the component (crash / blank render in dev only)
description:
## Defect

The dev-mode source-coordinate / view-tag annotation walk treats Reagent's `:r>` (raw createElement) and `:f>` (function component, the hooks escape hatch) interop heads as DOM tags. Only `:<>` and `:>` are exempt. So when a registered view's root is `[:r> Comp props …]` or `[:f> f args …]`, the walk splices an attrs map into position 1, the slot BOTH Reagent implementations read as the component. The result:

- a `:r>` root becomes `React.createElement(<a CLJS map>, …)`, which crashes with React's invalid-element-type error;
- a `:f>` root calls the attrs map instead of the user's function.

This happens only in dev, where `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` is true. The same view renders correctly in production. Spec 006 §Injection rules says an interop head is SKIPPED.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs:113-120` — `dom-tag?` excludes only `:<>` and `:>`. At `:164-180` the DOM-root branch splices `{:data-rf2-source-coord … :data-rf-view …}` in after the head whenever `(second out)` is not a map, which it never is for `:r>` / `:f>`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:641-644` — the walk runs on every dev render whenever no substrate wrap was applied. Neither Reagent nor reagent-slim publishes `:adapter/wrap-view`: a search for `wrap-view` under `implementation/adapters/**/src` finds only the UIx adapter.
- The JVM twin has the identical predicate and splice: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/jvm_source_coord_annotation.clj:73-81` and `:112-128`.
- How the heads are dispatched:
  - stock Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent/impl/template.cljs:307-308` — `:r> (raw-element (nth v 1 nil) v …)` and `:f> (function-element (nth v 1 nil) v 2 …)`;
  - reagent-slim `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:1259-1260`, `raw-element` `:1100-1117` and `function-element` `:1156-1172`, both taking the component from `(nth argv 1)`.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:765-773` (§Injection rules: `[fragment / interop-head / fn-component …]` — SKIP) and `:717-727` (§Documented exemption).
- Public entry point: `rf/reg-view` on the Reagent or reagent-slim adapter, dev build.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(defn- panel-impl [] (let [[n set-n] (react/useState 0)] [:button {:on-click #(set-n inc)} n]))
(rf/reg-view hooks-panel [] [:f> panel-impl])          ;; hooks via the :f> escape hatch
(rf/reg-view app [] (rf/frame-root {:id :app} [main])) ;; returns [:r> frame-root-fc #js {…} [main]]
```

In a dev build the walk rewrites these roots:

- `[:f> panel-impl]` becomes `[:f> {:data-rf2-source-coord … :data-rf-view …} panel-impl]`. On reagent-slim, `as-fn-component` then wraps the MAP and renders `(apply the-map [panel-impl])`, which is a map lookup returning nil. The panel renders nothing and its hooks never run.
- `[:r> frame-root-fc #js {…} [main]]` becomes `[:r> {attrs} frame-root-fc #js {…} [main]]`. `raw-element` then calls `React.createElement` with the map as the element type, and React throws "Element type is invalid".

The same code works under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`, which is the worst direction for a developer to discover it in.

## Evidence

Executed on the JVM twin, which shares the predicate and the splice branch line for line (`scratchpad/review-wave/core-reactive/probe_annotate.clj`, one-shot `clojure -M` over the frozen `implementation/core/src`, run from the scratch dir):

title: core-instrumentation: offset-rooted egress (get-path / project-egress :path) ignores ancestor sensitive declarations and ships the subtree raw
description:
## Defect

An offset-rooted egress walk ignores every classification declared on an ANCESTOR of the offset. `elide-wire-value` (and therefore `rf/project-egress` on a kindless value) seeds the walker's candidate declaration set with the bare offset path `#{seed-path}` and only ever tests candidates that start there. A frame that classifies `[:auth]` sensitive has its whole `[:auth]` subtree redacted in a whole-db walk, but a direct read of `[:auth :token]` or `[:auth :user]` — the exact MCP `get-path` shape Spec 015 §Direct reads prescribes — ships the value RAW under the off-box profile. The same root cause lets an indexed offset escape an index-free declaration: `[:items 0]` read directly is not redacted against `[:items :token]`, which a whole-db walk redacts in every element. The `:path` opt is documented as the "absolute app-db offset of `v`" (`elision.cljc:1196`), so a declaration at or above the offset must still govern the value.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1102-1106` — `elide-against-frame` seeds `#{seed-path}` and walks; nothing checks the offset's prefixes, and nothing replays the map-key / index forks along the offset.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:878-891` — `fork-decl-paths` keeps a non-empty seed alive forever (it never matched a prefix), so the walk below the offset can only match declarations that extend the offset itself.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:996-1039` — `walk-decider` `:decide` tests only the current candidate set.
- Public entry points: `rf/project-egress` kindless arm, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:647-652` (via `project-egress`, `:764-798`); `rf.elision/elide-wire-value` `:path` opt, `elision.cljc:1184-1314`.
- Reached off-box by the pair MCP `get-path` tool: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:51-67` passes `{:path <requested path> :frame F}` plus the off-box profile. Other offset callers with the same exposure: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs:89`, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:484`. The prescribed idiom is `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:374`.

## Failure scenario

1. An event returns `{:db (assoc db :auth {:token "SECRET-TOKEN" :user {:pw "hunter2"}}) :sensitive [[:auth]]}`.
2. An agent calls MCP `get-path` with `[:auth :token]` (or `[:auth :user]`).
3. The runtime evaluates `(rf/project-egress (get-in db [:auth :token]) {:frame F :path [:auth :token] :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})`.
4. Result: `"SECRET-TOKEN"` (and `{:name "bob" :pw "hunter2"}` for `[:auth :user]`) crosses the wire. The whole-db read of the same frame returns `{:auth :rf/redacted ...}`.

Index-free variant: declare `:sensitive [[:items :token]]`, db `{:items [{:token "T0"} {:token "T1"}]}`. A whole-db walk gives `{:items [{:token :rf/redacted} ...]}`; `get-path [:items 0]` returns `{:token "T0" :x 1}`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (core as a `:local/root` dep; nothing written into the tree). It seeds the registry with `rf.elision/apply-classification-effects` (the `install-class!` path `elision_test.clj` uses), then:

- CONTROL whole-db `project-egress` with `:path []`: `{:auth :rf/redacted, :public 1}`
- CONTROL offset `[:auth]`: `:rf/redacted`
- PROBE offset `[:auth :token]`, off-box-tool: `"SECRET-TOKEN"`
- PROBE offset `[:auth :user]`, off-box-tool: `{:name "bob", :pw "hunter2"}`; bare `elide-wire-value` gives the same result
- CONTROL whole-db with index-free decl `[:items :token]`: every `:token` redacted
- PROBE offset `[:items 0]`: `{:token "T0", :x 1}`

No test pins an offset below a declaration: `elision_test.clj` has no `:path` opt use at all, and `projection_cljs_test.cljc` passes `:path [:a]` only to check pass-through (line 171). Tracker search (full-text over a `bd export`) for ancestor / offset / seed-path / get-path finds no bead on this. The 2026-09-16 review of this slice (rf2-pk4i6.11) does not mention it. As a control, the same search finds 25 beads for `elide-wire-value`.

## Smallest fix

In `elide-against-frame`, derive the starting candidate set by replaying the walker's own descent from `#{[]}` along the offset's segments: `fork-decl-paths` for every segment, plus `fork-index-paths` for integer segments. At each prefix, apply the same sensitive, shadow and large decision `walk-decider` makes. If an ancestor matches sensitive, return the sentinel. If it matches large, return the marker. Otherwise walk `v` with the replayed candidate set instead of `#{seed-path}`. This touches only `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc`, plus a test in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj` (ancestor-sensitive, ancestor-large and indexed-offset cases). No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. `elision.cljc` is plain cljc with no reader conditional around `elide-against-frame`, so the JVM lane compiles it. `npm run test:cljs` (node lane) covers the CLJS side. The pair-mcp get-path tests (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/elision_test.cljs`) are a useful consumer check.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix — rf2-3x7nj.4.1 (2026-09-23, worker/instr-elision-3x7nj, PR #10279)

Reproduced at trunk 2c8b8847a3 (elision.cljc unchanged since the frozen review tree) with a bounded JVM probe, controls both ways: whole-db `{:auth :rf/redacted :public 1}`, offset `[:auth]` `:rf/redacted`, but offset `[:auth :token]` returned `"SECRET-TOKEN"` and `[:auth :user]` `{:name "bob" :pw "hunter2"}` under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`; `[:items 0]` returned `{:token "T0" :x 1}` against a whole-db walk that redacted every `:token`. The same seed also let a read below a `:large` declaration (`[:big :blob]` under `[:big]`) ship raw.

Fix, as the description prescribes, in `elide-against-frame` only: the walk now replays its own descent from `#{[]}` along the offset (`fork-decl-paths` per segment; `fork-index-paths` for an integer segment, which is the superset of the map-key fork for the same segment, so an integer-keyed map can only over-match), applying the walker's own `:decide` at the root and every strict prefix. Sensitive ancestor returns the sentinel; large ancestor returns the marker built for the read value at the offset (so `:path` / `:handle` name what was read, and `:rf.egress/include-large? true` still fetches it); a large ancestor shadowing a sensitive descendant descends, exactly as whole-db. No offset walks from `#{[]}` as before. After the fix the probe reads `:rf/redacted` for all three direct reads and `{:token :rf/redacted :x 1}` for `[:items 0]`.

Regressions in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj`: `offset-read-below-a-sensitive-declaration-redacts` (includes the exact `rf/project-egress` call the pair MCP get-path eval form makes), `offset-read-through-an-index-obeys-an-index-free-declaration`, `offset-read-below-a-large-declaration-elides`, and `offset-read-below-a-shadowing-large-ancestor-redacts-and-never-marks` (pins that the replay applies the nested-axis decision, so no digest is computed over a value holding a secret). Control: with the replay removed (loop started at the bare offset) the namespaces went 8 failures across the first three deftests, the whole-db and at-declaration control assertions staying green, same 113 tests / 306 assertions as the green run; restored, blob hash equal to the committed object.

Consumers: `get_path.cljs`, story `assertions.cljc` and xray `egress.cljs` already pass the absolute offset as `:path`, so they needed no change and pick the fix up from core. JVM suites of tools/story, tools/story-mcp, tools/mcp-base and tools/xray green on the fixed tree; the CLJS consumer tests are left to CI (shadow-cljs lane not granted to this worker).

Note for the record: Spec 009 §Wire marker says a `:vector` marker is "paginatable via get-path with an index range". Under this fix an index read below a large declaration returns a marker for that element unless the caller passes the large opt-in (`elision false` on the pair tools), which is the same rule the handle fetch at the declared path already follows. Followed the bead; flagging it in case a ruling wants descendant reads under `:large` to ship raw instead.
Merged-PR audit #10279 forward pointer: exact open finding rf2-ealv5 retains the incomplete pagination/descendant-large contract question. Added independent merged-runtime evidence that indexed batch reads remain markers by default and fetch raw with the large opt-in. Existing discovered-from link and bd ready membership verified.
Merged-PR audit #10279 (950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a; merged 2026-09-23T13:30:43Z). Completeness: All three implementation claims are addressed: ancestor and index-free classification governs offset reads; map traversal rebuilds records safely; all three trace-ring eviction/trim sites copy retained IDs. The existing open pagination-contract question rf2-ealv5 is reused with concrete measurement, not silently treated as resolved. Correctness: Independently ran exact merged core sources at 950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a: elision and trace-buffer suites 113 tests/306 assertions, zero failures/errors, exit 0. Additional indexed-batch large-offset probe 1 test/3 assertions passes and records marker/default versus explicit-large behavior. Verified worker root and loaded source identities. CI 74 success/14 skipped. Ancestor sensitive dominance, large-shadow suppression, marker handles and opt-ins traced; no additional material defect found. Implementation quality: Reuses the existing walker decision and candidate forks; record handling is a one-arm correction; ring repair copies only on eviction or trim. No public API growth. Existing policy follow-up remains separately trackable and ready. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-ealv5.

DONE — merged as PR #10279 (head b379dd211f), with its siblings in the same PR. CI 88/88 at band. Local: core 2328, epoch 557, ssr 689 exit 0 on the final base; the 21-artefact JVM sweep and the story / story-mcp / mcp-base / xray JVM suites exit 0 on the earlier base. Each control red with its fix removed, each restore blob-verified.

Frozen review tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23` at `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914`. All cites are against it. `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines before and after every probe.

- Supporting: the `:dev-http` block of `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (495-680); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs` (the only client); core `absolutise-file` and `editor-uri/absolute-path?`; Story `mount-shell!`/`unmount-shell!` and the hash handling in `url_state.cljc`. Upstream sources read from the jars actually pinned: shadow-cljs 3.4.10 `shadow/http/push_state.clj` and `shadow/cljs/devtools/server/dev_http.clj`; shadow-http 0.1.8 `ring.clj`, `server.clj`, `FileHandler.java`, `HttpRequest.java`; launch-editor 2.14.1 `index.js`, `get-args.js`, `guess.js`.

### Method
Read the server against the brief's checklist, then ran two bounded JVM probes from my scratch dir, depending on the frozen tree through `:local/root`, so nothing was written into the tree.
1. End to end: the REAL shadow-cljs 3.4.10 `:dev-http` server (`dev-http/start-build-server`, shadow-http 0.1.8), bound to `127.0.0.1` and to `::1` on ephemeral ports, with this namespace's `handler`. `launch!` was replaced by a spy that applies the real `file-exists?` and never spawns Node. Requests went over raw sockets so the request target was not normalised. The server was stopped when done, in about 20 s.
2. Handler level: requests shaped exactly as `start-build-server` hands them over, with a non-loopback socket rendering as `:remote-addr`.

Admission results. All of these were executed through the real server.
- A loopback POST with a loopback Host and a cross-port loopback Origin, the same with no Origin, and the IPv6 `::1` POST all answered 200.
- These all answered 403 and never reached the spy: `Origin: https://evil.example`; the DNS-rebinding `Host: evil.example:<port>`; `Host: evil.localhost`; `Origin: null`.
- A GET of the endpoint answered 405.
- `file=abc%00def` answered 422 `file-not-found`.

The peer check reads shadow-http's real `/127.0.0.1:port` and `/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:port` renderings and admits them. Non-loopback, IPv4-mapped, `X-Forwarded-For`, hostname-half and malformed peers are pinned by existing unit tests built from real `InetSocketAddress` objects, so they were not refiled.

Tracker searched with `--status all` for `open-in-editor`, `loopback`, `push-state`, `preflight`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `respondNoContent` and `testbed-support`. I read the close reasons of rf2-78s0d, rf2-8fms7, rf2-mpgs and rf2-cl8mg through `--json`. None rules on either finding below. Sibling slices rf2-3x7nj.27 and .29 were checked with `check_surface.py`: no overlap.

### Findings
| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.38.1 | P2 | handler's push-state fallthrough serves any index.html on disk to a network peer via a raw .. request path |
| rf2-3x7nj.38.2 | P3 (task) | CORS contract false on the real dev-http server - every endpoint response also carries shadow's ACAO *, and the 204 preflight goes out as 304 |

### Considered and rejected
- **No allowed-root confinement on `file` (`../`, absolute, drive letter, UNC, `%2e%2e`, symlink).** By design. The spec says absolute paths pass through, and the loopback boundary, not a root, is the control. An admitted caller is a same-machine process or page, and that caller can already open files. The probe confirmed that a cwd-relative `..` file resolves and launches, which is the documented behaviour.
- **NUL byte in `file`.** `File.exists` is false, so the request is a 422 before Node runs (executed).
- **UNC path causing an SMB/NTLM touch at `file-exists?`.** Only an admitted, same-machine caller can reach it. launch-editor 2.14.1 also refuses UNC paths.
- **Windows shell string inside launch-editor 2.14.1.** It calls `exec` with `shell: true` and `^`-escaping, and its regex does not escape `%`. This is upstream, it needs an attacker-named file on disk, and it can only be reached through loopback admission, so there is no privilege gain.
- **JVM-side command construction.** It is an argv vector (`ProcessBuilder` list), with no shell. `line` and `column` are digit-only through `->int`, and the editor hint is a closed whitelist.
- **CSRF.** A cross-origin form or `no-cors` POST carries a non-loopback or `null` Origin, and both are refused (executed). A simple GET is a 405. A missing Origin is accepted by design, and modern browsers always send one on POST.
- **DNS rebinding.** The Host check refuses `evil.example` and `*.localhost` (executed).
- **`127.999.x.x` accepted by the `loopback-host?` regex.** No browser can emit such a Host, and the peer check stays authoritative.
- **Duplicate `*` ACAO as a security weakening.** It is not one: the combined value makes browsers deny. The only defect is the contract falsehood filed as .38.2.
- **`{:custom …}` preference going to auto-detect, which may pick a different editor.** This is documented in spec lines 106-119, and the client halves were reviewed in rf2-3x7nj.27/.29.
- **Editor vocabulary gap.** None. Core's `known-editors #{:vscode :cursor :windsurf :zed :idea}` all map in `editor-command-by-keyword`.
- **Launch-shim capability probes (total drop, column differential, column-only, `LAUNCH_EDITOR`, `subl`/`zed` single-token argv).** All consistent with `get-args.js` 2.14.1.
- **`story_host.cljs`.** Routing matches `#/stories…` by prefix, as the spec says. `location.hash` is always a string, so a malformed hash is safe. Story's own URL state lives in the query string, so in-shell navigation fires no `hashchange`. Live-app hash changes re-render the same root rather than remounting it. The listener handle is replaced correctly across reloads.

### Could not verify
- A LAN-peer socket test of .38.1. Binding `0.0.0.0` would have exposed a port and could raise a firewall prompt. Instead, remote-peer reachability was executed at handler level with a non-loopback `:remote-addr`, and the `0.0.0.0` bind was confirmed by source (`dev_http.clj:61-64`, and no `:host` on any entry).
- Browser behaviour for .38.2, that is a CORS failure on a combined ACAO value and on a 304 preflight. This is stated from the Fetch spec, not run in a browser, because browsers were out of bounds.
- A real editor launch. The spy replaced `launch!`, per the limits. Timeout behaviour with blocking editors (a cold `idea` launch, a terminal `$EDITOR`) was reasoned about, not measured, and is not filed.

title: ssr-ring: pages whose route declares no :head ship <title>ssr-ring per-request frame</title> (hard-coded frame :doc feeds default-head)
description:
## Defect

Every page served by `ssr-handler` or `stream-handler` whose active route declares no `:head` — including every page of an app that uses no routing at all — ships `<title>ssr-ring per-request frame</title>`. The per-request frame is created with a hard-coded developer label `:doc "ssr-ring per-request frame"`, and Spec 011's default head rolls the frame's `:doc` into `:title` (`{:title (or (:doc (frame-meta frame-id)) "")}`). The caller cannot change the frame `:doc` (it is not a handler opt), so the internal adapter string becomes the browser-tab title and the search-engine title of those pages. The spec's intent — a sensible default from the app's frame metadata, or no title — is defeated by the adapter supplying its own debug label.

## Where

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:319-322` — `(rf/make-frame {:id frame-id :doc "ssr-ring per-request frame" :platform :server ...})`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:83-104` — `default-head` uses the frame `:doc` as `:title` (contract `spec/011-SSR.md:1329-1337`).
- Consumed via `lifecycle/resolve-head` (`lifecycle.clj:155-197`) in `pipeline.clj:650` and `streaming.clj:191`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:2037-2056` knows the title is this string and deliberately asserts only `<= 1` `<title>` ("contract-dependent").
- Public entries: `re-frame.ssr.ring/ssr-handler`, `re-frame.ssr.ring/stream-handler`.

## Failure scenario

A minimal SSR app (no routes, or a route with no `:head` such as a not-found or a simple content page) behind `ssr-handler` -> the served document's `<title>` is `ssr-ring per-request frame`; that is what the browser tab shows and what a crawler indexes. Declaring a route `:head` avoids it; nothing else does short of the raw `:head` string opt.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded JVM probe (`probe4_default_title.clj`, reviewer scratch dir), `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- ssr, no routing: title `"ssr-ring per-request frame"`.
- stream, no routing: title `"ssr-ring per-request frame"`.
- ssr, route without `:head`: title `"ssr-ring per-request frame"`.
- CONTROL, route with `reg-head` `{:title "My Page"}`: title `"My Page"`.

`git log -S` shows the `:doc` string arrived with the adapter's first ship (`3f1d623e96`, rf2-ny6v7) and was carried through a file split; no bead rules it deliberate (tracker search over all fields for "ssr-ring per-request frame": 0 hits).

## Smallest fix

Drop `:doc` from the per-request `make-frame` config (the default head then yields `:title ""`, which emits no `<title>`), or thread an optional caller opt into the frame `:doc` if a default title is wanted. Tighten `ring_test.clj`'s default-head test to assert the chosen outcome. Fence: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj`, `test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring`. No CLJS lane involved.

## Decision needed

Minor: no title by default (drop the `:doc`; it also labels the frame in dev tooling, which is the only cost), or a caller-supplied default (a new handler opt). Either removes the leaked label.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 23:18:11 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==
Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.14.4.leaked-frame-doc-title.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated below.
Trunk read at: e402782b8d. The cited paths are unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8.

RECOMMENDATION: Option 1, drop :doc "ssr-ring per-request frame" from the per-request make-frame (pipeline.clj:321).
- No spec change is needed: spec/011-SSR.md:1329-1337 already defines the title as (or doc "") and says routes that want a title declare :head.
- Tighten ring_test.clj:2037-2056 to assert zero <title> tags, and correct the shell.clj:128-133 docstring, which claims "a sensible title is always present".
- Option 2 (a new handler opt) is rejected for lack of demonstrated need: a route :head or the trusted :head string opt already covers a title.

DECISIVE FINDINGS (executed at trunk):
1. Three cases ship <title>ssr-ring per-request frame</title>: ssr-handler with no routing, stream-handler with no routing, and ssr-handler on a route without :head. Control: a route with reg-head {:title "My Page"} renders "My Page".
2. lifecycle/resolve-head on a server frame without :doc returns head-html with no <title> (model title ""). The same frame with the :doc returns the leaked title.
3. rg "ssr-ring per-request frame" finds 2 lines: the make-frame call and a test comment. Nothing else reads the string.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:19:58 AUSEST) ==

RULING: OPTION 1. Delete `:doc "ssr-ring per-request frame"` from the per-request `make-frame` (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:321). A page whose active route declares no `:head` then ships NO `<title>`. No new handler opt, no spec change, no hot-zone file.

This is a fix, NOT a won't-fix. Under the stance it is close to minutiae, but the fix is a one-line deletion that stops an internal debug label becoming the browser-tab and search-engine title of every page with no route `:head` (every page of an app with no routing, and every not-found page). Minutiae are not worth litigating in either direction, and here the cheaper outcome is the fix.

Verified at trunk f6bb999d6e (= origin/main after `git fetch origin main`, exit 0). The cited paths are unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8: the diff over them is empty, and the unfiltered control reads 31 files.

--- WHY ---

1. The dossier and Codex AGREE on Option 1. The deciding fact is the ownership chain, which Codex traced and this ruling re-read at trunk:

title: epoch: a :halted-depth record's :halt-reason :last-event ships the last-settled event's args RAW through rf/project-egress (and the replay/restore refusal carriers), bypassing registration classification
description:
## Defect

A `:halted-depth` epoch record carries the last-settled event vector, with its arguments RAW, at `[:halt-reason :last-event]`, and nothing on any egress path projects it. `rf/project-egress`'s epoch arm treats `:halt-reason` as a bookkeeping slot and passes it through untouched, so a runaway-loop halt sends the event's arguments off-box verbatim, including arguments the event's own registration declares `:sensitive`. The same record's `:trigger-event` is correctly redacted to `[<id> :rf/redacted]` in the same projection. Two epoch-owned siblings carry the same value verbatim too: the `replay-epoch!` refusal envelope (its `:tags :halt-reason`), which the pair-MCP `replay-epoch` tool relays over the wire as-is, and the `:rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record` error trace's tags. The raw record also skips registration classification ON-BOX: its `:trigger-event` and `:halt-reason :last-event` hold the declared-sensitive value, while every `:ok` record in the same ring holds it already substituted.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):

- Producer: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3416-3419` builds `halt-reason {... :last-event last-event}`. `last-event` is `(:event envelope)`, the raw envelope event of the last SETTLED event (`router.cljc:3841-3849`, `recur (inc depth) event ring`). The halting event is also passed raw (`router.cljc:3382-3383`, then `3500-3501`).
- Epoch commit: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:399-432` (`commit-halt-record!`) and `epoch.cljc:292-295` pin the raw explicit trigger. `assembly/build-record` stores `:halt-reason` verbatim (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:370`).
- Off-box pass-through: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:2437-2489` (`project-record-slots`). Its docstring (`:2445-2448`) names `:halt-reason` among the slots that "pass through untouched".
- Sibling carriers: `tool_pair.cljc:672-677` (replay refusal `:tags` gets `:halt-reason`) and `tool_pair.cljc:446-452` (the restore-non-ok-record trace tags get `:halt-reason`).
- Public entry points: `rf/project-egress` on any `rf/epoch-history` record, which is what pair-MCP `watch-epochs` / `epoch_egress`, Xray egress and the Story recorder use. Also `rf/replay-epoch!` (the pair-MCP `replay-epoch` tool, `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:2179`, returns "the framework's refusal envelope verbatim") and `rf/restore-epoch!`.

## Failure scenario

1. A frame has `:drain-depth 3`.
2. `(rf/reg-event :loop {:sensitive [[:token]]} (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ arg]] {:db (update (or db {}) :n (fnil inc 0)) :fx [[:dispatch [:loop arg]]]}))`
3. `(rf/dispatch-sync [:loop {:token "SECRET-TOKEN"}] {:frame :p/main})`
4. The ring reads `[:ok :ok :ok :halted-depth]`, and `(rf/project-egress (last (rf/epoch-history :p/main)))` returns `:halt-reason {:operation :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded, :depth 3, :queue-size 1, :last-event [:loop {:token "SECRET-TOKEN"}]}`. It returns the same thing under the default profile, under `:rf.egress/off-box-observability`, and under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`. The same projection shows `:trigger-event [:loop :rf/redacted]`.

A realistic trigger is a polling or retry loop that re-dispatches itself carrying a token. That loop is exactly the runaway the depth limit exists to catch.

## Evidence

EXECUTED with bounded JVM probes (process-local, run from a scratch `deps.edn` with `:local/root` into the frozen tree; probes in the reviewer scratch dir).

- probe1: the projected halt record contained `SECRET-TOKEN` under all three profiles. With `:halt-reason` dissoc'd it contained none, so the leak is exactly that slot.
- Control, both ways: the three `:ok` records of the same drain contain no `SECRET-TOKEN`, raw or projected, because registration classification substituted it at capture. The probe can therefore see a redaction when one happens.
- probe3: the raw halt record's `:trigger-event` read `[:loop {:token "SECRET-TOKEN"}]`, which is the on-box classification bypass. `(rf/replay-epoch! ...)` on the halt record returned `{:ok? false :reason :rf.epoch/replay-non-replayable-record ...}` containing `SECRET-TOKEN`. `restore-epoch!` on it returned false and emitted a `:rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record` trace containing `SECRET-TOKEN`.

Why no gate caught it: `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` builds its "no raw sensitive bytes anywhere" corpus from sensitive, large, bookkeeping and `:halted-destroy` records. It includes no `:halted-depth` record, and it asserts `:halt-reason` is preserved byte-for-byte (header, lines 41-42; check at :1017). Tracker searched first (`halt-reason`, `last-event`, `halted-depth`, `drain-depth-exceeded`, `project-record`, `halt record`): nothing covers it. The control search `after-deltas` does find rf2-3x7nj.4.2 and rf2-fc84b. This is a different slot from rf2-3x7nj.4.2 (after-deltas).

## Smallest fix

At the producer, core `router.cljc` `handle-depth-exceeded!`: make `:halt-reason` carry `:last-event-id` (ids only, exactly as the always-on `dispatch-error-record!` beside it already does, per rf2-fcbrjo) instead of the raw `:last-event` vector. Also pass the halting event through the same registration classification every trace carrier gets before it becomes the record's `:trigger-event`. That one change closes all three carriers and the on-box bypass.

As defence in depth for records already held, `project-record-slots` in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` should fail closed on any event vector under `:halt-reason`, reusing `elide-trigger-event-slot`.

Update the conformance corpus to include a `:halted-depth` record, and relax its "halt-reason byte-for-byte" assertion accordingly.

Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`, `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc`, `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` (and the epoch privacy test). Hot-zone: the spec pseudo-code at `spec/002-Frames.md:2026-2030` shows `:last-event` in `halt-reason`. Only an edit to it (optional, to match an id-only shape) touches a hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/epoch` (the conformance and privacy suites) and in `implementation/core` (router). Every file named is `.clj`/`.cljc` outside any `#?(:cljs ...)` branch, so the JVM lanes grade it. The pair-MCP relay needs no tool change: the replay refusal envelope and the restore-non-ok trace carry whatever `:halt-reason` the record holds, so the producer fix closes them. The epoch-side projection arm closes only the `project-egress` carrier.

## Decision needed

Mostly no. The one choice is whether `:halt-reason` keeps an event VECTOR (then classified at the producer and projected fail-closed at egress) or drops to `:last-event-id` alone. The id-only shape is recommended because it matches the always-on record.

title: xray-data-layer: diff engine promotes a surviving map to a wholly-:removed/:added root when all its keys are swapped (one-sided R5 walk; spec 004 says maps are immune) - {:form {:errors {:email ..}}} -> {:errors {:name ..}} strikes :form as removed
description:
## Defect

When a nested map loses all its old keys and gains new ones, the diff engine marks a container that still exists as wholly removed or wholly added.

The engine's R5 rule promotes a container to a wholly-`:added` or wholly-`:removed` root when every leaf on ONE side carries the same op. rf2-l0us2 found that this one-sided test is fooled by a set swap. A swap puts the before-members and after-members at disjoint paths, so each side looks uniform on its own. The fix took the union of both sides' members, but for sets only. Spec 004 and the engine docstring both state that maps "are unaffected — their slots are keyed by a shared key/index, so the one-sided uniformity walk was always correct for them".

That is false. A map whose every old key was removed and every new key added puts its before-leaves and after-leaves at disjoint paths exactly as a set swap does. So the SHALLOWEST ancestor whose one-side leaves all pass is promoted: the container itself, or any ancestor with no other leaf. The inspector then renders a surviving key as a wholesale removal or addition:

- the whole row is washed and its key text struck (R5 row of the slot-anchoring table);
- every descendant takes that wash with its `+` / `−` glyph and stripe suppressed, so the genuinely added leaf reads red.

This hits the App-DB tab, Epoch `:db` lens, Machine snapshot drill-in and Reactive sub values. It is also ordinary shape for app-db:

- a selection keyed by id: `{7 true}` → `{9 true}`;
- an errors map: `{:email …}` → `{:name …}`;
- a one-key "current modal" or "loading" map.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc:570-775` (`mark-wholly-changed`). The union of both sides is taken only in the `(set? data)` arm (`:661-667`). The `(map? data)` arm (`:647-654`) walks `data` alone, and `check-uniform` (`:682-688`) promotes on one-sided uniformity.
- Engine docstring claim: `engine.cljc:621-623`.
- Overlay: `engine.cljc:1154-1173` (swaps `:children` to `:added` / `:removed` with `:rf.xray.diff/wholly-changed? true`). When BOTH walks promote the same path, the op comes from whichever descendant iterates first.
- Renderer consumers:
  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:2837-2869` (`classify-container-op` returns the projected `:removed` / `:added`);
  - `edn_inspector.cljs:3756-3767` (descendants: glyph and stripe suppressed, `:wash-op` = the ancestor's op).
- Contract, spec-stale: `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:207-214`. Rendering contract: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:2642-2647` (R5) and `:2680` ("Parent key text struck when removed").

## Failure scenario

Executed (JVM), with each result taken from `engine/project`:

- **Nested map key swap.** `{:form {:errors {:email "bad"}}}` → `{:form {:errors {:name "required"}}}`.
  - Editscript: `[[[:form :errors :email] :-] [[:form :errors :name] :+ "required"]]`.
  - `wholly-changed-roots #{[:form]}`, and `container-ops [:form]` = `{:op :removed :change-count 2 :rf.xray.diff/wholly-changed? true}`.
  - `op-at [:form]` = `:removed`, and `wholly-changed-ancestor [:form :errors :name]` = `[:form]`.
  - The App-DB tab strikes `:form` as removed and paints the added `:name "required"` row with the red wash and no `+` glyph. Both `:form` and `:errors` still exist in `:db-after`.
- **The same shape inside a vector element.** `[{:z 5} {:z 9 :k 2}]` → `[{:k 2}]`.
  - Editscript morphs element 0 (`[[0 :z] :-] [[0 :k] :+ 2]`) and deletes element 1.
  - `wholly-changed-roots #{[0]}`, and `op-at [0]` = `:removed` for an element that is present, and is `{:k 2}`.

Controls, same run and correct:

- Genuinely new nested map: `{:user {}}` → `{:user {:prefs {:c 3}}}` promotes `[:user]` `:added`.
- Genuinely removed: `{:user {:prefs {:a 1}}}` → `{:user {}}` promotes `[:user]` `:removed`.
- One surviving key: `{:f {:a 1 :keep 0}}` → `{:f {:b 2 :keep 0}}` gives `[:f]` `:children`, not promoted.
- The sibling ruling's own case, set swap `{:tags #{:door/locked}}` → `{:tags #{:door/closed}}`, gives `[:tags]` `:children`.

So only the "every key replaced" map shape is wrong, which is exactly the set shape rf2-l0us2 fixed.

## Evidence

Executed with a one-shot `clojure -M` probe from my scratch directory, with nothing written to the tree. It loads the frozen tree's `tools/xray/src` and pinned `juji/editscript 0.6.5`, and prints raw edits beside `:path-ops`, `:container-ops`, `:wholly-changed-roots` and `op-at`.

- Renderer effect: inspected at the cited lines. `removed-ancestor?` is set only from the structural `::missing` sentinel (`edn_inspector.cljs:3994-4040`), so there is no renderer-side override of a projected `:removed` on a present container.
- Tests: `engine_cljs_test.cljc`'s R5 tests (`:42-65`) cover wholly-new, wholly-removed and a mixed subtree, and no key-swap case.
- Tracker: no bead covers map key-swap promotion. rf2-l0us2 and rf2-4vp8c are cited in source for sets only.

## Smallest fix

Take the same union for maps that `collect-leaves` already takes for sets. In the `(map? data)` arm, iterate the union of `data`'s keys and the `opposite` map's keys. A key present only on the opposite side then contributes a leaf path whose op (`:added` or `:removed`) breaks the one-sided uniformity at the map and every ancestor.

- A genuine new or removed subtree is unaffected: the opposite side is absent or empty, so the union is one side.
- The engine docstring and spec 004's "maps and vectors are unaffected" sentence change to say maps take the union too.

Fence:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc`;
- `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine_cljs_test.cljc`;
- `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md` (not a hot-zone file).

The fence overlaps the other two diff-engine beads filed under this surface, so sequence them.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `tools/xray` (JVM: `engine.cljc` and its `.cljc` test carry no `:cljs` branch on the changed forms). `npm run test:cljs` also runs the test on the node lane.

Spec 004 is under `tools/`, so no link gate reaches it through `mkdocs` staging. `check_doc_slugs.py` covers `tools/*/spec`: run it if links change, otherwise check by hand.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xray-chrome-config: pop-out L2/L3 seam drag binds the OPENER's document - the drag is dead and leaves a live drag armed on the host page that resizes and persists the list height on hover
description:
## Defect

In pop-out mode, dragging the L2/L3 seam does nothing, and it leaves a live drag armed on the HOST page.

`start-seam-drag!` attaches its `pointermove`, `pointerup` and `pointercancel` listeners to `js/document`. It also sets `js/document.body.style.cursor` to `row-resize`. The pop-out shell runs in the opener's JS realm, so `js/document` is the OPENER's document. The seam itself is painted into the pop-out's document.

What happens:

- The pop-out's pointer events never reach those listeners, so the drag does not resize.
- The release in the pop-out never reaches `seam-on-document-up`, so the listeners stay attached and `seam-drag-state` stays set.
- The opener's body keeps the `row-resize` cursor.
- When the pointer later moves over the host page, `seam-on-document-move` fires. It dispatches `[:rf.xray/set-events-list-height-px (+ start-height dy)]`, where `dy` mixes opener coordinates with a pop-out `start-y`. The pop-out's event-list height jumps around as the user hovers the host page, and each move persists through `update-setting!`. This lasts until the user clicks somewhere on the host page.

The same opener-document pattern appears for the modal focus trap, the shell dividers and the resizable table. That is filed as rf2-3x7nj.25.5, which explicitly leaves `resize_handle.cljs:291-296` and `:702-707` to this slice. This bead covers the seam drag at :702-707.

The panel-width drag at :291-296 has the same code but is not reachable in the pop-out. `Handle` renders only when `(= mode :inline)` (:594-595), so it is not a finding.

## Where

Cited at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle.cljs:666-709` is `start-seam-drag!`.
  - :700-701 sets the opener body cursor.
  - :702-707 runs `(.addEventListener js/document "pointermove" …)`, and the same for `pointerup` and `pointercancel`.
- `resize_handle.cljs:648-658` is `seam-on-document-move`, which dispatches `:rf.xray/set-events-list-height-px`.
- `resize_handle.cljs:634-646` is `seam-detach-document-listeners!`. Only `pointerup` or `pointercancel` on the opener document reaches it.
- `resize_handle.cljs:835-866` is `seam-handle-tree`, whose `:on-pointer-down` calls `start-seam-drag!`. There is no `setPointerCapture`, and there is no element-level move handler.
- `resize_handle.cljs:869-903` is `seam-handle-view`, headed unconditionally by `shell.cljs:3228` in `dynamic-chrome`. `surface-composer` (`shell.cljs:3281-3283`) mounts that chrome for Dynamic mode, the default, in both the inline and the pop-out shell.
- `mount.cljs:1746-1784`: `popout!` renders `[shell/ShellView {:mode :popout}]` into a node in `(.-document win)`. The code executing it is the opener realm's.
- `registry.cljs:661-671`: the height handler clamps against `js/window.innerHeight`, the opener's, then calls `config/update-setting!`, which persists.
- Public entry points: the pop-out, opened by the `⛶` button, `(xray/popout!)` or the palette's Ctrl+Enter. The drag is then a plain mouse gesture on the seam.
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md` §Splitter affordance ("click-and-drag from anywhere along the seam → resizes the list"). `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:366-377` says DOM events do not cross realms.

## Failure scenario

1. Pop out Xray. The pop-out is in Dynamic mode, the default, so the L2/L3 seam is visible.
2. Press on the seam, drag down, release. The event list does not resize.
3. Move the mouse over the host application window without clicking. The host page shows a `row-resize` cursor.
4. The pop-out's event list changes height with every pointer move over the host page, clamped to the opener's viewport. Each value is written to localStorage (`re-frame2.xray.settings.v1`).
5. Clicking anywhere on the host page finally detaches the listeners.

## Evidence

**Inspected only.** This is a multi-window, CLJS-only DOM interaction, and browsers and shadow-cljs are out of bounds for this review. I am confident for three reasons:

- `js/document` in code evaluated by the opener realm is the opener's document. That is the premise rf2-61i5 and rf2-3x7nj.25.5 already rest on. rf2-61i5 is why `popout!` installs a separate keydown listener on the pop-out's `doc` (`mount.cljs:1799-1801`, `keybinding.cljs:364-372`).
- The seam has no pointer capture and no element-level `pointermove`. The listener set is exactly the three `js/document` listeners.
- Only the document listeners call the detach function.

Control for the zero, re-run on the frozen tree: `git grep -c -e ownerDocument -e defaultView -e setPointerCapture -- tools/xray/src` finds 0 matches (exit 1). The same instrument finds 36 lines of `js/document` in `resize_handle.cljs`, so it can find what it looks for. rf2-3x7nj.25.5 records the same zero.

The keyboard path (`handle-seam-keydown!`, an element `:on-key-down`) and double-click reset work in the pop-out. Only pointer dragging is broken.

Tracker: `start-seam-drag!` and `seam-on-document-move` appear in 0 records of the tracker export. The control term `install-opener-gone-overlay!` appears in 2. rf2-3x7nj.25.5 is open and names these lines as outside its slice.

## Smallest fix

In `start-seam-drag!`, take the document from the event target, `(.. e -currentTarget -ownerDocument)`, and attach the listeners and the cursor to that document instead of `js/document`. Keep that document in `seam-drag-state` so `seam-detach-document-listeners!` removes the listeners from the same document.

Applying the same one-line change to `start-drag!` at :291-296 is cheap consistency, not a fix, because that path is inline-only.

Better still, fold this into rf2-3x7nj.25.5's fix, which needs the same owner-document helper for `shell.cljs` and `resizable_table.cljs`.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle.cljs`. Also touch `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs` and `resize_handle_dom_cljs_test.cljs` wherever they pin the listener target. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`resize_handle.cljs` is a `.cljs` file, so no JVM lane sees it. Two lanes grade it:

- `npm run test:cljs`, the node lane, runs `resize_handle_cljs_test`.
- The browser lane runs `resize_handle_dom_cljs_test`, whose name ends `-dom-cljs-test`.

Neither lane opens a real second window. Proving the pop-out behaviour takes a manual pop-out check.

## Decision needed

No. It could be sequenced with rf2-3x7nj.25.5 so one worker does all four document-scoped sites.
