title: pair-mcp: snapshot's :elided-large counts markers across the whole walked state, so summary and path-sliced replies report markers they do not contain
description:
## Defect

`snapshot`'s `:elided-large` indicator is counted app-side over the whole walked state: every frame's full `:app-db`, every `:sub-cache` entry, and every `:epochs` record. The count is taken **before** the client-side pipeline slices `:app-db` to `path`, or replaces slices with `{:rf.mcp/summary ...}` markers. The pipeline then uses that server count as-is. So the default `snapshot {}` (summary mode, which ships no app-db values) and any path-sliced read (`snapshot {:path [:user]}`) report `:elided-large N` for markers that are not in the response. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3045 defines the slot as "the count of `:rf.size/large-elided` markers ENCOUNTERED in the tool's response payload". The code comment justifying the shortcut ("Dedup never touches `:app-db` ... so the server-side count is exact post-pipeline") overlooks the path slice and the summary pass, both of which do remove markers.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`, under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/`:

- `snapshot.cljs:224-228` (the eval form) and `:249`/`:264`/`:305` (`server-elided` is threaded into the pipeline and out as the envelope's `:elided-large`): `:elided-count (count (filter ... (tree-seq coll? seq walked)))`, over the full walked per-frame map.
- `wire_pipeline.cljs:115-165` (`run-snapshot-map`): `slice-app-db-in-snapshot` (path slice, or `tree-summary` in the default summary mode) at `:136`, then `elided (if (some? server-elided) server-elided ...)` at `:150-152`, then `summarise-other-slices-in-snapshot` at `:154-155`. The indicator is never recomputed after those steps.
- `snapshot_pipeline.cljs:87-116` (`slice-app-db-in-snapshot`: "No path + summary mode (the default): summarise").

Entry point: MCP `tools/call` `snapshot`, with no args or with `:path`.

## Failure scenario

The frame declares `{:large [[:docs :body]]}` and holds a large body there.

- `snapshot {}` returns `:app-db {:rf.mcp/summary {...}}`, which contains no markers, together with `:elided-large 1`.
- `snapshot {:path "[:user]"}` returns the complete `[:user]` subtree, which contains no markers, together with `:elided-large 1`.

In both cases the agent is told that a large value was elided *from what it is looking at*. It searches the `[:user]` subtree for a marker that is not there, or treats a complete value as partial.

## Evidence

Inspected; CLJS-only files. Order of operations in `run-snapshot-map`: scrub, then `slice-app-db-in-snapshot`, then cap / diff-encode / dedup of `:epochs`, then `elided := server-elided`, then summarise the other slices. The server count comes from `walked` (`snapshot.cljs:224-228`), which is the pre-slice, pre-summary state. The `:epoch-vector` arm (`wire_pipeline.cljs:167-200`) is the control: it counts over its own post-encode payload (`count-elided-markers encoded`, `:196`), so those tools report what they ship. Only the snapshot arm uses the pre-pipeline count.

Tracker: rf2-g1t33.2 (closed, mcp-base spec audit) mentions `elided-large` generally. No bead covers snapshot's count source.

## Smallest fix

Count markers over the shipped `:app-db` / `:sub-cache` slices after `slice-app-db-in-snapshot` and `summarise-other-slices-in-snapshot` (`count-elided-markers` over those slices of `summarised`). For `:epochs`, keep counting before dedup, as the epoch-vector arm does. Alternatively, restrict the server count to the path and mode the client will ship. Fence: `wire_pipeline.cljs` (and possibly `snapshot.cljs`), plus a test with a declared-large slot outside the requested path. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm test` in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` (CLJS only).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict — FIXED in PR #10308 (2026-09-24 07:27:51 AUSEST, worker pair-mcp2-3x7nj)

Commit `e666cf45be`.

What changed: snapshot's `:elided-large` was the eval form's app-side count over the whole walked state (every frame's full `:app-db`, every `:sub-cache` entry, every epoch), so a summary-mode or path-sliced snapshot reported markers it never contained. `run-snapshot-map` now counts with `count-shipped-markers` AFTER the path slice and the summary pass; full-mode epochs are counted pre-dedup, because dedup pools identical markers. The `:server-elided` opt no longer feeds the snapshot-map arm.

Decisive measurement: restoring the `:server-elided` whole-state count turned pair-mcp `npm test` RED with 6 failures across the four count pins (`snapshot-summary-mode-counts-no-marker-it-does-not-ship`, `snapshot-path-slice-counts-only-the-addressed-subtree`, `snapshot-full-epochs-are-counted-pre-dedup`, `snapshot-map-arm-counts-what-ships-not-server-elided`); restored and blob-hash verified; green 1235 / 4577 / 0 failures.
Merged-PR audit #10308 (0d9c23f1549472549f0046f584112a1fdcb7b26a; merged 2026-09-23T21:56:41Z). Completeness: All seven tools honor the independent size override; sensitive opt-in remains launch-gated. Marker docs explain live paths and historical reads, digest slots are omitted unless strings, and snapshot indicators count shipped content. Dormant epoch-option/spec alignment already has separate rf2-aakv6/rf2-c5ggd work. Correctness: Reviewed all seven coercion changes, profile floor and marker construction, post-summary/pre-dedup counting, and checked the epoch-by-id recipe against its actual argument order. Accepted reported pair 1235/4577, CLJS 12583/63420, affected JVM suites and targeted negative controls; CI 77 successful checks. Implementation quality: Separates size ergonomics from sensitive-data authority without bypassing projection; truthful markers and counts reuse existing wire shapes. No material additional finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: story-ui-workspace: Run all and watch mode drop the run's :status, so a thrown fx, floor failure or :cannot-run records a green :pass dot
description:
## Defect

The sidebar's Run all button and watch mode record each variant's result without its run-level `:status`. `run-one-test!` builds the summary from `aggregate-summary` of `:assertions` plus timings, and never threads `(:status result)`. `record-test-run` therefore falls back to deriving the status from assertion counts.

Every verdict the agreement floor or a run-level refusal decides is lost on this path. That covers:
- a thrown fx or handler (a run-level `:error`, which spec 009 says lowers to `:fail`);
- an unconsumed schema violation;
- a non-ok epoch outcome;
- a run-level `:cannot-run`.

All of these are recorded as a green `:pass` dot, as long as the assertions that did run passed. The Tests pane's own write (`test_mode/state.cljs` `store-result!`) does thread `:status`. The same variant therefore shows a red dot after Re-run and a green dot after Run all.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/sidebar.cljs:690-721` is `run-one-test!`. The summary is built at `:711-715` with no `:status`.
- It is reached from `run-all-tests!` (`:723-734`, the widget's Run all button) and from `watch-rerun!` (`:736-749`, the watch-mode detector in `shell.cljs`).
- Contrast `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/state.cljs:130-138`, which threads `:status (:status result)` with the comment "so the sidebar dot reflects a tape-floor `:fail` / `:cannot-run` refusal the assertion counts alone might miss".
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/state/tests.cljc:115-156`, `record-test-run`: an explicit `:status` wins; otherwise the status is `:pending` for zero assertions and `:pass` when all pass.
- Contract: `tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md:330-360`. §Status semantics says a run-level `:error` lowers to `:fail` at `record-test-run` write time. §Run all says the widget and the pane "stay in sync".

## Failure scenario

1. A `:test`-tagged variant dispatches an event whose `:fx` runs a registered fx that throws. The `:db` still commits, and the script's single `path-equals` assertion passes.
2. `run-variant` returns `:status :fail`, because the effect row carries `:outcome :error`, which is agreement-floor evidence.
3. Click Run all, or let watch mode re-run the variant.
4. The sidebar dot is green `:pass` and the widget headline reads all-green.
5. Open the variant's Tests pane and click Re-run: the dot turns red.
6. Click Run all again: the dot turns green.

The same path records:
- a run whose only problem is a run-level `:cannot-run` as `:pass`, when its assertions passed, or as `:pending` otherwise;
- a vacuous zero-assertion run that the floor judged `:fail` as grey `:pending`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe from `tools/story` on the frozen tree (`034d0c8fc8`), using the `story_ui_test.clj` reset-fixture boot. The probe replicates `run-one-test!` exactly: `record-test-run` of `aggregate-summary` plus `:elapsed-ms`/`:ran-at-ms`, with no `:status`. It compares that against the pane's `store-result!` shape, which adds `:status`.

Variant `:story.probe/floor` (a throwing fx after the db commit):
- `run-variant` `:status` = `:fail`
- assertions = `[[:rf.assert/path-equals :pass]]`
- effects = `[{:fx-id :probe/boom ... :outcome :error}]`
- summary `{:total 1 :passed 1 :failed 0 :all-passed? true}`
- RUN-ALL dot = `:pass`; PANE dot = `:fail`; `test-summary` `:all-green?` = `true`

Control, `:story.probe/clean` (same shape, non-throwing fx): `:pass` on both paths.

The existing pin cannot catch this. `tools/story/test/re_frame/story_ui_test.clj:863-900` (`run-all-runs-declarative-expectation-variants`) replicates the same no-`:status` pipeline, so it mirrors the defect.

Tracker search: no bead names `run-one-test!` as dropping `:status`. The only mention is `rf2-20lwk`'s notes, which list it as one of the two dot writers and do not rule on it.

## Smallest fix

Add `:status (:status result)` to the summary in `run-one-test!` (`sidebar.cljs:711-715`), the same line `store-result!` carries. Better, have both writers call one shared "result → summary" helper in `ui/state/tests.cljc` so they cannot drift again.

Update the JVM pin in `story_ui_test.clj` to fold `:status` too, and add a floor-failure case (a throwing fx) beside it.

Fence: `ui/sidebar.cljs`, `ui/state/tests.cljc` (optional helper), `test/re_frame/story_ui_test.clj`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

- `sidebar.cljs` is CLJS-only, so the fix itself is compiled only by the CLJS lane (`npm run test:cljs`).
- A shared helper in `ui/state/tests.cljc` and the `story_ui_test.clj` pin are graded by the tools/story JVM artefact (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/story`).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## FIX — PR #10317 (worker/story-ws-3x7nj), 2026-09-24

Premise verified at trunk 51fe95a7fb with a JVM probe from tools/story. A variant whose `:dispatch-sync` event commits `:db` and then runs a throwing registered fx gave `run-variant` `:status :fail`, from one effect row with `:outcome :error`, while its single `path-equals` assertion passed. `aggregate-summary` reads `:all-passed? true`, so the `run-one-test!` fold recorded `:pass`.

One caveat: the tape needs `re-frame.epoch` loaded. With `-n re-frame.story-ui-test` alone the run records NO effects and reads `:pass`, so that namespace now requires `re-frame.epoch`.

Fix: `sidebar.cljs` `run-one-test!` adds `:status (:status result)` to the summary, the same slot `test_mode/state.cljs` `store-result!` threads.

The optional shared result→summary helper was NOT done. Its second writer, `test_mode/state.cljs`, is outside both this item's fence and the dispatch fence, so a one-caller helper would not stop the drift.

Tests:
- The three JVM replicas of the Run-all pipeline in `story_ui_test.clj` now fold `:status`.
- New JVM pin: `run-all-records-the-run-level-status`, with a throwing fx and a quiet-fx control.
- The real witness is the node-lane ns `re-frame.story.ui.run-all-status-cljs-test`. It drives the private `run-one-test!` and reads the dot.

Control: CI node-test job 107416574113 ran on control commit a6c4ee5669 (sources back at base, tests kept). `run-all-records-the-run-level-status` went RED at the dot assertion, with `:pass` recorded. Its precondition held: counts 1 passed / 0 failed. Its quiet-fx control stayed green. With the fix (50973da622, job 107409346262) the test is green. The fix sources were checked restored by blob hash, and the control commit was dropped.
Merged-PR audit #10317 (63e118215cb01387943edb775501b714367f58e3; merged 2026-09-23T23:38:52Z). Completeness: All four workspace findings are covered across canvas, grid, workspace, switchers and Run all. The run-owner listener also addresses open audit finding rf2-iftxj, annotated without status change. Correctness: Read every production diff and the actual rerun regression. Compiled plan drives component/substrates/args/decorators, override scope covers both missing render paths, status is preserved, and run generation guards reject stale settlement. Implementation quality: Consolidates previously duplicated plan reads and uses the existing run owner as the notification source. No additional public authoring knobs, no new actionable finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-iftxj.

title: http: CLJS JSON request bodies serialise a UUID as an object of cljs.core internals and drop keyword namespaces (JVM Cheshire sends the string / keeps the namespace)
description:
## Defect

On CLJS the managed-HTTP JSON request-body encoder, `re-frame.http.json/json-stringify`, is `(js/JSON.stringify (clj->js v))`. Two common EDN values get the wrong wire form, and the JVM (Cheshire) encodes both correctly:

1. **UUIDs are serialised as an object of cljs.core internals, not a string.** `clj->js` passes a `cljs.core/UUID` through unchanged: it is not a coll, a keyword or `IEncodeJS`. `UUID` has no `toJSON`, so `JSON.stringify` enumerates the deftype's own fields. `{:id (random-uuid)}` goes out as `{"id":{"uuid":"…","__hash":null,"cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$":…}}`, and under `:advanced` the field names are also renamed. The JVM sends `{"id":"…"}`.
2. **Keyword namespaces are silently dropped, in both keys and values.** `clj->js` defaults `:keyword-fn` to `name`. `{:user/id 1 :status :order/pending}` goes out as `{"id":1,"status":"pending"}` on CLJS and `{"user/id":1,"status":"order/pending"}` on the JVM.

This is the default path for every map body. `encode-body` uses it for `:request-content-type :json` AND for any Clojure collection sent with no content type. So a CLJS app sending an entity id gets a malformed payload with no error, and the same handler run through SSR (JVM) sends a different body.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree), host: **CLJS only** (the `:cljs` arm of a reader conditional).

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/json.cljc:51-56` (`json-stringify`; the CLJS arm at 56).
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc:137-138` (`:request-content-type :json`) and `:150-151` (default for colls).
- Reached from `prepare-body!`, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1698-1712`, on every attempt of `[:rf.http/managed {:request {:body {…} …}}]`.
- Contract: `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:168` (`:json` = JSON.stringify (CLJS) / Cheshire (JVM)) and `:209-211` (coll bodies JSON-encoded). Nothing documents a per-host difference in body encoding. The spec calls out per-host divergences row by row, and this one is not among them.
- ClojureScript in use: 1.12.145 (`implementation/core/deps.edn:36`). There, `clj->js` is `cljs/core.cljs:11130-11155` (`:or {keyword-fn name}`, UUID falls to `:else x`), and `deftype UUID` is `:11699-11725` (no `toJSON`).

## Failure scenario

Two CLJS cases:

- `{:fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request {:method :post :url "/api/orders" :body {:id (random-uuid) :status :order/pending}} :reply-to [:saved]}]]}`. The server receives `{"id":{"uuid":"6f1c…","__hash":null,"cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$":2153775104,"cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition1$":2048},"status":"pending"}`. The identical request from the JVM sends `{"id":"6f1c…","status":"order/pending"}`.
- `:body {:order/id 1 :customer/id 7}`. Both keys lower to `"id"` on the same JS object before serialisation, so one value silently overwrites the other and the server receives a single `"id"`. The JVM sends `{"order/id":1,"customer/id":7}`.

## Evidence

- **JVM arm, EXECUTED** (JVM probe, frozen tree, http `:test` classpath). `(re-frame.http.json/json-stringify {:id #uuid "6f1c2b3a-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" :status :order/pending :user/name "ann"})` gave `{"id":"6f1c2b3a-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","status":"order/pending","user/name":"ann"}`.
- **CLJS arm, EXECUTED against the compiled constructor, not a full CLJS run** (shadow-cljs is off-limits for this review). I extracted `cljs.core.UUID`'s compiled constructor from an existing shadow dev build (`implementation/out/hicasso-testbed/cljs-runtime/cljs.core.js:37153-37158` in the mayor checkout: it sets `this.uuid`, `this.__hash` and the two protocol-mask fields), then ran `JSON.stringify({id: new cljs.core.UUID("6f1c…", null), status: "pending"})` in node. Output: `{"id":{"uuid":"6f1c2b3a-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","__hash":null,"cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$":2153775104,"cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition1$":2048},"status":"pending"}`. The same compiled file contains 0 occurrences of `toJSON`.
- **Keyword half, INSPECTED** from the `clj->js` source above: the default `keyword-fn` is `name`, and it is applied to both keyword values and keyword keys through `key->js`.
- Tests: `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_json_cljs_test.cljs:85-93` and `http_json_test.clj:119-130` stringify only `{:a 1 :b "hello"}` / vectors / scalars. No UUID and no namespaced keyword, so neither host's behaviour is pinned. Tracker search for `json-stringify`, `clj->js`, `keyword-fn` and UUID+JSON found no bead on this.

## Smallest fix

CLJS arm only: `(js/JSON.stringify (clj->js v :keyword-fn #(subs (str %) 1)) (fn [_ x] (if (uuid? x) (str x) x)))`. That keeps namespaces the way Cheshire does and turns a UUID into its string through the JSON replacer. ## Gates

The change sits inside `#?(:cljs …)` in `json.cljc`, so only the CLJS lane compiles it: `npm run test:cljs`, which runs `http_json_cljs_test.cljs`. A JVM green says nothing about it. The JVM half of the new pin runs in `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/http`.

## Decision needed

Which host's keyword convention is canonical for JSON bodies? Cheshire keeps the namespace (`"user/id"`); `clj->js` drops it (`"id"`). I recommend Cheshire's, because dropping it can merge distinct keys. The UUID half needs no decision.

RULING: option (A). A keyword in a managed-HTTP JSON body keeps its namespace on BOTH hosts (Cheshire's convention): `:user/id` goes out as "user/id", `:id` as "id", in keys and values alike, and a UUID goes out as its canonical string wherever it appears (value or map key). Only the CLJS arm of `re-frame.http.json/json-stringify` moves; no option, no compatibility mode, no refusal of qualified keywords.

WHY
- It is the only option that is host-identical and cannot silently merge distinct keys. Today the browser sends `{:order/id 1 :customer/id 7}` as {"id":7} (the order id is lost with no error), while the JVM sends {"order/id":1,"customer/id":7}. The same handler run under SSR or a JVM test therefore sends different bytes from the browser, so a JVM test cannot vouch for the browser payload.
- It round-trips through the framework's own decoder: `json-parse` already keywordizes "user/id" to `:user/id` (namespace "user") on both hosts (JVM `(keyword k)` key-fn, json.cljc ~:95-101; CLJS `js->clj :keywordize-keys true`, ~:133). So today a CLJS app cannot round-trip its own namespaced keys and a JVM app can.
- The JVM arm is already correct, so the change is one arm on one host. json.cljc's own `json-parse` comment (rf2-x1uhu) already states the house rule: the helper is shared/promotable and "the two readers must behave identically"; this extends that to the writer.
- Precedent: commit 367d9a0c86 (2026-06-04, rf2-t2n04, "preserve keyword namespaces in wire structuredContent") made exactly this call for the pair-MCP JSON wire because name-only keys "silently corrupt key-bearing reads".
- The dossier and the independent Codex review AGREED on (A). Codex added two qualifications, both adopted below: bound the promise (not "lossless"), and compare parsed JSON in tests. Codex also corrected one argument against (C): a refusal would NOT strictly need a new `:rf.error/*` id, because `prepare-body!` (transport.cljc ~:1698-1712) already catches any encoder throw and delivers `:rf.http/transport` with `:stage :request-prep`. So (C) loses on ergonomics, not on cost.
- (B) drop-the-namespace loses: it makes a lossy, silently key-merging default canonical on both hosts, and moving the JVM needs either a pre-walk or a global Cheshire `add-encoder` on Keyword, which would change every Cheshire caller in the process (story-mcp's protocol encoder among them). Making (B) safe needs collision detection, which is (C).
- (C) refuse-qualified-keywords loses: "we trust the programmer" rejects a failed request for data a Clojure backend wants exactly as written. Under (A) the programmer keeps full control of the wire key: write `:id` (or "id") to send "id".

THE PROMISE, BOUNDED (Codex's correction to the dossier's "lossless" wording)
The rule is namespace-preserving and host-identical, NOT lossless. Keyword and UUID VALUES decode back as strings (ordinary JSON). A map holding both `:invoice/id` and "invoice/id" collides: Cheshire emits two members with the same name, CLJS keeps one, and both decode to one entry (Codex probe with `(array-map :invoice/id 11 "invoice/id" 22)`); RFC 8259 §4 already says duplicate names are not interoperable. Do not add key validation for this.

title: testbed-support: CORS contract false on the real dev-http server - every endpoint response also carries shadow's ACAO *, and the 204 preflight goes out as 304
description:
## Defect

The endpoint's CORS contract is false on the real shadow-cljs `:dev-http` server, in two ways the unit tests cannot see because they assert the Ring map rather than the wire. (1) shadow's `start-build-server` installs a handler FIRST in the chain that sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response, and shadow-http 0.1.8 keeps response headers in a case-SENSITIVE `HashMap`, so this namespace's lowercase `access-control-allow-origin` lands as a SECOND header: every endpoint response carries both `*` and the reflected origin (or `null`). (2) shadow-http's Ring adapter writes a nil body through `respondNoContent`, which forces status 304, so the loopback `OPTIONS` preflight the handler answers as 204 goes out as 304. A browser fails CORS on either (a combined `*, <origin>` value matches nothing; a preflight must have an ok 2xx status). The spec's "CORS reflects only a validated loopback origin; it never emits `*`" and "Loopback `OPTIONS` returns 204" are both untrue on the server the testbeds run. No shipped caller is hurt today — the core client posts a RELATIVE URL, so it is always same-origin and never CORS-checked — which also means the CORS machinery serves only a hypothetical cross-port caller, and that caller would see the editor launch server-side, the fetch reject on the duplicate header, and the client's `editor://` fallback open the file a second time.

## Where

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj:546-563` (`json-resp` writes lowercase `"access-control-allow-origin"`), `:590-596` (the 204 `OPTIONS` answer with no `:body`), at `034d0c8fc8`.
- `thheller/shadow-cljs` 3.4.10 `shadow/cljs/devtools/server/dev_http.clj:94-98`: the first `req-handler` reifies `(.setResponseHeader request "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" "*")` on every request.
- `com.thheller/shadow-http` 0.1.8 `shadow/http/server/HttpRequest.java:69` (`responseHeaders = new HashMap<>()`), `:344-345` (`setResponseHeader` is a plain `put`), `:365-367` (`respondNoContent` sets `responseStatus = 304`); `shadow/http/server/ring.clj:77-79` routes a nil body there.
- Contract: `tools/testbed-support/spec/README.md:77` ("it never emits `*`") and `:150-152` ("Loopback `OPTIONS` returns 204 ... never `*`").
- Tests asserting the Ring map only: `open_in_editor_server_test.clj:95-110` (`guard-allows-valid-local-post`, reflected origin "not `*`"), `:418-433` (`guard-options-preflight-reflects-loopback-origin`, `(= 204 ...)`).
- The only client, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs:67-80,101`, builds `"/__rf-open-in-editor?..."` (relative) and fetches it same-origin; `rg -i "cross-port"` over the tree finds the phrase only in this namespace and its test (`open_in_editor_server.clj:550,590`, `open_in_editor_server_test.clj:97`), so no cross-port testbed exists.

## Failure scenario

A page on `http://localhost:8042` POSTs `http://localhost:8031/__rf-open-in-editor?file=...&line=3&column=9` (the cross-port shape the handler's comments and `guard-allows-valid-local-post` describe). The server launches the editor and answers 200 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` AND `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:8042`; the browser combines them, the CORS check fails, `fetch` rejects, `fetch-launcher!`'s `.catch` runs `fallback!`, and the `editor://` URI opens the same file again. A non-simple cross-port request fails earlier, at the 304 preflight.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe ran the REAL shadow-cljs 3.4.10 `:dev-http` server (`dev-http/start-build-server`) bound to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port with this namespace's `handler` and `launch!` replaced by a spy (no Node spawned), then read raw responses over a socket. Loopback POST with `Origin: http://localhost:8042` -> `HTTP/1.1 200` with both `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:8042` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; the same-origin POST (no Origin) -> both `access-control-allow-origin: null` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; the 403 and 405 answers likewise carried both. Loopback `OPTIONS` with `Origin: http://localhost:8042` -> `HTTP/1.1 304` with both origin headers. Control: an off-endpoint 404 and the push-state 200 carry only shadow's `*`, so the second header is this namespace's. IPv6 (`::1` server, `[::1]` Host) showed the same duplicate. Security is NOT weakened: the duplicate makes browsers deny, and admission (peer, Host, Origin) is unaffected — every refusal case in the probe still answered 403.

Tracker: `bd search "preflight"` / `"Access-Control-Allow-Origin"` / `"respondNoContent"` `--status all` — rf2-8fms7 measured PEER renderings on a live shadow-http server but asserted the preflight's 204 only at the Ring level; nothing records the wire status or the duplicate header. Not previously filed or ruled.

## Smallest fix

Either (A, recommended — the only client is same-origin by construction): delete the CORS surface — the `OPTIONS` branch, the `access-control-allow-origin`/`vary` headers and `allow-origin` — and state "same-origin only" in the spec, updating the preflight/reflection tests. Or (B): make it real — emit the header as `"Access-Control-Allow-Origin"` (that exact casing replaces shadow's `*` entry in shadow-http's case-sensitive map) and give the preflight a non-nil `:body` so the adapter does not rewrite it to 304, then add one probe-level test against a started server so the Ring-map assertions stop standing in for the wire. Fence either way: `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj`, its test, `tools/testbed-support/spec/README.md`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM only: `clojure -M:test` from `tools/testbed-support/`. No CLJS change.

## Decision needed

Yes: (A) delete the unused cross-port CORS surface and declare same-origin only, or (B) keep and repair it so it works on shadow-http.

Keep all the admission checks — loopback TCP peer, loopback Host, loopback-or-absent Origin — and keep the endpoint POST-only. Do not repair CORS for shadow-http (B). The dossier and the independent Codex review both chose A. I re-verified the load-bearing facts at trunk 7fc78b7b72. `git log 034d0c8fc8..origin/main` over every cited path returns 0 commits (control: 11 commits touch spec/ over the same range).

1. The CORS surface has no caller.

The fetch is `(js/fetch url #js {:method "POST" …})`, so every real request is same-origin and no browser ever CORS-checks it.
   - A search for an absolute endpoint URL (`https?://[^"' ]*__rf-open-in-editor`) outside node_modules finds 0 source files; the only hit is this bead's own text in .beads/issues.jsonl. title: xray-shell-views: edn-inspector toggle past :max-depth is dead - the click stores an override the depth cap never reads
description:
## Defect

The EDN inspector's depth-capped toggle does nothing. A container at `depth >= max-depth` renders as `▸ {…}`, and the `▸` is a real control: `role="button"`, `tabIndex 0`, `aria-expanded false`, an `on-click` and an Enter/Space keydown, all wired to `toggle-fn`. The code comment on it says "click expands one level", and the spec says the same. Clicking it does dispatch `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/toggle-node`, and the reducer stores `{:expanded? true}` for that path. But `depth-capped?` is `(>= depth max-depth)` and consults no override. `expanded?` requires `(not depth-capped?)`, and `children` requires `(not depth-capped?)` too, so the stored override can never take effect. Nothing on screen changes. The next click stores `{:expanded? false}`, again with no visible effect. Content below the cap is reachable only by zooming, and zoom exists only in the mounts that pass `:zoomable? true`.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:2905-2922`: the capped branch. The comment reads "click expands one level". It is a focusable `role="button"` toggle.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3245`: `depth-capped? (>= depth max-depth)`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3283-3285`: `expanded?` requires `(not depth-capped?)`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3342`: `children` requires `(not depth-capped?)`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3235` and `:4789`: the default `max-depth` is 16. No production caller in `tools/xray/src` passes `:max-depth`. The grep returns only comments, at `panels/epoch/view.cljs:5799` and `settings/view.cljs:974`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_state.cljs:57-79`: the toggle reducer stores the override that is never read for a capped node.
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:4198-4199` says "`:max-depth` — hard cap on recursion depth; deeper levels render `{…}` collapsed and click expands one level." The ns docstring at `edn_inspector.cljs:112-113` says the same.
- Test: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs:822-836` (`depth-capped-triangle-uses-shared-triangle-style`) looks up testid `rf-xray-edn-inspector-test-m--toggle`. That is the ROOT path `[]` at depth 0, which is not capped under `:max-depth 1`, so the test does not exercise the capped branch it is named for. No test clicks a capped toggle.

## Failure scenario

Any value nested 16 or more containers deep: a tree-structured app-db (an outline, a parsed document, a nested comment thread, a route tree), a deep trace payload, or a sub value. The operator expands levels down to depth 16 and sees `▸ {…}`. Clicking it, or focusing it and pressing Enter, changes nothing, and screen readers announce a collapsed button that never expands. In a non-zoomable mount there is no way to see the content.

## Evidence

- **Inspected**: the three guards above, read together. `expanded?` and `children` are both conjunctions containing `(not depth-capped?)`, and `depth-capped?` depends on `depth` and `max-depth` alone. The reducer's stored `{:expanded? true}` reaches `resolve-expanded?` only through `expanded?`, which is already false.
- **Test gap**: the only capped-branch test addresses the root node's testid, and nothing asserts that a click past the cap renders children.

## Smallest fix

Let an operator override lift the cap for the clicked node: `depth-capped? (and (>= depth max-depth) (not (resolve-expanded? expansion-map panel-id mount-id path false)))`. With a `false` default, only a stored `{:expanded? true}` lifts it (`edn_inspector_state.cljs:90-99`). Its children then render at `depth + 1`, capped again, which is exactly "click expands one level". Add a test that renders past the cap with a stored `{:expanded? true}` override and asserts the children are painted.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs` and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`, the node lane (`.cljs` only).

## Decision needed

No. The spec already states the intended behaviour.
notes:
## Worker verdict (ednins-3x7nj, PR #10323) — FIXED

At trunk 63e118215c the premise holds as described: `depth-capped?` was `(>= depth max-depth)`, and both `expanded?` and `children` required it to be false.

Fix (render-container): `depth-capped?` is now `(and (>= depth max-depth) (not (resolve-expanded? expansion-map panel-id mount-id path false)))`, the item's Smallest fix verbatim. The ns docstring's `:max-depth` line now says a click expands one level.

Tests:
- New `depth-capped-toggle-expands-one-level-rf2-3x7nj-25-4` produces the override from the capped `[:a]` toggle's own on-click, dispatches it through the real reducer, and re-renders.
- It then asserts that `[:a]` is open with `:b` painted, and that `[:a :b]` is a collapsed toggle with nothing painted below it.
- `depth-capped-triangle-uses-shared-triangle-style` used to address the root's testid, which is uncapped. It now addresses `[:a]`, the node actually at the cap.

Control, from the sabotage run described on rf2-3x7nj.25.1: 3 failures in the new test ([:a] open, :b painted, [:a :b] toggle present). The pre-click control assertions and the dispatch-payload assertion stayed green. On the restored tree it passes (exit 0).
Merged-PR audit #10323 (84fedecee409bac4a4d35dfb3ecd41bcafab60c2; merged 2026-09-24T00:17:21Z). Completeness: All four inspector fixes land: visible cut-sequence marker, list/seq zoom plus honest stale-path fallback, record tags in all render forms, and one-level expansion at the depth cap. Correctness: Read full inspector diff and regression scope. Sequence marker retains the stated realisation bound, zoom visibility and value use the same resolver, record tags follow the actual CLJS printer, and depth overrides are read at the capped node. Accepted local CLJS 12691/63976, 22-failure targeted control and green final CI. Implementation quality: Uses existing printer and expansion state instead of new metadata or UI state. Optional collapsed record tags improve the same defect with little complexity. No actionable new finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: examples-real-apps: realworld_http logout leaves the unsent comment draft for the next account on the same article (the same-slug principal crossing rf2-3x7nj.42.4 fixed in the resources twin)
description:
## Defect

In `realworld_http`, a logged-out user's unsent comment draft survives into the next account's comment box on the SAME article.

The http twin resets `[:comment-form]` only on a NEW article identity. Its `:comments/load` resets the form only when the requested slug differs from `[:comments :slug]`, which is the rf2-84iek rule. Nothing on logout touches the form. The auth machine's `:clear-session` action scrubs the settings draft and the feed, but not `:comment-form`. `:auth/clear-session` clears only `[:auth :user]` and `[:auth :token]`.

So the following sequence leaks one user's words to another:

1. alice types a comment on alpha and does not post it.
2. alice logs out, which navigates home.
3. bob signs in on that tab and opens alpha.
4. `:comments/load` sees the same slug and treats it as a refresh, so it keeps the form. Bob's comment box is pre-filled with alice's unsent text, ready to post under his name.

A different article resets the form, so only the same-slug case leaks.

This is the principal-crossing half that rf2-3x7nj.42.4 fixed in the resources twin with `(dissoc :comment-form)` in `:auth/clear-session`. Item 42.4 named only the resources files, so the http twin, which was the model for the cross-article half, was left alone. rf2-fn0kx.7 treats a draft crossing to another principal as a real defect ("logout leaves the previous user's settings draft behind and the next account can PUT it").

## Evidence

EXECUTED on the JVM (bb) at trunk `51fe95a7fb` plus the rf2-3x7nj.42 branch. The branch does not touch these files. The probe lifts the shipped `:comments/load`, `:comment-form/edit-field`, `:comment-form/initialise`, `:auth/clear-session` and `:feed/initialise` out of `realworld_http/{comments,auth,favorites}.cljs` and drives them with a db-only dispatcher:

- same slug, across a logout, bob opens alpha: the draft reads `"alice's unsent words"`.
- control, a different slug: the draft on beta reads `""`.

## Smallest fix

Scrub the form on logout. Either add `[:dispatch [:comment-form/initialise]]` to the auth machine's `:clear-session` action beside `[:settings/form [:reset]]`, or reset `:comment-form` in `:auth/clear-session`. The action's comment already states the rule: "no per-user state outlives the session".

Files: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs`. No hot-zone file. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm). Any pin belongs in `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Decision needed

No. It is the same ruling rf2-3x7nj.42.4 applied to the resources twin.
notes:

title: xray-domain-panels-b: Trace db diff reports equal-but-rebuilt leaves as :modified (diff-paths tests identical? only)
description:
## Defect

The Trace panel's per-path db diff reports a `:modified` path whose before and after are EQUAL. `diff-paths` decides "unchanged" by `identical?` only. A non-map leaf that the handler rebuilt with an equal value is therefore emitted as `{:op :modified :path [...] :before v :after v}` with `(= v v)`. Two common idioms produce this: `(vec (remove :done todos))` when nothing is done, and a set re-built with `into`.

The runtime disagrees. The router treats "a distinct-but-`=` value" as no change, and `:rf.event/db-changed` fires only when the app-db partition changed by value. So whenever a db-changed row fires for a REAL change elsewhere, Xray attaches that real change plus phantom `~ [:todos] X -> X` rows, which claim a path changed although its value did not. That is the same value-equality the router applies to the whole partition.

`db-changed-diff-triples`' own docstring and spec 023 §10.1 both promise `[]` when `db-before == db-after`. That holds only for the identity case.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:135-194`. In `diff-paths`, the per-key walk (from line 148) treats `(identical? bv av)` at line 162 as the only no-diff test. Its `:else` arm (line 169) and the top-level non-map `:else` (line 193) both emit `:modified`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:1152-1189` is `db-changed-diff-triples`. Its docstring says it "Returns `[]` when `db-before == db-after`".
- `attach-db-diff`, just below, puts the triples on every `:rf.event/db-changed` row.
- Runtime contract: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1426-1437`. db-changed "fires only when the app-db partition changed"; db-noop covers "a distinct-but-`=` value collapsed to no change".
- Public entry: the Trace panel's db-changed row, which lists per-path changes under APP-DB CHANGES.

Since rf2-xuyac (spec 004:123-133) the App-DB tab uses Editscript, which is value-based. `diff-paths` survives only for this Trace surface, so the App-DB tab is not affected.

## Failure scenario

1. A handler does two things: `(-> db (assoc :loading? false) (update :todos #(vec (remove :done %))))`, where no todo is done.
2. The runtime sees `:loading?` change, so a db-changed row fires.
3. The Trace panel's diff shows `~ [:loading?] true -> false`, which is correct.
4. It also shows `~ [:todos] [{:id 1 ...} {:id 2 ...}] -> [{:id 1 ...} {:id 2 ...}]`, with both sides identical.

An operator chasing "why did my todo list re-render?" is told `:todos` changed, although its value is unchanged. A sub that compares by value would not propagate from it.

## Evidence

This was **executed** as a bounded JVM probe, running the real `trace-helpers/db-changed-diff-triples` (1-arity) on the pair above:

```
(= (:todos before) (:todos after)) -> true
triple count -> 2
  :modified [:loading?]  before=after?  false
  :modified [:todos]  before=after?  true
--- control: only the scalar flip, :todos untouched (shared)
  :modified [:loading?]
```

A second probe on `diff-paths` directly gave these results:

- an equal rebuilt vector gave `[{:op :modified :path [:todos] ...}]`;
- an equal re-built set gave `[{:op :modified :path [:user :roles] ...}]`;
- equal scalars gave `[]`, and a genuinely changed vector gave one `:modified`. These are the controls.

That the render path draws `before -> after` for `:modified` is **inspected**, not executed. It rests on the `redact-triples` docstring at `trace_helpers.cljc:1134-1150` ("db-diff-row draws before only for :modified") and on `trace.cljs`, which is CLJS.

Spec quote: `tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:217`: "When `db-before == db-after` the diff is `[]` and the DB row renders no per-path sub-list".

A tracker search (`diff-paths` together with identical, or equal) found no ruling on this.

## Smallest fix

In `diff-paths`, change the `:else` arm to skip when `(= bv av)`, and emit `:modified` only when the values differ. That is O(size of that leaf) and is paid only on leaves that are not already identical, so the O(changed paths) walk is unchanged in shape.

- Fence: `app_db_diff_helpers.cljc` and its test.
- No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`app_db_diff_helpers.cljc` has no reader conditional at `diff-paths`, so the `tools/xray` JVM suite grades it (`clojure -M:test`, `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh`).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fixed in PR #10332 (worker xpanels-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Reproduced at trunk 982fb2ce41: diff-paths on the bead's pair gave [:modified [:loading?]] and [:modified [:todos]] with before = after; a set re-built with into gave [:modified [:user :roles]].

Fix (app_db_diff_helpers.cljc diff-paths): an `=` leaf is no change, both in the per-key walk (a clause before :else) and in the top-level non-map arm. The `=` walk runs only on a leaf that is not already identical?, so the O(changed paths) shape holds. After the fix: only [:modified [:loading?]]; the rebuilt set gives []; the controls (equal scalars [], a changed vector :modified) are unchanged. Spec 023 §10.1 now says the empty-diff equality is by value.

Control: with the fix removed, diff-paths-equal-but-rebuilt-leaf-is-no-change and db-changed-diff-triples-skip-an-equal-but-rebuilt-leaf went red (JVM).
Merged-PR audit #10332 (78e6cc1baf60796452734b92ebc638b7a1e688a2; merged 2026-09-24T01:24:15Z). Completeness: All four domain-panel fixes match their sources: before-only whole instances/areas/top removals survive projection and use the inspector removed-root marker; graph keys/edges carry concrete query/render identities; severity stage follows namespaced stage or preceding non-severity chronology; equal rebuilt leaves produce no modified row. Both spec pages align. Correctness: Accepted JVM Xray 1413 tests/6945 assertions, 30 planted-control failures, node 12717/64074 with exactly the new 14 tests/63 assertions, and CI 38 successes. Read projection-to-view wiring and focused removed-ghost/key/edge/stage/equality regressions. No rerun or concrete residual found. Implementation quality: Reuses the shared inspector absence marker and diff engine; instance identity travels through existing rows rather than adding a new graph abstraction. Stage calculation remains a small fire-order fold; structural sharing short-circuits before leaf value comparison. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

CI at that head: 88 checks passed, all four workflow runs complete; CLJS relied on CI — the node-test job read 12717 tests / 64074 assertions against 12703 / 64011 on the merge-base main run, +14 / +63, exactly the tests this PR adds, all passing (red controls for the CLJS-only halves NOT run). title: examples-core: docs/async/http.md's handler 'condensed from managed_http_counter' initiates in :else, so the :status :cancelled reply a manual abort delivers re-issues the request
description:
## Defect

`docs/async/http.md` §"One handler with :reply-to" shows a reply-to-self handler labelled `;; From examples/core/managed_http_counter (core.cljs), condensed.` The condensation puts the request-issuing arm in the `cond`'s `:else` slot. The example itself stopped doing that under rf2-fn0kx.2 finding 7: all four of its reply-to-self handlers test `(nil? reply)` for initiation, and `core.cljs:139-144` explains why. With `:else`, a delivered status the `cond` does not list falls through to the initiation arm and RE-ISSUES the request. Since rf2-8slzk (a93b608cbd), the example carries `:request-id` and a Cancel button. The same guide page (§Cancellation, `http.md:315`) says a manual `:rf.http/managed-abort` "does deliver a reply — a `:status :cancelled` envelope", and it points readers at this example for the abort path (`http.md:327`). So a reader who copies the guide's handler and adds the Cancel the page teaches gets a Cancel that restarts the request it cancelled. The page is the only reply-to-self handler in `docs/` or `skills/` shaped this way. Spec 014 example A tests presence (`(if reply …)`), and `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:55-67` handles `:cancelled` explicitly and warns that `:reply-to` delivers `:ok` / `:error` / `:cancelled`.

## Where

- `docs/async/http.md:150-167`: the fenced snippet, whose initiation arm is `:else` at line 164.
- `docs/async/http.md:169`: the prose already frames it as presence ("The first time it runs there is no `reply`…").
- `docs/async/http.md:315`: manual abort delivers `:status :cancelled`. `docs/async/http.md:327` sends the reader to the example for the abort path.
- The example it claims to condense: `examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:88-155`, with a `(nil? reply)` initiation at `:145`, a `:cancelled` arm at `:117-120`, a settle-only `:else` at `:154-155`, and the rationale at `:139-144`.
- Public entry points: `[:rf.http/managed {… :request-id id :reply-to [:counter/+1]}]` plus `[:rf.http/managed-abort id]`, both taught on that page.

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

## Failure scenario

A reader copies the guide's `:counter/+1`, adds `:request-id :counter/+1` to its request, and adds a Cancel button that dispatches `[:rf.http/managed-abort :counter/+1]`, as §Cancellation on the same page describes.

1. The user clicks +1. The request is in flight and status is `:loading`.
2. The user clicks Cancel. The framework delivers `[:counter/+1 {:status :cancelled :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :user} …}]`.
3. Neither the `:ok` arm nor the `:error` arm matches, so control reaches `:else`. The handler returns `:status :loading` and a fresh `[:rf.http/managed …]`, and the request is issued again. The spinner never clears, and the cancel un-cancels itself.

Any other delivered status the `cond` does not list takes the same path. `:cancelled` is also what an actor-destroy delivers to an ordinary event.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. A JVM probe (`clojure -M`, no deps) read both handler forms straight out of the frozen tree's text and `eval`'d them as plain fns. The docs form came from the fenced block after the "condensed" marker, and the example form came from `rf/reg-event :http-counter/+1` in `core.cljs`. Both are pure `cond` bodies.

- Docs handler, `[:counter/+1 {:status :cancelled :rf.reply/cancel-reason :user :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :user}}]` → `{:db #:counter{:status :loading}, :fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request {:url "api/inc.json"}, :reply-to [:counter/+1]}]]}`, which RE-ISSUES the request.
- Example handler, same reply → `{:db #:http-counter{:status :idle, :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted, :reason :user}}}`, with no `:fx`.
- Controls: the docs handler given no reply issues the request, the same map as above, and given `{:status :ok :value {:delta 1}}` it gives `{:db #:counter{:count 1, :status :idle, :error nil}}`. So the probe exercises the real forms, and the `:cancelled` row is the only divergence.

Reply shape: `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:668` says a manual abort "DOES dispatch `:on-failure` with `:reason :user`". `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:552` gives an abort `:status :cancelled` with `:cancelled? true`.

Census: Grep for a line that is just `:else` over `docs/async` returns 1 hit, at `http.md:164`. `(nil? reply)` has 0 hits in `docs/`, `skills/` and `spec/`, but 4 hits in the example (control). Every other reply-to-self teaching snippet found (spec 014 example A, and `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md`) tests presence or handles `:cancelled`.

Tracker: rf2-3lycj edited this very fence (a one-character URL fix) and did not touch the arm. rf2-8slzk listed `http.md:327` among the five sentences that "become true as written" but did not look at the fence at `:150-167`. Full-text search of a `bd export` for `http.md:151` and `http.md:164` gives 0 hits (control: `docs/async/http.md` gives 16).

## Smallest fix

Make the condensation match what it claims to condense: initiate on `(nil? reply)`, and give `:cancelled` (or the `:else` catch-all) a settle-only arm that never issues. Alternatively, reshape it as spec 014 example A does: `(if reply (case (:status reply) :ok … :error … :cancelled …) <issue>)`. The fence is `docs/async/http.md` only, and is not a hot-zone file.

## Gates

The edit is confined to a fenced code block. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` strips fences before reading links, and `mkdocs build --strict` validates link resolution, not Clojure. So neither gate can go red on this edit. Verify by hand: re-evaluate the edited handler with a `:status :cancelled` reply and confirm it returns no `:fx`. A pure `cond` needs no runtime. Say so in the PR body.

## Decision needed

no
notes:
## Fix landed in PR #10340 (worker examples2-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Premise verified at trunk b0973944f9: the fence's initiation arm was `:else`.

Fix: the fence now initiates on `(nil? reply)`, and `:else` settles the UI (`:counter/status :idle`) and never issues. The `:ok` and `:error` arms are unchanged.

The edit sits inside a fenced block, so neither link gate inspects it. It was verified by hand with a JVM probe that evaluates the fence's handler and the example's `:http-counter/+1` as plain fns:
- HEAD: a `:status :cancelled` reply returned a fresh `[:rf.http/managed …]` fx, i.e. it re-issued. Exit 1.
- Fixed: `{:db #:counter{:status :idle}}` with no `:fx`, matching the example. Exit 0.
- Controls: no reply still issues the request, and `:ok` still bumps the count.

Search control on the whole file: the old initiation comment went from 1 to 0, and `(nil? reply)` went from 0 to 1. The positive control, the "condensed." marker, is present on both sides.
Merged-PR audit #10340 (1ac8076c8a628628cad544b0aedfdf374b0e4dd2; merged 2026-09-24T02:24:21Z). Completeness: All four scoped fixes are present: subscriptions across off-connection states, replayable linearlite ids, cancellation settling without reissue, and catalogue authoring surface. Disclosed SSR prose residue reuses open uoeyl item 21. Skill-leaf offline omission has a separately open audit companion because exact implementation srcqp is in progress. Correctness: Traced state hierarchy and connected override, app-db counter/effects, and nil-reply initiation. Accepted reported verbatim machine/fence probes and controls, routing 571 tests, static checks, CLJS/example compilation CI (70 success, 18 skipped). No test rerun; no runtime regression found. Implementation quality: Hoisted subscription action and recorded-state id allocation use existing primitives without new API. Documentation matches concrete behavior. The remaining skill sketch should be corrected minimally with its existing implementation worker. Actionable findings: rf2-rqh49. Existing finding updates: rf2-uoeyl.

title: docs(resources tutorial): Part 4's editor clears the shared :editor/save instance on every entry, teaching the pattern rf2-3x7nj.42.5 retires; clear aborts an in-flight save and drops its :invalidates
description:
## Defect

The resources tutorial, Part 4 (docs/resources/tutorial/04-mutations-and-invalidation.md), teaches the pattern that rf2-3x7nj.42.5 retires from the realworld_resources example: clear the shared :editor/save mutation instance on every editor entry.

- :226 presents it as the way to wipe a stale outcome: "You reach for it to wipe a stale :success / :error before re-using an instance id: the editor below clears :editor/save on every entry, so a fresh form never shows the last save's outcome." The same sentence correctly says clear "best-effort aborts any in-flight work", but it never draws the consequence.
- :457-462: the sample :editor/initialise (the editor route's :on-match) dispatches [:rf.mutation/clear {:instance :editor/save}].
- :486: submit executes under the same shared :editor/save.
- :504: the continuation clears it.
- The sample is headed "cf. examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs".

## Why it is wrong (read at trunk b15785613b)

:rf.mutation/clear is a CANCELLATION, not a forget.
- clear-handler (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1622-1735) aborts each in-flight attempt (:1731-1733), marks its work row :cancelled (:1699), and drops the instance.
- The late reply then takes succeeded-handler's STALE SUPPRESSION branch (:1878-1893). That branch runs no :invalidates and fires no continuation.

So a save still in flight when the reader re-enters /editor has its request aborted. The server may already have written it: an aborted request is no proof the server declined the write (realworld_http/profile.cljs:470-473). Its :invalidates never run, so fresh cached lists keep serving pre-write rows.

In the tutorial the path is reachable only after a confirm on a dirty draft, because the tutorial editor has no delete:
1. Save is in flight.
2. The reader leaves or re-enters /editor.
3. The :can-leave guard asks, and the reader confirms.
4. :editor/initialise clears the instance and aborts the save.

The reader confirmed discarding a DRAFT, not cancelling a save already sent.

## Direction (from the rf2-3x7nj.42.5 ruling, 2026-09-24)

The example moves to a per-session instance, [:editor/save <nav-token>]:
- it has no entry clear;
- its continuation clears the reply's own :instance;
- it checks the nav-token gate before the status, so a refused reply retires its own instance.

Two changes here:
1. Correct :226 so it no longer presents an entry-time clear as the safe reset over a write that may be in flight. Clear is the causal reset for an instance you know has settled. For a form the reader can leave mid-write, give each session its own instance.
2. Bring the sample in line with the example, or otherwise drop the entry clear without reintroducing the old outcome on a fresh form.

Design constraint the worker must weigh: Part 4's editor is deliberately simplified. It has none of the example's nav-token reply gate (rf2-gwye.39), so a late :ok reply after leaving can already navigate the reader. A per-session instance needs a session identity. The routing nav-token is available through the documented :rf.route/nav-token coeffect (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:335-350) or the public :rf/route sub's :nav-token (:405-407). Keep the tutorial's teaching budget in mind. The minimum acceptable change is item 1 plus removing the entry clear's claim to be safe.

## Gates

- mkdocs build --strict, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for links and anchors.
- No gate compiles or pins this page's code samples: git grep for the filename under scripts/, implementation/scripts/ and .github/ exited 1, while the same grep under docs/ found it. Verify the sample by hand against the ruled example once rf2-3x7nj.42.5 lands, and say so in the PR.

## Sequencing

Land after rf2-3x7nj.42.5, so the tutorial can cite the ruled example shape.
notes:
== WORKER REPORT (editor-3x7nj), PR #10350, 2026-09-24 ==

Landed in the same PR as rf2-3x7nj.42.5, as the commit AFTER it (83934469af after rebase onto 46ef83f136), so the page cites the ruled example shape. Premise verified at trunk 4c70b35a41: the :rf.mutation/clear paragraph at :226 and the entry clear at :457-462 were as the description says.

CHANGE (docs/resources/tutorial/04-mutations-and-invalidation.md)
- The :rf.mutation/clear paragraph keeps its point that clear best-effort aborts in-flight work and now draws the consequence: a write still in flight loses its request (no proof the server didn't perform it), its late reply is suppressed, so its :invalidates never run. Clear an instance whose write has settled; when a form needs a fresh start over a write that may still be out, give each session its own instance id.
- The editor sample now matches the example as 42.5 leaves it: (defn save-instance [nav-token] [:editor/save nav-token]); :editor/initialise has no entry clear; an :editor/save-instance sub over :rf/route; :editor/submit declares {:rf.cofx/requires [:rf.route/nav-token]} and uses the token in both :instance and :reply-to; :editor/replied declares the same cofx, asks the token FIRST (a refused reply clears the reply's own :instance and stops), does nothing on a current-page :error, and clears the reply's :instance on :ok.
- One design choice within the bead's stated latitude: the tutorial reads the token with the documented :rf.route/nav-token coeffect (the bead's first option; Part 3 already taught :rf.cofx/requires) where the example reads runtime-db via current-nav-token. Both read [:rf.runtime/routing :current :nav-token]; the view side is the identical :rf/route sub. One sentence introduces :nav-token on the route slice with a link to the routing glossary's nav-token entry.
- The two later mentions of the target, [:editor/replied] at "is data" and in the "Going deeper" box, now read [:editor/replied nav-token] so they match the sample.

GATES

description:
## Gap (stale claims in `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` at trunk `fe8de195bd`, measured against `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59`)

The page says (line 37) "The behavioural baseline is XState v6" and then teaches the mapping in v5 spellings v6 removed, without marking them. Six claims are stale; the page's own "v5/v6" framing (line 3) is why most of it is defensible, and the fix is to label, not to rewrite.

1. **Lines 38-40.** "v5 helpers such as `assign`, `sendTo`, `raise`, and `setup()` map onto the data-first forms below." `setup()` is not a removed v5 helper: v6 keeps `setup({ schemas, states, actions, guards, actors, delays })` and `machine.provide({...})`. Measured, probe `xs/D-1-grammar-shapes.mjs` §3a: `setup({ guards, actions, delays })` exposes `guards.isBig` / `actions.note` to transition functions and the machine has `provide`. (`xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §4: "`setup()` still exists in v6 and still accepts `actions`, `guards`, `actors`, and `delays`".) Corrected: "v5 helper creators such as `assign`, `sendTo`, `raise` and `enqueueActions` map onto the data-first forms below; v6's `setup()` / `createMachine({ guards, actions })` registries map onto the machine-local `:guards` / `:actions` maps."

2. **Line 61.** Row "`guard` | `:guard` named in `:guards`". v6's authoring API has no `guard` transition property — the condition lives inside the transition function, which returns `undefined` to decline (`xs-docs/transitions.md` line 37: "There is no `guard` property"); the alpha.59 runtime still honours an object-form `guard` (probe `xs/D-1-grammar-shapes.mjs` §1c) but the docs do not teach it. Corrected xstate column: "a condition inside the transition function (v5 `guard`)".

3. **Line 62.** Row "`actions` / `assign` | `:action` returning `{:data … :fx …}`". v6: the transition function returns `{ context }` and enqueues effects through `enq`; `assign` is removed (`6.0.0-alpha.1`). Corrected xstate column: "the transition function's `{ context }` return + `enq(...)` (v5 `actions` / `assign`)".

4. **Lines 70-71.** Rows "`raise`" and "`sendTo`" — v6 spellings are `enq.raise` / `enq.sendTo`. Label them.

5. **Line 73.** Row "`internalEvents` | `:internal-events #{…}`". v6's canonical form is `schemas.internalEvents`, a map keyed by event type with wildcard keys; the top-level array is the deprecated migration form (`6.0.0-alpha.42`; measured `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §A/§B — both forms reject an external send with `reason: 'internalEvent'`). Corrected xstate column: "`schemas.internalEvents` (v6 map; alpha.1 `internalEvents` array deprecated)".

6. **Line 135.** "An XState action may perform work or use `assign` to update context." In v6 an entry/exit function returns a shallow `{ context }` patch and queues side effects through `enq`; there is no `assign` (`xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §1). Corrected: "In XState v5 an action performed work or used `assign`; in v6 an entry/exit function returns a `{ context }` patch and queues effects through `enq`. A re-frame2 action returns a value: …" — which makes the section's point (returned data, not performed work) land against the version the page says it targets.

Worth one added clause, not counted: line 56 (`type: "history"` → `:type :history`) — v6 requires a non-empty default `target` on every history state (`6.0.0-alpha.27`; measured `xs/D-1-grammar-shapes.mjs` §6a: `Missing history target on "(machine).p.h"`), while re-frame2's `:default-target` is optional and falls back to the compound's `:initial` (measured `jvm/D/D-j2-grammar.clj` §c; `spec/005` line 3529). A v6 reader will otherwise assume `:default-target` is mandatory.

Confirmed, no change: line 306 "Quiet no-op, matching modern XState" — measured at alpha.59 (`xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §D4: unhandled event, value unchanged, status `active`); line 247-248 durations — `"5s"` rejected at registration (`jvm/D/D-j2-grammar.clj` §d1); line 156 (`:choice` is a vector, not a routing function) — v6 rejects the array form (`xs/D-1-grammar-shapes.mjs` §8c: `Missing choice function`), re-frame2 rejects the fn form (`jvm/D/D-j2-grammar.clj` §e1: `:rf.error/machine-bad-choice`).

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/D-1-grammar-shapes.mjs` §1c, §3a, §6a, §8c; `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §A, §B, §D4 (outputs beside them). Documented: `CHANGELOG-next.md` `## 6.0.0-alpha.1`, `## 6.0.0-alpha.27`, `## 6.0.0-alpha.42`; `xs-docs/xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §1, §4, §12; `xs-docs/transitions.md` line 37. Scratch root: `C:/Users/miket/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-miket-code-re-frame2/72748c69-1ead-489c-bbb7-ab2f08e25858/scratchpad/xstate-parity/`.

## re-frame2 evidence

`docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` lines 3, 37-40, 56, 61-62, 70-73, 135, 156, 247-248, 306 at `fe8de195bd`. Probes `jvm/D/D-j2-grammar.clj` §c, §d1, §e1; tests `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_history_smoke_test.clj` (`default-target-absent-falls-back-to-initial`), `timeout_test.clj`, `choice_test.clj`.

## Why it matters

This is the page an XState developer reads first. It promises a v6 baseline and then shows `assign` / `guard` / `internalEvents` as the XState side, so a v6 developer does not recognise the left column and a v5 developer concludes the page is v5. Labelling costs a few words per row.

title: xstate-parity: coming-from-xstate.md and xstate-translation.md carry no lifecycle rows (stop vs destroy runs :exit, status/output after termination, re-birth vs dead letter, error not terminal)
description:
## Gap

The two XState-facing translation records — `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` (the §Mapping table) and `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md` — map the CHART (states, guards, actions, invoke, final, after, raise, sendTo, output) and stop there. Neither carries a lifecycle row, and dimension C measured four lifecycle facts in which XState v6 and re-frame2 differ observably for a porter, all four ruled or by design on the re-frame2 side, none written where a porter looks:

1. **Stop vs destroy.** XState `actor.stop()` runs NO exit actions (measured); re-frame2's only stop is `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` and it DOES run the active configuration's `:exit` cascade before teardown (measured, pinned). There is no `actor.stop()` row at all — the word "destroy" appears on the page only inside the `:final?` and `:spawn` prose.
2. **Status after termination.** XState keeps `status done|error|stopped` and `output` on the snapshot; re-frame2 removes the snapshot (`[:rf/machine id]` reads `nil` for never-started, finished AND destroyed alike) and reports completion on the `:rf.machine/done` trace (`:output`) and teardown on `:rf.machine/destroyed :reason`. No row for `snapshot.status` / `snapshot.output` / `subscribe({complete, error})`.
3. **Events after termination.** XState drops them as dead letters (`onRejectedEvent` reason `stopped`; state unchanged). re-frame2 RE-BIRTHS a finished or destroyed singleton from `:initial` and processes that event (D5/D7) — the same chart and event sequence ends in a different state. The page says `:final? true` "auto-destroys; omit it on a resting leaf" but not that the next event restarts the machine.
4. **Error is not terminal.** XState errors the actor (and its children) on any throw; re-frame2 rolls the macrostep back, emits `:rf.error/machine-action-exception`, and the machine keeps answering events (Cross-Spec §11). No row.

These are not changes to make in re-frame2 (each is DIVERGE-RULED or LEAD in the dimension C matrix); they are the rows a porter needs so as not to "fix" them.

## XState evidence

- `xs/C-1.out`: `after stop: status stopped value working log [… unchanged …]`; `send after stop: value working status stopped`; `done: status done output {"n":0}`; `late subscribe on done actor: ["complete"]`.
- `xs/C-6.out`: `send to stopped: [{"inspect":"stopped"},{"hook":"stopped","event":"go","origin":"external"}] status stopped value a`.
- `xs/C-2.out`: `a) transition fn throws: status error … send after error: status error`.
- `xs-docs/create-actor.md` §Actor members, `xs-docs/snapshots.md` §Status, `xs-docs/inspection.md` (dead letters).

## re-frame2 evidence

- `jvm/C/c1.out` (fe8de195bd): `after explicit destroy: snapshot nil | sub nil | log (exit ran?) [:working-exit]`; `after finish (:final?): snapshot nil … ops [… [:rf.machine/done … :output 42 …] [:rf.machine/destroyed … :reason :rf.machine/finished …]]`; `dispatch after finish (re-birth?): snapshot {:state :working …} … [:rf.machine/started {… :cause :lazy …}]`.
- `jvm/C/c2.out`: `action throws: snapshot {:state :a …} | ops [… :rf.error/machine-action-exception …]` then `machine still alive after throws? snapshot {:state :b …}`.
- Rulings: spec/005 D4/D5/D7 (3329-3332), §Destroy is silent-idempotent (2923), §What auto-cancels on destroy (3745-3757, the `:exit` substitute), Cross-Spec-Interactions §11 (line 125); test `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/destroy_exit_cascade_test.clj` (`exit-fires-on-explicit-destroy`).
- Record state: `rg -c 'destroy|stop\(|status|dead letter' docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` → 4 hits, all prose about `:final?` / `:spawn`, none a table row; `skills/…/xstate-translation.md` → 1 (the `:final?` row). The mapping table has 29 rows and no `actor.stop()`, `actor.getSnapshot().status`, `subscribe`, or dead-letter row.

## Why it matters

The re-birth difference (3) silently produces a different state from the same chart: a ported wizard with a `type: 'final'` success state that later receives a stray event restarts from its initial state in re-frame2 where XState would ignore it. The `:exit`-on-destroy difference (1) is the one an XState author will not think to rely on — and it is the re-frame2 answer to the cleanup XState delegates to actor-logic teardown functions. Both belong in the page the porter reads first.

## Options

1. **Add a "Lifecycle" block to the §Mapping table (docs-only).** Rows: `createActor(m).start()` → `[:rf.machine/start]` kick or first event; `actor.stop()` → `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` (runs `:exit`; XState runs none); `snapshot.status === 'done'` / `.output` → `:rf.machine/done` trace `:output`, snapshot removed; `subscribe({complete})` → `:rf.machine/done` / `:rf.machine/destroyed`; send after done/stop → XState dead letter vs re-frame2 re-birth (D5) / `:rf.error/no-such-handler` for a spawned address; throw in an action → XState actor error vs re-frame2 rollback + `:rf.error/machine-action-exception`. Mirror the four rows into `xstate-translation.md`'s divergence table.
2. Add only the two silent-difference rows (re-birth, error-not-terminal) — smaller, leaves the porter without the stop/`:exit` row that answers "where does my cleanup go".

## Recommendation

Option 1. Sequence after (or merge with) rf2-2n6uv.3.3, which edits the same page for v5-spelling staleness.

## Fence

- `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` (also touched by rf2-2n6uv.3.3 — sequence), `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md`
- no spec, no runtime

## Gates

- `python -m mkdocs build --strict` (covers `docs/`); `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for anchors; the skill file is under `skills/`, the docs gate's root. Table column counts verified by hand.

## Decision needed

No.

description:
## Gap

XState v6 ships model-based testing in core as `xstate/graph` (28,860 bytes of dist): `getAdjacencyMap` / `getShortestPaths` / `getSimplePaths` BFS over the pure `transition()` keyed on a serialized snapshot; `createTestModel(machine).getShortestPaths()` -> `path.test({ states, events })` executors (alpha.54: executors receive the full event); `getPathsFromEvents(logic, events)` replays a fixed sequence without exploring (alpha.59); `toDirectedGraph` for visualizers; `filterEvents` / `stopWhen` / `limit` / `serializeState`. re-frame2 has NO harness — spec/005 §Future :4731-4755 and spec/008 :983-993 defer `re-frame.machines.test` post-v1 behind a written reconsideration trigger: "Either an AI-implementor needs the coverage corpus for cross-language conformance, or app-side machines start exhibiting edge-case bugs that hand-written tests miss."

(defn adjacency [definition init events & {:keys [limit] :or {limit 10000}}]
  (loop [queue (conj clojure.lang.PersistentQueue/EMPTY init) parent {init nil} edges []]
    (cond
      (> (count parent) limit) {:refused :limit-exceeded :limit limit :visited (count parent)}
      (empty? queue) {:vertices (set (keys parent)) :edges edges :parent parent}
      :else
      (let [s (peek queue)
            nexts (for [ev events :let [r (m/machine-transition definition s ev)] :when (= :ok (:status r))]
                    [ev (select-keys (:snapshot r) [:state :data])])
            new (remove #(contains? parent (second %)) nexts)]
        (recur (into (pop queue) (map second new))
               (into parent (map (fn [[ev s']] [s' [s ev]]) new))
               (into edges (map (fn [[ev s']] [s ev s']) nexts)))))))
(defn shortest-path [{:keys [parent]} target]
  (loop [s target acc ()] (if-let [[p ev] (parent s)] (recur p (cons ev acc)) (vec acc))))
