title: xstate-parity: a history target is resolved from the PRE-transition recording and always treated as external re-entry — a self-transition to the owning compound's own history exits/re-enters the compound, and with :reenter? true restores the DEFAULT child where XState restores the child that same exit just recorded
description:
## Gap

XState resolves a history target during the ENTRY phase, after the exit phase has recorded the owning compound's configuration, and it treats a history target like any other target for the exit-set computation. Two consequences on the same chart (`p {initial a; states {a, b {initial b1; states {b1, b2}}, hist {type history, target a}}}`, machine at `p.b.b2`): (i) a transition declared on `p` with `target: '.hist'` and NO `reenter` keeps `p` standing — `p` was never exited, nothing is recorded, the default target `a` is entered — log `["enter:a"]` only, value `p.a` (history-states.md: "The default target is used whenever nothing has been recorded, including an internal self-transition to `.hist` before the parent has ever been exited"); (ii) the same transition WITH `reenter: true` exits `p` (recording `hist -> b`) and then restores what the exit just recorded: `["exit:p","enter:p","enter:b","enter:b1"]`, value `p.b.b1`.

re-frame2 resolves the history pseudo-state from the PRE-transition snapshot's `:rf/history` while computing the geometry, and marks every history restore as an external re-entry. On the same chart: (i) the plain self-transition to `[:p :hist]` exits and re-enters `p` — `[:exit/p :enter/p :enter/a]` — running `p`'s `:exit`/`:entry` (and so restarting its `:after` timers and `:spawn` children) where XState runs nothing of `p`'s; (ii) with `:reenter? true` it exits `p`, records `{[:p] :b}`, and then enters the DEFAULT target `:a` — `[:exit/p :enter/p :enter/a]`, `[:p :a]` — a different final state from XState's `p.b.b1`. The ordinary restore-from-outside cases (never entered -> default; shallow -> recorded child + its initial; deep -> recorded leaf; per-region history; a history target that restores its own source per alpha.41) all match.

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/B-8-history.mjs` -> `xs/B-8-history.out` (alpha.59). Row `8d internal self-transition to .hist before p ever exited` = `{"value":{"p":"a"},"log":["enter:p","enter:a","enter:b","enter:b2","enter:a"],"historyValue":{}}` (the log is birth + toB2 + the transition; the transition contributed only `enter:a`). Row `8e reenter:true to .hist while inside p at b.b2` = `{"value":{"p":{"b":"b1"}},"log":[...,"exit:p","enter:p","enter:b","enter:b1"],"historyValue":{"m.p.hist":["m.p.b"],...}}`. Controls on the same run: `8a` never-entered -> `p.a`; `8b` shallow -> `p.b.b1`; `8c` deep -> `p.b.b2`; `8h` per-region -> `{"r1":{"inside":"y"},"r2":"two"}` — all matching re-frame2. `xs/B-14-handoffs.mjs` row `H1` (history restoring its own source, alpha.41) = `["exit:b1","exit:b","enter:b","enter:b1"]`, kid restarted — also matching re-frame2.

Documented: `xs-docs/history-states.md` §What gets recorded ("The parent's active configuration is captured during the exit phase, before exit actions run") and the warning quoted above. Source (`B/xs-src/stateUtils.ts`): `exitStates` writes `changedHistory` for every exited node that owns a history child, then `historyValue = changedHistory || historyValue` BEFORE `enterStates`; `addDescendantStatesToEnter` reads `historyValue[stateNode.id]` from that updated value; `getTransitionDomain` forces the source into the exit set for a history target only when the restored set contains the source itself (`restoresSourceViaHistory`, the alpha.41 change at CHANGELOG-next.md:521).

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed: `jvm/B/B-8-history.clj` -> `jvm/B/B-8-history.out` at trunk `7d72690192`. Row `8d [shallow]` = `{:value [:p :a], :log [... :exit/p :enter/p :enter/a], :history {[:p] :b}}`; row `8e [shallow]` (`:reenter? true`) = `{:value [:p :a], :log [... :exit/p :enter/p :enter/a], :history {[:p] :b}}`; row `8e-deep` = `{:value [:p :a], ... :history {[:p] [:p :b :b2]}}` — the recording is written by the same transition's exit, and the restore ignores it. Controls: `8a` -> `[:p :a]`, `8b` -> `[:p :b :b1]`, `8c` -> `[:p :b :b2]`, `8h` -> `{:r1 [:inside :y], :r2 :two}`; `jvm/B/B-14-handoffs.clj` `H1` -> `[:exit/b1 :exit/b :enter/b :enter/b1]`, kid `:h1kid#2` -> `:h1kid#3`.

Spec: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3546` §Restoring ("the runtime resolves the target leaf as follows: 1. A recording exists ... 2. No recording exists ... resolves the pseudo-state's `:default-target`") and :3531 ("The pseudo-state is resolved at transition time to a real leaf path") — silent on WHICH snapshot's recording is read when the same transition exits the owning compound; §Recording (:3533) says recording happens "as part of the exit cascade's commit". Engine: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` `compute-transition-geometry` :3073-3091 (`history-restore` resolved via `resolve-history-target machine snapshot ...` against the incoming snapshot, and `target-base` taken from its `:resolved-leaf` before any exit set exists), :3172 `external-re-entry? (or reenter? (some? history-restore))` (every history target is external re-entry, which is what exits `p` in case (i)), and `record-exit-history` :1794 which writes `:rf/history` later, during the cascade. No test pins either case: `machine_history_smoke_test.clj` covers deep/shallow/per-region restores from outside the compound; `grep -rn hist` over `implementation/machines/test/` finds no self-target-to-own-history fixture.

## Why it matters

Case (ii) is a same-chart-different-state divergence: "restart this compound but come back to the child I was in" (`{:target [:p :hist] :reenter? true}` on `p`) lands on the default child here and on the remembered child in XState/SCXML. Case (i) is the row-4 shape again through the history door: `p`'s `:exit`/`:entry` run, so its `:after` timers restart and its `:spawn` children respawn, where XState touches nothing of `p`. Both are edge geometries — a transition to the compound's own history from inside that compound — so P3; but both are silent, and the reenter case gives a different `:state`.

## Options

1. Resolve the history target against the post-exit recording (runtime only): compute the exit set first (as today for the non-history path), record `:rf/history` for exited compounds, THEN resolve the pseudo-state — the SCXML exitStates-then-enterStates order; and stop forcing `external-re-entry?` for a history restore whose resolved leaf is a proper descendant of the declaring compound (keep it only when the restored configuration contains the source, the alpha.41 case already matched). Fixes both (i) and (ii); no existing pinned behaviour changes (the from-outside restores are unaffected because the owning compound is not exited by them).
2. Fix only (ii) — read the just-recorded value on a `:reenter?` restore — and record (i) in spec/005 §Self-transitions as the re-frame2 rule (a history target is always external). Smaller diff, leaves the row-4-shaped divergence in place.
3. Spec-only: document both behaviours under §Restoring as deliberate. No breakage, no parity.

## Recommendation

Option 1. It is the SCXML ordering the spec already describes for recording ("as part of the exit cascade's commit") and the runtime already has both halves (`record-exit-history`, and the descendant-target geometry that keeps the declaring compound standing); the change is sequencing plus one predicate, and it removes a `:state` divergence.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (`compute-transition-geometry` :3073-3091, :3172; `resolve-history-target` :1712; `record-exit-history` :1794)
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_history_smoke_test.clj` (new fixtures for the two self-target cases)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §Restoring :3546 and §Self-transitions :342 (one sentence each) — HOT-ZONE (sequence, never parallel)

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` if a `*_cljs_test.cljc` history fixture is added (`machine_history_unit_cljs_test.cljc` is node-lane only); the conformance corpus is untouched unless a fixture under `spec/conformance/fixtures/` encodes a self-target to own history (none found by name); `check_doc_slugs.py` + `python -m mkdocs build --strict` for the spec sentence.

## Decision needed

No — option 1 is a sequencing fix inside the engine with no ruling against it; if the `external-re-entry?` half is judged a deliberate re-frame2 rule, option 2 is the fallback.

title: xstate-parity: the machine ROOT is not a state node — root :entry/:exit/:tags/:spawn register and are silently inert (flat and parallel), root :after/:timeout rejected, while XState v6 honours all of them on the root
description:
## Gap

XState v6: the root of `createMachine` is a state node like any other. Root `entry`/`exit` run at actor start and at completion (`xs/A-7.out`: `start log: root entry | a entry`, `go log: a exit | named:1 | root exit | status done`); root `after` fires on a flat machine, survives child transitions, and fires on a parallel root (`xs/A-8.out`: `ROOT after on flat machine -> "b"`, `ROOT after survives child transition (a->c) -> "b"`, `ROOT after on parallel root -> {"x":"x2","y":"y1"}`); root `timeout` fires (`ROOT timeout on flat machine -> "b"`); root `tags` join the snapshot's tag union (`xs/A-14.out`: `tags: ["roottag","atag"]`); a root `invoke` lives for the machine's lifetime across child transitions (`xs/A-9.out`: `root invoke survives a->b, n= 102`); a root `always` fires at start (`xs/A-14.out`: `root always (guard true) -> status active value "b"`). Docs: `xs-docs/states.md`, `delays.md`, `invoke.md`.

re-frame2: the spec records `:entry` / `:exit` / `:spawn` as "per-state" keys and only `:on` as "per-state and top-level" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:214-218` at `20d5050bdc`), `:after` as "a state-node key (alongside :on, :entry, :exit, :always, :spawn)" (`:2351`), and `:always` as "Not on the root machine" (`:2105`). But registration ACCEPTS every one of them on the root and the runtime never reads them. `known-state-node-keys` is ONE set for root and child (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1457`) and the root walk only ADDS keys (`:1572`, `at-root?` → `known-machine-root-extra-keys`). Measured `jvm/A/A-7.out` with a live state-level control (`control log [:a-entry :a-exit :b-entry]`): the flat root's `:entry` is absent at birth (`after start: log [:a-entry]`), its `:exit` is absent both on reaching `:final?` (`log [:a-entry :a-exit :d-entry] snapshot nil`) and on explicit `:rf.machine/destroy` (`log [:a-exit]`); on the PARALLEL root the same four slots register and are equally inert (`after start: log [:x1-entry] tags #{:x1-tag} prkid live? false`, `after destroy: log [:x1-entry]`) — root `:tags` never enter the union and root `:spawn` spawns nothing. `jvm/A/A-2.out` (`:data` trail) agrees for root `:entry` / `:always` / `:tags` / `:spawn`, and `jvm/A/A-1.out` shows root `:output-key` and root `:final?` also register silently (`root-output-key OK`, `root-final? OK`) although a state node refuses `:output-key` without `:final?` (`output-key-non-final` → `:rf.error/machine-output-key-without-final`). The ONE root slot that is refused loudly is `:after` / `:timeout` on a non-parallel root: `:rf.error/machine-non-parallel-root-after-not-supported` (`root-after-flat`, `root-timeout-flat`; pinned by `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/root_after_non_parallel_test.clj`), while the parallel root DOES honour `:after` (`spec/005:4683`, a LEAD row).

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/A-7.mjs` → `xs/A-7.out` (root entry/exit), `xs/A-8.mjs` → `xs/A-8.out` (root after/timeout, flat and parallel), `xs/A-9.mjs` → `xs/A-9.out` (root invoke), `xs/A-14.mjs` → `xs/A-14.out` (root always, root tags). One XState-side caveat for whoever implements root `:exit`: `actor.stop()` does NOT run any exit action (`xs/A-14.out`: `root exit on actor.stop() ... stop log:` empty) — only completion does — so "root exit on destroy" is a re-frame2 design choice, not something XState pins.

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed: `jvm/A/A-7.clj` → `jvm/A/A-7.out` (root slots by effect, with control), `jvm/A/A-2.clj` → `jvm/A/A-2.out` (root slots by `:data` trail), `jvm/A/A-1.clj` → `jvm/A/A-1.out` (registration acceptance, root section), `jvm/A/A-6.clj` → `jvm/A/A-6.out` (parallel-root acceptance of `:always` / `:after` / `:timeout` — all `:registered`). Spec: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:214-218`, `:2105`, `:2351`, `:4683` at `20d5050bdc`. Code: `validation.cljc:1457-1500`, `:1572`. Pin: `root_after_non_parallel_test.clj` pins the ONE rejection; no test pins the silent acceptance of the other root slots (searched `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/` for `root-entry`, `root :entry`: 0 files; control `root_after` names 1).

## Why it matters

An XState author reaches for root `entry` (a birth log / analytics event), root `exit` (cleanup when the machine completes), a root `invoke` (a connection or ticker alive for the machine's whole life regardless of state) and root `tags` constantly. In re-frame2 those declarations register and do nothing — the exact silent-swallow failure `validate-state-node-keys!` was written to prevent on CHILD nodes (it refuses `:invoke` with a message naming `:spawn`) — and it reads as "works, probably" until a production machine ships with no cleanup. The substitute for machine-lifetime behaviour is to wrap the whole tree in one compound state, which is what XState's root IS; nothing tells the author that.

## Options

1. Reject on the root at registration (smallest; spec + runtime, one validator arm): `:entry` / `:exit` / `:always` / `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` / `:tags` / `:final?` / `:output-key` on a non-parallel AND a parallel root → a new `:rf.error/machine-root-slot-not-supported` mirroring `-non-parallel-root-after-not-supported`, the message naming the substitute (wrap the tree in one compound). Breaks only machines that declared inert slots, and loudly.
2. Implement the root as a state node for the four cheap slots (spec + runtime): `:entry` at birth before the initial cascade, `:exit` at `:final?` / destroy after the leaf's exit, `:tags` in the union, `:spawn` for machine lifetime — plus option 1's rejection for `:always` / `:after` / `:timeout` on a non-parallel root (`:always` is ruled at `spec/005:2105`; `:after` already refused). Existing machines change behaviour only if they declared these slots, in which case they start doing what the author meant.
3. Full root-as-state-node including `:after` / `:timeout` / `:always` on a non-parallel root (largest; the parallel-root `:after` precedent in `transition.cljc` generalises).

## Recommendation

Option 2. Root entry/exit is the commonest XState use, the runtime already has root-owned slots for the parallel root, and reject-what-you-do-not-run closes the silent-swallow hole for the rest. If no new root capability is wanted, option 1 alone still resolves the silence.

## Fence

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE: §Transition table grammar table `:214-226`, §State nodes, a new root-node paragraph, error-id list `:4776`); `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (HOT ZONE) only if a root schema is split from `:rf/state-node`; `spec/Conventions.md` (HOT ZONE) if the new error id is catalogued there; `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc`; for option 2 also `transition.cljc`, `lifecycle_fx/{finalize,destroy}.cljc`, `parallel.cljc`; new tests beside `root_after_non_parallel_test.clj`.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` if any `#?(:cljs ...)` branch moves (timer / destroy paths); the conformance corpus if a fixture gains a root slot.

## Decision needed

Yes: reject root slots outright (option 1), implement root `:entry`/`:exit`/`:tags`/`:spawn` and reject the rest (option 2, recommended), or full root-as-state-node (option 3)?
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 19:08:11 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: `ai/decisions/rf2-2n6uv.5.1.root-as-state-node.md` in the mayor checkout (`ai/` is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own). Read at trunk `7d72690192` (= origin/main as the local ref stood); trunk moved 2 commits past the campaign's `20d5050bdc`, none touching `implementation/machines` or spec/005/Spec-Schemas/Conventions, and every finding was RE-MEASURED at `7d72690192` (probe `decisions-sep23/rf2-2n6uv.5.1.probe.clj`, exit 0).

RECOMMENDATION: option 2 — make the root honour `:entry` (birth, before the leaf cascade), `:exit` (after the leaf exits, on finality and on destroy), `:tags` (in the union) and `:spawn` (machine-lifetime child under decl-path `[]`), keep the flat-root `:after`/`:timeout` rejection and the `:always`-not-on-root ruling unchanged, and refuse the remaining never-read root slots with one new error id. Option 1 (refuse all) is the honest minimum if no root capability is wanted; option 3 reopens two written rulings for a need one compound wrapper already meets.

Decisive findings, inline:
1. MECHANISM — `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:690-711` `nodes-along-path` loops from `(:states machine)` with an empty accumulator, so the root is never a `[prefix node]` pair; every consumer (`compute-tags` :746-752, `run-active-exit-cascade` :2874-2930, the geometry's entered/exited pairs :3264-3268 that `run-spawn-phase` :3442-3471 reduces over, and `bootstrap-step` `parallel.cljc:447-467`) is blind to root `:entry`/`:exit`/`:tags`/`:spawn`; `compute-tags-parallel` `parallel.cljc:329-337` unions region tags only. Measured at trunk with the state-level control firing `[:a-entry :a-exit :b-entry]`: flat root after start `log [:a-entry] tags #{:a-tag} rxkid live? false`, at `:final?` `[:a-entry :a-exit :d-entry] snapshot nil`, explicit destroy `[:a-exit]`; parallel root `tags #{:x1-tag} prkid live? false`. A child-level `:invoke` typo is refused `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key` while the same silent-swallow class on the root registers.

PRECEDENT + MUST — `lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:531-565` (comment) and `:567-609` (`validate-non-parallel-root-after!`) refuse a flat/compound MACHINE root `:after`/`:timeout` and a parallel REGION-root `:after` precisely to keep "no accept-but-inert path"; the parallel MACHINE root's `:after` is the supported root-owned form (spec/005:1780-1786, :4683 ALIGNED; `transition.cljc:3384-3412`) — so the bead title's "root :after rejected" holds for the NON-parallel root only. `spec/Conventions.md:1160-1166` §No silent swallow is the MUST the four inert slots violate; its machines row (:1188) fixed this class for child nodes, not the root. The error id is catalogued in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2237` only, absent from spec/005's list (:4776).
3. SPEC SPLIT — `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2557` `(def TransitionTable [:ref ::state-node]) ;; a TransitionTable IS the root state-node`, versus `spec/005-StateMachines.md:214-218` labelling `:entry`/`:exit`/`:spawn`/`:spawn-all` "per-state", :2105 `:always` "Not on the root machine", :2351 `:after` a state-node key, :2237 tag union "root → every compound ancestor → leaf" (not true of the runtime today), :342 and :1786 the root never exits on an ordinary transition (option 2 must keep that; rf2-gdne8's root `:same-state` fix is the RED-guard). §Deliberate omissions vs xstate (:3218-3236) never mentions a root invoke, so no ruling excludes root `:spawn`. No prior ruling: 8 `bd search` phrases 0 hits (control "parallel" 236 KB); identity-selected `.beads/issues.jsonl` finds the phrases only in this bead and its parent.
4. BREAKAGE — EDN-parsed census of all 243 conformance fixtures: 0 of 160 `:definition` maps carry a root `:entry`/`:exit`/`:tags`/`:spawn` (controls: 14 root `:on`, 28 parallel roots, 0 parse errors; the 2 root-slot hits are parallel-root `:after`, the supported form); tree regex: 0 `:type :parallel` maps declare the slots against 13 declaring root `:on`/`:after`. So option 1 breaks nothing in-tree and option 2 changes only machines that declared the slots.

Smallest next step under option 2: one PR in `implementation/machines` — root `:entry`/`:exit` + the reject arm; RED case `[:root-in :a-in]` at birth (today `[:a-in]`) and `… :a-out :root-out` at finality/destroy; controls: state-level cascade unchanged, root `:on`/`:same-state` must NOT run root exit (spec/005:342), the 8 pins in `root_after_non_parallel_test.clj` unchanged. Lane: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` plus `npm run test:cljs` (machines' `*_cljs_test.cljc` run on the node lane only). Interactions: dimension E's validation drafts land in the same `validation.cljc` — sequence, do not parallel.
== RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 21:02:00 AUSEST, under the project stance; dossier + Codex Recommendation weighed) ==

QUESTION. The machine root accepts :entry / :exit / :tags / :spawn (and other state-node keys) at registration and never runs them: refuse them all, make the root honour the useful ones, or make the root a full state node?

OPTIONS AND SIZES.
- Option 1: refuse every never-read root slot at registration. One validator arm + one error id + spec rows. Size S. Honest, but every flat machine wanting birth/teardown behaviour must wrap its tree in a compound (its :state turns from a keyword into a vector path, and every sub, test and tool reading it moves).
- Option 2: the root honours :entry, :exit, :tags, :spawn; everything else never read at the root is refused. Size M (spawn is the expensive quarter, see below).
- Option 3: full root-as-state-node, incl. flat-root :after / :timeout / :always and a root resolver. Size L; retires two written rulings (spec/005 "Not on the root machine" for :always; the flat-root :after refusal).
- Leaving it: ruled out. spec/Conventions.md:1164 (No silent swallow) is a MUST: "A user-supplied value that is recognised as input but cannot be honoured MUST produce a structured warning or error."

RULING: OPTION 2, STAGED.
- THIS BEAD (one PR): the root honours :entry, :exit and :tags; a new registration refusal covers every root key no runtime consumer reads, and that refusal INCLUDES root :spawn for now. This closes the silent swallow for every slot in one PR.
- ROOT :spawn is genuinely separate work and is filed as its own follow-on bead (discovered-from this one). When it lands it lifts the root-:spawn refusal. Until then a root :spawn is refused loudly with a message naming the substitute.
- Option 3 is NOT taken: the :always-not-on-root ruling (spec/005:2105) and the flat-root :after refusal stand unchanged; their premises have not changed and a compound wrapper's :after already outlives child transitions.

WHY.
1. Stance: power and low friction without gold plating. Birth log, teardown cleanup and a whole-machine tag are the three things an author actually writes at the root; each lands on a mechanism the runtime already has (the birth cascade, the single destroy-time exit entry point, the tag union). A machine-lifetime behaviour deserves a machine-lifetime owner, not a synthetic wrapper state that changes a flat machine's :state shape (Codex's API argument, independent of parity).
2. It removes the accept-but-inert path exactly as validate-non-parallel-root-after! already does for :after in the same validator, whose own comment states the principle: "no accept-but-inert path".
3. It is additive: machines that declared these slots start doing what the author meant; nobody else changes. In-tree census found zero declarations (below).
4. Trust the programmer, don't litigate the minutiae: no new public vocabulary, no root :always, no flat-root :after, no root-schema split.

AGREEMENT / DISAGREEMENT.

title: INCOMPLETE audit handoff: infinite-resource stale marks (resolution reported)
description:
Recovery of prior merged-PR audit work, explicitly requested by Mike on 2026-09-25.

Source: rf2-wcsjy; status at recovery: closed. No original Bead has been reopened or claimed. This is a new, independently trackable record.

Historical handoff — resolution already reported. This record does not assert that the original defect still exists.

Evidence and scope
Original claim and required correction, preserved verbatim:
Residual left open by rf2-3x7nj.10.1 (PR #10293, merged), flagged unmeasured in that item's ruling and confirmed still open by the implementing worker: a load-more success on an infinite feed clears a stale mark the feed ALREADY had before that page's attempt started, and a later refetch-sweep page clears a mark kept by an earlier page the same way. 10.1 made a success keep a stale mark stamped with its own attempt; these paths clear marks stamped by a DIFFERENT (earlier) attempt or by none. Measure first at trunk; if it reproduces, a page settle should clear only a mark stamped with its own attempt, as 10.1's rule already does for the ordinary settle.

## Decision needed

No — extend 10.1's own rule to the infinite-feed page settles.



Resolution recorded on source (closed_at 2026-09-24T02:15:59Z):
DONE — merged as PR #10337 (head 9e8860e1af), landed at trunk 8a0088d422 by rebase. CI at that head: 88 checks, 0 pending, 0 failed, all four workflow runs complete; the CLJS lanes are CI's runs (the node lane counted exactly +5 tests over the merge base, matching the JVM delta). Local: resources JVM 922 tests (917 at merge base) exit 0; core, epoch, reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, ssr-ring and tools/xray green; 83 static checks, the link-anchor gate and mkdocs --strict green. CONTROL: the new tests failed on unfixed trunk (13 failures across 5 new tests); with the fix in, each of six parts removed one at a time failed only its own test, and every restore matched the committed blob hash.

rf2-wcsjy: both audit cases reproduced at trunk (load-more of page 3 on an invalidated owner-free feed cleared the stale mark; a refetch-all sweep invalidated during page 0 kept page 0 stale but the page-1 leg cleared it), plus a THIRD case of the same class — an ensure refetching an invalidated feed with a multi-page sweep cleared the mark at page 0, so a later page failing left the feed reading fresh over pre-invalidation data. The description's rule ('clear only a mark stamped with its own attempt') was INVERTED against the defect; the worker followed the audit note instead: the feed stays stale until the invalidation is actually covered. Rule now (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc, events.cljc): a load-more append never clears the mark; page 0 clears a mark that predates it only when no sweep follows, otherwise the mark stays until the sweep's last page settles; a mark landing mid-sweep, or a sweep stopping early, leaves the feed stale. Required second change: the owned-entry follow-up refetch fires only for a mark written during the settling attempt — without it the sweep restarts in a loop, which the existing 10.3 test catches. One sentence added to spec/016-Resources.md §Refetch and invalidation of an infinite feed.

title: machines engine: a :type :choice state silently accepts :on-done and unknown keys (engine/viz disagree)
description:
## What

Worker mviz3-4v2t6 reported this while mirroring the leaf `:on-done` refusal into tools/machines-viz (rf2-xnbyt, PR #10409). It is an engine gap, and `implementation/` was outside that worker's fence. Re-verify at your trunk.

The engine accepts `:on-done`, and ANY unknown key, on a `:type :choice` state:
- the state-node key check (the one that raises `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`) skips choice states;
- the choice state's own forbidden-key list does not include `:on-done`.

The viz checks the state AFTER `:choice` is desugared to `:always`, so it refuses both, and the two now disagree. The unknown-key half predates PR #10409; the new leaf check added `:on-done` to it.

That is a silent swallow, which spec/Conventions.md forbids: a choice state has no completed compound child, and an unknown key is never read.

## Required correction
- Make the engine's registration check refuse unknown keys on a choice state, using the existing `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`, and refuse `:on-done` there. Reuse the existing leaf rule where it applies.
- Add a row to the engine/viz parity test (tools/machines-viz engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc), as PR #10393 and PR #10409 did.
- Red-first, with the fix removed.
- Check spec/005's choice-state section says what the code does.

## Fence
implementation/machines/src and implementation/machines/test; the viz parity test row; spec/005's choice-state rows. HOLD: spec/005 and implementation/machines are held by worker xroot-51 (rf2-2n6uv.5.1); dispatch after its PR merges.

Desugaring removes type/choice but retains these other keys, so the viz node check refuses the lowered leaf while registration accepts it. Correct unknown BARE keys and impossible on-done with the existing category; retain the intentional namespaced-extension carve-out and valid choice behavior. This is an engine correction plus parity row, already scoped here; no new grammar framework. Accepted implementer probe; no audit test rerun.

title: FALSE: Resources on-box redaction covers live-work identities
description:
Audit of PR #10419 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10419), exact merged tree b63ae63f57a12e74927dd7b7763ba1e6f43e2dfc. This prose sweep disclosed pre-existing behavior issues; this new open Bead independently tracks the correction. Evidence below is source-traced; no runtime test rerun is claimed.

implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:110-128 constructs [:rf.work/resource scoped-key generation], where scoped-key includes scope and params. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc:876-887 preserves the raw :work/id in ledger-row; live-work at 945-954 carries it through. resources.cljs:1357-1359 reads the observed raw runtime ledger, 1546 calls reply/live-work, and live-work-row-view:499-501 renders (str (:work-id row)) directly into a visible span. A running sensitive resource whose scope or params contain a secret therefore displays that secret in the live-work identity despite the panel redacting its instance slots. The proposed work-row scoped-key-summary leak in related in-progress rf2-ghtaa is not the demonstrated DOM route: work-row-view:399-444 does not render those scope/params summaries. The live-work identity is a concrete separate route.

Required correction
At the existing on-box presentation boundary, render sensitive identity payloads under the same resource classification policy while retaining raw internal identity for joins and cancellation. Reuse the existing redaction machinery or resource sensitivity gate; do not change work-id semantics. Add a live-ledger/panel regression with a sensitive scope/params sentinel absent from rendered text and a non-sensitive identity control. Coordinate rf2-ghtaa without changing its status.

title: INCOMPLETE: persisted-state install still leaks classified secrets through its event traces
description:
Audit of PR #10462 at fc06937c472e6f93c7121060a330bd29a87dce57. The new per-actor classification reconstruction fixes subsequent snapshot egress for singleton and spawned actors, including server frames. A separate P1 leak remains in the event carrying the saved state. This new open finding is required by the audit policy even though rf2-87xgd already tracks implementation work.

Evidence: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:1358-1368 registers :rf/install-frame-state with framework authority and documentation but no :sensitive declaration. Its argument is the whole raw persisted frame-state, including classified machine data and any app-db secrets. classification.cljc:1263-1264 projects :rf.event/v through event registration metadata; snapshot-owned claims do not classify that enclosing event argument. router.cljc:1330-1334 includes the original event in frame-state-changed, and the ordinary dispatched/run-start/run-end traces carry it as well. The implementer measured saved-secret surviving project-trace-event in 4 of 6 install traces. Re-lowering machine claims after the commit cannot protect this separate event-vector path.

Required correction: follow the explicit rf2-87xgd ruling: mark the install event payload sensitive as a whole using the existing event-meta classification mechanism, in the shared standard metadata used by both registrar and image generation. Whole-payload trace redaction is sufficient; public fields remain readable in installed state. Check :rf/hydrate for the same carrier leak and apply the same existing declaration if affected. Add a regression with machine and app-db secrets proving no projected install trace/egress exposes them, while installed values remain readable and an ordinary event trace is unchanged. Show the regression failing without the declaration. No per-path derivation or new projection mechanism is needed. Author-reported executions are accepted; no suites were rerun during this audit.
notes:

- the evidence sites are events.cljc about :1358-1368, classification.cljc about :1263-1264 and router.cljc about :1330-1334.

title: An in-place navigate request ([:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge ...}]) names no route, so its declared-sensitive query values still egress raw on the event trace
description:
Found by rf2-dhzgm's worker (PR #10618, merged at trunk ea482b136a), outside its fence. Spec 012 now documents it as an open carrier. Reproduce it first.

PR #10618 made `[:rf.route/navigate …]` and `[:rf.route/url-requested …]` redact what their route declares sensitive:
- core's event projection routes their first argument through the `:routing/project-url-change-event-args` hook;
- behind the hook, `re-frame.routing/project-nav-event-arg` redacts declared `:params`, `:query` and `:fragment` for a `:to` request, and routes a URL through `redact-declared-url`.

An IN-PLACE request, such as `{:query-merge {...}}`, names no `:to` route. The projection runs without a frame, so it cannot look up the current route's declaration, and declared query values ride raw.

Evidence wanted:
1. A JVM regression: a route declaring `[:query :token]`, navigate to it, then `[:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge {:token "S"}}]`, and check the event trace.
2. Show it red at base and green with the fix. Controls: an undeclared query key rides verbatim, and a `:to` request is unchanged.

The fix is small only if the event projection can reach the target frame's current route. If it genuinely cannot (the projection is frame-less by design), record that with evidence and close this as a documented carrier, which is what Spec 012 already says. Do not add a new late-bind hook to get there. The mayor rules that the frame-less route is an acceptable answer under the stance.
close_reason:
DOCUMENTED CARRIER, pinned by PR #10623. The event projection is frame-less by design. It cannot reach the target frame's current route through the existing :routing/project-url-change-event-args hook. No hook was added and no signature was changed, per the ruling.

Call chain, verified at trunk 2daba64dd7:
- core classification.cljc project-trace-event holds frame-id off (:tags :frame). It passes that only to the frame-qualified projectors (db, sub, view, machine). project-event-tags hands on the event alone.
- redact-event-by-registration is [event]. It is itself the :classification/redact-event-by-registration hook, (fn [event]).
- The always-on consumers (error_emit, the projection sink, the router halt record) carry the frame, but only wrap the call in :live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution. That binds rf.registrar/*generation*, an image generation, not a frame id. Its docstring says resolution is derived from the carried frame target, never from an ambient binding.
- The routing hook is (fn [arg]). project-nav-event-arg finds a route only via the request's :url or :to.

Decisive measurement (a scratch probe, JVM, routing :test classpath): an in-place [:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge {:token ...}}] was dispatch-synced with {:frame :probe/f2}, and rf.frame/*current-frame* was recorded inside the hook. The :rf.event/dispatched row is projected at ENQUEUE, outside the router's per-handler binding (router.cljc, binding rf.frame/*current-frame* (:frame envelope)).
- That row saw *current-frame* :rf/default when another frame was ambient, and nil when none was, while its own :frame tag was :probe/f2.
- The 3 in-drain rows saw :probe/f2.
So the only ambient frame channel is unbound, or names the wrong frame, on the enqueue row.

Pin: routing_url_trace_classification_cljs_test.cljc, an-in-place-request-rides-verbatim-because-it-names-no-route.
- The declared :token rides verbatim, and the request is identical?.
- Control: the undeclared :page rides.
- Control: a :to request naming the same route redacts the same key.
Namespace: 9 tests / 38 assertions / 0 failures, exit 0.
- Plant A (the projector redacts :token in an in-place :query-merge): exit 1, 2 failures, both pin assertions. The controls stay green.
- Plant B (redact-declared-target dropped): exit 1, 2 failures, both :to arms. The pin stays green.
Both restores were verified by blob hash.

Spec 012 §Lowering and re-rooting now says why an in-place request stays open: the route it edits is the frame's current route, and the event-vector projection is frame-less. A :to request is redacted.

- core JVM: 2163/12199/0 both.

title: Lead: a held resource sub's LIVE value ships data loaded under a declaration its re-registered owner dropped
notes:
== MAYOR RULING 2026-09-29 18:1x AUSEST: yes, the LIVE value keeps it too ==
Union the claims in the LIVE runtime-db's registry into the current value's projection, exactly as rf2-lafas does for the prior value from the prior inputs. That is the one-binding change the lead describes.
Why under the stance: data loaded under a declaration stays classified until it is reloaded under the new registration, which is when the registry reconciles. The prior and live values then agree, and a held sub cannot emit on its next recompute what it just redacted on the previous one. It is the existing mechanism applied consistently, not new machinery.
Regression: the lead's probe (re-register without the declaration, then an unrelated recompute) with the identical-run control; show it red with the fix removed. Add one Spec 016 sentence only if the prior-value sentence does not already cover it.
== FENCE: routed to worker/resegress2-lafas (PR #10631), 2026-09-29 18:24 AUSEST. The worker accepted it as one commit in #10631. Do not dispatch separately. Cleared when that worker closes this bead, or reports it declined. ==
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #10631 (branch worker/resegress2-lafas), commit "fix(resources): a held sub's live value keeps the claims it was computed under".

The ruling was followed: project-read-sub-egress now unions the claims from the LIVE runtime-db's registry into the current value's projection, as rf2-lafas does for the prior value from the prior inputs. That covers the data claims and each carried key's claims. The change is the inputs-db binding, which reads the live runtime-db for a current value and the prior inputs for a prior one.

Decisive measurement (JVM). New tests in re-frame.resources-prior-value-reregistration-cljs-test:
- the probe: re-register without [:data :ssn], then recompute through an unrelated app-db write;
- its unchanged-registration control;
- a pin of the reconcile boundary.
With the live union removed (the binding restored to prior-only), the namespace read 10 tests / 70 assertions / 3 FAILURES, all in the re-registered probe: :rf.resource/data and :rf/resource carried "lafas-ssn-ONE" in :rf.sub/value. The control and every other test stayed green. Restored, the default-form blob hash equals the committed blob, and the namespace reads 0 failures. Resources suite on the final tree: 948/8301/0, exit 0.

CORRECTION TO THE RULING'S PREMISE, recorded in Spec 016 and pinned. The ruling reads the registry as reconciling when the data is RELOADED. It reconciles on ANY commit of the owner family in the frame: events/with-classification-lowering wraps every resource handler that writes runtime-db. The pinned test shows it: after the re-registration, an ensure of a DIFFERENT resource releases the profile's data, so the next recompute ships it raw. The Spec 016 sentence therefore says the claims last until the family's next commit reconciles the registry, after which data not reloaded since is classified by the current declaration alone.

Integrate any persistent warning state with the existing warning-cache reset convention so test isolation and reload/reset behavior remain predictable. title: Coverage gap: recorder auto-assert over an unchanged recording is unpinned
description:
Found by rf2-3h7v2.11 (owner), not fixed there: a pruning PR adds no tests.

`re-frame.story.recorder.play-export/auto-assert-steps` picks its paths with `(or (and seed-db (changed-top-paths seed-db final-db)) (top-paths final-db))`. For a recording that changed nothing (seed = final) the seeded branch must yield no assertions, which holds only because `changed-top-paths` returns an empty lazy seq (truthy). If it returned nil, the `or` would fall through to `top-paths` and the export would assert every top-level key of an unchanged db. No test drives auto-assert with seed = final; the removed `changed-top-paths-shape` identical-maps row used `empty?`, which nil satisfies too.

Measured at 7b53a53815: wrapping `changed-top-paths`'s `for` in `seq` (nil when nothing changed) leaves the whole tools/story JVM suite green (1882 tests / 7445 assertions, exit 0). The fix is one recording->script-body row with `:auto-assert? true` and identical `:seed-db` / `:final-db`, expecting no `:assert-db` step.

title: epoch egress: three assertions compare empty collections and cannot fail
description:
Owner: rf2-98kzs.14 (found while pruning implementation/epoch/test; not fixed there).

Three epoch egress assertions run over empty collections, so they cannot fail on the fault they name.

- `re-frame.epoch-egress-redaction-cljs-test/shared-axes-lift-through-the-door-but-epoch-only-axes-do-not`: the `:args` assertion is an `every?` over the `:effects` of the record `login-record!` builds. That cascade returns no fx, so `:effects` is `[]` and the `every?` is vacuously true. The test's own comment beside it says as much.
- `re-frame.epoch-privacy-test/project-egress-renders-and-subruns-pass-through-when-value-free` claims `:sub-runs` rows pass through byte-for-byte. But the `:login` cascade reads no sub, and the plain-atom substrate renders nothing, so both checks compare `[]` with `[]`. Only replacing the whole slot could fail it.
- `re-frame.epoch-privacy-test/project-egress-handles-missing-payload-slots` is named for missing slots, but its record literal carries every slot (set to nil or `[]`). So the projection's absent-slot guards are never reached. Its docstring also says halted-destroy records carry nil `:db-before` / `:db-after`, and `rollup-strict-boolean-on-halted-destroy` plus the live halted-destroy tests in `epoch_test.clj` show real snapshots instead.

Fix shape: give each a non-empty input (an fx-bearing cascade, a cascade that runs a sub, and a record with the slots actually dissoc'd), and correct the docstring.

title: Live HTTP examples in docs/async/
description:
## This section

`docs/async/` teaches `:rf.http/managed` and async effects with static code only. With HTTP and its stubs in the engine, the request lifecycle can run in the page.
- `http.md`:
  - the basic `:on-success` / `:on-failure` request, against a stub;
  - a `:reply-to` handler branching on `:status`;
  - a stubbed failure (`{:reply {:failure {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx ...}}}`, or whichever kind the page teaches; check `re-frame.http.test-support` for the shape);
  - `:decode`, where a stub can show it;
  - interceptors (`rf/reg-http-interceptor`). `disposePage` clears them on navigation, so they are safe in a cell.
- `tutorial.md`: the article-loading walkthrough as a sequence of cells on one page.
- `continuations-are-data.md`: `:on-success [:article/loaded slug]` showing the reply appended to the event vector.
- `http-going-further.md`: retries and abort, but only if they are clear with a stub. A `:dispatch-later` or retry delay is fine, because frame destroy cancels it.
- `http-machines.md`: a machine that spawns `:rf.http/managed`, run against a stub. Machines and HTTP are both in the engine now.
- `custom-effects.md`: a custom `reg-fx` beside a managed request, if the page contrasts them.
- `http-tracing.md`: leave static unless a cell can show something visible without Xray.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
close_reason:
PR #10797 (docs(async): live HTTP examples against stubs) converts four pages to live cljs-rf2 cells, 7 cells in all, each running against re-frame.http.test-support stubs routed with :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}. http.md has 2 cells: the two-handler :on-success/:on-failure request (intro ok, missing 404), and the :reply-to handler, renamed :article/fetch so it does not replace :article/load. tutorial.md has 3: Step 1, Step 2's failure->message, and Step 2's view with a stubbed 503. continuations-are-data.md has 1: [:article/loaded slug reply] shown live. http-machines.md has 1: the :article/request machine spawning :rf.http/managed, idle to ready.

Left static:
- http-going-further.md (interceptors): the engine's SCI has no parse-long. The rate-limit :after cell read "ERROR: Unable to resolve symbol: parse-long", and the :before auth header is invisible because stubs key on method and url only.
- custom-effects.md: no HTTP, and the clipboard effect shows none of the page's points.
- http-tracing.md: traces need Xray.
- index.md: a routing page.
- Inside the converted pages, :decode, :accept, retry, timeout, supersession and abort stay static, because stubs return an already-decoded reply immediately.

Verification: a headless Playwright run against mkdocs serve, with the shared engine at digest b87ee336, exited 0 across 88 checks. It checks the mount count, that no result area shows ERROR, the expected text after each click, and a navigate-away-and-back pass. In the planted fault, rf/reg-evnet made the continuations cell show "ERROR: Unable to resolve symbol: rf/reg-evnet" and the run exited 1; after restore, the blob hash equals the committed blob. Gates: mkdocs build --strict exit 0, check_doc_slugs exit 0 (a planted broken anchor turned it red), all 47 scripts/check_*.py exit 0, and PR CI 21 success / 67 skipped / 0 failed. check_require_alias_dialect reads only .clj/.cljs/.cljc, not markdown, and the cells keep the section's http-test-support alias.

title: re-frame-migration: M70 reg-interceptor lift ignores the existing value's own :id (GH #10888)
description:
GitHub #10888. skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md's automatic M70 recipe calls lifting an existing interceptor value to (reg-interceptor :app/x existing-value) plus metadata references mechanical, and none of its three examples constrain existing-value's :id. implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor_registry.cljc (about L159 at e0949be398) rejects a static value whose non-nil :id differs from the positional registration id with :rf.error/invalid-interceptor. Counterexample: (def progress {:id :enrich :after identity}) (rf/reg-interceptor :app/progress progress) fails at load. Reusing a shared legacy constructor id is not preserving either: shared-id registration can overwrite an earlier value.

Ask: make the recipe case-based and id-aware. Show the preserving already-matching stable-id case and the checks required before a mechanical lift. For missing, mismatched or shared generated ids, link the existing naming/identity decision guidance and require an explicit preserving plan - never silently choose names, erase or replace ids, or reuse a colliding constructor id. Preserve input order, function identity/behaviour, attachment scope and definition-load obligations. Acceptance per the issue: examples obey the id-match contract; a matching stable-id value succeeds; the mismatch example is held/explained; distinct legacy values cannot collapse under one generated id; compile-only success is not registration/boot acceptance. Verify against interceptor_registry.cljc at tip (a JVM control is cheap).

Mayor triage 2026-10-05 at trunk 3af4c530a2: valid; actioned. The worker puts 'Fixes #10888' on its own line in the PR body and closes neither the issue nor this bead; the mayor closes the bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #10898 (merged 2026-10-05 00:05Z as 4b84ec2c60, commit 49076dfcf6); GitHub #10888 reads CLOSED. Source: interceptor_registry.cljc's reg-interceptor* throws :rf.error/invalid-interceptor when a static value's non-nil :id differs from the registration id. The automatic M70 recipe in auto-cross-cutting.md is now case-based and id-aware. Its example block states the preserving-case assumption the rewrites rely on. Before a lift, the recipe reads the value's :id and lifts mechanically only when that id is stable, unique and equal to the registration id; otherwise the site is Type B. Type B links MIGRATION.md M-70's naming half and orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §2, and requires an approved plan that keeps chain order, function identity, attachment scope and the load obligation. The recipe forbids silent naming, stripping or replacing ids, and reusing a shared constructor id, and says a clean compile is not acceptance. The README's M-70 "All three become" block gained a comment stating the id-match requirement, plus a linked pointer to the case split. JVM control (fresh JVM, public API only, exit 0): {:id :enrich} registered under :app/progress threw :rf.error/invalid-interceptor (the red); a value whose :id matched registered and ran; two values from one constructor under the same id showed the second silently replacing the first, so the earlier event ran [:second].

title: Test-suite pruning, third pass: implementation/core events, effects and interceptors
description:
Child of rf2-n6gq4 (test-suite pruning, third pass). One worktree, one PR: implementation/core events, effects and interceptors.

Read rf2-n6gq4 first. Its description is the rule for every child: Mike's instructions (the five steps, the deletion question, the delete, merge and keep lists, "Prove it" and the report), what changes from the second pass, and the repo mechanics. A later RULING note on the epic wins where the two differ.

In short: assume this suite has more tests than it needs, and prune it to the smallest suite that still catches every bug it catches today. Do not change the code under test. For every test ask: if it were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch? Prove each group of deletions by breaking the code and seeing a surviving test fail.

title: pair-mcp freshness: read the selected build's relay heartbeat, guard empty samples, stop prescribing a blanket shadow-cljs stop (GH #10917)
description:
GitHub #10917. discover-app reaches a live app but reports :liveness :unknown, and the unknown hint tells the agent to run `npx shadow-cljs stop`, killing ALL shadow JVMs, including unrelated watches. That is a harmful remediation, hence P1. Two causes, both verified at source and live. (1) tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/freshness.cljs (about L133) does `(apply max (keep :last-pong runtimes))` guarded on `(seq runtimes)`, so a connected runtime without :last-pong throws ArityException, which the catch turns into nil. (2) Per the issue's comments, on Shadow CLJS 3.4.10 the worker-runtime :last-pong field is the OLD :cljs-repl-pong location and stays absent. The live heartbeat is the relay client's :last-pong, matched to the selected worker's runtime ids. Mike verified a private repair: read relay heartbeats only for the selected worker's runtime ids; reject mismatched, missing, invalid or future timestamps; guard empty samples; keep the compile-cycle and flush checks. Mayor verified at trunk d0b29226e8: the apply-max line is at freshness.cljs:133, and the 'kill ALL shadow' hint is at about L306.

Ask: use the supported heartbeat source for the actual Shadow version, matched to the selected build's runtimes. Keep available worker/build/runtime facts when heartbeat data is absent. Report a precise heartbeat-unavailable reason with a bounded recovery, and never infer zombie JVMs or prescribe stopping unrelated watches. Keep conservative semantics: missing data never becomes proof of freshness. Regression cases: no worker, zero runtimes, missing heartbeat, recent heartbeat, stale heartbeat, and a relay client unrelated to the build.

Mayor triage 2026-10-05 at trunk d0b29226e8: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10917 --json body,comments`), comments included: they carry later diagnosis and a verified private repair where one exists. title: Floor gate: inventory every supported runtime host (embedded, desktop, webview), not only the CI test browser (GH #10955)
description:
GitHub #10955, filed by Mike. The React 19 floor gate clears only the browser that the CI test runner executes. An app with a separately supported embedded or desktop renderer (Electron, a webview, a kiosk browser) can pass modern-browser CI while its real host is never assessed. Mayor verified at trunk 0bf7691c13:
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md Check 5 (L82-88) says it clears "the browser the CI test-runner executes the migrated bundle in", and its fix is a CI-browser bump.
- GO (L94) and the NO-GO note treat a stale CI-browser pin as a mechanical bump.
- SKILL.md Phase 0b (L76) and the done checklist (L160, "CI browser bumped") say the same.
- A case-insensitive search of skills/re-frame-migration for electron, webview and desktop finds no supported-host inventory. The control needle "Check 5" finds 2 lines in floor-gate.md.

Ask (docs; generic for any app with more than one runtime endpoint; no consumer launcher, OS, vendor, service layout or IPC names):
1. Inventory every runtime the app actually supports at the floor gate: CI browsers, deployed browsers where pinned, and embedded, desktop or webview hosts. Record each one's declared floor separately from its source or package version and from any observed execution version.
2. Give each distinct host an explicit acceptance item. A CI-browser bump clears CI only; it does not silently clear a separately pinned desktop renderer. Acceptance means the host's actual supported boot or entrypoint and meaningful host interactions, run on the optimized artefact with the genuine application prerequisites.
3. Before attributing a modern-API token to incompatibility, assess the polyfill or provider actually loaded and its contract. Before reporting a migration regression, compare the pre-migration producer and host contract.
4. For a host with updater, profile, filesystem or other persistent effects, discover and prove an appropriate isolated execution boundary. Never invent launcher flags, and never count a renamed directory as isolation. If the boundary or the genuine prerequisites are unavailable, state the exact remaining host gate while independent migration work continues.
Keep Check 5's CI-browser bump as it is: that fix is valid. This adds the missing supported-host inventory beside it. Keep the GO/NO-GO, Phase 0b, the done checklist and the "six checks" count agreeing everywhere they are stated. Check whether the corpus (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md, a hot-zone file) states the browser floor, and align it if so.

SEQUENCING: blocked by rf2-vpd7m (GH #10947, PR #10954), which holds floor-gate.md, SKILL.md Phase 0b and the corpus README for the raw-HTML inventory. Dispatch after #10954 merges, and build on its text.

Mayor triage 2026-10-06 at trunk 0bf7691c13: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10955 --json body,comments`). The PR carries 'Fixes #10955' on its own line; the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.

title: Pending leave confirmation outlives its page: a late :rf.route/continue after moving to C skips C's :can-leave
description:
## Bug

A pending leave confirmation parked on page A survives a successful navigation from A to C. A later `[:rf.route/continue <id>]` for that old question then navigates C to B with `:bypass-leave? true`, so C's `:can-leave` guard is never asked and C's unsaved work is dropped without a prompt. An app that renders its "Leave?" dialog from `:rf/pending-navigation` keeps showing the stale dialog on page C, which makes the late confirm easy to hit.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:323-347`: a rejected leave parks `{:id :destination :target :rejecting-route …}` at `[:rf.runtime/routing :pending-navigation]`.
- `decisions.cljc:526-536` (`continue-handler`): it checks only that the id matches, dissocs the slot, and dispatches `[:rf.route/navigate (merge destination policy {:bypass-leave? true})]`. It never checks that the current route is still the `:rejecting-route`.
- Only `continue-handler` (`:534`) and `cancel-handler` (`:546`) ever clear the slot.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:106-123` (`merge-route-slice`) merges under `:current` only. `commit-navigation` (`:180-348`), which both the navigate door and the URL door use, never touches `:pending-navigation`.

Repro (*probed* on the JVM at 9b20bf0093, whose routing sources are identical to 475bdcaacf; script `managed-routing-pending.clj`, using `re-frame.routing-test-support/reset-runtime`):

```clojure
(rf/reg-route :page/a {:can-leave :a/can-leave?} "/a")
(rf/reg-route :page/b {} "/b")
(rf/reg-route :page/c {:can-leave :c/can-leave?} "/c")
;; :a/can-leave? / :c/can-leave? are false while :a-dirty? / :c-dirty? are set
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/handle-url-change "/a" {:rf.route/cause :link}])
(rf/dispatch-sync [:a/dirty true])
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :page/b}])                     ; blocked, parks pn-1
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :page/c :bypass-leave? true}]) ; e.g. save-then-go
(rf/dispatch-sync [:c/dirty true])                                        ; C now refuses to leave
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/continue "pn-1"])
```

Observed:
- After the commit to C: the current route is `:page/c`, and the pending slot is still present with `:rejecting-route :page/a`.
- After `continue`: the current route is `:page/b`, although C's `:can-leave` was false.
- Control: a fresh `navigate {:to :page/b}` from C is blocked (it parks `pn-2`).

Contract:
- Spec 012:744 says the slot "is non-nil only while a `:can-leave` guard holds a blocked navigation awaiting `:rf.route/continue` / `:rf.route/cancel`". After the move to C, nothing on the current page holds it.
- Spec 012 §Navigation blocking (:1642) says continue bypasses the leave the user confirmed. The user confirmed leaving A, not C.

## Expected

A successful full (re)activation commit retires any parked leave question, so a late `continue` or `cancel` of the old id is a no-op.

## Fix direction

`commit-navigation` dissocs `[:rf.runtime/routing :pending-navigation]` on a full activation commit. That is one site, shared by both doors.

These keep the slot exactly as today, per Spec 012:1452 and :1664:
- fragment-only commits;
- exact no-ops;
- resource replans;
- entry denial (which commits nothing).

Add one sentence to Spec 012 §The leave decision saying that a successful activation retires the pending value.

## Acceptance

- A new test in `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_can_leave_test.clj` fails before the fix:
  1. Block A→B.
  2. Commit A→C, once via `:bypass-leave? true` and once via a clean guard.
  3. Make C's `:can-leave` false.
  4. Dispatch `[:rf.route/continue <old-id>]`.

  Assert the route stays `:page/c` and `:rf/pending-navigation` is nil right after the commit.
- The existing tests keep passing: wrong-id continue/cancel (`:142`), the pending-nav protocol (`:75`), and entry denial preserving an unrelated pending leave.
- A fragment-only navigation while a leave is pending leaves the slot byte-identical.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (Sol 12, insight 3), adopted by the Opus routing review as D12 / action 3.
- Related: rf2-inhw8 (routing prune follow-ups; a different defect). The link-door bead in this batch rewrites the same commit path. Sequence the two, or land this one-line dissoc first.
- Hot zones: none. `spec/012-Routing.md` is not on the hot-zone list.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/routing.md` §D12; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/12-routing.md` §3.

title: skills/README.md: state the family's authoring rules once (one owner per fact, copy census before folding feedback, load references by relevance, observed vs claimed evidence) and repair the residual stale copies
description:
## Problem

Skills learn the same lessons one at a time, because the family authoring guide (`skills/README.md`) has no rule for them. Their copies then drift.

- **Restated facts drift.** This is the biggest cause of rework across the skills this week (see the parent epic). Fix workers are briefed from the issue, which cites one passage, so other copies survive and come back as reopens or new issues. Only re-frame-migration has a feedback-folding procedure (`spec/improving.md`), and it has no copy-census step either.
- **Count caps on reference loading.** Rules like "load at most two leaves" truncated composed tasks and had to be removed skill by skill:
  - re-frame2: ea6ab19972 (rf2-jo4dg), then 7de24b0350 (rf2-m5q0v.1) for the copies round 1 missed
  - re-frame2-xray: 6f18496e27 (rf2-zawbl)
  - re-frame2-pair: 930e012efb (rf2-uk8u3)

  The cap came from the parent skill's "context economy" pillar.
- **Observed results vs claims.** Five of the six smaller skills learned on the same day, separately, to report what was observed apart from what was inferred or handed off:
  - re-frame2-setup: a compile does not prove a mount (dcccfc2916)
  - re-frame2-improver: a grep signal is not a finding, and an applied fix must be rechecked (5004713090)
  - re-frame2-implementor: a slice result is not the aggregate score, and "not run" beats an invented number (254097e7f9)
  - re-frame2-pair-retro: a catalogue match, or today's docs, say nothing about the session's build (965d61440b, 1314a6602e)
  - re-frame2-xray: `status()` cannot diagnose a preload that never compiled (3b06e8286a)

  The two migration skills got the same fix that day (rf2-m5q0v.3, .4). `skills/README.md` §"Verification posture — follows role, by design" says posture follows role, but this rule applies regardless of role and is written down nowhere.

## Residual stale copies (verified at trunk 9e84689562)

- `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:19` still says reference leaves load "at most two at a time".
- `skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/README.md:233` still grades "reading `>3` leaves for a single prompt" as pathological.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:42`: the executor paragraph lists install → compile → watch → URL, with no `npm test`.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:56` says the skill "stops at 'the counter mounts'". dcccfc2916 removed exactly that sentence from `design.md`.
- `skills/README.md` §Verification posture, the `re-frame2-setup` row (~L222), which calls itself the single source: it lists `npm install` + compile + watch + URL, with no `npm test`. It says "done" needs the programmer to confirm the counter, which contradicts the verified/handed-off split dcccfc2916 introduced.

## Direction (about 10-15 lines in `skills/README.md`, plus the copy repairs)

Add a short section to `skills/README.md` (near §Layout convention) with four rules:

1. **One owner per fact.** A fact about the framework, a tool or a procedure is stated in one file. Summaries (`SKILL.md` routers, READMEs, `docs/skills/*` mirrors, `spec/design.md`) name and link it, and never copy its conditions.
2. **Copy census before folding feedback.** Before fixing a reported fact, search its key tokens across the skill (`SKILL.md`, `references/`, `spec/`, `evals/`), its `docs/skills/` mirror, and the sources it cites (the corpus, the tool's docs). Fix every copy in the same commit, or collapse them to the owner, and list the copies in the PR body. Bump a tool pin rather than adding version caveats (cf. 411baa81ec).
3. **Reference loading.** Start from the leaf the task names, add others as their concerns apply, and leave unrelated leaves unloaded. No count caps.
4. **Evidence.** Report what was observed separately from what was inferred or handed off. A proxy (a compile, a grep hit, a catalogue match, a slice score) never stands in for the thing it proxies.

Then:

- Point `skills/re-frame-migration/spec/improving.md` Part 1 §4 at rule 2, rather than restating it.
- Repair the five residual copies above. In setup's `SKILL.md`, the intro and cardinal rule link to its §Canonical greenfield path instead of restating it.

## Acceptance

- `skills/README.md` carries the four rules once.
- `improving.md` points at rule 2.
- A git grep for leaf-count caps (`at most (one|two)` near "leaf/leaves/reference", and `>3` leaves) under `skills/` returns no loading caps. `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:216`'s "default route is SKILL.md plus at most one leaf" is a legitimate default-route pin, not a cap, and stays.
- The setup row in §Verification posture names `npm test`, and says browser checks are handed off as unverified.
- `check_doc_slugs.py` exits 0, and the setup and improver structural tests (`bb`) exit 0.

## Hot zone

None. The only overlap is with the sibling Pair bead (`skills/re-frame2-pair/`), and only at `spec/design.md:19`. That is one line, so it can go in either bead; say which in the PR.

title: ssr-node: a replacement isolate that fails to boot shrinks the pool for good while /health says ok and serve never exits
description:
## Bug

When ssr-node replaces a dead isolate and the replacement fails to boot, the pool loses that slot for good. `/health` keeps answering 200 `status: "ok"`, and the launcher waits only for SIGTERM/SIGINT, so the supervisor the README relies on never sees a failure to restart. A one-isolate pool ends at zero isolates, answering every render with a 503 `service-saturated` after the admission timeout, which is a status callers treat as retryable. The trigger is ordinary: render deadlines terminate workers routinely, and after an in-place bundle swap every replacement fails the build-identity check, so the pool shrinks by one slot per timeout.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-node/src/pool.cjs:199-251` (trunk 475bdcaacf) — `release` deletes the dead isolate, calls `_startReplacement()` once, and on failure logs (`reportReplacementFault`) and refuses current waiters with `ISOLATE_LOST`; the slot is never restored. `:208` says so: "A pool that cannot replace an isolate is a pool that shrinks."
- `pool.cjs:126-136` — a replacement whose `buildId` differs from the serving one is closed and refused `BUILD_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` ("the bundle changed on disk under a running service").
- `implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:253-265` — `handleHealth` always writes 200 with `status: 'ok'`, whatever `isolates.total` is.
- `implementation/ssr-node/bin/serve.cjs:166-172` — after the ready line, `main` awaits only SIGTERM/SIGINT; there is no service-failure exit.
- Repro, *probed* (plain `node` against the trunk sources, using the repo's `test/fixtures/flaky-boot.cjs`, whose replacements fail to boot once `RF2_SSR_NODE_FLAKY_BOOT=1` is set):
  ```js
  const service = await createService({ modulePath: FIXTURE, isolates: 1,
    defaultTimeoutMs: 300, maxTimeoutMs: 5000, admissionTimeoutMs: 250 });
  const t = await serve({ service, port: 0 });
  process.env.RF2_SSR_NODE_FLAKY_BOOT = '1';
  await post({ protocol: 1, entry: 'app/hang' });   // deadline kills the isolate
  ```
  ```
  health before {"status":200,"bodyStatus":"ok","isolates":{"total":1,"ready":1,...,"replacements":0}}
  hung render   504 :rf.ssr-node/render-timeout
  (stderr)      [rf.ssr-node] a replacement isolate failed to boot from .../flaky-boot.cjs: ...
  health after  {"status":200,"bodyStatus":"ok","isolates":{"total":0,"ready":0,...,"replacements":1}}
  later render  503 :rf.ssr-node/service-saturated "no isolate became free within 250 ms (pool of 1)"
  later render  503 :rf.ssr-node/service-saturated
  health still  {"status":200,"bodyStatus":"ok","isolates":{"total":0,...}}
  ```
- Contract: `implementation/ssr-node/README.md:738-744` — run the service "behind a supervisor that restarts on exit"; "a restart loses nothing but warm isolates". Initial boot already requires every configured isolate to start (`pool.cjs:98-117`), so a partly booted pool is not otherwise a supported state.

## Expected

A pool that can no longer reach its configured size stops reporting healthy and exits non-zero, so the supervisor restarts it.

## Fix direction

Make a failed replacement terminal, with no retry or backoff knobs: on replacement boot failure (build-identity mismatch included), close the service, refuse current and later callers with one stable closed code, terminate the remaining workers, make `/health` non-200, and have `serve.cjs` exit non-zero. This trades in-flight renders on healthy siblings for a restartable failure. If Mike prefers degraded capacity instead, the minimum is a truthful `/health` (non-200 below configured size) plus a documented recovery owner; the current silent shrink is neither.

## Acceptance

- Extend the existing replacement-failure fixture (`test/egress.test.cjs` §6, `fixtures/flaky-boot.cjs`) so that after a failed replacement: a later call gets the stable terminal refusal (fails today: 503 `service-saturated` after the admission wait), `/health` is not 200 `ok` (fails today), the launcher process exits non-zero (fails today: it keeps running), and no worker thread survives.
- Gate: `node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs` (plain node, no shadow-cljs).

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (ssr-node §4), adopted by Opus's cross-review (ssr-hosts D8, A1). Probed during bead drafting.
- Prior judgement: the correctness review rf2-3x7nj.15 (closed 2026-09-23) listed "pool shrinks permanently after a failed replacement, and `/health` keeps `status: ok` even at `total: 0`" under "considered and rejected" as deliberate, citing the `pool.cjs` comment, the unconditional stderr line and `isolates.total` in `/health`. That judgement did not weigh the launcher never exiting or the README's restart-on-exit recovery contract. rf2-2hmg (closed) made the stderr diagnostic unconditional.
- Related: rf2-6c25z (open) carries an ssr-node addendum noting no test drives a failed replacement with no caller waiting; this bead's test covers it.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr-hosts.md` D8, insight 2, A1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/30-ssr-node.md` §4.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (ssr-review, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) == Fixed in PR #11062, commit 5eb5dd1eab (branch worker/ssr-review). Not closed: the mayor closes on merge.

Premise held at tip f81adde3c5: Pool.release's replacement-failure arm logged, refused current waiters and kept serving at reduced size; handleHealth always wrote 200 "ok"; bin/serve.cjs awaited only SIGTERM/SIGINT.

Fix, the bead's primary direction per the mayor's choice (THIS IS THE REVERSAL POINT if Mike prefers degraded capacity): a failed replacement (a boot failure, or a bundle swapped on disk that loads a different buildId) is terminal. Pool sets failed, refuses waiters AND every later acquire() with ONE stable code — :rf.ssr-node/isolate-lost with REPLACEMENT_FAILED_REFUSAL, the code waiters already received, so the existing section-6 row is unchanged — then close()s itself (remaining workers terminate; an in-flight render on a healthy sibling is refused service-closed, as on any shutdown) and resolves pool.whenFailed. Service exposes failed / whenFailed. /health answers 503 with status "failed". bin/serve.cjs races the signal against whenFailed and exits 1, logging why. No retry or backoff knob. README (replacement paragraph, HTTP table, exit codes, Health) and the launcher's exit-code table updated.

Tests: egress.test.cjs section 6 gained "a replacement that cannot boot is TERMINAL: a later caller is refused, /health is not ok, and no worker survives" (two isolates, so a merely shrunken pool would have served the later call; waits on every worker thread's exit event). serve.test.cjs gained "a replacement that cannot boot ends the launcher with exit 1, so its supervisor restarts it" (copies flaky-boot to a temp dir, rewrites its buildId after the ready line, hangs one render; covers the build-identity route). Lane: node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs (plain node, no shadow-cljs). Red at base (later call served, i.e. refusal null; launcher still running after 20 s), green with the fix (9 suites, egress 26/26, serve 5/5, exit 0), red again with pool.cjs, service.cjs, http.cjs and bin/serve.cjs reverted to their pre-fix blobs, restored and verified by blob hash.

Coverage note for rf2-6c25z's ssr-node addendum: the new egress row is the "failed replacement with no caller waiting" case, and the serve row is the "replacement that loads a different buildId" case.
== HASH NOTE (ssr-review) == The branch was rebased onto trunk 4fed7ab27e before review; the fix commit is now 074147061f (was 5eb5dd1eab).
