So a ported `(reg-interceptor :app/unwrap {:before …})` that reshapes `:event` leaves every outer interceptor's `:after` seeing the reshaped payload, not the event vector, and nothing reports it.

Suggested addition to this item's fix: the M-59 interceptor recipe must stash the original event in its `:before` and restore `:event` in its own `:after`. re-frame2 does not do this for it.

title: core(interceptors): no non-throwing way for an interceptor to stop the rest of its chain; :rf/skip-handler? skips only the handler
description:
## Gap

An interceptor cannot stop the rest of its chain without throwing. v1 apps did this by emptying the context's `:queue` in a `:before` (auth guards, "not ready yet" gates). re-frame2 offers two partial routes, and neither one matches:

- `:rf/skip-handler? true` skips the handler alone (implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc, `wrap-event-handler`: `(if (:rf/skip-handler? ctx) ctx ...)`). Every later stage's `:before` and every `:after` still runs (`execute-chain` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc walks a fixed vector; only a captured `:rf/interceptor-error` short-circuits the `:before` pass).
- A throw reaches as far as v1's abort did (later `:before`s and the handler are skipped; only entered stages unwind). But the event commits nothing, not even an effect the guard added (such as a redirect `:fx` row), and each stopped event reports `:rf.error/interceptor-exception` on the always-on error channel (spec/002-Frames.md §Interceptor chain execution; spec/009 catalogue row).

## What a migrating author does today

The re-frame-migration skill (guided-interceptors-subs.md §Chain aborts) ports the guard to `(assoc ctx :rf/skip-handler? true)` in its `:before`, then has every later stage on the effective chain (frame refs, then event refs) check `(:rf/skip-handler? ctx)` and return `ctx` unchanged. A stage the app does not own cannot be made to check.

## v1 evidence

re-frame 1.4.3 `re_frame/interceptor.cljc` `invoke-interceptors` (lines 112-122): the loop pops the next interceptor from `:queue`, pushes it onto `:stack`, then calls it, and stops when `:queue` is empty. `change-direction` (lines 144-155) then primes `:queue` from `:stack`, so the `:after` pass runs only the interceptors up to and including the one that emptied it.

## Question

Whether v2 wants a non-throwing "stop here" signal for interceptors (one that skips later `:before`s and the handler, unwinds only entered stages, and still commits the guard's own effects), or whether skip-handler plus per-stage checks is the intended answer. If the latter, close with that ruling so the skill's guidance stands.

Suggestion, not a work order. Found while porting the migration skill's chain-abort guidance.

title: spec/013 and the M-30 skill section say per-flow :fx fires on flow output change; v1 also fired it on dead->live and on registration, which drives re-fetch on re-entry
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- spec/013-Flows.md §Migration from v1 alpha flows, the "Per-flow `:fx`" row (line 483).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md §M-30 also carries the flow-map conversion, the per-flow `:fx` bullet (line 276).

## What it says

- spec/013 :483: "Dropped. Dispatch an event from a handler if you need fx on flow output change."
- breaking-changes :276: "per-flow `:fx` — dropped. Dispatch a follow-up event whose handler reads the flow's output and emits the effect."

## What happened (generic)

v1's per-flow `:fx` fires on three transitions, not one:

- live -> live, when the inputs changed;
- dead -> live;
- registered -> live.

Apps use the dead -> live case to re-fetch when a tab or panel becomes live again with unchanged inputs. A follow-up event keyed to "output change" never fires there, so the re-fetch on re-entry disappears without an error.

## Evidence

re-frame v1 release 1.4.7 `src/re_frame/flow/alpha.cljc`:174-179:

```clojure
(case bardo
  [:live :live]       (when dirty? (concat fx (flow-fx …)))
  [:dead :live]       (concat fx (flow-fx …))
  [:registered :live] (concat fx (flow-fx …))
  nil)
```

Observed on a ~170-file app's widget-flow design unit.

## Suggested change

List all three firing transitions in both places. Say that the rewrite must reproduce each one the app relies on. In particular, the dead -> live case needs the event that flips the gate to dispatch the follow-up itself, because the output may not change.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): floor-gate Check 4 omits that the shadow-cljs 2 -> 3 bump drops the node-libs-browser polyfills, so a Node built-in require then fails the compile
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md, Check 4 "CLJS / shadow-cljs / Closure-compiler toolchain-skew check" (lines 73-93, the bump at line 87), and setup.md "The coord swap (M-0)" (line 22), which carries that bump into the M-0 dep-file pass.

## What it says

Line 87: "bump shadow-cljs to the version re-frame2 builds with ... This is a `package.json` `devDependencies` edit (`"shadow-cljs": "<reference-version>"`) plus an `npm install`". Check 4 then names three hazards of the bump: the `NoSuchFieldError` skew (:77-83), the Clojure 1.12 floor (`Invalid token: byte/1`, :89), and the watch-server-only reader form (:91). The reference pin it cites is shadow-cljs 3.4.10 (:85).

## What happened (generic)

For any v1 app on shadow-cljs 2.x, the bump to 3.x also removes the Node built-in polyfills from the build. shadow-cljs 2.x depended on `node-libs-browser` and mapped each Node built-in (`stream`, `crypto`, `path`, `os`, `events`, ...) to a browserify polyfill. shadow-cljs 3.x depends only on `buffer` and `process`. After the bump, any JS dependency in the build graph that requires another Node built-in fails the compile with `The required JS dependency "<name>" is not available`. That reads like a migration failure, not a toolchain change. Check 4 does not name this hazard, and a floor experiment that overlays the new shadow-cljs onto the old `node_modules` (for example `npm install --no-save`) keeps the old polyfill tree in place, so it cannot see the failure. Observed on a ~170-file app: the M-0 lockfile lost 114 packages (273 -> 159 `node_modules/` entries), the whole node-libs-browser tree.

## Evidence

* npm metadata in the two lockfiles: shadow-cljs 2.23.3 lists `"node-libs-browser": "^2.2.1"`. shadow-cljs 3.4.10 lists `"buffer": "^6.0.3"` and `"process": "^0.11.10"`, and `node-libs-browser` appears 0 times in the post-bump lockfile.
* shadow-cljs source, 2.28.3 jar, shadow/build/npm.clj:249-279: `(def node-libs-browser {... "crypto" "crypto-browserify" ... "path" "path-browserify" ... "stream" "stream-browserify" ...})`, citing webpack's node-libs-browser index.js. The 3.4.10 jar's npm.clj (1154 lines) holds 0 occurrences of node-libs-browser. In 3.4.10, shadow/build/resolve.clj:88-92 still lists the native module names, and a miss raises the `"The required JS dependency \"%s\" is not available"` error (:471).
* `git grep -n -i "node-libs\|polyfill\|node builtin\|node-builtin\|Node built"` over skills/ finds one unrelated hit (floor-gate.md:109, an `Object.fromEntries` host polyfill). Control: the same files hold 12 and 10 `shadow-cljs` mentions.
* The observed app needed no added polyfill, so this is a verified hazard, not an observed compile failure.

## Suggested change

In Check 4, after the Clojure-floor paragraph, add one paragraph: "shadow-cljs 3 no longer ships Node built-in polyfills (it dropped node-libs-browser; only `buffer` and `process` remain). A JS dependency that requires another built-in fails the compile with `The required JS dependency "<x>" is not available`. Fix it by adding that polyfill as an explicit dependency (for example `events`, `util`, `stream-browserify` with a `:js-options :resolve` entry), or by stubbing it out with `:resolve {"<x>" false}` when it is never reached in the browser." Also say that the floor experiment must resolve the bumped lockfile from scratch (`npm install --package-lock-only`, then `npm ci`, in a scratch worktree), not overlay the new version onto the old `node_modules`.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): orchestrating §2's Wave-0 contract fixes machine and interceptor ids but not the cross-unit call contracts M-11 creates (a helper in one unit reached from another unit's callback)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order), raised by the coordinating agent. Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md:

- §2 "The Wave-0 id-contract" (lines 61-71);
- §4 "Wave sequencing" (lines 85-93);
- read with §1's one-file-one-owner rule (line 51).

The census it reads is the M-11 row of inventory-and-plan.md Step 3.

## What it says

- :65-69 list three kinds of contract row: machine-ids, interceptor-ids and awaited event-ids.
- :71: "The contract is just *"id → owning unit"* for every machine-id and interceptor-id the migration introduces, plus each awaited event's owner and the dispatches it appends."
- :51: "two workers must NEVER touch the same source file".

## What happened (generic)

M-11 creates a third kind of cross-unit seam that §2 does not cover. Take a helper in unit A's file that reads the frame ambiently (dispatch or subscribe) and is reached from a callback in unit B's file. It can be fixed in only two ways:

- at B's call site, with `with-frame` around the call or a frame argument passed in;
- or by changing A's helper signature, which every caller's unit must then follow.

One-file-one-owner means A cannot edit B's call site, and B cannot edit A's helper. Nothing in §2 publishes these seams, so each one is found mid-sweep by whichever unit trips on it, and the orchestrator relays it between units by hand.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- Observed 3 times on a ~170-file app's fan-out: a modal opener, a preset-apply helper and a report-id lookup, each across a different unit pair. Each was found mid-sweep and relayed by hand.
- rf2-vhqcz covers the guided-views side of the same case: which frame-passing shape the helper takes. Its comment of 2026-10-28 05:46, item 3, proposes recording that shape in the Wave-0 contract. This item owns the orchestration and inventory side, so it can land in orchestrating-a-large-migration.md independently of that row.

## Suggested change

- **Phase 0a.** The M-11 census records, for every helper that reads the frame, which files reach it from a callback (and so which units), not only that the site exists.
- **§2.** Add call-contract rows to the Wave-0 contract. Each row gives:
  - the helper and its owning unit;
  - each caller unit;
  - the frame-passing shape the owner chose: a frame or frame-api argument, `with-frame` at the caller, or a value hoisted into the render;
  - which unit edits what.
  Publish these rows with the id rows, before Wave 1.
- **§4.** A caller unit whose fix depends on the helper's shape waits on that row, not on the helper's unit landing (the same argument rf2-0fne3 makes for ids).

title: spec(002): §The binary fx-handler signature's example registers :dispatch through reg-fx, which reg-fx now refuses
description:
spec/002-Frames.md §The binary fx-handler signature opens with this example, captioned "re-frame2's standard :dispatch fx, frame-aware":

    (reg-fx :dispatch
      (fn [m event]
        (rf/dispatch event {:frame (:frame m)})))

`:dispatch` is not a `reg-fx` registration: it is a reserved body in `re-frame.fx/reserved-fx-handlers`, run by `handle-one-fx` before any registry lookup. Since PR #11678 (rf2-30k48), `reg-fx` refuses `:dispatch` and `:dispatch-later` with `:rf.error/fx-registration-invalid`, so a reader who copies the example gets that throw. Conventions §Reserved fx-ids already said user code MUST NOT register one.

Fix: illustrate the binary signature with a user fx id instead (e.g. `:my-app/dispatch-in-frame`), keeping the point the example makes — `(:frame m)` is the frame id, fed into the `:frame` opt. One code block in a hot-zone file; sequence behind whatever holds spec/002.

Acceptance: the example registers no reserved fx-id; `check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.
